$315, because a month's supply of that covered insulin is capped at $105
$105, but only after the yearly Part B deductible has been satisfied
$35, because the cap covers the whole supply however long it lasts
preguntas.explicacion: Insulin covered under the Part B durable medical equipment benefit costs the patient no more than $35 for a month's supply, and the yearly Part B deductible is not applied to it. A three-month supply is capped at $35 for each of those months, which generally comes to no more than $105 in all. A Medigap policy that pays the Part B coinsurance should cover that amount.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting started with telehealth, Types of telehealth
preguntas.subtema: Remote patient monitoring · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice is listing what its remote monitoring program will accept. Which group of devices does the guidance name?
opciones: Pacemakers, glucose meters, blood pressure monitors, heart rate monitors, wireless scales, oximeters
Blood pressure monitors, fitness trackers, applications that record exercise, and dose reminders
Glucose meters, oximeters, wireless scales, and applications that store discharge instructions
Pacemakers, oximeters, secure messaging platforms, and applications that store health education
preguntas.explicacion: Remote patient monitoring means patient data and clinical information traveling to the provider, whether from devices kept in the home or keyed in and sent electronically by the patient. Named as examples: pacemakers, glucose meters, blood pressure monitors, heart rate monitors, wireless scales and oximeters. Fitness trackers, exercise applications and medicine reminders belong to mobile health, not here.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare Summary Notice (MSN)
preguntas.subtema: Accessible formats · CMAA 5 k65, k78 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA II.F.1.c(2) / 2027 II.F.1.d(3) · RMA II.A.2 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with very low vision says she cannot read her Medicare summary notice. What can she be told is available?
opciones: The notice in an accessible format, large print or Braille among them
The notice read out by a Medicare representative over the telephone
The notice in large print, but only for the electronic version of it
The notice in an accessible format, once her provider requests it for her
preguntas.explicacion: The summary notice can be had in an accessible format where the beneficiary needs one, with large print and Braille given as the examples. Electronic delivery is a separate choice, and it brings an e-mail carrying a link to the notice for any month in which a claim has been processed.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Helping patients prepare for their telehealth appointment
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth preparation · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.2.a · CMAA 4H k62 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: How early should a patient be told to connect for a video appointment, and why?
opciones: Fifteen minutes early, to leave room for last-minute troubleshooting
Thirty minutes early, so staff can complete the whole intake by telephone
Five minutes early, since the platform will reconnect automatically if it drops
Exactly on time, so the virtual waiting room does not fill with early arrivals
preguntas.explicacion: The guidance for getting set up tells patients to pick a spot with plenty of light and not to sit with a window behind them, to keep the camera steady and at eye level showing head and shoulders, to wear loose clothing where skin has to be shown, to find somewhere quiet, to close other applications, and, for a video appointment, to sign on fifteen minutes ahead so there is room to sort out any last-minute trouble.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: What Information is Protected
preguntas.subtema: Security Rule scope · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which information does the HIPAA Security Rule protect, as distinct from the Privacy Rule?
opciones: Only health information that is kept or transmitted in electronic form
Health information in any form, including paper charts and spoken conversations
Only the demographic fields the practice sends in a standard claim transaction
Only information that has already been encrypted or otherwise rendered unreadable
preguntas.explicacion: National standards for one subset of the health information that identifies an individual are what the Security Rule sets: the electronic PHI a regulated entity creates, receives, keeps or transmits. The Privacy and Breach Notification Rules go wider; this one does not reach PHI held on paper or spoken aloud. Its text sits in 45 CFR Part 160 and in Part 164, Subparts A and C.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases, chapter 5: Unpacking Deliveries
preguntas.subtema: Verifying deliveries · CCMA 5T · RMA II.B.5.a · CMAA 7D k99 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A shipment of vaccine arrives at the desk. Which check belongs to verifying the contents of that delivery?
opciones: Comparing what is inside against the packing list and looking for damage
Signing the carrier's manifest and moving the sealed box to the storeroom
Recording the arrival in the temperature log kept on the storage unit door
Waiting for the coordinator's shift to start before the box is touched at all
preguntas.explicacion: Unpacking is where verification happens: examine the shipping container and its contents for damage, compare the contents against the packing list, check that the right diluents came in the right quantity, and read the expiration dates. Leaving the box sealed defeats the check and the cold chain at the same time.

preguntas.fuente: USPS, Compare Mail Services: Media Mail
preguntas.subtema: Media Mail · CCMA 5O · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7G k96 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: An office is shipping loose-leaf medical reference pages and their binders to a satellite clinic on the cheapest eligible service. What must staff know about it?
opciones: Media Mail takes those pages and binders, and every package may be opened for inspection
Media Mail takes any office paper, and the contents of a package are never examined
Ground Advantage takes those pages, and packages of paper are exempt from inspection
Priority Mail takes those pages, and books are the only content it accepts by weight
preguntas.explicacion: Medical loose-leaf pages and binders are on the short list of what qualifies for Media Mail, along with books, printed music, recordings and manuscripts. The trade for the low price is that every Media Mail package may be opened and inspected, and anything ineligible inside means somebody pays the higher postage.

preguntas.subtema: Correction period · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3B k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: A violation is due to willful neglect. What period does the regulation give for correcting it before the top penalty tier applies?
opciones: Thirty days from the first date the entity knew, or would have known with reasonable diligence
Sixty days from the first date the entity knew, matching the deadline for breach notification
Ten working days from the first date the entity knew, as with new hire vaccination records
Six years from the first date the entity knew, matching the documentation retention period
preguntas.explicacion: Tier three catches willful neglect that gets put right inside a window of 30 days. The clock starts the day the entity, or the business associate acting for it, first knew of the violation, or would have known of it had reasonable diligence been used. Let that window close without correcting and the case drops into the fourth tier, the costliest one.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Part D (Drug Coverage) costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who put off joining a Medicare drug plan asks when a late enrollment penalty starts to apply.
opciones: Once she has gone sixty-three days or more without coverage as good as Part D
Once she has gone thirty days or more without coverage as good as Part D
Once eight months have passed since her job-based health coverage ended
Once her first seven months of Medicare eligibility have run out entirely
preguntas.explicacion: The way to dodge the Part D penalty is to join a drug plan when Part A or Part B first starts, and never to spend sixty-three days or more with no creditable drug coverage, meaning coverage similar in value to Part D. Someone on a limited income and with limited resources who qualifies for Extra Help pays no late enrollment penalty at all.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, "Talking With Your Older Patients", Families and caregivers as part of the health care team
preguntas.subtema: Caregivers · CCMA 6C k195 · CMAA 2A k16 · RMA I.D.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: A cognitive test is about to be done on an older patient whose son came along. Why might the son be asked to step out?
opciones: So he cannot answer for her or cover for any lapses
So he can finish her paperwork out in the waiting area
So he can be asked about her condition on his own
So the score can be worked out before she is told
preguntas.explicacion: Asking the companion to step out for part of the visit makes room for sensitive topics and gives the patient private time. During a test of cognitive abilities it serves a second purpose the guidance states outright: the companion is then unable to answer for her or to paper over her cognitive lapses.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, Administration for Community Living: Aging and Disability Networks
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4D k164 community resources · CMAA 2H k30
preguntas.pregunta: An older patient living alone needs home-delivered meals and help around the house. Which organization is the one to contact?
opciones: The Area Agency on Aging, which serves older adults regionally and locally
The Aging and Disability Resource Center, which only funds senior centers
The Center for Independent Living, which handles meals for older adults
The State Council on Developmental Disabilities, which arranges meals
preguntas.explicacion: Area Agencies on Aging work at the regional and local level on what older adults need to keep living independently, with homemaker assistance and meals delivered to the home among the examples given. Aging and Disability Resource Centers are the ones that give information and counseling about long-term services and help people reach programs.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Clinician & Group Survey; and Surveys
preguntas.subtema: Patient satisfaction surveys · CCMA 6J k207 · CMAA 2B k16
preguntas.pregunta: Which domains does the CAHPS Clinician and Group Survey cover?
opciones: Access, communication, care coordination and staff
Cleanliness, quiet, food service and discharge timing
Billing accuracy, waiting time, parking and signage
Staffing ratios, credentials, office hours and equipment
preguntas.explicacion: Every version of the survey asks about the same broad areas: how easily care can be obtained, how providers communicate, how care is coordinated, and how the staff treat people. The core items work across primary and specialty practices, and may take supplemental items. The CAHPS program itself began in 1995.

preguntas.subtema: Dental code set · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · CMA III.G.1 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: A practice adds a dental service line and asks which code set covers it, and who keeps that set up to date. What is the answer?
opciones: The dental procedure code set, kept by the American Dental Association
The dental procedure code set, kept by the federal health department
The procedure coding system for inpatients, kept by the federal health department
The common procedure coding system, kept by the American Medical Association
preguntas.explicacion: For dental services the regulation names the Code on Dental Procedures and Nomenclature. The American Dental Association is the body that maintains it and distributes it. The federal health department keeps the diagnosis set, the inpatient procedure set, and the level of the common procedure system that covers supplies and equipment.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC); and Medicare.gov, Federally Qualified Health Center services: Costs
preguntas.subtema: Community resources for care · CCMA 4D k162 · CMAA 2H k30 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient without insurance asks where she can be seen for primary care on a sliding scale based on what she can pay. What fits?
opciones: A federally qualified health center, whose fees slide with the patient's ability to pay
An ambulatory surgical center, where Part B pays the facility fee for an approved surgery
A hospital emergency department, which evaluates a sudden illness that quickly worsens
A skilled nursing facility, where daily skilled nursing or therapy is given short term
preguntas.explicacion: Federally qualified health centers are federally funded nonprofit centers and clinics that serve areas and populations which are medically underserved. They furnish primary care regardless of the patient's ability to pay, and the fee follows a sliding scale tied to that ability. Centers also offer lower fees to people with limited income.

preguntas.fuente: TRICARE, Health Plans
preguntas.subtema: Insurance types · CMA III.G.4.d (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182
preguntas.pregunta: Which TRICARE plans are the premium-based ones available worldwide?
opciones: TRICARE Reserve Select, Retired Reserve and Young Adult
TRICARE Prime, Prime Remote and the Family Health Plan
TRICARE Select, Select Overseas and Prime Remote Overseas
TRICARE Prime, the Prime demonstration and TRICARE For Life
preguntas.explicacion: The premium-based group, the one available worldwide, holds TRICARE Reserve Select, TRICARE Young Adult and TRICARE Retired Reserve. The plans listed for the United States are Prime, Prime Remote, the Uniformed Services Family Health Plan option, a Prime demonstration, Select and TRICARE For Life; the overseas group holds Prime Overseas, Prime Remote Overseas and Select Overseas.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms: Maximum Out-of-pocket Limit
preguntas.subtema: Cost sharing · CMA III.G.6.e (2027 III.G.6.c-d) · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: What does the maximum out-of-pocket limit that the federal government sets each year actually do?
opciones: It caps the cost sharing for covered care given inside the network
It caps the premium a plan may charge one family over the year
It caps what a provider outside the network may bill the patient
It caps the deductible a plan may apply to one single service
preguntas.explicacion: The federal figure is the ceiling on what one individual or family can be made to pay in cost sharing over the plan year for covered care taken in network, and it applies to most kinds of plan. A plan's own out-of-pocket limit may be lower than that ceiling. Premiums and balance-billed charges are never part of it.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Medicare Advantage (Medicare Part C); and Medicare.gov, Parts of Medicare
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.b / 2027 III.G.4 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: What is a Medicare Advantage Plan?
opciones: A private plan under contract with Medicare that delivers Part A and Part B benefits
A private plan sold by insurers that pays the patient's share of Original Medicare
A federal plan that replaces Part A for patients treated in a network of hospitals
A state plan that covers premiums and deductibles for people with low income
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare Advantage, also called Part C, comes from private companies under contract with Medicare to deliver every Part A and Part B benefit, usually with drug coverage on top; the types include health maintenance organizations and preferred provider organizations. Private insurance that pays the patient's share of Original Medicare is Medigap, and help with premiums for people on a low income comes through Medicaid.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Inappropriate Medical Abbreviations", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k10 · CMAA 1 k7 · RMA I.B.3.a
preguntas.pregunta: An institution allows DOA, which some staff read as date of admission and others as dead on arrival. Which rule does that break?
opciones: A permitted abbreviation may carry only one universal meaning
A permitted abbreviation may be used only in handwritten orders
A permitted abbreviation may be used only by the ordering provider
A permitted abbreviation may be used only after a pharmacist reviews it
preguntas.explicacion: Two meanings behind one set of letters is exactly the failure the rules are meant to stop: if an abbreviation is permitted at all, it must have a single universal meaning, and DOA is the classic example of one that does not. The same policy requires that nothing on the approved list also appear on the banned list.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with COPD asks what those letters mean. Which expansion is correct?
opciones: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, a disease of the lungs
Chronic obstructive peptic disorder, a stomach disease
Congenital obstructive pulmonary defect, a lung disease
Chronic occlusive peripheral disease, an artery disease
preguntas.explicacion: COPD is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, the long-standing lung condition that makes breathing hard. The look-alike abbreviations belong elsewhere: PUD is peptic ulcer disease, CHD is congenital heart disease and PAD is peripheral arterial disease, the arteries outside the heart.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Access to Medical Care for Individuals with Mobility Disabilities
preguntas.subtema: ADAAA compliance · CMAA 3A (ADAAA)
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with a disability comes in with a companion. Whom should the staff address?
opciones: The patient, as with anyone else; the companion stays if the patient wants
The companion, who can relay the information back to the patient later
The companion, unless the patient asks in writing to be addressed directly
The patient, but only once the companion has been asked to leave the room
preguntas.explicacion: Staff address the patient directly, exactly as they would any other patient: having a disability does not mean the person cannot speak for themselves or understand results. Whether a companion stays during the exam or the discussion is the patient's decision. A patient may also come alone, and the practice must give reasonable assistance.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Introduction; and Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Patient rights · CCMA k215 · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32
preguntas.pregunta: What is the relationship between an ethical principle and a patient right?
opciones: A right appears when a body with authority enforces an ethical standard
A right appears when a professional society publishes it in its own code
A right appears when a majority of patients in a survey come to expect it
A right and an ethical principle are the same thing under a different name
preguntas.explicacion: Human rights are the minimum standards for how people can expect to be treated; ethics are the customary standards for how people should treat others. Every patient right rests on one or more ethical principles, and a right exists at the moment an organization with the authority to enforce that ethical standard actually enforces it. As ethics shift over time, so do rights.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information
preguntas.subtema: Electronic notice delivery · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice takes its first new patients through an online intake before any in-person visit. What does the notice rule require?
opciones: An electronic notice sent automatically with the first request, and an attempt at a return receipt
A paper notice mailed within thirty days of the electronic request for service being received
An electronic notice posted on the web site only, since online patients can read it there
A telephone call reading the notice aloud, since electronic delivery cannot be acknowledged
preguntas.explicacion: Where the first delivery of service happens over the Internet, by e-mail or in some other electronic way, the notice goes out electronically, automatically and at the same moment as the patient's first request for service, and the provider has to make a good faith effort to get back a return receipt or another response transmission. Any web site describing the entity's services or benefits must carry the notice prominently as well.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting started with telehealth, Understanding telehealth technology options
preguntas.subtema: Consent before a video visit · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: When does the telehealth guidance say informed consent for a video visit has to be obtained?
opciones: Before the appointment, alongside a platform that meets the privacy requirements
At the start of the appointment, once the clinician has confirmed who the patient is
Only where the session will be recorded or a third party is to be brought into it
After the appointment, when the visit is documented as having been done by video
preguntas.explicacion: Patients may worry about privacy and about data security, both over what they share during a visit and over home devices that collect their health data. Providers are told to deliver telehealth from private locations, to apply safeguards that are reasonable to the protected health information, to use a platform that meets the privacy requirements, and to obtain informed consent from the patient before the telehealth appointment.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fighting Identity Theft with the Red Flags Rule
preguntas.subtema: Identity theft protection · CCMA 5F · CMA III.H.2.b · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 4C k63 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: How many elements must a written identity theft prevention program contain under the Red Flags Rule?
opciones: Four: identify, detect, respond and update
Three: identify, detect and report to the police
Five: identify, detect, respond, update and insure
Two: identify the red flags and train the staff on them
preguntas.explicacion: The program must include reasonable policies for identifying the red flags of identity theft in day-to-day operations, procedures designed to detect the flags it identified, the actions to take when one is detected, and a way of keeping the program current against new threats. A red flag is a suspicious pattern, practice or activity signaling possible identity theft, such as an identification document that does not look genuine.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: The note describes a threatened condition that in the end did occur. How is it coded?
opciones: As a confirmed diagnosis, just as if it had been documented outright
As threatened, using the index subentry for that term where it exists
As threatened, since that is the word the provider used in the record
Not at all, because a threatened condition is an uncertain diagnosis
preguntas.explicacion: A condition the note calls impending or threatened is coded as a confirmed diagnosis if it did in fact occur. Only when it did not occur does the coder look for a subentry for impending or threatened, and where no such subentry exists the underlying conditions are coded instead of the threatened one.

preguntas.subtema: Medicare Advantage records · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: A plan holds a Medicare Advantage contract. For how long must it keep the books and records behind that contract?
opciones: Ten years, so that the accounting and the services can be audited and inspected
Seven years from the date of service, as with orders and certifications in Part B
Five years, as with the medical records a hospital keeps to take part in Medicare
Six years from creation, as with the documentation the privacy standards require
preguntas.explicacion: Every retention period in this area belongs to a different rule, and the trap is borrowing one for another. The Medicare Advantage contract obliges the organization to keep its books, records and other evidence of accounting for ten years, enough for CMS to audit the finances and to inspect the quality and timeliness of the services.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms: Out-of-pocket Limit
preguntas.subtema: Insurance terminology · CMA III.G.6.e (2027 III.G.6.c-d) · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient adds up what she has spent and asks which of it will never count toward her out-of-pocket limit.
opciones: Her premium, any balance-billed charge, and care the plan does not cover
Her copayments and the deductible she paid earlier in the same plan year
Her in-network coinsurance on services the plan does in fact cover for her
Her deductible and the coinsurance she paid at a preferred provider's office
preguntas.explicacion: The out-of-pocket limit is the most a person could pay in a coverage period for her share of covered services, after which the plan usually pays the whole allowed amount. It never includes the premium, balance-billed charges or care the plan does not cover, and some plans leave out out-of-network payments and certain other expenses as well.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Exclusive Provider Organization (EPO) Plan
preguntas.subtema: Commercial plan types · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: Which managed care plan covers services only from doctors, specialists and hospitals in its network, except in an emergency?
opciones: An exclusive provider organization plan
A preferred provider organization plan
A point of service plan with referrals
A fee-for-service indemnity arrangement
preguntas.explicacion: The exclusive provider organization is the managed care plan whose coverage stops at the edge of the network, with the emergency exception. A PPO pays something for outside providers at a higher cost to the patient. A point of service plan also pays less outside the network and adds the referral rule. Fee for service is a payment method, one payment per service delivered, not a network design.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Body Parts and Disorders; Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A soft fatty lump under the skin is reported as a lipoma. Which two word parts build that term?
opciones: A root meaning fat plus an ending meaning tumor
A root meaning fat plus an ending meaning inflammation
A root meaning muscle plus an ending meaning tumor
A root meaning fat plus an ending meaning enlargement
preguntas.explicacion: Lip- and lipo- name fat, and so does adip-; the ending -oma is a tumor. The endings that crowd around it say something else entirely: -itis is inflammation, -megaly is enlargement and -osis is an abnormal condition. Muscle is my- or myo-, so a tumor built on that root would be a myoma.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Selective Access
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, confidentiality · CMAA 3B k38 safeguards · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital gives its laboratory technologists access to laboratory records but not to the full medical history. What is that practice called, and does HIPAA allow it?
opciones: Selective, role-based access, which is exactly the way the rule expects internal access to work
Selective, role-based access, which the rule discourages because it slows care coordination
A limited data set, which HIPAA permits only for research, public health or health operations
A hybrid entity designation, which limits the rules to the components that do covered work
preguntas.explicacion: Holding each worker to the part of the record their role requires is exactly what the rule asks: the policies have to name who, or which classes of people, need access, which categories of information they need, and on what conditions. A limited data set is a stripped-down form of information for research and similar uses, and a hybrid entity is an organizational choice, not an access control.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Claim Denial Rate
preguntas.subtema: Authorizations and denials · CMAA 6E, 4G k67 · CCMA 5M k183 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: A denial arrives stating that the billed procedure differs from the one authorized. What does the source of that problem suggest for next time?
opciones: Update the authorization before the claim goes out when the procedure changes
Send the claim unchanged, since the payer matches authorizations automatically
Bill the patient for the difference, since the authorization covered part of it
Wait for the appeal decision before asking the payer to change any authorization
preguntas.explicacion: Among the causes of denials, billing a procedure code that differs from the authorized one is listed with its own remedy: update the information before submission or justify the discrepancy clearly. Some payers will change an authorization only up to 14 days past the date of service, after which the denial tends to become permanent, so waiting for an appeal wastes the window. Nothing in that mismatch makes the balance a patient responsibility.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(g)(1), (g)(3) and (g)(5), Personal representatives
preguntas.subtema: Personal representatives · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.3.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: A parent asks for the lab results of their 8-year-old child. How does HIPAA treat the parent?
opciones: As the child's personal representative, acting as the individual for that PHI
As a third party who needs the child's own signed authorization first
As a family member entitled only to a verbal summary at the visit
As a personal representative only after a court has appointed the parent as guardian
preguntas.explicacion: Under section 164.502(g) a personal representative is treated as if they were the individual. For an unemancipated minor that representative is the parent, the guardian or a person acting in loco parentis who holds authority under applicable law to make health care decisions, and it covers the PHI relevant to that role, with no court appointment needed. The exceptions are services the minor may lawfully consent to alone, and situations of abuse or endangerment where the entity may refuse to treat the person as representative; state law can widen or narrow parental access.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Anatomical Terminology, Directional Terms
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k13 · CMA I.C.6.e (2027 I.C.6.d) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k11 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A report describes one structure as cranial to another. Which directional term is used for that same idea?
opciones: Superior, toward the head end of the body
Inferior, away from the head end of the body
Anterior, toward the front of the body
Posterior, toward the back of the body
preguntas.explicacion: Most directional terms travel in pairs that mean the same thing: superior and cranial point toward the head, inferior and caudal away from it, anterior and ventral name the front, and posterior and dorsal the back. That is why the hand belongs to the superior extremity and the foot to the inferior one.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.404(a), (b) and (d), Notification to individuals
preguntas.subtema: Breach notification deadline · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3E k33
preguntas.pregunta: A breach of unsecured PHI has just been discovered. How fast must the covered entity notify the individuals affected?
opciones: No more than 60 calendar days after discovery, and without unreasonable delay
Within 30 days after discovery, matching the right-of-access deadline
Within 90 days after discovery, the period a substitute web notice stays posted
By the end of the calendar year, regardless of the number of individuals
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.404 requires notice to every individual whose unsecured PHI was accessed, acquired, used or disclosed, or is reasonably believed to have been. Two limits apply at once: no unreasonable delay, and 60 calendar days from discovery as the outer edge. A breach counts as discovered the first day it is known, or would have been known with reasonable diligence, to any workforce member other than the one who caused it. Written notice travels by first-class mail, or by e-mail if the person agreed to that; where contact details are missing for 10 or more people, a substitute posting on the website or a media notice runs for 90 days.

preguntas.subtema: Activity review · CCMA 5 k189 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which administrative safeguard makes a practice review, on a regular basis, records of system activity such as the audit logs and the reports on access and on security incidents?
opciones: Information system activity review, part of the security management process
Audit controls, the technical standard that makes the system record the activity
Evaluation, the periodic check of whether the policies still meet the standards
Security reminders, the periodic updates sent to every member of the workforce
preguntas.explicacion: Audit controls make the system capable of recording and examining activity; the duty to actually read what it recorded is a different, required specification of the security management process, called information system activity review. A practice can satisfy one and fail the other.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Nonverbal Communication
preguntas.subtema: Nonverbal cues · CCMA 6C k197 · CMAA 2C k14 · CMA F.1.d / 2027 F.1.e · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is counted as nonverbal communication?
opciones: The pace at which the conversation is carried
The words chosen so the receiver understands
The feedback message returned to the sender
The handout given in the patient's own language
preguntas.explicacion: Nonverbal communication covers facial expressions and body language, the tone of voice and the pace of the conversation, and it may carry more weight than the words themselves. Choosing words the receiver understands is the definition of verbal communication; the return message is the feedback step of the cycle; a handout is written communication.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", Issues of Concern: Children
preguntas.subtema: Consent for minors · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c · NCMA 4.7 · CMAA 3D k40
preguntas.pregunta: When a parent authorizes a procedure for their 9-year-old, what is that authorization called?
opciones: Informed permission, since consent itself belongs to the patient
Implied consent, because the parent brought the child in for care
Proxy consent, given under a durable power of attorney for the child
Waived consent, the category used when a patient cannot sign for themselves
preguntas.explicacion: Children, typically those under 18, cannot give informed consent, so the parent or legal guardian permits the treatment and the process is named informed permission instead. Implied consent is inferred from the patient's own situation, such as an emergency. A waiver is when the patient voluntarily gives the consent process up, and a power of attorney is a document an adult signs about their own care.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: malpractice
preguntas.subtema: Malpractice · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3A k31
preguntas.pregunta: How is malpractice defined as a legal term?
opciones: Professional negligence: breaching the duty to follow accepted professional standards
Any error a professional makes while a patient is under that professional's care
An intentional act by a professional that the client did not agree to beforehand
A breach of the written contract between a professional and the paying client
preguntas.explicacion: Malpractice is professional negligence, the tort that arises where a professional breaks the duty owed to a client, and that duty is generally to keep to the professional standards that are generally accepted. Every other element of a negligence tort still has to be shown too: the duty, the breach, both kinds of causation and the damages. Doctors and lawyers are the commonest defendants.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow, Follow up after telehealth visits
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth scheduling · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether every one of her follow-ups can now be booked by video. How does the workflow guidance answer that?
opciones: It can bridge between office visits, but some care needs one
It replaces office visits once the patient is set up on it
It is limited to the first visit for any new problem
It is used only when the patient cannot travel to the office
preguntas.explicacion: Virtual care is put forward as a bridge that sits between visits to the office: part of the care still calls for the patient to be in the room, and it is the mixture of the two that supports care management. Nothing in the guidance limits virtual visits to new problems or to patients who cannot travel.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Home health services: Coverage details
preguntas.subtema: Home health aide coverage · CCMA 4D k162 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: Under what condition does Medicare pay for a home health aide?
opciones: Only while the patient also gets skilled nursing or therapy at the same time
Only while the patient is also enrolled in the hospice benefit during that period
Only after the patient has used up all 100 days of skilled nursing facility care
Only when the aide has passed the state competency exam for nursing assistants
preguntas.explicacion: Home health aide care on a part-time or intermittent basis is covered only where the patient is at the same time receiving skilled nursing care, or physical therapy, or occupational therapy, or speech-language pathology services. Aide help covers bathing, walking or grooming, feeding, and changing the bed linens. Custodial care alone, with no skilled service beside it, is not covered.

preguntas.subtema: Order documentation retention · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: A physician orders a Part B diagnostic test. How long must documentation of that written order be kept and made available to CMS?
opciones: Seven years from the date of service
Five years from the date of service
Six years from the date of service
Three years from the date of service
preguntas.explicacion: The enrollment regulation puts the duty on both sides. Whoever furnishes the Part A or Part B service that was ordered or certified, referred or prescribed, and the physician or eligible professional who ordered it, must each hold the documentation for seven years from the date of service and give CMS or a Medicare contractor access on request. That documentation includes the NPI of the ordering professional.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Telehealth: Description
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth modalities · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient describes a non-face-to-face exchange with her doctor that took place through the practice's online portal. What is that called?
opciones: An e-visit, one of the ways of communicating with a provider through telehealth
A virtual check-in, a brief real-time exchange lasting ten minutes or less
Remote patient monitoring, which sends clinical data from a device to the provider
Store-and-forward, where an image is uploaded for a specialist to read later
preguntas.explicacion: Telehealth means medical services taken from a provider elsewhere in the country over audio and video, and in some cases over audio alone. Two of the named routes are e-visits, exchanges that are not face to face and that usually run through the practice's online portal, and virtual check-ins, short live exchanges that usually last ten minutes or less.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A documented condition has no code of its own, and the Alphabetic Index shows the abbreviation NEC. What does that point the coder to?
opciones: The other specified code for that condition in the Tabular List
The unspecified code for that condition, which NOS also stands for
The excluded code above the note, which is never reported alongside
The manifestation code, which is bracketed and sequenced second
preguntas.explicacion: NEC stands for not elsewhere classifiable and, in both the Index and the Tabular List, represents the other specified code: it is used when the record has detail for which no specific code exists. NOS stands for not otherwise specified and is the equivalent of unspecified, which is used when the record does not have enough detail to be more precise.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k12 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what the note means by an upper respiratory infection. Which everyday term matches it?
opciones: The common cold
A stomach bug
A urinary infection
A skin infection
preguntas.explicacion: URI stands for upper respiratory infection, which is another name for the common cold. Translating it out loud is part of the job, because the abbreviations the staff use daily are not the words a patient uses. A urinary tract infection is UTI, one letter away and a completely different problem.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Hospice care: Facility
preguntas.subtema: Hospice settings · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: Where can a patient receive Medicare-approved hospice care?
opciones: At home or in the place where the patient lives, and in an inpatient hospice facility
Only in a freestanding inpatient hospice facility approved by Medicare for that use
Only in the patient's private home, since the benefit is built around care at home
In any hospital that takes Medicare, whenever a bed on the medical floor is free
preguntas.explicacion: Hospice care is usually given at home or in another place where the patient lives, such as an assisted living facility or a nursing home, and under certain conditions in an inpatient hospice facility. If the team decides inpatient care in a hospital is needed, the team has to make the arrangements; otherwise the patient can be left responsible for the entire cost.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.500(a)-(c), Applicability; 45 CFR 164.502(e); StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", To Whom Does HIPAA Apply
preguntas.subtema: Covered entities and business associates · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33
preguntas.pregunta: Which of the following is a HIPAA covered entity?
opciones: A health care provider that transmits claims electronically
An outside computer repair company that services the lab's servers
A pharmaceutical sales representative who visits the clinic
An accredited agency that conducts patient satisfaction surveys
preguntas.explicacion: The Privacy Rule binds covered entities, which are health plans, health care providers that transmit health information electronically, and clearinghouses, and it binds business associates as regards a covered entity's PHI; a clearinghouse acting as a business associate follows a narrower set of sections. Outside computer repair firms, survey agencies, equipment companies and pharmaceutical representatives are examples of third parties who reach PHI only through business associate arrangements, which require written satisfactory assurances.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse: Prevent, Detect, Report (MLN4649244), Criminal Health Care Fraud Statute
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: A group of clinics ran a scheme, knowingly and willfully, to obtain money from a health benefit program. Which law is aimed at exactly that?
opciones: The criminal health care fraud statute, which reaches any such program
The civil False Claims Act, which asks for no specific intent at all
The Anti-Kickback Statute, which reaches payment made for referrals
The exclusion statute, which keeps offenders out of those programs
preguntas.explicacion: The criminal health care fraud statute covers knowingly and willfully carrying out, or trying to carry out, a scheme to defraud a health care benefit program or to obtain its money by false pretenses, and it is punished with fines, imprisonment or both. The other laws named reach false claims, remuneration for referrals and participation itself.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow, Preparing for telehealth visits
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth accommodations · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with hearing loss is being booked for her first video visit. Which planning question does HHS file under meeting patient needs?
opciones: How the practice will support patients with a disability such as hearing or vision loss
How the practice will bill for the extra minutes a supported appointment will take up
How the practice will judge whether the request suits a telehealth appointment at all
How the practice will know that its staff are comfortable using the new technology
preguntas.explicacion: Meeting patient needs takes in how the office will work out what accommodations a patient might need, how and when reminders reach her, how support will be arranged for a patient whose disability is a hearing loss or a loss of vision, and how a caregiver or other helper will be supported through the visit. Judging appropriateness is a scheduling question; comfort with the technology is a staffing one.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, How Medicare works with other insurance
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMA III.G.3.a (2027 III.G.3.a) · CMAA 5 k75 · CCMA 5B · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: How far does the primary payer go before a claim passes to the secondary payer?
opciones: It pays up to the limits of its own coverage and sends on the rest of the balance
It pays the whole allowed amount and sends on only the patient's own cost sharing
It pays half of the allowed amount and sends on the remaining half of the balance
It pays up to the limits of the secondary plan and sends on the unpaid remainder
preguntas.explicacion: The primary payer covers up to the limit of its own coverage and hands what is left over to the secondary payer. Where the secondary payer does not pick that remainder up, the patient can be left owing it. This ordering of payment is what coordination of benefits means. Where the group health or retiree coverage is the one paying second, it may pay nothing at all until the patient has signed up for Part B.

preguntas.fuente: plainlanguage.gov, Plain language guides, Overview
preguntas.subtema: Communication by channel · CCMA 6C k196 · CMAA 2C k19
preguntas.pregunta: What does the Plain Writing Act of 2010 require of content written for the public?
opciones: That it be written for its specific audience
That it be reviewed by a certified translator
That it be offered in at least three languages
That it be tested on a panel of ten readers
preguntas.explicacion: Plain language means content that is clear and easily understood; besides being more efficient and more effective it is a legal duty, since it was the Plain Writing Act of 2010 that required whatever is written for the public to be written for its specific audience. Testing content for understanding is guidance, not the statutory requirement.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System: How We Conduct Case Surveillance
preguntas.subtema: Communicable disease reporting · CCMA 7F k222 · CMA E.6.a / 2027 E.5.a · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k43
preguntas.pregunta: Who legally requires a positive result for a notifiable condition to be reported, and to whom?
opciones: State law requires it to the health department; notifying the CDC is voluntary
Federal law requires it to the CDC; notifying the health department is voluntary
State law requires it to the CDC, which then informs the health department
Accreditation standards require it to both, on the same reporting form
preguntas.explicacion: Hospitals, providers and laboratories report positive results or diagnosed cases to the appropriate health department under state disease reporting laws, and that case reporting is mandatory. What the state and local health departments then send on to the CDC is de-identified data about confirmed cases, and that notification is voluntary.

preguntas.fuente: DOL, Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Outlook Handbook: Medical Assistants
preguntas.subtema: Administrative responsibilities · CCMA 1 k2 · CMA II.F.4 · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 1 k2 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which duties does the Bureau of Labor Statistics list on the administrative side of a medical assistant's job?
opciones: Answering telephones, scheduling appointments and restocking office supplies
Setting the fee schedule and negotiating the practice's contracts with health plans
Auditing the practice's claims for fraud and reporting findings to the payer
Approving which staff members may open the electronic health record system
preguntas.explicacion: Medical assistants take on both administrative and clinical work, and often specialize in one of the two. On the administrative side the Handbook describes helping patients get to grips with their insurance and obtain coverage: filling out forms, coding the information, ringing the companies about a bill. It also lists keeping medical and office supplies inventoried and restocked, answering the telephone and scheduling appointments.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: What should I know before my telehealth visit?
preguntas.subtema: Patient instructions · CMAA 4E k59 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks the scheduler whether she can take her video visit while she drives to work. What does the patient guidance say?
opciones: She should not, since a telehealth visit is not to be taken while driving or on errands
She may, if she switches to audio only and pulls over whenever an examination is required
She may, provided the car has hands-free equipment and the connection is private
She should not, unless the appointment is a brief exchange of ten minutes or less
preguntas.explicacion: The tips for a successful visit tell the patient to stay on track, which means leaving food and drink alone while the visit lasts, and to stay safe, which means not taking a visit at the wheel or in the middle of errands. She is also told to sign on early so she can message or telephone the office if the video refuses to start, and to be patient when the clinician runs late.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Data Safeguards
preguntas.subtema: Processing mail · CCMA 5O · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7D · NCMA 3.6
preguntas.pregunta: Incoming mail includes lab reports for several patients. What does the Privacy Rule require of the way it is handled?
opciones: Reasonable safeguards protecting it against uses the rule does not permit
An accounting entry for each report before it is filed in the record
A business associate agreement with the carrier that delivered the mail
A written authorization from each patient whose report arrived that day
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity has to keep safeguards in place, administrative, technical and physical alike, that protect against uses and disclosures the rule does not permit and that hold incidental ones down. What counts as reasonable shifts with the size of the entity and the nature of its business; the examples given are shredding documents that hold PHI before throwing them out, and keeping records under lock and key or behind a pass code.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Part A (Hospital Insurance) costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74, 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A hospice patient being cared for at home asks what she may be charged for a medicine given to control her pain.
opciones: A copayment of up to $5 for each drug prescribed for pain or symptom control
A copayment of up to $35, the ceiling that applies to a month of covered insulin
Twenty percent of the approved amount, as with most services covered by Part B
Five percent of the approved amount, which is the share for inpatient respite care
preguntas.explicacion: Covered hospice services cost the patient nothing under Part A. What she may still owe is up to $5 in copayment on each prescription drug, and on similar products used at home to relieve pain and control symptoms, plus five percent of the amount approved for respite care given as an inpatient. The $35 ceiling belongs to covered insulin under Part B.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, section 809
preguntas.subtema: Collections · CMAA 6D · CCMA 5 k187 · CMA III.G.9.f (exam through June 2027)
preguntas.pregunta: A patient disputes a medical debt in writing within the 30-day window. What must the collector do?
opciones: Stop collection until it mails the patient verification of the debt
Stop collection permanently and close the account as uncollectible
Continue collection while it asks the provider for the chart notes
Report the dispute to a consumer reporting agency within five days
preguntas.explicacion: When the consumer disputes the debt in writing inside the 30 days, or asks for the original creditor's name and address, the collector must stop collecting the disputed portion until it has obtained either verification of the debt or a copy of the judgment and mailed that to the consumer. The pause is temporary, not a cancellation, and failing to dispute a debt may not be treated by a court as an admission of liability.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), MSP Contractor Claims Investigation
preguntas.subtema: Claim follow-up · CMA III.G.3.b(4) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6 k87 · CCMA 5 k185
preguntas.pregunta: A claim reaches the Medicare contractor with another insurer's remittance attached but no record of the other coverage. What may come next?
opciones: A questionnaire to the patient or the insurer asking for the other coverage details
A denial issued at once, because the coverage details cannot now be reconstructed
A request that the provider resubmit without the other insurer's remittance attached
A conditional payment issued at once, to be recovered from the other insurer later
preguntas.explicacion: Where the contractor does not hold full information on other insurance that might be primary, it asks the secondary payer contractor for more, and that contractor may send the patient, the employer, the insurer or the attorney a questionnaire for developing the secondary claim. It is used when a claim arrives with another insurer's explanation of benefits or remittance, when payment information appears in the electronic loops, or when the patient or an attorney reports it.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), Your Responsibilities
preguntas.subtema: Insurance verification · CMA III.G.3.a (2027 III.G.3.a) · CMAA 5B k66 · CCMA 5B
preguntas.pregunta: Registration finds an open workers' compensation record in a Medicare patient's eligibility file. May the hospital turn her away?
opciones: No, because care may not be refused over an open or closed secondary payer record
Yes, because admission may wait until the compensation carrier confirms it will pay
Yes, because admission may be refused unless she signs a responsibility agreement
No, because care may not be refused, but the claim waits until the record is closed
preguntas.explicacion: A provider may not refuse Part A or Part B services, nor refuse admission to a hospital or a skilled nursing facility, on the strength of an open or closed record for a group or non-group health plan, a no-fault or workers' compensation record, or a claim mistakenly denied over one of them. Doing so runs against Medicare law and policy. The claim still goes to the primary payer first, but the care does not wait for that.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) General Information
preguntas.subtema: Procedural coding · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · CMA III.G.1.c · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: What separates HCPCS Level I from HCPCS Level II?
opciones: Level I is CPT, kept by the AMA; Level II names supplies and equipment and is kept by CMS
Level I is CPT, kept by CMS; Level II names supplies and equipment and is kept by the AMA
Level I codes diagnoses and Level II codes the procedures done to treat them
Level I is used by hospitals for inpatient care and Level II by offices for visits
preguntas.explicacion: HCPCS has two subsystems. Level I is Current Procedural Terminology, a numeric system of five digits that the American Medical Association maintains and republishes each year. Level II is a standardized alphanumeric system, a letter followed by four digits, for products, supplies and services outside Level I such as ambulance and durable medical equipment, and CMS maintains it. Diagnoses are coded in ICD-10-CM.

preguntas.subtema: Contingency operations · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A burst pipe closes the suite, and the technicians need to get inside the damaged office to bring the data back. Which specification should have planned for that?
opciones: Contingency operations, which arrange facility access in support of the recovery plans
Emergency access procedure, which gets a clinician to the record during an emergency
Applications and data criticality analysis, which ranks what has to come back first
Testing and revision procedures, which put the contingency plan through a rehearsal
preguntas.explicacion: Contingency operations is the physical safeguard: procedures allowing access to the facility so that lost data can be restored under the disaster recovery and emergency mode plans. The emergency access procedure is the technical twin, and it is about reaching the information itself, not the building.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Hospital-wide Hazards: Fire Hazards, 29 CFR 1910.38(b) and 1910.39(b)
preguntas.subtema: Emergency action plan · CPT D1 1A 1L k24 · PBT VI.G.2 · CMA I.B.8.a / 2027 I.B.7.a · RMA II.B.7.c · NCMA 2A.9 · CMAA 3A k45
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic with 8 employees asks whether its emergency action plan must be in writing. What does OSHA's rule provide?
opciones: With 10 or fewer employees the plan may be communicated orally
It must be in writing regardless of size and posted at each exit
With fewer than 25 employees it may be oral; above that it must be written
It may be oral only if the clinic also has no fire prevention plan
preguntas.explicacion: Under 29 CFR 1910.38(b), as the eTool summarizes it, an emergency action plan is normally written, kept at the workplace and available to employees; where there are 10 employees or fewer, the employer may simply brief them orally. Section 1910.39(b) sets the same threshold for the fire prevention plan. The two plans stand apart, so having or lacking one changes nothing for the other. With 8 employees this clinic may brief its staff by word of mouth, though the minimum elements of 1910.38(c) still have to be covered.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 2.1
preguntas.subtema: Downtime job aid · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which job aid does the contingency guidance suggest an organization hand its staff for use during an outage?
opciones: A small self-contained card or checklist of the resources and actions available
A printed copy of the whole electronic record of every patient booked that day
A telephone list of the software developer's support engineers and their hours
A binder holding the last six months of temperature and equipment inspection logs
preguntas.explicacion: Next to training and drills the guidance names a concrete tool: a job aid, which it describes as a reference card or checklist, small and self-contained, that helps staff locate the resources and the actions open to them while the record system is down. It is meant to work when nothing on the screen can be consulted.

preguntas.subtema: Automatic logoff · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: The record system ends a session by itself after fifteen idle minutes. Which technical specification is that, and what is its status?
opciones: Automatic logoff, an addressable specification of the access control standard
Unique user identification, a required specification of that same standard
Emergency access procedure, a required specification of that same standard
Person or entity authentication, a standard with no specification of its own
preguntas.explicacion: Access control carries four specifications: unique user identification and emergency access are required, while automatic logoff and encryption are addressable. Ending a session after a predetermined period of inactivity is automatic logoff, so it may be replaced by an equivalent measure if the practice documents why.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 14: Encourage Questions
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k160 education methods · CMAA 2A · CMA F.3.a · 2027 F.1.h
preguntas.pregunta: Which wording is recommended for inviting a patient's questions?
opciones: "What questions do you have?", asked several times during the visit
"Do you have any questions?", asked once at the close of the visit
"Is there something you did not understand?", asked at the close of the visit
"You can call the office later if questions come up", said at checkout
preguntas.explicacion: Open wording signals that there is time and that questions are expected, while a yes-or-no version invites a no even when questions exist. The invitation is repeated at several points rather than saved for the end, and it is backed by sitting at the patient's level and looking at them instead of the screen.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Introduction to the Americans with Disabilities Act, Title III
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.F Laboratory Regulations, ADA · CCMA 7A k214 · RMA I.C.1.c laws and acts · CMAA 3A ADAAA compliance
preguntas.pregunta: Under which title of the ADA does a private physician's office or an independent laboratory fall?
opciones: Title III, which covers nonprofits and businesses that serve the public
Title I, which covers employers with fifteen or more employees
Title II, which covers the programs of state and local governments
Title IV, which covers telecommunication companies and relay service
preguntas.explicacion: The law splits into five titles by the kind of organization. A doctor's office or a hospital is named among the nonprofits and businesses that serve the public, which is Title III. A public hospital, or a clinic run by a state or local government, falls under Title II instead; Title I is the employment title, and Title IV covers telephone companies.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), When Patients Change Their Minds
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMA III.G.3.c (2027 III.G.3.c) · CMAA 5 k77 · CCMA 5 k186
preguntas.pregunta: Having signed the advance written notice, the patient changes her mind about the option she picked. How is that handled?
opciones: She adds explanatory notes to the notice, signs and dates them, and marks her new choice
A fresh notice is issued and the first one is destroyed so that nobody is confused
Staff cross out the option she chose and initial the change on her behalf on the form
The change goes in the chart alone, since the signed notice itself may not be altered
preguntas.explicacion: Should the patient change her mind once she has completed and signed the notice, she is asked to add explanatory notes to it, to sign and date those notes, and to mark her new selection clearly. Where that cannot be done in person, the office adds the notes showing the new selection and sends her a copy at once to sign, date and return, then gives her the revised notice.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Yearly "Wellness" visits: Description
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4A pre-visit review · CMAA 2G
preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives for a yearly "Wellness" visit expecting a head-to-toe physical. How is the visit described?
opciones: A conversation to build a prevention plan, not a routine physical exam
A routine physical exam that also produces a written prevention plan
A conversation that replaces every screening test for the coming year
A routine physical exam that Medicare covers once every two years
preguntas.explicacion: The yearly visit is built around a conversation with the provider to create or update a personalized prevention plan, and it is explicitly not a routine physical. Specific health complaints belong in a separate appointment so the visit stays on prevention. The patient leaves with a written checklist of the screenings and vaccines due.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Defining the PCMH: 5. Quality and Safety
preguntas.subtema: Delivery models · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: Which activity shows the medical home's commitment to quality and safety?
opciones: Measuring performance and patient experience, and sharing the results publicly
Keeping in-person hours long enough that urgent needs are seen the same day
Reaching most of a patient's physical and mental health needs in one practice
Passing the patient's information to the hospital before a planned admission
preguntas.explicacion: The quality and safety function shows itself in evidence-based medicine and in decision-support tools that steer shared decision making with patients and with families, in performance measurement and improvement, in measuring patient experience and satisfaction and responding to them, and in population health management. Publishing quality and safety data marks a system- level commitment.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth troubleshooting · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient calls minutes before her video visit to say the picture keeps freezing. Which step is on the troubleshooting list the office hands out beforehand?
opciones: Closing every other application, and if that fails trying a different device
Removing the platform and installing it again so the settings are rebuilt
Carrying the router into the same room and starting the appointment again
Waiting for the clinician to drop the call so the visit can be rebooked
preguntas.explicacion: Patients are easier in their minds when they already know what to do if something goes wrong, so the office gives them the common fixes in advance: restart the computer or the device; check it is charged or plugged in; check the connection is strong enough for the platform; shut every other application; bring the browser up to date; try a different device; and ring the number given for help.

preguntas.subtema: Defective authorization · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A release form comes back to the desk with the line describing the purpose of the disclosure left blank. What is the status of that authorization?
opciones: Defective, because an element required of the form has not been filled in
Defective, unless the patient initials the blank line in front of a witness
Valid, because the purpose may be supplied by the party asking for the records
Valid, because a patient who starts the request need not state a purpose at all
preguntas.explicacion: An authorization is not valid where any required element has been left incomplete, where its expiration has passed, where the entity knows it was revoked, or where material information in it is known to be false. A description of each purpose is one of the core elements; only where the patient initiates the request does asking at her own request suffice.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Physical Properties and Shapes; Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A school screening letter uses the word scoliosis. Which two word parts build that term?
opciones: A part meaning twisted plus an ending meaning abnormal condition
A part meaning humped plus an ending meaning abnormal condition
A part meaning twisted plus an ending meaning an inflammation
A part meaning shape plus an ending meaning abnormal condition
preguntas.explicacion: Scoli- and scolio- mean twisted, and -osis is a condition, usually an abnormal one, so the term names something twisted. Its neighbors in the group of shapes are kypho-, humped, and morph- or morpho-, shape itself. Had the ending been -itis the word would have named an inflammation instead.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fighting Identity Theft with the Red Flags Rule: Detect Red Flags
preguntas.subtema: Verifying a new patient · CCMA 5F k190 · CMA III.H.2.b · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 5A k66 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A new patient is being registered at the desk. Which identity check does the Red Flags guidance describe for someone opening an account in person?
opciones: Take a name, an address and an identification number, and look at a current government card
Take a name, an address and an identification number, and telephone the number she gave
Take a name, a date of birth and her mother's maiden name, and look at a current card
Take a name, an address and an identification number, and copy the card into the record
preguntas.explicacion: Reasonable procedures for verifying someone opening a new account may include getting a name, an address and an identification number, and, in person, checking a current identification card issued by a government, such as a driving license or a passport. That may then be compared against other sources. Data easily found in a wallet does not authenticate anyone.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Public Health Activities
preguntas.subtema: Reporting to authorities · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.5.a · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k37 · NCMA 4.10
preguntas.pregunta: A county health department, acting under state law, asks the office to report a case of a communicable disease. What is required?
opciones: Nothing further, since a public health authority may receive the report without authorization
A signed authorization from the patient, because the diagnosis is sensitive information
A subpoena, because a government agency reaches records only through legal process
A business associate agreement with the department before the report can be transmitted
preguntas.explicacion: Public health activities are one of the twelve national priority purposes. A covered entity may disclose PHI to a public health authority that the law authorizes to receive it in order to prevent or control disease, injury or disability, and to authorities that take reports of child abuse and neglect. The same paragraph also covers warning a person who may have been exposed to a disease that is communicable, where law authorizes it.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Filing a claim; and CMS, MLN Booklet: CMS-1500 & 837P, Time Limits
preguntas.subtema: Claim submission · CMAA 6 k85, 6C k87 · CCMA 5L k185 · CMA III.G.3.b(1)
preguntas.pregunta: A patient was seen on March 22. What is the deadline for filing that Medicare claim?
opciones: March 22 of the following year, one full calendar year after the service
September 22 of the same year, six months after the date of the service
December 31 of the same year, the close of the calendar year of service
March 22 two years later, since Medicare allows 24 months for filing
preguntas.explicacion: A Medicare claim has to be in no later than 12 months, one full calendar year, after the date the services were given; the program's own example is a March 22 visit, whose claim is due by March 22 the following year. A late claim is denied, and that denial is not an initial determination, so there is nothing to appeal.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(f)(1); OSHA Brief 3636, Hazard Communication Standard: Labels and Pictograms, Label Elements
preguntas.subtema: Label elements · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: Which elements must appear on the label of a shipped container of a hazardous chemical under the Hazard Communication standard?
opciones: Product identifier, signal word, hazard and precautionary statements, pictograms and supplier contact
Product identifier, CAS number, concentration, flash point, PEL and the date of preparation
Signal word, pictograms, the 16-section SDS summary, lot number, expiration date and PPE symbol
Chemical name, NFPA hazard rating, storage temperature, disposal method, supplier name and phone
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(1) of 29 CFR 1910.1200 and OSHA's labeling brief list six elements for a container that leaves the workplace: the product identifier, a signal word, hazard statements, precautionary statements, pictograms, and the supplier's name, address and telephone, be that the manufacturer, the importer or another responsible party. The product identifier has to match section 1 of the SDS. CAS numbers, concentrations, flash points and exposure limits live in the SDS sections on composition, physical properties and exposure controls, not on the label; an HMIS-style PPE symbol may be added only as supplementary information.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, About Child Abuse and Neglect
preguntas.subtema: Signs of abuse · CCMA 7F k222 · CMA E.6.c / 2027 E.5.b · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k43
preguntas.pregunta: How is child abuse and neglect defined for public health purposes?
opciones: Harm, or the threat of it, to a child under 18 by someone in a custodial role
Harm to a child under 12 caused by a parent or a legal guardian only
Any injury to a child under 18 that required treatment at a hospital or clinic
Any harm to a child under 18 caused by an adult outside the family
preguntas.explicacion: The definition covers every type of abuse and of neglect suffered by a child under 18 at the hands of a parent, of a caregiver, or of anybody else in a custodial role such as a coach, a teacher or a religious leader, where the result is harm, potential harm or the threat of harm. It is not limited to injuries needing treatment, nor to people outside the family: the opposite is more common.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, "Communicating With and About People with Disabilities", Tips
preguntas.subtema: Person-first language · CCMA 6B k195 · CMAA 2D k17
preguntas.pregunta: Which wording puts the emphasis on accessibility rather than on disability?
opciones: The accessible restroom on the first floor
The handicapped restroom on the first floor
The special restroom on the first floor
The disabled restroom on the first floor
preguntas.explicacion: Signage and directions are written to emphasize the need for accessibility rather than the disability, so accessible parking and an accessible restroom replace the handicapped versions. Special sits with the words to avoid, alongside slow and afflicted, because it points at the person instead of the facility.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Specific Techniques; and Common Pitfalls
preguntas.subtema: Therapeutic techniques · CCMA 6C k199 · CMA F.2 / 2027 F.1.d · CMAA 2E k21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient goes quiet after being told a biopsy has been ordered. What is the therapeutic response?
opciones: Stay with the silence and hold back from interrupting
Offer reassurance that the result will surely come back fine
Move on to the paperwork so the visit keeps its schedule
Give an opinion on how the patient ought to be taking it
preguntas.explicacion: Silence is itself a technique: it demonstrates attentiveness by minimizing interruption. False reassurance is a pitfall that can rupture the relationship badly if the hoped-for outcome never arrives, an abrupt change of subject can be taken as dismissive, and value judgments get in the patient's way.

preguntas.subtema: Expiration of an authorization · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: An authorization names the records, the sender and the recipient, but nothing about when it stops. Which core element has been left out?
opciones: An expiration date, or an event that ends the authorization
A statement of the fee the recipient of the records will pay
An estimate of how long the copies will take to be prepared
A list of the staff members allowed to assemble the records
preguntas.explicacion: The core elements are the information described specifically, who may disclose it, who may receive it, the purpose, an expiration date or expiration event tied to the individual or the purpose, and the individual's dated signature. For research, wording such as the end of the study, or none at all, is accepted as the expiration.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, Exclusions Program; and CMS, MLN Booklet MLN4649244
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: Why does an office check the List of Excluded Individuals and Entities before hiring?
opciones: Federal programs pay nothing for the work of an excluded person
Excluded people must be reported to the state licensing board first
The list shows which providers have been sanctioned by their payers
Hiring from the list requires prior approval from the contractor
preguntas.explicacion: Exclusion means the federal health care programs will not pay for items or services that the person or entity furnishes, orders or prescribes, and payment is refused whoever submits the claim, the employer included.
