Anyone who hires someone on the list may face civil monetary penalties, which is why the public list is checked before hiring and periodically afterwards.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A discharge summary lists DVT after a long hospital stay. Which problem does that abbreviation record?
opciones: A clot that has formed in a deep vein
A defect in the vessels of the circulation
A disturbance of the rhythm of the heart
A disease of the arteries outside the heart
preguntas.explicacion: DVT stands for deep-vein thrombosis, which is a blood clot. The abbreviations that sit near it name other circulatory problems: AVM is an arteriovenous malformation, a defect in how the vessels are built; AFIB is atrial fibrillation, a disturbance of the heart's rhythm; and PAD is peripheral arterial disease, of arteries outside the heart.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(b)(3)(i)-(iii), Hazard Communication, laboratories
preguntas.subtema: SDS access · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: When must safety data sheets be accessible to laboratory employees under the Hazard Communication standard?
opciones: During each work shift, while employees are in their work areas
Within 10 working days of a request, through the safety officer
During business hours only, in the administrator's office
At the annual training, when the chemical inventory is reviewed
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (b)(3)(ii) of 29 CFR 1910.1200 has the employer keep the safety data sheets that arrive with shipments of hazardous chemicals and keep them readily accessible on every shift to laboratory employees while they are in the areas where they work; the same wording governs sealed-container operations in (b)(4)(ii). Labels on incoming containers stay intact, and the training of paragraph (h) is given. A sheet obtainable only days later, or only in an office during business hours, fails the test.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicare Program Integrity Manual, chapter 3, section 3.3.2.4
preguntas.subtema: Signature log · CCMA 5 k189 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 7A · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Records submitted for review carry initials nobody can identify. Which document is meant to resolve that?
opciones: A signature log matching the printed name of the author to the initials used
An amendment adding the missing names to each of the disputed chart entries
A business associate agreement with the company that scanned the paper charts
An accounting of disclosures listing everyone who has opened the record so far
preguntas.explicacion: A signature log lists the typed or printed name of an author alongside the initials or the illegible signature used in the documentation. It may sit on the page itself or stand as a separate document. Reviewers are told to consider every log submitted regardless of when it was created, and may not deny a claim just because the log leaves out credentials, although listing them is encouraged.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Part A costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74, 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient moves to a skilled nursing facility and stays thirty days. What does Part A leave her to pay in 2026?
opciones: Nothing for the first twenty days, then $217 for each of the ten that follow
No charge for the first sixty days, then $434 for each of the ten that follow
A charge of $217 for every one of the thirty days, counting from admission
The whole cost herself, because a skilled nursing stay sits outside Part A
preguntas.explicacion: A skilled nursing facility stay costs the patient nothing for days one to twenty, then $217 a day from day twenty-one to day one hundred, and the whole cost from day one hundred and one onwards. Part A helps pay for inpatient care in hospitals and in critical access hospitals, for skilled nursing facilities, and it also covers hospice and some home health care.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Nonmaleficence
preguntas.subtema: Nonmaleficence and competence · CPT D1 1D k26 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7C · CMA II.E.7 · RMA I.C.4.a · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k48
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist declines to attempt an arterial puncture she has not been trained to perform. Which ethical principle does this reflect?
opciones: Nonmaleficence: avoiding a risky procedure outside one's competence
Beneficence: bringing goodness by attempting any procedure the patient needs
Justice: giving each patient the same procedures regardless of skill
Autonomy: the phlebotomist's right to choose which tasks to do
preguntas.explicacion: Nonmaleficence means not bringing harm, and the Hippocratic tradition lists attempting a risky procedure outside the practitioner's competence among the things to avoid, together with violating privacy. Staying within one's training is therefore an ethical duty as well as a scope-of-practice rule. Beneficence would be misread if it meant attempting anything a patient needs regardless of skill; justice concerns fair distribution of resources; and autonomy in medical ethics refers to the patient's self-determination, not the worker's preferences.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Skilled nursing facility (SNF) care: Coverage details
preguntas.subtema: Observation status and SNF coverage · CCMA 4H · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient spent two nights in the hospital under observation, then one night as an admitted inpatient. Does that meet the qualifying stay for a SNF?
opciones: No, because time spent under observation does not count toward the three-day stay
Yes, because three nights inside the building satisfy the three-day qualifying stay
Yes, because observation nights count whenever the patient is later admitted
No, because a qualifying stay has to reach seven days counting the discharge day
preguntas.explicacion: Time under observation services or in the emergency department before admission does not count toward the three-day qualifying inpatient stay, even overnight. Only days as an admitted inpatient count, starting the day of admission and leaving out the day of discharge. A doctor in an ACO approved for a three-day rule waiver, or a Medicare Advantage plan, may set the requirement aside.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms: Excluded Services
preguntas.subtema: Insurance coverage · CMA III.G.3 (2027 III.G.3) · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A treatment appears on the plan's list of excluded services. What does the patient need to be told?
opciones: The plan does not pay for it or cover it at all
The plan pays for it once the deductible is met
The plan pays for it outside its own network only
The plan pays for it if it is preauthorized first
preguntas.explicacion: Excluded services are the health care services a plan does not pay for or cover, so no amount of cost sharing or paperwork turns them into a covered benefit. Meeting a deductible, going out of network or obtaining a preauthorization all belong to services the plan does cover, which is what makes those answers tempting.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Defining the PCMH: 1. Comprehensive Care
preguntas.subtema: Team-based care roles · CCMA 4G k167 · CMA II.F.4.c / 2027 II.F.2.c · CMAA 1 k1 · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which group of workers does the medical home model name as part of the care team?
opciones: Advanced practice nurses, pharmacists, nutritionists and social workers
Only the physician and the nurse, with other disciplines seen on referral
Hospital case managers and payer staff, who direct the practice's decisions
The hospice nurse, the chaplain and the medical director of the agency
preguntas.explicacion: Comprehensive care takes a team, and the model names its members: physicians and nurses, nutritionists, physician assistants, pharmacists, advanced practice nurses, educators, care coordinators and social workers. Smaller practices may build virtual teams instead, linking themselves, and their patients, to the providers and services their own communities hold.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Filing an appeal, Your right to a fast appeal
preguntas.subtema: Denials and appeals · CMA III.G.5.b (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6E · CCMA 5M
preguntas.pregunta: A patient on Medicare is told her skilled nursing coverage ends on Friday and she believes she still needs it. What is she entitled to?
opciones: A fast appeal, plus a written notice before the services end telling her how to ask
A fast appeal, but only once the standard first-level appeal has been decided
A standard appeal, since fast appeals cover only inpatient hospital stays
A standard appeal, since fast appeals cover only drugs a plan refuses to pay
preguntas.explicacion: The fast appeal is for the patient who believes Medicare-covered services are stopping too soon, and it reaches services from a hospital, from a skilled nursing facility, from a home health agency, from hospice, or from a rehabilitation facility for comprehensive outpatient care. Before the services stop the provider has to give a written notice explaining how to ask for one, and the patient should ask for that notice if it does not turn up.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Numbers and Amounts
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks why one lab result is labeled hyperglycemia and another hypoglycemia. Which pair of prefixes explains the difference?
opciones: Hyper- means above or excessive; hypo- means under or deficient
Hyper- means quick or rapid; hypo- means slow or delayed
Hyper- means large or long; hypo- means small or short
Hyper- means outer or outside; hypo- means within or inner
preguntas.explicacion: These two prefixes sit in the group of numbers and amounts: hyper- is above, beyond or excessive, and hypo- is under or deficient. Attached to the root for sugar and the ending -emia, a blood condition, they name too much and too little glucose in the blood. Fast and slow are tachy- and brady-; large and small are macro- and micro-.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, What Is Health Literacy? Overview
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k166 barriers to care · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.3.a · 2027 F.1.h
preguntas.pregunta: What does organizational health literacy add to the definition?
opciones: The duty of organizations to equitably enable people to use health information
The duty of organizations to test each patient's reading level at intake
The duty of organizations to publish their materials in at least six languages
The duty of patients to tell the practice when a handout is too difficult
preguntas.explicacion: Alongside personal health literacy the 2020 definitions name organizational health literacy: how far an organization equitably enables people to locate information and services, grasp them and use them for their own health decisions. It places responsibility on the practice, and it ties health literacy to health equity.

preguntas.fuente: NHA Candidate Handbook (2026), Disciplinary Actions for Misconduct
preguntas.subtema: Unethical conduct · CCMA 7C · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: A candidate is asked by a classmate to describe the questions on the exam he just sat. What is the risk if he does?
opciones: Misconduct, which can void scores, revoke the credential and bar retesting
A written warning, after which the credential continues without change
A delay in scoring, which is lifted once the candidate signs an attestation
A fee for re-registration, which the candidate pays before the next attempt
preguntas.explicacion: Misrepresenting eligibility, giving a false attestation, breaching the rules of conduct for testing, or not following the codes of ethics, all count as misconduct. Anything capable of compromising an exam's security, its validity or its integrity draws discipline, which can run to invalidating scores, revoking the credential and banning the person from that exam or any other one offered.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information: Providing the Notice
preguntas.subtema: Acknowledgment of the notice · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A new patient takes the notice of privacy practices and politely declines to sign the acknowledgment. What must the front desk do?
opciones: Record what was tried in order to get the acknowledgment, and why it failed
Record the refusal and hold the appointment until a signed acknowledgment is on file
Record the refusal and post a second copy of the notice by certified mail within 60 days
Record the refusal and count the notice as acknowledged once the visit is documented
preguntas.explicacion: A direct treatment provider hands the notice over no later than the date of first service and, emergencies aside, tries in good faith to get a written acknowledgment that it was received. Where no acknowledgment can be had, the file records what was attempted and why it came to nothing. The notice also goes to anybody who asks for it.

preguntas.subtema: Record confidentiality · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: Besides limiting who may receive information from a chart, what else must a hospital's confidentiality procedure prevent?
opciones: Unauthorized people gaining access to the records or altering what is in them
Authorized staff consulting a record outside the hours the department is open
Clinicians correcting an entry that they themselves made earlier in the same day
Copies leaving the department without the medical record service's own stamp
preguntas.explicacion: The condition asks for a procedure that keeps the records confidential in two directions: information and copies go only to authorized individuals, and unauthorized individuals must not be able to reach the records or change what they contain. Originals leave the hospital only under federal or state law, a court order or a subpoena.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Termination and the critically ill · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.4.d(2) · RMA I.C.1.c · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient already served with a termination notice is admitted in a critical condition the week the notice period runs out. What does the practice owe her?
opciones: To hold the termination until she is medically stable again
To end care on the date in the letter and refer the hospital to it
To hold the termination until she signs a fresh consent to treat
To end care on the date in the letter unless she asks for more time
preguntas.explicacion: Staying clear of an abandonment claim means giving notice that is adequate and a fair chance to line up another clinician. Where there is an emergency, or the patient is critically ill, termination has to wait until she is medically stable again. Courts have held that the duty to go on treating someone at a critical stage of illness applies whatever her ability to pay.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Benefits of This Model
preguntas.subtema: Effect on demand · CMAA 4A k49 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Physicians at a practice fear that offering same-day appointments will bring a flood of extra visits. What does the reported experience suggest?
opciones: Demand tends to fall, mostly because patients more often get to see their own clinician
Demand tends to rise sharply, which is why a contingency plan is needed from the first day
Demand stays flat, but the visits shift out of the afternoon and into the morning session
Demand tends to fall, mostly because patients settle more of their problems by telephone
preguntas.explicacion: Against what many physicians anticipate, the demand for appointments goes down, and the reason given is that patients more often manage to see their own clinician. Seeing one's personal physician strengthens continuity of care, which goes with better care and higher satisfaction. Practices also report savings, because fewer no-shows free clinical and staff time.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(h)(5)(i), Sharps injury log; govinfo, Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act, Pub. L. 106-430, sec. 3(5)
preguntas.subtema: Sharps injury log · CPT D1 k12 k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: Which three items must the OSHA sharps injury log record for each incident?
opciones: The type and brand of device, the department or work area, and how the incident happened
The injured employee's name, the source patient's status, and the prophylaxis given
The date of the training, the trainer's qualifications, and the attendees' job titles
The route of exposure, the written opinion, and the vaccination dates of the employee
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(5)(i), added by the Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act, asks the log for three things at minimum: which device was involved, by type and brand; where it happened, meaning the department or the work area; and an explanation of how the incident came about, all of it written so that the injured employee's confidentiality holds. Names, source status and prophylaxis live in the confidential medical record; training details in the training record; and the route of exposure and the written opinion in the post-exposure evaluation file.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Specific Techniques
preguntas.subtema: Therapeutic techniques · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2E k21 · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant is wrapping up a long intake interview. Which technique both shows active listening and can close it?
opciones: Summarizing what was said, in the interviewer's own words
Reflecting the patient's words back, at times word for word
Offering social pleasantries that put the patient at ease
Providing the rationale for why the information is needed
preguntas.explicacion: Summarizing pulls together what the patient said in the interviewer's own words. It demonstrates active listening, builds a shared understanding, and occasionally serves to complete the interview. Social pleasantries belong at the start, and reflecting repeats a single statement rather than gathering several.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth instructions · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: How does the telehealth guidance want the setup steps delivered to a patient who has never used the platform?
opciones: As written step-by-step instructions, or as direct personal support from staff
As a single reminder message sent on the morning the appointment is due to start
As a printed leaflet given to her at the next office visit she attends in person
As a spoken summary during the opening minutes of the video appointment itself
preguntas.explicacion: Skills and comfort vary from patient to patient, and so do their computers, their software versions and their bandwidth, so what needs reviewing is never the same twice. What the guidance asks for is a written set of instructions covering every step of the process from beginning to end, plus a tip: have a coordinator, a nurse, an administrative staff member or a community health worker take the patient through it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship", Clinical Significance: Standardized notification
preguntas.subtema: Termination of care · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.d(2)(b) · NCMA 4.9 · CMAA 3A k31
preguntas.pregunta: What belongs in a letter terminating care?
opciones: The end date, cover until then, emergency resources and a records release
The end date, the clinical reason, and the name of the replacing clinician
The end date, the balance owed, and the date the account goes to collections
The end date, a copy of the chart, and the patient's signed acknowledgement
preguntas.explicacion: The letter states the date the relationship ends, says the clinician stays available for care and medication refills until then, points toward emergency help such as a local crisis center, and offers to send the records on to a new clinician once the patient authorizes it, with a release form enclosed. Giving a reason is usually optional, and naming specific colleagues is debated.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.3 Strategies to Improve Communication with Patients with Impaired Speech
preguntas.subtema: Speech impairment · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(6) / 2027 F.1.d(6) · CMAA 2D k17
preguntas.pregunta: Which strategy fits a patient whose speech is impaired?
opciones: Phrasing questions so a yes or a no can answer them
Phrasing questions so only a long answer will serve
Directing the questions to the family member instead
Speaking louder and faster to shorten the exchange
preguntas.explicacion: Phrase questions so the patient can answer yes or no, while staying alert that expressive aphasia can produce an automatic answer that is wrong. Cut excess noise, offer a writing tablet, flash cards or a picture board, present one idea at a time, speak slowly without shouting, and repeat back what was said.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), Table 1 and Conditional Payments
preguntas.subtema: Secondary records and payers · CMAA 5 k72, 6C k87 · CCMA 5L k185 · CMA III.G.4.f / 2027 III.G.4
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient is treated for a back injury he suffered at work, and workers' compensation is open. Where does the claim go first?
opciones: To workers' compensation, which pays first for the job-related injury care
To Medicare, which pays first and then recovers from workers' compensation
To the patient, who pays and files for reimbursement from both payers
To the group health plan, which pays first for any injury of an employee
preguntas.explicacion: Workers' compensation pays first for health care items and services tied to a job-related illness or injury, and claims to a non-group health plan reach that insurer ahead of Medicare. A conditional payment from Medicare is possible when a contested case drags on, but that is an exception it later recovers, not the normal first step. Billing the patient up front is prohibited when another payer is primary.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 6A, 5 k68 · CCMA 5I k184 · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with no signs or symptoms comes in only for routine laboratory testing. What is reported as the reason for the visit?
opciones: A code for a specified special examination encounter, with no symptom code
A code for the chronic condition she is followed for, as the reason for the visit
A code from the symptoms chapter, since no definitive diagnosis has been reached
A code for a general medical exam with an abnormal finding, plus that finding
preguntas.explicacion: For an encounter for routine laboratory or radiology testing where there are no signs, symptoms or associated diagnosis, the guidelines assign the Z code that covers a specified special examination encounter, and that Z code is the reason for the visit. A chronic condition she is followed for may still be sequenced after it as an additional diagnosis, and a test run at the same visit to evaluate a symptom brings its own reason with it. Symptom codes need a symptom in the record.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Task Assistance
preguntas.subtema: Teamwork · CCMA 6L k202 · CMAA 2F k21
preguntas.pregunta: What do effective teams frame every offer and request for assistance around?
opciones: Patient safety, which is the context for asking and offering
The staffing plan, which sets who may take on extra work
The chain of command, which settles who asks whom for help
The workload the team leader balanced at the start of the day
preguntas.explicacion: Task assistance builds a trusting team, and an effective team frames every offer of help, and every request for it, in terms of patient safety. Members are expected to protect each other from overload and to make asking for help normal; resilience is strengthened by something as simple as offering ten free minutes to a colleague.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, FAQ: What is a patient portal?
preguntas.subtema: Portal self-scheduling limits · CMAA 4E k56 · CCMA 5U k172 · CMA III.H.3.a (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient uses the portal at midnight to book a visit for chest pain that started an hour earlier. What is wrong with that use of the portal?
opciones: Portal self-scheduling is offered for non-urgent appointments, which this is not
Portal self-scheduling is offered only to patients seen within the past year
Portal self-scheduling is offered only during the hours the office is open
Portal self-scheduling is offered only for visits with her own primary clinician
preguntas.explicacion: The portal is open at any hour from any internet connection, and beyond reading her own record some portals let a patient send a secure message to the clinician, ask for a refill, look up benefits and coverage, change her contact details, make a payment, download forms and book appointments that are not urgent. That last limit is built into the scheduling feature itself.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 485.610(c); and CMS, MLN Booklet MLN006400 Information for Critical Access Hospitals
preguntas.subtema: Critical access hospital location · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: How far from another hospital must a critical access hospital normally be located?
opciones: A drive of more than 35 miles on primary roads, or 15 in mountainous terrain
More than a 15-mile drive on primary roads, or 35 miles in mountainous terrain
More than a 25-mile drive on primary roads, with no exception for the terrain
More than a 50-mile drive on primary roads, or 25 miles where roads are secondary
preguntas.explicacion: The condition of participation places the hospital more than a 35-mile drive on primary roads from another hospital or critical access hospital. Where terrain is mountainous or only secondary roads exist, the distance drops to a 15-mile drive. A primary road means a numbered federal or state highway with two or more lanes each way. States could also certify a necessary provider before 2006.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.3 Strategies for Communicating with Patients with Impaired Hearing and Vision
preguntas.subtema: Hearing impairment · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(2) / 2027 F.1.d(3) · CMAA 2D k17
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant has to give discharge steps to a patient with impaired hearing. Where should the assistant stand?
opciones: Two to three feet away, facing them in good light
Ten to twelve feet away, so the whole face is in view
Just behind the patient's better ear while speaking
At the doorway, with the voice raised to carry over
preguntas.explicacion: Get the patient's attention first, cut the background noise, and position yourself two to three feet away. Facing them directly in a well-lit room is what makes lip reading possible; turning away mid sentence undoes it. Gestures help, shouting does not, and the preferred method of communication goes in the record.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Tort in Healthcare", Clinical Significance and Issues of Concern (damages)
preguntas.subtema: Burden of proof · CPT D1 1D · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7A k221 · CMA II.E.4.a · RMA I.C.1.c · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k31
preguntas.pregunta: What is the burden of proof in a civil tort case such as a malpractice claim?
opciones: A preponderance of the evidence: more likely than not
Beyond a reasonable doubt, as in criminal cases
Clear and convincing evidence agreed by a unanimous jury
Proof to a certainty, the standard applied to damages
preguntas.explicacion: A tort case is decided on a preponderance of the evidence, meaning more likely than not, better than 50 percent. The criminal yardstick of beyond a reasonable doubt has no place here, and in a number of states the jury need not even be unanimous to hold a tortfeasor responsible. One is liable for a tort rather than guilty of it. Damages are a separate question: they have to be proved to a certainty instead of estimated, and statutes may cap them, but that goes to the amount awarded, not to the burden for establishing liability.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Good and Bad; and StatPearls, "Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)" (NBK559281)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: An imaging report describes hepatomegaly. Which ending carries the meaning of enlargement?
opciones: -megaly, which is added to the root for the organ
-sclerosis, which is added to the root for the organ
-ectasis, which is added to the root for the organ
-trophy, which is added to the root for the organ
preguntas.explicacion: The ending -megaly means enlargement, and hepat- names the liver, so hepatomegaly is an enlarged liver. The near neighbors mean other things: -sclerosis is a hardening, -ectasis an expansion or dilation of a hollow structure, and -trophy is growth in the sense of nourishment, as in atrophy and hypertrophy.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Teach-Back
preguntas.subtema: Patient education · CCMA 4F k160 · CMAA 2G
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant has just explained how to use a new inhaler. How does a teach-back confirm the patient understood?
opciones: The patient explains the information in their own words
The patient signs the instruction sheet before leaving
The patient answers yes when asked whether it was clear
The staff member repeats the instruction a second time
preguntas.explicacion: Teach-back means the sender asking a patient, or a family member, to put back in their own words the information they need to know or the actions they need to take. It checks whether the sender explained clearly, which a yes-or-no question and a signature on a sheet of paper cannot do.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, How Medicare drug plans work, Tiers
preguntas.subtema: Drug formulary · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.5.a(2) (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks why her copayment for one drug is higher than for another in the same plan.
opciones: The drugs sit in different tiers of the plan's list, and higher tiers cost more
The drugs sit in different tiers of the plan's list, and higher tiers are generic
The plan charges more for drugs bought before the deductible has been met
The plan charges more for drugs a specialist prescribed than for others
preguntas.explicacion: Plans place covered drugs in tiers, and a drug in a lower tier generally costs the patient less. In the example given, tier 1 holds most generic drugs with the lowest copayment, tier 2 preferred brand-name drugs, tier 3 non-preferred brand names, and a specialty tier the very high-cost drugs. Generics sit at the bottom, not the top, and the tier does not depend on who wrote the prescription.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Where is the HIPAA Privacy Rule Applicable; 45 CFR 164.520(b)(1)(ii)(C)
preguntas.subtema: Stricter state law · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.2.a(2) · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33
preguntas.pregunta: State law is stricter than HIPAA about disclosing HIV test results. Which rule governs the disclosure?
opciones: The more stringent rule, in this case the state law
HIPAA, since federal law always preempts state law
Whichever rule the facility's privacy official prefers
Neither; HIV results are excluded from PHI altogether
preguntas.explicacion: Many states have privacy rules stricter than HIPAA, especially for HIV, mental health, genetic and substance-use information, and federal rules on substance use disorder records are stricter as well; where a more stringent rule exists it takes precedence over HIPAA in that jurisdiction, while HIPAA still applies to everything else. The notice of privacy practices must reflect the more stringent law when it limits a use or disclosure. HIV results are ordinary PHI under HIPAA; the extra protection comes from state law, not from an exclusion.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication (companions)
preguntas.subtema: ADAAA compliance · CMAA 3A (ADAAA)
preguntas.pregunta: A deaf patient arrives with her 12-year-old son, who offers to interpret for a routine visit. What should the office do?
opciones: Provide a qualified interpreter; a minor may interpret only in an emergency
Let the son interpret, since the patient brought him and agrees to it
Ask the patient to reschedule the visit with an adult relative who can interpret
Write notes back and forth, which meets the rule for any medical visit
preguntas.explicacion: Responsibility for effective communication sits with the covered entity, which cannot require anyone to bring their own interpreter. A minor child accompanying the patient may be relied on only in an emergency with an imminent threat, and only when no qualified interpreter is available. An interpreter is generally needed for taking a history or discussing a serious diagnosis.

preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, symptom and sign
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k10 · NCMA 1.10
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports nausea and fatigue, and the exam records a fever and a rash. Which entries are symptoms and which are signs?
opciones: Nausea and fatigue are symptoms; fever and rash are signs
Nausea and fatigue are signs; fever and rash are symptoms
All four are symptoms, since the patient came in reporting them
All four are signs, since a provider recorded them in the chart
preguntas.explicacion: A symptom is something the person feels and can only report: pain, nausea, fatigue, anxiety. A sign is something found on the exam or on a test, so anyone can observe it: fever, swelling, a skin rash, a high blood pressure or a high blood glucose. Both matter, but only one of them can be measured.

preguntas.fuente: NIH, Office of Dietary Supplements: Dietary Supplements — Federal Regulation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k161 nutrition education · CMA I.A.6.g(2) · 2027 I.A.6.g(2) · CMAA 2G
preguntas.pregunta: A supplement bottle says the product supports heart health. What must appear alongside a claim like that?
opciones: A statement that the FDA has not evaluated it and it treats no disease
A statement that the FDA has approved it for supporting heart health
A statement that a physician must be consulted before any purchase
A statement that the product was tested in a clinical trial for the heart
preguntas.explicacion: Manufacturers are allowed to say that a supplement promotes health, or that it supports a part or a function of the body, but the package must then carry the disclaimer: no evaluation of the claim has been made by the Food and Drug Administration, and the product is not intended for diagnosing, treating, curing or preventing disease.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology
preguntas.subtema: Platform changes · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: The telehealth platform will be upgraded next month. What does the guidance tell the practice to do about the patients already using it?
opciones: Tell them about the change and what they have to do to be ready for their visit
Wait until one of them reports a problem and walk her through the new version then
Book no video visits at all until every one of them confirms the update is installed
Send the instructions only to the patients whose first video visit is still to come
preguntas.explicacion: The guidance closes on what to do when the platform changes: where the telehealth platform gets updated, the practice tells its existing patients about the change and about anything they must do so as to be ready for the visit. Patients new to the platform are the ones who get the full step-by-step walkthrough, but the existing ones cannot simply be left to find out for themselves.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Exceptions to Informed Consent
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7 · CMAA 3D k40
preguntas.pregunta: Which situation is a recognized exception to the requirement for informed consent?
opciones: A life-threatening emergency with no time to obtain consent
A test the clinician considers clearly in the patient's interest
A patient who speaks a different language from the staff
A patient carrying a psychiatric diagnosis such as schizophrenia
preguntas.explicacion: The recognized exceptions are three: the patient is incapacitated, a life-threatening emergency leaves no time, or the patient voluntarily waives consent. A clinician's view that the test is good for the patient is the paternalism the consent literature warns against; language barriers call for an interpreter; and a psychiatric diagnosis by itself does not remove the right to consent.

preguntas.fuente: NAIC, Coordination of Benefits Model Regulation (Model 120), Definitions
preguntas.subtema: Insurance rules · CMAA 5B k75 · CCMA 5E k182
preguntas.pregunta: Under the birthday rule, which part of a parent's date of birth matters?
opciones: The month and the day, since the year of birth is left out of the rule
The month and the year, since the older parent's plan is treated as primary
The year alone, since the parent covered longer holds the primary plan
The day alone, since the earlier day of the month decides the order
preguntas.explicacion: The model regulation defines birthday as referring only to the month and day in a calendar year, and it expressly leaves out the year the parent was born, so the older parent has no advantage. The plan that covered a parent longer is the tie-breaker when the two birthdays match, a separate rule that does not turn on the birth year either.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Referral
preguntas.subtema: Referrals · CCMA 5P k177 · CMA III.G.5.a · RMA II.B.2.c · CMAA 4G k67 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient in an HMO calls to book with a cardiologist and has no order from her primary care doctor. What is missing?
opciones: A referral, the written order from her primary care doctor for the visit
A preauthorization, the plan's decision that the visit is medically necessary
A claim, the request for payment the office sends after the appointment
An accounting of disclosures covering the records the specialist will receive
preguntas.explicacion: A referral is a written order from the primary care doctor sending the patient to a specialist or for certain services. Many health maintenance organizations require that order before care from anyone but the primary care doctor, and without it the plan may refuse to pay. Preauthorization is a different decision, made by the insurer about medical necessity.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse: Prevent, Detect, Report (MLN4649244)
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · CMA III.G.2 · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: What separates fraud from abuse in the Medicare program?
opciones: Fraud involves knowing deception; abuse causes needless program cost without it
Fraud is committed by providers only; abuse is committed by patients and staff
Fraud is billed to a federal program; abuse is billed to a commercial insurer
Fraud is punished by the payer; abuse is punished only by the state licensing board
preguntas.explicacion: Fraud typically means knowingly submitting false claims, misrepresenting facts, or paying or taking remuneration for referrals. Abuse is the label for practices that cause unnecessary program costs, directly or indirectly, or that fall short of professionally recognized standards. Which of the two applies depends on the facts, the intent and the knowledge involved, and either can bring administrative, civil and criminal liability.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.508(c)(1)-(4), Core elements and requirements
preguntas.subtema: Authorization elements · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: Which element must a valid HIPAA authorization contain?
opciones: An expiration date or event, plus the individual's signature and date
A notarized seal and the signature of the treating physician
The patient's Social Security number and insurance identifier
A statement that the authorization cannot be revoked once it has been signed
preguntas.explicacion: The core elements in 164.508(c)(1) are a specific description of the information, the person or class authorized to disclose it, the recipient, the purpose, an expiration date or event, and the individual's signature and date, with the authority of any personal representative described. The required statements then tell the individual of the right to revoke in writing, whether treatment or benefits may be conditioned on signing, and that the recipient may redisclose the information. It must be in plain language and the individual receives a copy. Notarization is not required, and a no-revocation clause would contradict the rule.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Reproductive System: Male Reproductive System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(8) (2027 I.C.6.f(8)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12
preguntas.pregunta: Which structures make up the male reproductive system?
opciones: Testes, epididymis, vas deferens, ejaculatory ducts, seminal vesicles, prostate and penis
Testes, epididymis, ureters, ejaculatory ducts, seminal vesicles, bladder and penis
Testes, Fallopian tubes, vas deferens, accessory glands, prostate, urethra and penis
Testes, epididymis, vas deferens, adrenal glands, seminal vesicles, kidney and penis
preguntas.explicacion: The male system is a pair of testes plus a network of excretory ducts, namely the epididymis, the ductus or vas deferens and the ejaculatory ducts, and to those are added the penis, the bulbourethral glands, the prostate and the seminal vesicles. The ureters and the bladder belong to the urinary system, even though the two share the urethra.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Home health services: Who's eligible
preguntas.subtema: Resources for clinical services · CCMA 4D k162 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: Which two conditions must a patient meet at the same time for Medicare to cover home health services?
opciones: Needing skilled services part-time or intermittently, and being homebound
Needing daily skilled services, and a prior inpatient stay of three days
Being homebound, and having a prognosis certified as 6 months or shorter
Needing custodial help with daily living, and a doctor's order for an aide
preguntas.explicacion: Home health coverage rests on two conditions at once. The patient must need skilled services part-time or intermittently, and must be homebound, which means leaving home is not recommended or takes considerable effort and help. Somebody needing skilled care beyond the part-time or intermittent level does not qualify for the benefit.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Coordination of Benefits & Recovery Overview
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMA III.G.3.a (2027 III.G.3.a) · CMAA 5 k75 · CCMA 5B
preguntas.pregunta: Which entity collects, manages and reports the other insurance coverage a Medicare patient holds?
opciones: The Benefits Coordination & Recovery Center, working for the secondary payer program
The Medicare Administrative Contractor, working for the secondary payer program
The Commercial Repayment Center, working for the secondary payer program
The clearinghouse, working for the providers that route their claims through it
preguntas.explicacion: The Medicare Secondary Payer program keeps Medicare from paying first where it should not, and coordination of benefits rules settle which payer goes first. Collecting, managing and reporting whatever other insurance covers a beneficiary is the job of the Benefits Coordination & Recovery Center. The Commercial Repayment Center does something else entirely: it pursues recovery when a group health plan should have paid first.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Conflict Management", Function: Types of Conflict in Healthcare
preguntas.subtema: Conflict management · CCMA 6J k209 · CMAA 2B k26
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant is torn between staying in her current post and going back for a degree. Which type of conflict is that?
opciones: Intrapersonal conflict
Interpersonal conflict
Inter-sender conflict
Intragroup conflict
preguntas.explicacion: Intrapersonal conflict is the struggle inside one person among values, goals or role demands that compete, and the example given is weighing bedside work against further study. Interpersonal conflict is between two people, inter-sender conflict comes from incompatible instructions issued by two legitimate authorities, and intragroup conflict is tension inside one team.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse: Prevent, Detect, Report (MLN4649244), What's Medicare Fraud?
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic sends Medicare claims for appointments its patients never kept. How does CMS class that practice?
opciones: As fraud, since it claims payment for care never given
As abuse, since it adds cost the program need not bear
As waste, since the appointment slot could not be reused
As an error, since the schedule was not kept up to date
preguntas.explicacion: Claiming from Medicare for an appointment the patient never kept sits on the CMS list of fraud examples, alongside billing for services never provided and upcoding. Abuse covers practices that push unnecessary cost onto the program without that knowing deception, which is why the two are told apart by intent and knowledge rather than by the amount.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, When does Medicare coverage start?
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient turning 65 next month asks how long the first chance to sign up for Medicare lasts.
opciones: Seven months: the three before the birthday month, that month, and the three after
Seven months: the six before the birthday month and the birthday month itself
Three months: the month of the birthday and the two months that follow it
Twelve months: the whole calendar year in which the person turns 65 years old
preguntas.explicacion: The Initial Enrollment Period lasts 7 months: it opens 3 months before the month of the 65th birthday and closes 3 months after it, so the birthday month sits in the middle rather than at one end. Missing it can mean waiting to sign up and then paying a monthly penalty for late enrollment for the whole time the person keeps Part B.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet MLN006400 Information for Critical Access Hospitals: regulatory requirements
preguntas.subtema: Critical access hospital beds · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: A small rural hospital wants to be certified as a critical access hospital. What is the limit on its inpatient capacity?
opciones: No more than 25 beds used for inpatient or swing bed services at any one time
No more than 10 beds, the same cap that applies to a distinct part psychiatric unit
No more than 50 beds, half of which must be set aside for swing bed services
No more than 100 beds, above which the hospital is paid as an acute care hospital
preguntas.explicacion: A certified critical access hospital may hold no more than 25 inpatient beds, used for inpatient or for swing bed care. It may also run a distinct part rehabilitation unit and a distinct part psychiatric unit, each with up to 10 beds, and those beds sit outside the 25. Beds dedicated to hospice care do count toward the maximum of 25.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Rural health clinic services: Description; and 42 CFR 491.2
preguntas.subtema: Rural health clinic · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: What sets a rural health clinic apart from other Medicare outpatient clinics?
opciones: It sits in a non-urbanized area designated a shortage area and gives primary care
It runs only for surgery on patients who do not need to be kept in a hospital bed
It gives 24-hour emergency services with on-site or on-call staff every day of the week
It provides an intensive rehabilitation program with continued medical supervision
preguntas.explicacion: Rural health clinics sit in non-urbanized areas and deliver preventive services and primary care on an outpatient basis, in rural shortage or underserved areas. A shortage area is one the Department has designated as short of personal health services or of primary medical care manpower. Physicians, NPs, PAs, nurse-midwives, psychologists, social workers and counselors may furnish the services.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Ending the relationship · CCMA 5 k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.b · CMAA 4F k60 · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: A clinician wants to drop a patient he finds difficult and demanding. What do the ethical guidelines say?
opciones: Being a challenging patient is not on its own a ground for ending the relationship
Any patient may be dismissed at will, since the relationship rests on mutual consent
Dismissal is allowed once the patient has been rude to a member of the office staff
Only the health plan may end the relationship, by removing the patient from the panel
preguntas.explicacion: The clinician-patient relationship usually begins by mutual consent and is governed by State law. Ethical guidance holds that a clinician may not terminate it merely because someone is a challenging patient, and that irresponsible health behaviors do not release the professional from the duties of the relationship. The expected route is to try to resolve the conflict and, failing that, seek help from a consultant.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 3: Raise Awareness
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k167 team roles · CMAA 2F
preguntas.pregunta: A practice manager asks who in the office needs health literacy training. What does the toolkit call for?
opciones: Everyone, from front office staff through the medical director
Only the clinicians, since they are the ones who explain diagnoses
Only the medical assistants, who do most of the patient teaching
Only staff assigned to patients flagged as having low literacy
preguntas.explicacion: Putting universal precautions in place asks every staff member, from the front desk to the medical director, to know what health literacy is and to work at making care clearer. Practices are pointed toward staff meetings and short sessions with videos or a slide presentation, and a quiz can measure what staff learned.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, National Correct Coding Initiative, Submitting an Appeal
preguntas.subtema: Denials and appeals · CMA III.G.5.b (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6E · CCMA 5M
preguntas.pregunta: A claim is denied by a correct coding edit and the practice wants to appeal. Where does the appeal go?
opciones: To the Medicare contractor that processed the claim
To the contractor that keeps the edit files updated
To the committee that maintains the coding manual
To the Inspector General, who reviews the denials
preguntas.explicacion: Appeals of denials tied to the correct coding edits go to the Medicare administrative contractor or the qualified independent contractor, following the ordinary appeals route. The contractor that maintains the edit files cannot process a claim-specific appeal and does not forward one, so an appeal sent there simply loses time.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule, Notification by a Business Associate
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics · CMAA 3E k44 · NCMA 4.3 disclosure laws
preguntas.pregunta: A billing company discovers that it exposed patient data belonging to one of the clinics it serves. Whom must it notify, and how quickly?
opciones: The clinic, with no unreasonable delay and 60 days after discovering it at the latest
The affected patients, with no unreasonable delay and 60 days after discovery at the latest
The Secretary of HHS, with no unreasonable delay and 60 days after discovery at the latest
The clinic, within 60 days of the end of the calendar year in which it was discovered
preguntas.explicacion: A breach at or by a business associate travels upward: the business associate tells the covered entity, with no unreasonable delay and at the latest 60 days after discovery, and should identify the individuals affected and hand over whatever the covered entity needs for its own notices. Ultimate responsibility for notifying individuals stays with the covered entity, though it may delegate the task.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: Two separate conditions treated at one visit both fall under the very same diagnosis code. How many times is that code reported?
opciones: Once, since a unique code is reported only once for an encounter
Twice, once for each of the two conditions the provider documented
Twice, because the units reported have to match the work done
Once, and only where the two conditions are on the same side
preguntas.explicacion: A unique diagnosis code goes on an encounter a single time. The rule covers bilateral conditions where no distinct codes identify laterality, and it covers two different conditions that are classified to the same code. Units of service belong to procedure reporting, not to the diagnosis list.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 15: Make Action Plans
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4F facilitate compliance · CMA F.3.a · 2027 F.1.h · CMAA 2G
preguntas.pregunta: What is a patient action plan, and who builds it?
opciones: A few easy steps toward a health goal, worked out with the patient
A few easy steps toward a health goal, written by the clinician alone
The full treatment plan for a chronic condition, signed by the patient
A schedule of the follow-up appointments the practice has booked
preguntas.explicacion: An action plan lays out one or more easy steps toward a health goal, such as losing weight or managing a chronic condition better, and patient and health professional create it together. Nurses, clinicians, health coaches, diabetes educators and medical assistants can all do the action planning once trained for it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Issues of Concern: Storage of PHI Data; Use of Wireless Networks
preguntas.subtema: Portable media and wireless · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k34
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist wants to keep her worklist on a personal flash drive and check it over the clinic's open wireless network. What is the guidance?
opciones: Avoid storing it on portable media, and use only encrypted networks
Store it on the drive but keep the drive locked in the staff room
Use the open network, since the worklist holds no test results
Store it on the drive after deleting the names, keeping the numbers
preguntas.explicacion: Portable media are a documented source of breaches: laptops and flash drives get stolen, so workers are told not to keep patient data on them, and to encrypt it if it must be kept, or better, to view the data without storing it. Where several computers reach records over a wireless network, the network's encryption has to be switched on, and staff must stop using an unencrypted one because of the risk of interception.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Credentialing", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Credentialing · RMA I.C.2.a · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k48
preguntas.pregunta: How is a diploma or certificate verified during credentialing?
opciones: By checking with the primary source that issued the document
By reviewing the original document the applicant brings in person
By having the applicant sign a sworn statement of authenticity
By confirming it with the applicant's two professional references
preguntas.explicacion: A national body sets credentialing standards, and one of its key features is that any certificate, diploma or degree gets verified with the primary source: handing over an original is no longer enough. Cases of workers holding posts on certificates that were bogus and experience that was falsified are exactly what the process exists to catch.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.3 Active Listening and Attending Behaviors
preguntas.subtema: Active listening · CCMA 6C k202 · CMAA 2A k21 · CMA F.1.g · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: What separates active listening from passive listening?
opciones: The listener verifies their understanding with the speaker
The listener stays quiet and never interrupts the speaker
The listener concentrates on presenting their own viewpoint
The listener assumes the message was understood correctly
preguntas.explicacion: Three kinds of listening get named: competitive, where you are busy with your own point of view; passive, where you assume you understood without checking; and active. In active listening you show interest and then verify, often by restating what was said. That verification is the dividing line.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information
preguntas.subtema: Notice of privacy practices · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.2 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A new patient is registering at the front desk. When must the notice of privacy practices be given to her?
opciones: By the date of the first service at the latest, with a good faith effort at written acknowledgment
Within thirty days of the first visit, matching the deadline for responding to an access request
At the second visit, once the office knows the patient intends to keep using the practice
Only if the patient asks for it, since the notice is posted in the reception area anyway
preguntas.explicacion: Where the treatment relationship is a direct one, the provider hands the notice over by the date of the first service at the latest and tries, in good faith, to obtain written acknowledgment of receipt. Where no acknowledgment can be got, the provider documents what was tried and why it did not work. The notice also has to be posted prominently at the site and kept available for people to take away.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Anatomical Terminology, Body Cavities
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k36 · CMA I.C.6.d (2027 I.C.6.c) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k11 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks which organs lie in the pelvic portion of the ventral cavity. Which answer is right?
opciones: Most of the urogenital system, together with the rectum
Most of the gastrointestinal tract, with the kidneys
The heart and the lungs, with the large blood vessels
The brain in the upper part and the spinal cord below
preguntas.explicacion: The ventral cavity is divided by the diaphragm into the thoracic cavity above, which holds the heart, lungs, trachea, esophagus, large vessels and nerves, and the abdominopelvic cavity below. That lower one splits again: the abdominal portion holds most of the gastrointestinal tract with the kidneys and adrenal glands, the pelvic portion most of the urogenital system and the rectum.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Mandatory & Optional Medicaid Benefits
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.c / 2027 III.G.4
preguntas.pregunta: A family moving to another state asks whether their child's Medicaid lab work will still be covered. Which service must every state Medicaid program cover?
opciones: Laboratory and X-ray services, which federal law lists as mandatory
Eyeglasses and dentures, which federal law lists as mandatory benefits
Physical therapy, which federal law lists as mandatory for adult patients
Prescription drugs, which federal law lists as mandatory for every state
preguntas.explicacion: Federal law splits Medicaid benefits into mandatory and optional. Mandatory benefits, which every state must provide, include inpatient and outpatient hospital care, laboratory and X-ray services, physician services, nursing facility care, home health, family planning and the screening program for children. Prescription drugs, eyeglasses, dentures and physical therapy are on the optional list, which is why coverage differs from state to state.

preguntas.fuente: EEOC, Harassment (employer liability)
preguntas.subtema: Employment law compliance · CMAA 3A (federal employment law)
preguntas.pregunta: When is an employer automatically liable for a supervisor's harassment?
opciones: When the harassment ends in a firing, a lost promotion or lost wages
When the harassment is reported to human resources and not corrected
When the harassment occurs anywhere on the employer's own premises
When the harassment is witnessed by at least one other employee
preguntas.explicacion: Liability is automatic where a supervisor's harassment ends in a negative employment action: termination, a failure to promote or to hire, a loss of wages. If it produces a hostile environment instead, the employer escapes liability only by proving it tried to prevent the behavior and to correct it promptly, and that the employee unreasonably failed to use those channels.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs; and HHS, Who is eligible for Medicare?
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Why do most people pay no premium for Medicare Part A?
opciones: They or a spouse paid Medicare taxes while working, usually for 10 years or more
They or a spouse enrolled in Part B, which pays the Part A premium for them
They enrolled during the Initial Enrollment Period rather than waiting to sign up
They receive care from providers who accept the Medicare-approved amount in full
preguntas.explicacion: Part A comes without a premium for people who paid Medicare taxes while working long enough, generally ten years or more, or whose spouse did; those who fall short may be able to buy Part A. Signing up on time avoids a late enrollment penalty but does not create the premium-free status, and a provider who accepts assignment changes what the patient owes for services, not the premium.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Group health plan; and Glossary: Health Insurance Marketplace
preguntas.subtema: Commercial plan types · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's coverage comes through her husband's employer. What kind of plan is that?
opciones: A group health plan, offered by an employer to employees and their families
A group health plan, offered by an insurer directly to individual subscribers
An individual plan bought through the Marketplace with a premium tax credit
A supplemental policy that pays what the primary policy leaves unpaid each year
preguntas.explicacion: A group health plan is coverage an employer or an employee organization offers to its workers and their families, which is exactly the husband's arrangement. Coverage sold straight to one person is an individual policy, and the premium tax credit is tied to buying through the Marketplace. A policy that pays after another one is supplemental coverage, a different product entirely.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Long-term care: Description, Coverage details and Who's eligible
preguntas.subtema: Long-term care coverage · CCMA 4D k165 · CMAA 2H k30 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A family assumes Medicare will pay for their mother's nursing home stay for help with bathing and dressing. What should they be told?
opciones: Medicare does not pay for long-term care, though Medicaid may if the state's rules are met
Medicare pays in full once a doctor certifies that daily personal care is necessary
Medicare pays after the patient has used all 100 days of the skilled nursing benefit
Medicare pays whenever the nursing home is certified and accepts Medicare assignment
preguntas.explicacion: Long-term care, also called custodial care, is medical and non-medical help for people with a chronic illness or disability, mostly assistance with the basic tasks of everyday life. Because most of it is non-medical, neither Medicare nor most health insurance, Medigap included, pays for it. A person may qualify through Medicaid if the state's rules are met, or buy private long-term care insurance.

preguntas.fuente: USPS, Compare Mail Services
preguntas.subtema: Ground shipping · CCMA 5O · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7D k99 · NCMA 3.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which service does the Postal Service describe as the affordable ground option for packages, with insurance included?
opciones: USPS Ground Advantage, with up to one hundred dollars of insurance
Priority Mail Express, with up to one hundred dollars of insurance
First-Class Mail, with up to one hundred dollars of insurance
Certified Mail, with up to one hundred dollars of insurance
preguntas.explicacion: Ground Advantage is presented as the affordable, reliable route for parcels weighing as much as 70 pounds inside the country, expected to arrive in two to five days, with a hundred dollars of insurance built in and extra coverage available up to five thousand. It is also the primary option for hazardous materials that cannot travel by air.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Specific Techniques
preguntas.subtema: Therapeutic techniques · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2A k22 · CMA F.2 / 2027 F.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's voice breaks while she describes her diagnosis. The assistant names the emotion and reflects it back. Which technique is that?
opciones: Exploring feeling tones
Providing the rationale
Summarizing the visit
Clarifying the account
preguntas.explicacion: Exploring feeling tones is listed as identifying and empathizing with the patient's emotional state and reflecting it back to them. Providing rationale explains why information is needed, summarizing restates the content in the provider's own words and can close the interview, and clarifying draws out detail from a statement that was not clear.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Promoting Interoperability Programs
preguntas.subtema: Government regulations · CCMA 5 k179 · CMAA 6 k85
preguntas.pregunta: Which program replaced the electronic health record incentive program for eligible clinicians?
opciones: The Merit-based Incentive Payment System, created by MACRA in 2015
The Hospital Value-Based Purchasing program, created for inpatient care
The Medicare Shared Savings Program, created for accountable care groups
The Quality Improvement Organization review of hospital discharge decisions
preguntas.explicacion: MACRA, the Medicare Access and CHIP Reauthorization Act of 2015, closed the electronic health record incentive program as it applied to eligible professionals and folded similar requirements into the Merit-based Incentive Payment System, where promoting interoperability is one of four performance categories. Hospitals and critical access hospitals carry on under a promoting interoperability program of their own.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Helping patients prepare for their telehealth appointment
preguntas.subtema: Privacy options before a visit · CMAA 4E k59 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.3.g · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient booking a visit about a sensitive matter says she may not be able to speak freely at home. Besides helping her find a private spot, what does the guidance offer?
opciones: Other channels such as e-mail, text or the platform's chat, which matter where safety is a concern
A recording of the visit she can watch later, held on the platform under her own account
An office appointment instead, since a sensitive matter cannot be handled over a video link
A code word agreed with the clinician that will end the video call without alarming anybody
preguntas.explicacion: When sensitive topics are going to come up at an appointment, the office is asked to talk through why privacy matters and when, and to offer tips on finding somewhere private at home, in the car or at a friend's house. Other channels are named alongside that, e-mail, text, or the platform's chat feature, especially where personal safety could be an issue.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: The Intervention
preguntas.subtema: Where open access works · CMAA 4A k49 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A fee-for-service practice is told that open access only suits capitated managed care. Is that right?
opciones: No: it is reported to work in fee-for-service settings as well as in managed care
Yes: the model rests on capitation, since a same-day slot is not separately billable
Yes: the model was designed inside managed care and has not been tried outside it
No, but it holds up only where the practice also carries a large managed care panel
preguntas.explicacion: Experts in designing and implementing the model report that it works in fee-for-service settings as much as in managed care. Its logic has nothing to do with how a visit gets paid for: it brings queuing theory and industrial engineering to bear on matching the demand for visits against the supply of clinician time, on the supposition that the trouble is not a shortage of capacity but an imbalance between the two.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare Summary Notice (MSN)
preguntas.subtema: Denied item on the notice · CMAA 5 k78 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.5.b / 2027 III.G.3.b / 2027 III.G.3.b · RMA II.A.2 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient brings in her Medicare summary notice showing one service as denied. What does the guidance tell her to do first?
opciones: Ring the provider's office to check that what it submitted was correct
Ring Medicare to open an appeal against the decision on that service
Ring her supplemental insurer to see whether it will pay the balance
Ring the provider's office to ask for the charge to be written off
preguntas.explicacion: For a denied item or service the first step is a call to the office of the doctor or supplier to make sure the information sent in was right; if it was not, the office may resubmit. Only if the patient disagrees with the decision itself does she appeal, and the last page of the notice sets out step by step when and how to do that.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow, Conducting telehealth visits
preguntas.subtema: Pre-visit paperwork · CMAA 4H k62 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.1 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A first video visit is being booked for a new patient. Which paperwork step does the workflow guidance place before the appointment?
opciones: Asking her to complete forms online covering the reason, insurance, symptoms and history
Asking her to bring printed forms to the nearest office on the morning of the appointment
Asking her to complete the forms with the clinician during the first minutes of the visit
Asking her to post the completed forms so the record is updated before the day arrives
preguntas.explicacion: Among the things done before a video visit, the guidance has the office ask the patient to complete forms online covering why she is coming, her insurance details, her symptoms and her medical history. Where she is not comfortable entering that electronically, a staff member gathers the same information before the visit begins.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 17: Shadow patients
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k167 team roles · CMAA 2F
preguntas.pregunta: A practice wants to know how hard its forms and its system really are for patients. Which method does the toolkit describe?
opciones: Shadowing: an observer follows diverse patients through the whole visit
Mailing a satisfaction survey to every patient after the visit ends
Asking the staff to rate how clear they believe their own forms are
Timing how long each patient takes to fill out the intake paperwork
preguntas.explicacion: Practices are usually unaware of how much trouble patients have reading forms, understanding information and moving through the system, and patients are the ones who can point it out. In shadowing, someone quietly follows a patient from arrival to departure, asks afterward what went well and what was hard, and fills out an observation form.

preguntas.fuente: NAIC, Coordination of Benefits Model Regulation (Model 120), Effect on the Benefits of This Plan
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMAA 5B k75, 6C k87 · CCMA 5L k185
preguntas.pregunta: How does a secondary plan decide what it pays on a claim?
opciones: It pays after the primary plan, so the total stays within the allowable expenses
It pays at the same time as the primary plan, each covering half of the claim
It pays the full balance the patient still owes, deductibles and copays included
It pays the difference between the billed charge and what the primary plan paid
preguntas.explicacion: The secondary plan waits for the primary plan to pay, then meets some or all of what remains unpaid among the allowable expenses, cutting its own benefits so that the two payments together do not exceed the total allowable expenses on the claim. An allowable expense is a health care cost, deductibles, coinsurance and copayments included, that at least one plan covers, so a charge nobody covers falls outside the calculation.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Telehealth Systems, Function
preguntas.subtema: Facilitated virtual visit · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 4B k54 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: In a facilitated virtual visit, what is the role of the medical assistant at the patient's site?
opciones: Collecting objective data with equipment and transmitting it to the remote clinician
Interpreting the findings and deciding whether the patient needs an in-person visit
Recording the encounter so the clinician can review the video after the appointment
Waiting outside the room, since a facilitated visit requires the patient to be alone
preguntas.explicacion: This is a synchronous model: the patient travels to a nearby site stocked with diagnostic equipment, usually a clinic, while the clinician joins from somewhere else. On site a telehealth facilitator, described as a medical assistant or a nurse, works the tools (digital stethoscope, thermometer, pulse oximeter), gathers the objective findings and sends them across for the clinician to evaluate.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow
preguntas.subtema: What shapes the workflow · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.1 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Two practices adopting telehealth find their workflows end up looking very different. Which factors does the guidance say the changes depend on?
opciones: The vendor chosen, the size and setting of the practice, the patient population and the services given
The vendor chosen, the age of the record system, the state licensing board and the payer mix
The size and setting of the practice, the services given, and the number of exam rooms it keeps
The patient population, the services given, and whether the practice owns its own building
preguntas.explicacion: Telehealth reshapes several processes at once: check-in, triage, consent, scheduling, billing, documentation and the structure of the appointment. How far each one shifts depends on which telehealth vendor was chosen, on the size and the setting of the practice, on its patient population and on the services it provides. The record system is expected to merge easily into whatever workflow comes out.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Timeliness
preguntas.subtema: Right of access · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient submits a written request for a copy of her chart on March 3. By when must the office act on it?
opciones: No later than 30 calendar days from receipt of the request, and sooner where possible
No later than 60 calendar days from receipt, the same period allowed for an amendment
No later than 10 working days, the period set for verifying the requester's identity
No later than 6 years from receipt, matching the accounting of disclosures period
preguntas.explicacion: Access has to be provided within 30 calendar days of receiving the request. OCR treats that as an outer limit and encourages faster responses, noting that a portal or personal health record can make access almost immediate, and that patients reasonably expect speed from an office that uses health information technology every day.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Part A (Hospital Insurance) costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who never worked long enough to earn premium-free Part A asks what buying it will cost her in 2026.
opciones: Either $311 or $565 a month, depending on how long she or her spouse paid the taxes
A flat $202.90 a month, which is what every enrollee pays for Part A in 2026
A flat $283 a year, payable once the first hospital benefit period has opened
A flat $1,736 a year, the same figure as the inpatient hospital deductible
preguntas.explicacion: Part A costs most people nothing, because Medicare taxes were paid long enough by them or by a spouse, generally ten years' worth. Someone who does not qualify may be able to buy it: in 2026 the amount is either $311 or $565 a month, depending on how long those taxes were paid. Part B has to be taken as well in order to buy Part A.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, Sections 1, 7, 8 and 11
preguntas.subtema: SDS section 8 · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: Which Safety Data Sheet section tells the reader which gloves and eye protection to use with a chemical and lists its exposure limits?
opciones: Section 8, on exposure controls and personal protection
Section 7, Handling and Storage, with incompatibilities
Section 11, Toxicological Information, with routes of exposure
Section 1, Identification, with the emergency phone number
