preguntas.explicacion: Section 8 brings together the OSHA permissible exposure limits and ACGIH threshold limit values, the engineering controls such as local exhaust ventilation, and the personal protective measures, down to the glove material, for example nitrile or PVC, and its breakthrough time. Section 7 gives safe handling and storage conditions and incompatible chemicals; Section 11 describes toxic effects, symptoms and carcinogen listings; Section 1 identifies the product and supplier and gives the emergency telephone number.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow, Preparing for telehealth visits
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth scheduling decisions · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5B k170 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Before a practice starts booking video visits it is told to settle several scheduling questions. Which one belongs on that list?
opciones: How the office will decide that a particular request suits a telehealth appointment
How the clinician will write the visit up in the record once the video call ends
How the practice will train its current health care team to use the new platform
How the practice will support a caregiver who is helping the patient during the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Under scheduling, the questions are when telehealth appointments will be offered, whether patients will book online or by telephone, how the office will judge whether a telehealth appointment is appropriate, and how and when reminders go out. Training the team is a staffing question, supporting a caregiver falls under meeting patient needs, and documentation comes afterwards.

preguntas.fuente: NAIC, Coordination of Benefits Model Regulation (Model 120), Definitions
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMAA 5B k75, 6C k87 · CCMA 5L k185
preguntas.pregunta: Which charge is not an allowable expense when two plans coordinate benefits?
opciones: A service that neither of the two plans covers for that patient
A copayment the patient owes under the terms of the primary plan
A deductible amount applied by the primary plan to the claim
A coinsurance percentage left unpaid after the primary plan pays
preguntas.explicacion: An expense is allowable where at least one of the plans covers some part of it as a health care expense, and deductibles, coinsurance and copayments all count. Something no plan covering the person covers is not allowable, nor is an amount a provider is barred by law or by contract from charging, nor a reduction the primary plan made because the patient ignored a plan rule such as precertification.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicare Program Integrity Manual, chapter 3, section 3.3.2.4
preguntas.subtema: Signature requirements · CCMA 5 k189 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 7A · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A provider wants to sign chart notes with a rubber stamp because handwriting is slow. What does CMS say?
opciones: A stamp is not usually acceptable, apart from a disability accommodation
Stamped signatures are acceptable whenever the provider keeps the stamp locked away
Stamped signatures are acceptable if a signature log lists the stamp and its owner
Stamped signatures are acceptable on orders but never on progress notes or reports
preguntas.explicacion: A handwritten signature is a mark made by a person to signify knowledge, approval, acceptance or an obligation. CMS says a stamp is not usually acceptable, and lets one be used only under the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, by an author with a physical disability who can show a contractor that the disability prevents signing. A signature log is a different device altogether, for tying initials or an illegible signature to a name.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: The record describes the same condition as both acute and chronic, and the Index has separate subentries at the same level. What does the coder do?
opciones: Code both of them, and sequence the acute or subacute code first
Code both of them, and sequence the chronic code first of the two
Code the chronic one alone, since it is the longer-standing problem
Code the acute one alone, since it is what brought her in this time
preguntas.explicacion: Where the same condition is written up as acute or subacute and also as chronic, and the Alphabetic Index carries separate subentries indented to the same level, both codes go on and the acute or subacute one is sequenced first. Signs and symptoms that routinely accompany a disease process are not coded in addition unless the classification says so.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Error Prevention and Root Cause Analysis", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.B Quality Improvement, incident reporting · CCMA 6 k211 · CMAA 3E k44
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist spots two tubes carrying the wrong patient's label and pulls them before they reach the analyzer. How is this classified in patient safety terms?
opciones: A near miss, because the error occurred but was intercepted before it could reach the patient
A sentinel event, since any wrong-patient error meets the severity threshold set for those
A preventable adverse event, since harm from a labeling error is assumed until it is disproved
An error of execution that reached the patient but produced no harm that could be measured
preguntas.explicacion: A near miss is an error that happens but does not reach the patient, whether through timely intervention or through luck. Nothing was reported, so no harm followed and neither of the harm-based categories fits: a preventable adverse event needs harm caused by the error, and a sentinel event needs death, severe or permanent harm. Near misses are still worth reporting, because they show where the system is thin.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Parts of Medicare; and What Part B covers
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.b / 2027 III.G.4 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient asks which part pays for the doctor visit and the walker ordered today.
opciones: Part B, which covers provider services, outpatient care and durable equipment
Part A, which covers provider services, outpatient care and durable equipment
Part D, which covers provider services and the equipment ordered during them
Medigap, which covers provider services once Part A benefits are exhausted
preguntas.explicacion: Part B is the medical insurance half: services from doctors and other providers, outpatient care, home health, durable medical equipment such as walkers and wheelchairs, and many preventive services. Part A is hospital insurance, Part D pays for prescription drugs, and Medigap is private supplemental insurance that helps with the patient's share of costs in Original Medicare rather than covering new categories.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN909188 Chronic Care Management Services: definition
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4E k162 clinical resources · CMAA 1 health care delivery
preguntas.pregunta: Which patients qualify for Medicare chronic care management services?
opciones: Those with 2 chronic conditions or more, expected to run at least 12 months
Those with 2 chronic conditions or more, expected to run at least 3 months
Those with 1 chronic condition or more, expected to run at least 12 months
Those with 3 chronic conditions or more, expected to run at least 6 months
preguntas.explicacion: Chronic care management covers a patient with multiple chronic conditions, meaning two or more, that are expected to last at least twelve months or until the patient dies, and that place the patient at real risk of death, acute worsening or functional decline. The services themselves are non-face-to-face.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Access to Medical Care for Individuals with Mobility Disabilities: Overview
preguntas.subtema: Which title applies · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.c · CMAA 7 k98 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Under which part of the disability law is a privately owned medical office covered?
opciones: Title III, which reaches businesses and non-profits that serve the public
Title I, which reaches employers with fifteen or more people on the payroll
Title II, which reaches the services and programs of state and local government
Title IV, which reaches the companies that provide telephone and relay services
preguntas.explicacion: A private hospital or medical office is a place of public accommodation, and doctors' offices and hospitals are named among the businesses that serve the public. A clinic run by a state or a city falls under Title II instead, and Title I is the employment side, which applies to the same office as an employer.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · CMA III.G.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: What does an Excludes2 note allow?
opciones: Reporting both codes when the patient happens to have both conditions
Reporting either code, but never the two of them for the same encounter
Reporting the excluded code alone, since it takes the place of the other
Reporting both codes only when the record documents an inpatient stay
preguntas.explicacion: An Excludes2 note means not included here: the excluded condition is not part of what the code above represents, but a patient may have both at once, so using the two codes together is acceptable when the record supports it. That is precisely what separates it from Excludes1, where the two conditions cannot occur together. Neither note depends on the care setting.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Health Care Payment and Remittance Advice (835/ERA)
preguntas.subtema: Remittance advice · CMA III.G.3.b(3) (exam through June 2027) · CMAA 5 k79 · CCMA 5 k181
preguntas.pregunta: A remittance advice carries an adjustment that is not attached to any of the claims listed on it. How is that one explained?
opciones: By a provider level balance code, used for adjustments not tied to a single claim
By a claim adjustment reason code, used for adjustments not tied to a single claim
By a remittance advice remark code, used for adjustments not tied to a single claim
By a claim adjustment group code, used for adjustments not tied to a single claim
preguntas.explicacion: Adjustments can fall at line, claim or provider level. Line and claim adjustments are explained by the group code, the reason code and the remark code together. A provider level adjustment usually has nothing to do with any particular claim on that remittance, and provider level balance reason codes carry it: interest added because Medicare paid a clean claim late, a deduction for an earlier overpayment, or an increase under an incentive plan.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Helping patients prepare for their telehealth appointment
preguntas.subtema: What to expect on connecting · CMAA 4E k59 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who has been told to connect early asks what she will see while she waits. What does the guidance say to describe for her?
opciones: A virtual waiting room, or hold music, until the clinician joins the appointment
A message telling her to ring the front desk so that she can be let in
A form she has to finish on screen before the video will start at all
A recorded message that reads out the practice's policy on canceling appointments
preguntas.explicacion: Appointment setup guidance tells the office to describe what the patient will meet when she connects early, and names the virtual waiting room and hold music. Connecting fifteen minutes ahead for a video appointment is what leaves room for last-minute troubleshooting, so she needs to know that the wait is expected and not a sign that something has gone wrong.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Drug coverage (Part D); and HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Medicare Part D
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.b / 2027 III.G.4 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: How does a person with Original Medicare get prescription drug coverage?
opciones: By joining a separate Medicare drug plan run by a private company
By joining a separate Medigap policy run by a private company
By asking the pharmacy to bill Part B for the drugs bought there
By enrolling in Part A, which adds drug coverage after the first year
preguntas.explicacion: Part D coverage arrives in two ways: a standalone Medicare drug plan bolted onto Original Medicare, or a Medicare Advantage plan that already has drug coverage built in. Either way, private companies Medicare has approved run the plans. Medigap helps with the patient's share of costs, not with pharmacy drugs; Part B covers only limited outpatient drugs; and Part A adds no drug benefit.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, "Talking With Your Older Patients", Obtaining a thorough history
preguntas.subtema: Questioning techniques · CCMA 6C k200 · CMAA 2A k15 · RMA I.D.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: Several staff members would normally each gather part of an older patient's history. What does the guidance advise?
opciones: Have the patient tell the story once, since repeating tires them
Have each staff member ask again, so that errors are caught
Have the caregiver give the history so the patient can rest
Have the history taken from scratch again at every follow-up
preguntas.explicacion: Flexibility is needed with older patients, and where possible the patient should tell their story only once, because giving it to one staff member and then again to another is tiring. The history is built up and updated visit by visit rather than started over, and it is the patient, not the companion, who tells it.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Premium; and Glossary: Deductible
preguntas.subtema: Insurance terminology · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · CMAA 5C · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: Which term describes the amount a person pays every month for their health insurance, whether or not they use any care?
opciones: Premium
Deductible
Copay
Network
preguntas.explicacion: The premium is the monthly price of the coverage itself, owed whether or not any service is used. HealthCare.gov adds that, on top of it, the patient usually pays other costs when care is actually received: a deductible, copayments and coinsurance. Its glossary describes a copay as a fixed amount per covered service, such as $30. The network is the set of contracted providers, not a payment at all.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medigap basics
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient bought a Medicare SELECT policy and has changed her mind about it. What right does she have?
opciones: Twelve months in which to switch across to a standard Medigap policy instead
Six months in which to switch, matching the Medigap open enrollment period
Thirty days in which to switch, after which the policy holds for the whole year
No right to switch, since every policy with the same letter is the same anyway
preguntas.explicacion: Some states also sell a kind of Medigap policy called Medicare SELECT, and a buyer of one has the right to change her mind within twelve months and move to a standard Medigap policy. That is separate from the six-month Medigap Open Enrollment Period, which governs when a policy can be bought without health questions in the first place.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Telehealth: Coverage details
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth-appropriate visits · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5B k170 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient asks whether her diabetes education can be done by video instead of in the office. What does Medicare list?
opciones: Diabetes self-management training is among the services it covers by telehealth
An annual wellness visit with a physical examination is covered by telehealth
A screening mammogram read at the imaging center is covered by telehealth
A vaccine given at the patient's own home by a nurse is covered by telehealth
preguntas.explicacion: Plenty of services that normally happen face to face can be delivered by telehealth. Medicare names advance care planning, rehabilitation for the heart and the lungs, caregiver training, assessments of cognition, screening for depression, training in diabetes self-management, medical nutrition therapy, outpatient psychotherapy and speech therapy, and warns that the list is not everything it covers.

preguntas.fuente: NHA Candidate Handbook (2026), Recertification Requirements
preguntas.subtema: Professional development · CCMA 7C · RMA I.C.4.e · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: How long is an NHA certification valid, and what keeps it current?
opciones: Two years, with ten continuing education credits inside each cycle
Two years, with twenty continuing education credits inside each cycle
Five years, with ten continuing education credits inside each cycle
Three years, with fifteen continuing education credits in each cycle
preguntas.explicacion: A certification runs for two years from its issue date and expires on the date printed on the certificate. Inside each two-year cycle the holder submits documentation of at least ten continuing education credits relevant to their field. Certified pharmacy technicians are the exception: twenty hours, including one of pharmacy law and one of patient safety.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicaid and dual eligibility
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMAA 5B k75, 6 k84 · CCMA 5E k182 · CMA III.G.4.c / 2027 III.G.4
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is enrolled in both Medicare and full Medicaid. In what order do the programs pay?
opciones: Medicare pays first and Medicaid pays last, after any other coverage
Medicaid pays first and Medicare pays last, after any other coverage
Both pay half of the allowed amount for each Medicare-covered service
The patient chooses which program is billed first for each service
preguntas.explicacion: A patient holding both programs is dually eligible. On Medicare-covered services Medicare pays first, and Medicaid comes last, behind Medicare and behind any other insurance the person holds. The state also pays the Part B premium for full-benefit dual eligibles and may cover deductibles, coinsurance and copayments. The order is set by the rules, so it is neither split evenly nor chosen by the patient.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, HETS EDI - How to Enroll, Enrollment Information for Providers
preguntas.subtema: Medicare eligibility verification · CMAA 4C k58 · CCMA 5 k181 · CMA III.G.3 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: A practice is enrolling so that it can check Medicare eligibility electronically. Which of its own identifiers does the enrollment ask for?
opciones: Its PTAN and the NPI it uses to bill Medicare electronically
Its PTAN and the tax identification number of the practice
Its NPI and the Medicare number of each beneficiary checked
Its NPI and the enrollment date of every patient on its list
preguntas.explicacion: The enrollment asks for the name of the person authorized to sign for the organization, an email address, the Provider Transaction Access Number, and the individual or group National Provider Identifier used to bill Medicare claims electronically, along with the dates the relationship with the vendor or clearinghouse begins and ends. A group number used for claims has to be the one used here too.

preguntas.subtema: Cost of employee copies · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA II.B.5.c · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: An employee asks for a copy of her exposure record for the first time. What may the employer charge her?
opciones: Nothing for that first copy; a later request for another copy may be charged
A reasonable search and copying fee, since the record is the employer's own
No charge at any time, since copies of these records are free to employees
A flat administrative fee set by the employer and applied to every request
preguntas.explicacion: The employer has to hand over the copy at no cost, or lend the record so a copy can be made, or make copying facilities available free of charge. Once a record has gone out at no cost, administrative costs that are reasonable and applied without discrimination may be charged for further copies, except on a first request covering information newly added.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Preauthorization
preguntas.subtema: Authorizations · CMAA 4G k67 · CCMA 5H k183 · CMA III.G.5.a · RMA II.A.4 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: An insurer's letter uses the word precertification. Which term means the same thing?
opciones: Prior authorization, another name the federal glossary gives the same decision
Predetermination, the plan's estimate of the dollars it expects to pay later
Coordination of benefits, the way payers settle which of them pays first
Assignment of benefits, the patient's permission to pay the office directly
preguntas.explicacion: The federal glossary lists prior authorization, prior approval and precertification as other names for preauthorization, the plan's decision that a service is medically necessary before it is delivered. Coordination of benefits sorts out the order in which two payers pay a claim, and assignment of benefits is a form the patient signs so the plan pays the office rather than the patient.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Claim
preguntas.subtema: Claims and revenue cycle · CCMA 5L k181 · CMA III.G.3.b · RMA II.A.1 · CMAA 6C k89 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: After a visit, the office sends the insurer a request for payment for the services provided. What is that request called?
opciones: A claim
A copay
A referral
A denial
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov defines a claim as the request for payment that the patient or the provider sends to the insurer for items or services believed to be covered. It comes AFTER the care. A copay is the fixed amount the patient pays for a covered service, a referral is the primary care doctor's written order to see a specialist, and a denial is an answer the plan gives, not a request the office sends.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Section 6.P The Axioms of Service Recovery
preguntas.subtema: Service recovery · CCMA 6J k207 · CMA F.1.h / 2027 F.1.g · CMAA 2B k16
preguntas.pregunta: What is described as perhaps the most important step in recovering from a service failure?
opciones: Letting the person tell the story and vent the frustration
Handing the person a written apology signed by a manager
Offering a free service to make up for what went wrong
Explaining the process that let the failure happen at all
preguntas.explicacion: Recovery has a psychological side as much as a physical one, and the step that matters most is listening while the person tells their story and describes what the failure cost them. Work in a spirit of partnership toward the fix, though not by opening with a question about what they want you to do about it.

preguntas.subtema: Sharing information · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA E.2.a(1) · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: Which element must appear on a written consent to disclose substance use disorder records?
opciones: A description of each purpose for which the disclosure is being made
A notarized signature witnessed by two members of the program staff
A statement that the consent cannot be revoked before it expires
A copy of the recipient's own privacy notice attached to the form
preguntas.explicacion: The written consent, on paper or electronic, must carry the patient's name, who is authorized to disclose, a specific description of the information, the recipient, a description of each purpose, how the patient may revoke it, an expiration date or event, the signature and the date. Revocation is a required element, not something the form can waive.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Administrative Simplification: Health Care Payment and Remittance Advice and EFT; and HealthCare.gov, Glossary: coinsurance
preguntas.subtema: Electronic remittance advice · CMAA 5 k79 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.3.b(3) (exam through June 2027)
preguntas.pregunta: What is an electronic remittance advice?
opciones: The plan's explanation to the provider of how a claim's charges were adjusted and paid
The plan's explanation to the patient of what the visit cost and what remains to be paid
The provider's electronic request for payment sent to the plan after the visit
The bank message that moves the plan's payment into the provider's account
preguntas.explicacion: An electronic remittance advice explains to the provider how the health plan adjusted the charges on a claim, taking account of contract terms, secondary payers, benefit coverage and expected copayments and coinsurance. The document sent to the patient is the explanation of benefits or, in Original Medicare, the summary notice; the request for payment is the claim; and the money itself moves by electronic funds transfer.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Inpatient care; and Medicare.gov, Inpatient hospital care: Description and Who's eligible
preguntas.subtema: Inpatient vs outpatient setting · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient stays overnight in the hospital after a doctor writes an order admitting her. How is that stay classified?
opciones: Inpatient care, because a doctor's order admitted the patient to the hospital as an inpatient
Outpatient hospital service, the category that covers observation and same-day surgery
Skilled nursing facility care, which also supplies a semi-private room, meals and nursing
Long-term custodial care, the help with daily living given in chronic illness or disability
preguntas.explicacion: Inpatient care is what a person receives once admitted as an inpatient to a facility such as a hospital or a skilled nursing home. Two conditions apply: a doctor orders the admission because inpatient treatment is needed, and the hospital takes Medicare. Observation and same-day surgery are paid instead as outpatient hospital services.

preguntas.subtema: Copy of the authorization · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient signs an authorization at the desk so her records can go to her attorney. What does the practice owe her before she leaves?
opciones: A copy of the authorization she has just signed
A log of every disclosure the form will produce
A written estimate of the copying fee she will owe
A receipt showing the date the records were sent
preguntas.explicacion: When it is the covered entity that asks the individual for an authorization, the individual has to be handed a copy of the form she signed. The entity documents and keeps the signed authorization as well. The form is written in plain language and warns that information released under it may be passed on again and lose the rule's protection.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 3, Guidelines for Using a Medical Interpreter
preguntas.subtema: Interpreters · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.1.c(3) / 2027 F.1.d(4)
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant is about to take a history through a medical interpreter. Which practice applies?
opciones: Speaking in the first person and keeping idioms out of it
Speaking in the third person so the meaning stays clear
Grouping several questions so the exchange moves faster
Shortening the visit, since two people now do the talking
preguntas.explicacion: The guidelines say to speak in the first person, to avoid idioms, abbreviations, slang, jokes and jargon, to use short sentences and ask one question at a time, and to let the interpreter finish before starting the next topic. Extra time is set aside for these visits rather than cut, and questions are never stacked.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, "Communicating With and About People with Disabilities", People-first language
preguntas.subtema: Person-first language · CCMA 6B k195 · CMAA 2D k17 · RMA I.D.1.e
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant is charting about a patient who gets around in a wheelchair. Which phrasing follows people-first language?
opciones: A person who uses a wheelchair
A wheelchair-bound patient
A person confined to a wheelchair
A handicapped person in a wheelchair
preguntas.explicacion: People-first language puts the person ahead of the disability, using constructions such as a person who or a person with, and it promotes understanding, dignity and respect. Wheelchair bound and confined to a wheelchair stress the limitation, and handicapped sits in the do-not-use column.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Specific Techniques
preguntas.subtema: Therapeutic techniques · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2E k21
preguntas.pregunta: What does closing the door or the curtain before an interview demonstrate?
opciones: Respect for privacy, and it holds down interruptions
Compliance with the personal zone of 18 inches to four feet
A check-back that confirms the patient heard the question
Cultural negotiation over who may stay in the room
preguntas.explicacion: Respecting privacy and minimizing interruptions is listed as a technique in its own right: depending on the setting, close the door or draw the curtain. The personal zone is a proxemics measurement, a check-back confirms a message between staff, and cultural negotiation settles competing care needs.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 14.1 Sensory Perception, Somatosensation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(10) (2027 I.C.6.f(10)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is a general sense rather than a special sense?
opciones: Somatosensation, whose receptors are spread through many organs
Gustation, whose receptors are spread through many organs
Olfaction, whose receptors are spread through many organs
Equilibrium, whose receptors are spread through many organs
preguntas.explicacion: The special senses each have their own organ: taste, smell, hearing, balance and vision. Somatosensation is a general sense instead, a group of modalities including pressure, vibration, light touch, temperature, pain and proprioception, and its receptors sit in skin, muscles, tendons, joints and the walls of the viscera.

preguntas.fuente: EEOC, Harassment
preguntas.subtema: Employment law compliance · CMAA 3A (federal employment law)
preguntas.pregunta: When does offensive conduct at work cross the line into unlawful harassment?
opciones: When enduring it becomes a condition of staying, or it is severe or pervasive
When the person harassed suffers an economic loss such as lost wages
When the conduct is repeated on at least three separate occasions
When the harasser is a supervisor rather than a coworker or an outside vendor
preguntas.explicacion: Harassment turns unlawful on either of two grounds: enduring the conduct becomes a condition of staying employed, or the conduct is severe or pervasive enough that a reasonable person would find the workplace intimidating, hostile or abusive. Petty slights and isolated incidents usually do not qualify, and no economic injury is needed. The harasser can be anyone, a non-employee included.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Fees for Copies
preguntas.subtema: Access fees · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which cost may a practice include in the fee it charges a patient for a copy of her record?
opciones: The labor of copying the information, plus postage when she asks to have it mailed
The time staff spend searching for and retrieving the chart from the storage room
The share of the electronic system's annual license attributable to storing her data
The cost of verifying her identity and documenting the request in the practice log
preguntas.explicacion: The fee has to be reasonable and cost based, and only four components may go into it: labor for copying, whether on paper or electronically; supplies such as a CD or USB drive if portable media are requested; postage where the copy is mailed; and preparing an explanation or summary if the patient agreed to one. Verification, documentation, search and retrieval, and system maintenance may not be charged, even where state law allows it.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.524(a)(1)-(4), Standard: Access to protected health information
preguntas.subtema: Exceptions to access · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: Which information is excluded from the HIPAA right of access?
opciones: Psychotherapy notes and information compiled for a legal proceeding
Laboratory results, which belong to the ordering physician until released
Billing records, which are financial rather than clinical
Records older than 6 years, which need not be retained
preguntas.explicacion: The right of access in 164.524(a)(1) covers PHI in a designated record set for as long as it is kept, with two exceptions: psychotherapy notes, and anything assembled in reasonable anticipation of a legal action, civil, criminal or administrative, or for use in one. Access may also be denied without review in limited cases such as certain correctional and research situations, and with a right to review where a licensed professional judges that access is likely to endanger someone. Laboratory and billing records are part of the designated record set and stay accessible.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Home health services: Provider requirements
preguntas.subtema: Coordinating home health · CCMA 4E · CMAA 1 k1 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: Before home health services are certified for a patient, what has to happen?
opciones: A provider assesses the patient face to face and orders care from a certified agency
A hospice physician meets the patient face to face and recertifies the prognosis
The patient completes three days as an inpatient in a hospital that accepts Medicare
The agency files a claim so that the contractor can decide medical necessity in advance
preguntas.explicacion: A health care provider, a nurse practitioner for example, must assess the patient face to face before certifying the need for home health. The care has to be ordered by a provider and delivered by a home health agency that Medicare has certified. The three-day inpatient stay belongs to skilled nursing coverage and the recertified prognosis to hospice.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, section 805(a)
preguntas.subtema: Collections · CMA III.G.9.f (exam through June 2027) · CMAA 6D · CCMA 5 k187
preguntas.pregunta: A collection agency working the practice's old accounts telephones a patient at seven in the morning. What does the statute presume?
opciones: That a convenient hour runs from eight in the morning to nine at night, where she is
That a convenient hour runs from nine in the morning to eight at night, where she is
That any hour suits until the consumer says otherwise to the collector in writing
That any hour suits once the collector has sent the written validation of the debt
preguntas.explicacion: The collector is barred from communicating with a consumer at an unusual time or place, or at one it knows or should know is inconvenient. Absent knowledge to the contrary, it has to assume the convenient window runs from eight in the morning to nine at night, local time where the consumer is. Only the consumer's consent or a court order changes that.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Net Collection Rate
preguntas.subtema: Aging of accounts · CMA III.G.9.b (exam through June 2027) · CMAA 6 k86 · CCMA 5 k187
preguntas.pregunta: What does the net collection rate measure, and what is its benchmark?
opciones: The share of expected revenue a practice actually collects; above 95%
The share of claims paid on the very first submission with no rework; above 95%
The share of claims that pass every edit before they are sent out; above 95%
The share of accounts still unpaid after ninety days have gone by; under 15%
preguntas.explicacion: Net collection rate is the percentage of the revenue a practice expected that it actually collected, and the benchmark is above ninety-five percent. The review cited measures it on bills more than a hundred and twenty days old, where a low figure means the receivables team is not working the older balances: a follow-up opportunity rather than a loss. The other three figures are real benchmarks too, but they belong to first-pass resolution, clean claims and receivables past ninety days.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Access to Medical Care for Individuals with Mobility Disabilities: Commonly Asked Questions
preguntas.subtema: Assistance at the visit · CCMA 4 k157 · CMA II.F.1.c(4) / 2027 II.F.1.d(1) · RMA I.D.1.c · CMAA 7 k98 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: Booking a patient who uses a wheelchair, a receptionist tells her to bring somebody along who can help her onto the table. Is that acceptable?
opciones: No, she may come alone and the practice provides the assistance she needs
No, unless the office has no lift and no member of staff trained to transfer
Yes, so long as the same is asked of every patient who uses a wheelchair
Yes, because helping a patient undress falls outside a receptionist's duties
preguntas.explicacion: A patient may bring a friend or relative if she wishes, but she may equally come by herself, and the provider then gives the reasonable assistance that lets her receive the care: help with dressing, with getting on and off the table, with positioning, and with staying balanced once there. The staff member asks the patient what help she wants and how.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Body Parts and Disorders
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k12 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k9
preguntas.pregunta: Which pair correctly matches an everyday word with the root used for the same structure?
opciones: Windpipe with trache-, and voice box with laryng-
Windpipe with laryng-, and voice box with trache-
Windpipe with pharyng-, and voice box with bronch-
Windpipe with bronch-, and voice box with pharyng-
preguntas.explicacion: The trachea is the windpipe and the larynx is the voice box, so trache- and laryng- go with those plain words. The other two roots name neighbors along the same route: pharyng- is the throat, and bronch- the large airway that leads from the trachea into a lung.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Reasons for Termination
preguntas.subtema: Why patients are dismissed · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.b · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: In the review of 536 formal terminations, which cause came second after repeated no-shows, and how large was it?
opciones: Disrespectful or disruptive behavior, at 22 % of the cases reviewed
Self-termination by the patient, at 22 % of the cases reviewed
Nonadherence with the treatment plan, at 15 % of the cases reviewed
Violation of an opioid agreement, at 15 % of the cases reviewed
preguntas.explicacion: Repeated appointment no-shows headed the list at 38 %. Disrespectful or disruptive behavior came next at 22 %, then so-called self-termination at 15 %, violating an opioid contract at 4 %, non-adherence with treatment plans at 3 %, and illegal behavior such as altering a written prescription at 2 %.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Defining the PCMH: 4. Accessible Services
preguntas.subtema: Delivery models · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these belongs to the accessible services function of the medical home?
opciones: Access to a member of the care team by telephone or electronically at any hour
A shared decision-making aid used with the patient during an office visit
A written plan of care built together with the patient and the whole team
A registry that tracks the practice population for chronic disease care
preguntas.explicacion: Accessible services means waiting times cut short for urgent needs, in-person hours extended, a member of the care team reachable by telephone or electronically at any hour, and other ways of communicating such as email and care by phone. The practice answers to what patients prefer about access. Decision-support tools and population health management sit under quality and safety.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: Two terms sit side by side in one report: arteriosclerosis and stenosis. Which contrast between those endings is correct?
opciones: The first names a hardening and the second a narrowing or blockage
The first names a narrowing and the second a hardening or stiffening
The first names a hardening and the second an expansion or dilation
The first names a blockage and the second a softening or weakening
preguntas.explicacion: Sclera- and sclero- mean hardness, and -sclerosis is a hardening; on the artery root that gives hardened arteries. Sten- and steno- mean narrowed or blocked. Two more parts fall into that space and mean the opposite or something else: -ectasis is an expansion or dilation, and -malacia is a softening.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Conflict Management", Issues of Concern: A Practical Stepwise Approach
preguntas.subtema: Conflict management · CCMA 6J k209 · CMAA 2B k26 · CMA F.1.f / 2027 F.1.f
preguntas.pregunta: A supervisor sits two staff members down to work through a dispute. What comes before the substance is discussed?
opciones: Ground rules on respectful language, equal time and privacy
A list of possible solutions, hybrids included, from both sides
A written plan naming who will do what and by which date
A checkpoint set to see whether the agreement is holding up
preguntas.explicacion: The stepwise approach opens with ground rules settled before any substantive discussion: language kept respectful, speaking time shared equally, confidentiality maintained. Separating the people from the problem comes next. Generating options, agreeing a concrete plan and scheduling follow-up are all real steps, but they sit later in the same sequence.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026, Section I.B.10
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is seen for a scar left by a burn two years ago. How is that coded?
opciones: With two codes, the residual condition first and the sequela code second
With two codes, the sequela code first and the residual condition second
With one code only, since a sequela is a combination code by definition
With no sequela code, because more than a year has passed since the burn
preguntas.explicacion: A sequela is what remains once the acute phase of an illness or an injury is over, and the examples given include a scar from a burn, a deviated septum following a nasal fracture, and infertility after old tuberculosis. Coding one usually takes two codes: the condition or nature of the residual goes first, the sequela code second. No time limit applies.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans and patient cost · CMAA 5C k76, 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Under Original Medicare in 2026, what does a patient generally pay for a covered Part B service after the yearly deductible?
opciones: 20% of the Medicare-approved amount, when the provider accepts assignment
20% of the provider's own charge, which may sit above the approved amount
A fixed copayment of $20 for each service, set by the Medicare fee schedule
A share of 20% for equipment only, since visits are paid in full by Part B
preguntas.explicacion: Part B coinsurance is usually 20% of the Medicare-approved amount for each covered service or item once the yearly deductible, $283 in 2026, has been paid, and it applies when the provider accepts the approved amount as full payment. The share is figured on that approved amount, not on the provider's own charge; it is not limited to equipment, since doctor visits carry the same 20%; and Part B has no single fixed copayment per service.

preguntas.subtema: Header of the notice · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice is laying out its notice of privacy practices. What has to sit at the top of the page as a header, or otherwise be displayed prominently?
opciones: A statement that the notice covers how the patient's information is used, shared and reached
A statement that the practice is a covered entity subject to federal privacy enforcement
A statement that the patient consents to treatment, to payment and to operations
A statement of the date the notice takes effect and the officer who approved its wording
preguntas.explicacion: The regulation prescribes a header telling the reader that the document describes how medical information about them may be used and disclosed and how they can get access to it, and asking that it be reviewed carefully. The effective date is required too, but it is not the header; the whole notice has to be in plain language.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Administrative Requirements
preguntas.subtema: Privacy administration · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.5 · CMAA 3B k33 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Besides written policies, which administrative duties does the Privacy Rule place on a covered entity?
opciones: Naming a privacy official and a contact for complaints, and training the whole workforce
Naming a privacy official whose approval is needed before any record leaves the office
Training only the staff who handle claims, since billing carries the greatest privacy risk
Filing the practice's privacy policies with the Office for Civil Rights before they take effect
preguntas.explicacion: The rule obliges a covered entity to name a privacy official who answers for its policies and its procedures, plus a contact person or office to take complaints and answer questions. It has to train every member of the workforce as their functions require, sanction those who break the policies, mitigate any harm it comes to know about, and never retaliate against someone who exercises a right or files a complaint.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Credentialing", Issues of Concern: privileging
preguntas.subtema: Scope of practice · RMA I.C.6 · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k48
preguntas.pregunta: Does holding a professional license mean a person may provide any service in that field?
opciones: No: each state's law and the licensing body set what the license permits
Yes, as long as the employer's job description includes that service
Yes, once the institution has finished credentialing that professional
No: only the institution's privileges list decides, and state law does not
preguntas.explicacion: Every state has its own laws on medical practice, and simply holding a license does not mean the holder may deliver whatever service they want: an advanced practice nurse cannot start prescribing on that basis alone, and a family physician cannot start inserting central lines. Credentialing checks the qualifications; privileging then authorizes a specific set of services after evaluating credentials and performance.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Procedures, Diagnosis and Surgery
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.c (2027 I.A.2.c) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A surgeon repairs a torn tendon and the operative report names the procedure with the ending -rrhaphy. Which act does that ending name?
opciones: Suturing the structure named by the root
Crushing the structure named by the root
Binding the structure named by the root
Puncturing the structure named by the root
preguntas.explicacion: The ending -rrhaphy is a suture, so a tendon repair with stitches carries it. Its neighbors on the same list name other acts: -desis is a surgical binding, -tripsy a crushing, and -centesis a surgical puncture that draws off fluid. Two more, -pexy and -plasty, anchor a part in place and rebuild it.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Charge Capture
preguntas.subtema: Revenue cycle phases · CMAA 6 k81, 6B · CCMA 5K k181
preguntas.pregunta: What happens during charge capture?
opciones: The visits, services and facility fees documented are assembled for the billing team
The payer's decision on each service is recorded against the patient's account
The patient's coverage and billing address are confirmed with the health plan
The unpaid balances older than 90 days are separated for collection follow-up
preguntas.explicacion: Charge capture starts immediately after care is delivered: the documented visits, the services provided and the facility fees are gathered and sent to the billing department, and copayments collected are recorded at the same time. Posting the payer's decisions belongs to remittance processing, confirming coverage is patient data verification, and sorting aged balances is accounts receivable follow-up.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Denial of Access
preguntas.subtema: Denial of access · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: The practice decides to deny part of an access request. What must the written denial contain?
opciones: The basis for the denial in plain language and how to complain to the practice or to OCR
The name of the workforce member who located the records and the date they were pulled
A copy of the practice policy on retention and disposal of protected health information
The fee schedule for copies, so the patient can decide whether to renew the request later
preguntas.explicacion: A denial, whole or partial, has to reach the individual in writing inside 30 calendar days of the request, or 60 where an extension was announced. It has to be in plain language, has to set out the ground on which access was refused, has to explain the right to a review of that decision and how to ask for one where it applies, and how to complain to the covered entity or to the HHS Office for Civil Rights. Whatever the ground does not cover still has to be released.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, FAQ: What is a patient portal?
preguntas.subtema: Patient portal · CCMA 5U · CMA III.H.3.a (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.B.6.c · CMAA 4E k56 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what she can see through the practice's patient portal at two in the morning.
opciones: Allergies, medications, immunizations, recent visits, discharge summaries and lab results
Only the balance she owes the practice and the date of her next scheduled appointment
Only the documents a staff member has chosen to release to her during office hours
The complete record of every patient the practice treats, filtered by her search terms
preguntas.explicacion: A patient portal is a secure web site that opens personal health information round the clock, from anywhere there is an Internet connection, entered with a username and a password of one's own. What can be looked at there includes allergies, medications, immunizations, recent visits to the doctor, discharge summaries and laboratory results.

preguntas.subtema: Uses requiring authorization · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: Which use of protected health information always requires a HIPAA authorization, even when it relates to treatment, payment or operations?
opciones: Sale of protected health information
Referral of the patient to a specialist
Consultation between two treating providers
Submission of a claim to the health plan
preguntas.explicacion: Three things need an authorization whatever else the rule allows: psychotherapy notes in most of their uses and disclosures; marketing that goes beyond a face-to-face communication or a gift of nominal value; and any disclosure amounting to a sale of PHI, where the authorization has to say that the covered entity will be paid. Section 164.502(a)(5)(ii) separately forbids selling PHI except under such an authorization. Referrals, consultations between treating providers and claims are treatment and payment activities that 164.506 permits.

preguntas.subtema: Device and media controls · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: What does the device and media controls standard cover, taken as a whole?
opciones: Hardware and media coming into the office, leaving it, and moving around inside
Hardware bought from an approved supplier and kept on the practice's asset list
Media held by the software vendor on the practice's behalf under its contract
Hardware that stores records, but not the media used only to back them up
preguntas.explicacion: The standard asks for policies on hardware and electronic media that hold the information: how they come into a facility, how they leave it, and how they move around inside. The four specifications then fill that in: disposal and media re-use are required; accountability and a data backup before equipment moves are addressable.

preguntas.subtema: Revoking an authorization · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient telephones to cancel the authorization he signed last week. What does the rule require of a revocation, and what does it not undo?
opciones: It must be in writing, and it does not undo what was already done in reliance on it
It must be in writing, and it does not undo disclosures made in the previous six years
It may be spoken, and it does not undo what was already done in reliance on it
It must be in writing, and it undoes every disclosure the form had authorized
preguntas.explicacion: An individual may revoke an authorization at any time, provided the revocation is in writing. Two things survive it: action the covered entity has already taken in reliance on the authorization, and, where the form was signed to obtain insurance coverage, the insurer's right under other law to contest a claim or the policy.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow, Preparing for telehealth visits
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth scheduling · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Staff at a practice about to start booking video visits ask how to get ready for the first one. Which step does the guidance suggest?
opciones: Do a practice run of a telehealth visit with a co-worker
Run the first week of visits with audio only, then add video
Ask a patient to test the platform and report back on it
Book the first video visits at the end of the working day
preguntas.explicacion: Among the things a practice settles before it offers telehealth are staffing, technology, scheduling and how it will meet patient needs, and the guidance closes that list with a tip: try the visit out with a co-worker first. Audio-only is offered as a fallback when the video fails, not as a way of phasing the service in.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Claim Submission
preguntas.subtema: Claim scrubbing · CMAA 6C k89, 6 k81 · CCMA 5L k181
preguntas.pregunta: Before claims leave the office, software checks them for formatting errors, wrong codes and unsupported documentation. What is this step called?
opciones: Scrubbing the claims, done during submission to catch errors before the payer sees them
Adjudicating the claims, done during submission to settle what the payer will pay
Posting the claims, done after payment to record the money against each account
Auditing the claims, done yearly to sample records for the compliance program
preguntas.explicacion: In the claim submission step of the revenue cycle, scrubbing is the review that detects coding errors, formatting problems and unsupported documentation before claims reach the payers. Adjudication is what the payer does afterwards, posting records payments once the remittance advice arrives, and a compliance audit is a periodic review of records rather than a check on outgoing claims.

preguntas.subtema: Standing orders and order sets · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 7A · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital wants to use pre-printed order sets for a common admission. What does the medical record condition require before they may be used?
opciones: Review and approval by the medical staff and by nursing and pharmacy leadership
Review and approval by the medical staff and by the governing body of the hospital
Review and approval by the medical staff and by the accrediting organization used
Review and approval by the ordering practitioner at the time each set is applied
preguntas.explicacion: Standing orders, order sets and protocols, whether pre-printed or electronic, may be used only where the hospital has had them reviewed and approved by the medical staff together with its nursing and pharmacy leadership, has shown they follow guidelines that are nationally recognized and evidence-based, and has arranged for them to be reviewed regularly. Each use is still dated, timed and authenticated promptly.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth privacy setup · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 4B k55 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient plans to join her video visit from a coffee shop network. What should the office check with her beforehand?
opciones: Whether she understands how the platform handles security on public Wi-Fi
Whether the coffee shop has agreed in writing to act as an originating site
Whether her device is enrolled in the practice's own equipment inventory list
Whether she is willing to sign a waiver releasing the practice from the rules
preguntas.explicacion: The checklist for finding out what technology a patient has asks whether she owns a device with a camera and a microphone, whether her internet connection carries enough bandwidth, and whether she has somewhere with secure internet from which to take the appointment; it adds that a patient on public Wi-Fi needs to understand how the telehealth platform handles security. Providers are told to deliver telehealth from private locations and to apply reasonable safeguards.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 1.1
preguntas.subtema: Redundant internet path · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A small clinic cannot run two cable connections in separate trenches. What backup route to the internet does the guidance suggest for a practice that size?
opciones: A wireless access point over the mobile network, able to carry a cloud-hosted system
A wireless access point over the mobile network, used only to send claims overnight
A dial-up line kept on standby, which carries the read-only copy of the records
A second cable from the same provider, brought into the building by another route
preguntas.explicacion: Larger organizations are expected to hold a redundant path to the internet, two different cables in different trenches, with a microwave or other wireless link acceptable when two different providers supply it. Smaller ambulatory clinics are told to have at least a cellphone-based wireless access point capable of running a cloud-hosted record system.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting started with telehealth, Types of telehealth
preguntas.subtema: Mobile health · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's telephone application records her walking and reminds her when a dose is due. Which telehealth category covers that?
opciones: Mobile health, one of the other asynchronous forms available to patients
Remote patient monitoring, which sends clinical data on to her provider
Synchronous telehealth, because the reminder reaches her in real time
A virtual check-in, because each exchange runs for ten minutes or less
preguntas.explicacion: Mobile health is the use of a digital device, a smartphone for instance, or of something the patient wears, in support of her own health; the examples given are a fitness tracker, applications that record exercise, automatic reminders about when a medicine is due, and storage of things like discharge instructions. Remote monitoring, by contrast, sends patient data on to the provider.

preguntas.fuente: The Joint Commission, 2026 Ambulatory Health Care National Patient Safety Goals
preguntas.subtema: Two identifiers · CCMA 3A2 · CMA I.A.1 · RMA II.B.4.a · CMAA 3A k42 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is checking in for an injection. Which practice does the 2026 ambulatory patient safety goal require?
opciones: Using at least two ways to identify the patient, such as name and date of birth
Using the room number as the second identifier once the patient has been seated
Using the patient's insurance member number as the only identifier at check-in
Using one identifier at registration and a second one only before a procedure
preguntas.explicacion: The first ambulatory goal is to identify patients correctly, and the wording is to use at least two ways to identify a patient, the example given being name and date of birth. The purpose stated is making sure each patient receives the correct medicine and treatment. The same goal appears, worded for residents and for individuals served, across the other program settings.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Section 6.P Service Recovery Programs
preguntas.subtema: Service recovery · CCMA 6J k207 · CMAA 2B k16 · NCMA EKB 22 · CMA F.1.h / 2027 F.1.g
preguntas.pregunta: A patient complains loudly that nobody called back with her results. Which two steps open service recovery?
opciones: Apologize and acknowledge, then listen and ask openly
Fix it quickly and fairly, then offer some atonement
Follow up afterward, and remember what was promised
Document the complaint, then route it to a manager
preguntas.explicacion: The six-step process runs: apologize and acknowledge; listen, empathize and ask open questions; fix the problem quickly and fairly; offer atonement; follow up; and remember your promises. Fixing and atoning come only after the person has been heard, which is where recovery is won or lost.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Premium tax credit
preguntas.subtema: Affordable Care Act · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: What is the premium tax credit?
opciones: Help that lowers the monthly cost of a Marketplace plan, based on income
Help that lowers the deductible of a Marketplace plan, based on family size
A refund of premiums paid for job-based coverage during the previous year
A discount an insurer applies for staying with the same plan several years
preguntas.explicacion: The premium tax credit is financial help that lowers the monthly payment for a plan bought through the Marketplace, figured from household information and estimated income; incomes between 100% and 400% of the federal poverty level qualify in every state. Discounts on what is paid at the point of care are cost-sharing reductions, a different item, and the credit is available only through the Marketplace.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicare Shared Savings Program - About: ACO Providers and Suppliers
preguntas.subtema: Delivery models · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these may take part in the Medicare Shared Savings Program as part of an ACO?
opciones: Federally qualified health centers and rural health clinics, among others
Hospitals with more than one hundred inpatient beds, and none of the smaller ones
Physician group practices that employ no advanced practice nurses at all
Medicare Advantage plans alone, since they already carry all of the risk
preguntas.explicacion: Those who may take part are: networks of individual practices; group practice arrangements of ACO professionals; joint ventures or partnerships set up by hospitals with ACO professionals; federally qualified health centers; critical access hospitals that bill under Method II; hospitals employing ACO professionals; rural health clinics; and certain teaching hospitals.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Common Barriers to Communication
preguntas.subtema: Communication by channel · CCMA 6C k196 · CMAA 2A k27 · CMA F.3.b / 2027 F.1.i
preguntas.pregunta: Why is important information delivered face to face rather than by email or text when possible?
opciones: Tone, facial expression and body language travel with it
A written message cannot be stored in the medical record
A written message reaches the receiver much more slowly
A spoken message needs no feedback from the receiver
preguntas.explicacion: Providing information by email or text is often less effective than speaking in person: the receiver cannot see the nonverbal communication that goes with the message — tone of voice, facial expression, general body language — and misinterpretation follows. Face to face keeps those signals attached.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", How do you ensure password protection; StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Passwords and Unique User Identification
preguntas.subtema: Password safeguards · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k38
preguntas.pregunta: Which password practice is consistent with HIPAA security guidance?
opciones: Unique passwords for each user, never shared, written down or emailed
A single department password changed each year at annual training
Passwords posted near the workstation so that coverage staff can log in quickly
Passwords of consecutive digits, which are easier to audit
preguntas.explicacion: Every worker who accesses patient records needs a unique, strong password that mixes letters, numbers and symbols, is changed periodically, is never shared, verbalized, written down near the computer or emailed, and is not built from consecutive digits or easily guessed information; the IT department checks password quality before granting access. Uniqueness matters because HITECH requires systems to track each user's activity. Passwords alone are considered weak protection, which is why some institutions add biometric authentication.

preguntas.fuente: AAMA, Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Standards for CMAs (AAMA), Grounds for Discipline; and Possible Sanctions
preguntas.subtema: Unethical conduct · CCMA 7C · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: A candidate is found to have copied answers during the certification exam. What may follow?
opciones: Sanctions up to permanent revocation, with the certificate returned
A written reprimand only, since no patient was harmed by the conduct
A required retake at full price, with the credential left untouched
Referral to the state licensing board, which imposes the sanction
preguntas.explicacion: Copying answers, letting somebody else copy, and giving or taking advice about exam content without authorization are listed as grounds for discipline, alongside obtaining certification by fraud and distributing exam material. The sanctions available run from denial of eligibility and invalidated or withheld scores through probation and reprimand to temporary or permanent revocation, with the certificate and wallet card returned.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Procedures, Diagnosis and Surgery
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.c (2027 I.A.2.c) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: Fluid is drawn off from around a lung in a procedure called a thoracentesis. Which act does that ending name?
opciones: A surgical puncture made in order to remove fluid
A surgical opening made from an organ to the outside
A surgical binding that fixes two structures together
A crushing of something hard that has formed inside
preguntas.explicacion: The ending -centesis is a surgical puncture that removes fluid, and thorac- names the chest, so the two together say where and what. The endings around it name other acts: -ostomy and -stomy make an opening, -desis is a surgical binding and -tripsy is a crushing, as in the treatment of a stone.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.530(d), (f), (g) and (h), Administrative requirements
preguntas.subtema: No retaliation · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33
preguntas.pregunta: A patient files a privacy complaint against a clinic. What does HIPAA say about how the clinic may respond?
opciones: It may not intimidate or retaliate against the patient for filing the complaint
It may decline further treatment, since the relationship of trust has been broken
It may require the patient to waive the complaint as a condition of care
It may share the complaint with other providers so they are warned
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.530(g) forbids a covered entity from intimidating, threatening, coercing, discriminating against or retaliating against any individual for exercising a right under the rule or taking part in any of its processes, including filing a complaint, and 164.530(h) forbids requiring individuals to waive their rights as a condition of treatment, payment, enrollment or benefits. The entity must have its own complaint process, document complaints and their disposition, and mitigate any harm from a violation. Sharing the complaint with other providers would itself be an unpermitted disclosure.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Conflict Management", Issues of Concern: Conflict Management Styles
preguntas.subtema: Conflict management · CCMA 6J k209 · CMAA 2B k26
preguntas.pregunta: Why should a compromise not be counted as collaboration?
opciones: In a compromise no party fully reaches its own goals
In a compromise only one of the parties gives way
In a compromise the issue is postponed, not settled
In a compromise the more assertive party gets its way
preguntas.explicacion: Compromising is moderate on both axes: something is conceded by each side to reach a middle ground that is expedient, and since nobody gets everything wanted it should not be mistaken for collaboration, which works out an integrative solution meeting the substantive needs of all sides. One side yielding is accommodating, and postponement is avoiding.

preguntas.fuente: NAIC, Coordination of Benefits Model Regulation (Model 120), Order of Benefit Determination Rules
preguntas.subtema: Insurance rules · CMAA 5B k75 · CCMA 5E k182
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has coverage as an employee under her own plan and as a dependent under her husband's plan. Which plan pays first for her care?
opciones: Her own plan, since coverage other than as a dependent comes first
Her husband's plan, since coverage as a dependent comes first
The plan whose subscriber has the earlier birthday in the year
The plan that has covered her for the longer period of time
preguntas.explicacion: First in the order of benefit determination comes the non-dependent or dependent rule. Whichever plan covers the person as a retiree, an employee, a member, a subscriber or a policyholder pays first; the plan covering that same person as a dependent pays second. The birthday rule is for a dependent child, and length of coverage is reached only when the earlier rules leave the order unsettled.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Health Care Payment and Remittance Advice (835/ERA)
preguntas.subtema: Electronic remittance advice · CMAA 5 k79, 6B · CCMA 5K k182
preguntas.pregunta: What advantage does an electronic remittance advice have over the standard paper remittance?
opciones: Payments and adjustments can be posted automatically to the billing system
Payments arrive sooner because the money travels with the remittance file
Denied claims are automatically resubmitted to the payer for a second review
The patient's share is waived on claims the payer reports on an electronic file
preguntas.explicacion: The amount payable for each line or claim, and each adjustment applied to it, can be posted automatically from an electronic remittance into accounting or billing software, which removes the manual keying a paper remittance demands; electronic files also carry more detail. The money itself travels separately as an electronic funds transfer, denials still have to be worked, and nothing waives the patient's share.

preguntas.subtema: Backup before a move · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: The server holding the record system is about to be carried to a new suite. Which physical safeguard specification speaks to that move?
opciones: Data backup and storage: a copy that can be retrieved exactly is made before the move
Contingency operations: facility access is arranged so that lost data can be restored
Disaster recovery plan: the written procedures that restore data once it has been lost
Emergency mode operation: the critical processes keep running while systems are down
preguntas.explicacion: Three of these belong to the contingency family and answer what happens after an emergency. The one written for a planned movement of equipment is data backup and storage, an addressable specification of device and media controls: copy the information first, so that a mishap in transit does not take the only version with it.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Administrative Simplification: Transactions; and CMS, Administrative Simplification: Code Sets Overview
preguntas.subtema: Claim submission · CMA III.G.3.b(1) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6C k87 · CCMA 5L k185
preguntas.pregunta: An organization wants to test a proposed change to one of the standard transactions. What does it need first?
opciones: An exception granted by the Secretary for that test
A waiver granted by its Medicare contractor for it
A license from the committee that owns the format
A complaint filed through the enforcement tool first
preguntas.explicacion: An organization may ask the Secretary to be excepted from using a standard transaction so that it can test a modification it proposes for that standard, and CMS publishes the principles for requesting one. The enforcement and testing tool is where violations are reported, which is a different route with a different purpose.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Billing: CMS-1500 & 837P (MLN006976)
preguntas.subtema: Claim submission · CMAA 6C k87, 6 k85 · CCMA 5L k185 · CMA III.G.3.b(1) · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: Which form is the standard paper claim that a physician office sends for professional services?
opciones: The CMS-1500, designed and maintained by the National Uniform Claim Committee
The CMS-1500, which the American Medical Association designs and maintains
The CMS-R-131, used when the office expects Medicare to deny the service
The CMS-1490S, used by a patient who has to file the claim personally
preguntas.explicacion: CMS-1500 is the paper claim that non-institutional providers and suppliers send to Medicare administrative contractors, and to many other payers besides; the National Uniform Claim Committee designs and maintains it. What the American Medical Association maintains is the CPT code set. CMS-R-131 is the advance beneficiary notice, and CMS-1490S is the request a patient files to be paid back directly.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), Routine Notice Prohibition
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMA III.G.3.c (2027 III.G.3.c) · CMAA 5 k77 · CCMA 5 k186
preguntas.pregunta: A practice wants to hand every Medicare patient an advance written notice of non-coverage as a matter of routine. When is that permitted?
opciones: For experimental care, frequency limits, certain supplier cases and always-denied items
Whenever the office suspects the claim may come back denied over a coding error
Whenever the patient asks for an estimate before agreeing to go ahead with care
Under no circumstances, since a routine notice is forbidden without exception
preguntas.explicacion: There is no reason to hand the notice out routinely, and there are four exceptions: items and services that are experimental; services carrying frequency limits set by statute, by regulation or by a national or local coverage determination; equipment or supplies refused because the supplier lacked a supplier number or made an unsolicited call; and care that is always denied as not medically necessary.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse: Prevent, Detect, Report (MLN4649244)
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · CMA III.G.1.a(2), III.G.2 · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: A provider bills visits at a higher level of complexity than the record supports. What is that?
opciones: Upcoding, an example of fraud when it is done knowingly
Unbundling, an example of fraud when it is done knowingly
A medically unlikely edit, which the contractor applies to the claim
A contractual adjustment, which the office posts after payment
preguntas.explicacion: Knowingly billing for a level of service higher than what was provided or documented in the medical record is upcoding, and it is listed among the examples of Medicare fraud; misusing codes that way also appears as an example of abuse, since the line depends on intent. Unbundling splits one service into parts, an edit is a payment control, and an adjustment is a bookkeeping entry.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow, Conducting telehealth visits
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth troubleshooting plan · CMAA 4H k62 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Before a patient's first video visit, what does the workflow guidance have the office tell her about technical trouble?
opciones: How to deal with problems, and what happens if they carry on, such as moving to audio only
How to deal with problems, and that the visit is canceled if they carry on past the start time
To ring the vendor's help line, which handles the problems the practice cannot resolve
How to deal with problems, and that a failed connection is logged as a missed appointment
preguntas.explicacion: On the list of things done before the visit, the office makes sure the patient knows what to do about technical problems and what happens should they persist, dropping to audio only for instance. The same list carries the reminder, guidance on the technology, the forms, a staff walk-through of audio, camera and lighting, consent, and finding somewhere quiet and private.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Skilled nursing facility (SNF) care: Description; and Description
preguntas.subtema: Skilled vs custodial care · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: How does Medicare describe skilled care, as opposed to custodial care?
opciones: Nursing and therapy that only professionals or technical personnel can safely perform
Help with dressing, bathing and using the bathroom given by a trained personal aide
Housing and meals with staff on hand around the clock for residents who live there
Comfort measures for a terminal illness, arranged and supervised by a hospice team
