preguntas.explicacion: Skilled care is nursing and therapy that can only be delivered safely and effectively by professional or technical staff, or under their supervision. It is given where the patient needs skilled nursing, or skilled therapy, in order to treat a condition, to manage it, to observe it and to evaluate the care. Custodial long-term care, by contrast, is mostly help with the basic personal tasks of everyday life.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 482.13(c) and (d), Standards: Privacy and safety; Confidentiality of patient records
preguntas.subtema: Access to hospital records · CPT D1 k13 k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA I.C.1.e · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32
preguntas.pregunta: Under 42 CFR 482.13(d), how may a hospital patient request access to their own medical records?
opciones: By oral or written request, in the format requested if readily producible
Only by written request notarized and signed by the attending physician
Only through an attorney, since records are hospital property
Only after discharge, once the record has been completed and coded
preguntas.explicacion: The confidentiality standard gives the patient access to their medical records, the current ones included. The request may be spoken or written; the record arrives in whichever form and format was asked for when that is readily producible, electronic included, and otherwise as readable hard copy or in some agreed format, within a reasonable time. The hospital may not frustrate legitimate efforts to obtain records, and it has to answer as fast as its record system allows. The same standard protects the confidentiality of clinical records and, separately, the right to personal privacy and to care in a safe setting.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Other Issues
preguntas.subtema: De-escalation · CCMA 6I k208 · CMA F.1.f / 2027 F.1.f · CMAA 2B k26
preguntas.pregunta: Which position is recommended while verbally de-escalating an agitated patient?
opciones: A moderate distance, at a right angle, exits in view
A close seat directly facing them, with steady eye contact
A closed posture with folded arms, standing over them
A spot between the patient and the door of the room
preguntas.explicacion: Verbal de-escalation overlaps with therapeutic technique but balances staff safety against patient comfort: hold a moderate distance while not appearing guarded, keep body language and tone calm and open, stand at a right angle with the exits in mind, and leave the person free to walk out easily.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Billing: CMS-1500 & 837P (MLN006976), ASCA Exceptions
preguntas.subtema: CMS billing requirements · CMAA 6 k85, 6C k87 · CCMA 5J k180
preguntas.pregunta: A small practice wants to keep sending paper claims to Medicare. When is that allowed?
opciones: When it meets an exception under the Administrative Simplification Compliance Act
When it prefers paper, since the choice of format is left to each practice
When the claim is for a patient who also has a commercial secondary payer
When the practice has fewer than 50 full-time equivalent employees billing
preguntas.explicacion: Initial Medicare claims go electronically unless the biller qualifies for a waiver or for an exception under the Administrative Simplification Compliance Act, which lists them. They include practices with fewer than 10 full-time equivalent employees, roster billing by mass immunizers, demonstration projects, and certain secondary payer claims carrying more than one primary payer and more than one allowed amount. Preference is not a ground, and the employee threshold is 10, not 50.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, When can I sign up for Medicare?, Special Enrollment Period
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient signs up for Part B during the eight-month window that opened when she retired. When does that coverage begin?
opciones: The month after her completed forms reach Social Security
The same month her completed forms reach Social Security
The first day of the calendar quarter that follows them
Three months after the forms are signed and posted off
preguntas.explicacion: The special enrollment period for Part B runs for eight months from the day the patient or the spouse stops working, or from the end of the job-based coverage, whichever of the two lands first. Coverage starts in the month that follows the arrival of her completed forms at Social Security or at the Railroad Retirement Board, and an extra form proving the job-based coverage goes in with them.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: negligence (Legal Duty of Care)
preguntas.subtema: Negligence · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a(1) · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3A k31
preguntas.pregunta: Where does the duty of care in a clinic come from?
opciones: From the relationship itself, as between a doctor and a patient
From the written service agreement the patient signs at check-in
From the facility's accreditation by an outside review organization
From the professional license the state issues to the practitioner
preguntas.explicacion: Duty is the first element of negligence, and some relationships create it by themselves. The list runs from a shop and its customer, or an inn and its guest, to a landowner and a lessee and, of course, a doctor and a patient. It can also arise from creating the risk, from knowing that one's conduct will harm the person, or from voluntarily undertaking to protect them.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals 1.4: Health Care Settings (Primary Care)
preguntas.subtema: Levels of care · CCMA 1A k7 · CMAA 1 k1 · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: Immunizations, health screening and wellness teaching in a clinic belong to which level of health care?
opciones: Primary care, the level that promotes wellness and works to prevent disease
Secondary care, the level reached once a person has an illness or an injury
Tertiary care, the level that treats the long-term effects of a chronic condition
Palliative care, the level that treats the discomfort of a serious illness
preguntas.explicacion: Health care runs on several levels. At the primary level the work is promoting wellness and preventing disease: protection such as immunizations, education, screening done early, and attention to the environment; physician offices, public health clinics and school nursing are typical settings. Secondary care starts once someone has contracted an illness or injury, and tertiary care aims at restoring function after chronic disease.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266)
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMA III.G.3.c (2027 III.G.3.c) · CMAA 5 k77 · CCMA 5 k186
preguntas.pregunta: The list of items expected to be denied will not fit on the advance written notice. What does the guidance allow the office to do?
opciones: Attach a sheet matching each item to a cost estimate and the reason for denial
Run the notice on to a second page, since the format may be extended as needed
Issue one notice for each item, each of them signed by the patient in its turn
Note the extra items in the record, since the patient has already been told of them
preguntas.explicacion: The notice cannot exceed one page. Attachments listing further items and services are permitted, and they have to match those items clearly to cost estimates and to the reason a denial is expected. The notice is also to be issued on the approved standardized format with every required blank completed, explained in full, and signed and dated after an option is chosen.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Yearly "Wellness" visits: How often; and Costs
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4C preventive medicine · CMAA 2H · CMA I.A.5 · 2027 I.A.5
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with Medicare asks how often the yearly "Wellness" visit is covered. What is the answer?
opciones: Once every 12 months, at no cost when the provider accepts assignment
Once every 12 months, with the Part B deductible applied each time
Once every 6 months, at no cost when the provider accepts assignment
Once every 24 months, at no cost when the provider accepts assignment
preguntas.explicacion: Part B covers the visit once every 12 months and the patient pays nothing where assignment is accepted by the provider; the Part B deductible does not apply. Costs can still appear if extra tests or services outside the preventive benefit are done during the same appointment.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Inappropriate Medical Abbreviations", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k10 · CMAA 1 k7
preguntas.pregunta: What are health care institutions expected to maintain so that abbreviation use stays under control?
opciones: An approved list, a banned list and an audit process to check compliance
An approved list only, since a banned list duplicates the national one
A banned list only, because the approved ones are assumed safe
A yearly staff survey, since written policies have little practical effect
preguntas.explicacion: Each organization has to develop its own list of approved and not approved abbreviations, make sure nothing appears on both, and put a system or audit process in place to confirm that staff comply. Committees that oversee this usually include a physician, a nurse, a pharmacist and risk management staff.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, "Talking With Your Older Patients", Families and caregivers as part of the health care team
preguntas.subtema: Caregivers · CCMA 6C k195 · CMAA 2A k13 · RMA I.D.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: An older patient arrives at the visit with an adult daughter. What is settled first?
opciones: How the patient sees the companion's role in the visit
How the daughter would summarize the medical history
Whether the daughter can sign the visit paperwork
Whether the patient will step out for a private word
preguntas.explicacion: To protect and honor privacy, ask the patient how they see the companion's role before going on. Sit so both can be addressed face to face and do not aim the remarks only at the companion. Asking the companion to step out comes later, for sensitive topics or a check of the patient's cognition.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Health Topic: Patient Rights, What is informed consent?; 42 CFR 482.13(b)(2)
preguntas.subtema: Withdrawing consent · CPT D1 k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA II.E.3.a · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7 · CMAA 3D k40
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who signed a consent form for a procedure says she has changed her mind. What does patient-rights guidance say?
opciones: She may change her mind about consent at any time
She is bound by the signed form until the procedure is done
She may withdraw only if a second physician agrees
She may withdraw only in writing, with 24 hours' notice
preguntas.explicacion: Informed consent is a process in which the provider gives the information needed to decide, including the risks and benefits of the care and details of the condition, and the patient must understand it before consenting; a signature on a form is written consent, but the patient has the right to change her mind at any time. The CMS condition frames the same idea as the right to make informed decisions and to request or refuse treatment. No second opinion, notice period or written withdrawal is required to revoke consent.

preguntas.subtema: Evaluation standard · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: The practice has just merged with another and doubled its staff. Which Security Rule standard is triggered by a change of that kind?
opciones: Evaluation, a periodic technical and non-technical check of the safeguards in place
Assigned security responsibility, which names the official who runs the policies
Isolating clearinghouse functions, which walls off part of a larger organization
Response and reporting, which identifies and documents any security incidents
preguntas.explicacion: Evaluation calls for a periodic review, technical and non-technical, showing how far the policies and procedures still meet the rule's requirements. The baseline is the standards as first implemented, and the review is repeated whenever changes in the environment or in operations bear on the security of the information, which is exactly what a merger is.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Filing an appeal; and CMS, Health Care Payment and Remittance Advice (835/ERA)
preguntas.subtema: Denials and appeals · CMA III.G.5.b (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6E · CCMA 5M
preguntas.pregunta: A patient in a Medicare Advantage plan asks the office where the rules for appealing her plan's decision are written down.
opciones: In her own plan materials, since the plan must tell her in writing how to appeal
In the Medicare Summary Notice, which carries the appeal rules for every plan
In the remittance advice the plan sends the office once it processes the claim
In the plan's drug formulary, which carries the appeal rules for every benefit
preguntas.explicacion: Appeal rights depend on the kind of coverage. For a Medicare Advantage plan, another health plan or a drug plan, the details are in the plan's own materials, and the plan is obliged to put in writing how to appeal; its contact information is usually on the membership card. The Medicare Summary Notice goes to people in Original Medicare, and a remittance advice is sent to the provider, not to the patient.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN: NPI - What You Need to Know
preguntas.subtema: National Provider Identifier · CCMA 5 k183 · CMA III.H.2 · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 6 k89 · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: What is the National Provider Identifier assigned to a clinician?
opciones: A ten-digit number carrying no information about the provider
A nine-digit number that encodes the State where the provider practices
A ten-digit number that changes whenever the provider moves or is renamed
A number issued by each health plan for use in its own claims only
preguntas.explicacion: The NPI is a ten-digit numeric identifier that carries no information about the provider, not the State of practice, not the provider type, not the specialization, and it stays the same when name, address or taxonomy change. The registry that assigns it is NPPES. In HIPAA standard transactions it takes the place of older provider identifiers.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting started with telehealth, Finding a telehealth vendor
preguntas.subtema: Platform capacity · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A clinician wants to bring a specialist into some of her video visits. Which question about the platform settles whether that is possible?
opciones: Whether it allows more than two participants in one telehealth session
Whether it supports visits taken on demand rather than booked in advance
Whether it limits the number of individuals who may use the technology
Whether it integrates with the electronic health record the practice keeps
preguntas.explicacion: Among the questions put to a prospective vendor are whether the product supports on-demand visits, what it costs and whether the charge is per visit or a single one, whether there is a cap on the number of individuals who may use it, and whether it allows more than two participants in a session, for instance when a specialty consult is to be brought in.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Innovation Center: Value-Based Care (treating the patient as a whole person)
preguntas.subtema: Barriers to care and community resources · CCMA 4D k166 · CMAA 2H k30
preguntas.pregunta: In value-based care, why does the team ask about transportation, food and living conditions?
opciones: Because those nonmedical factors bear directly on the person's well-being
Because the plan needs them to set the premium the person will be charged
Because the state requires them before Medicaid eligibility can be decided
Because the coding rules require them on every claim the office sends out
preguntas.explicacion: Value-based care teams spend time working out what might stand between a person and her care. Patients may be asked about nonmedical factors that bear directly on well-being: whether transport is reliable and food is healthy, what family relationships are like, what the general living conditions are, and what health goals she has for herself. Providers then connect her to local social services and programs.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: The note records only appendicitis, with nothing about acute or chronic. Which code does the coder assign?
opciones: The default code, the one listed beside that main term in the Alphabetic Index
The other specified code, the one the Index marks with the abbreviation NEC
The acute code, because acute is the nonessential modifier under that term
No code at all, until the provider has been queried about the missing detail
preguntas.explicacion: The code sitting next to a main term in the Alphabetic Index is the default code. It stands either for the condition most commonly associated with that term or for its unspecified code, and the guidelines take appendicitis as the example: document the condition without anything further, acute or chronic for instance, and the default code is what gets assigned.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, HHS Agencies & Offices: Office of Inspector General
preguntas.subtema: Regulators the office answers to · CMAA 3A · NCMA 4.13
preguntas.pregunta: Which office inside the health department protects the integrity of its programs and the welfare of the people in them?
opciones: The Office of Inspector General, which oversees program integrity
The Office for Civil Rights, which oversees discrimination and privacy
The Departmental Appeals Board, which reviews disputed legal decisions
The Office of Global Affairs, which leads work in global health diplomacy
preguntas.explicacion: The Office of Inspector General protects the integrity of the department's programs and the health and welfare of the people taking part in them. The Office for Civil Rights is the one making sure people receiving services face no discrimination and can trust that their health information stays private and secure. The Departmental Appeals Board reviews disputed legal decisions.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guides
preguntas.subtema: SAFER guide structure · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: How is the 2025 set of guides on the safe use of record systems arranged, and where should an organization begin?
opciones: Eight guides in three groups, starting with the two foundational ones
Eight guides in two groups, starting with the one on contingency planning
Three guides in eight sections, starting with the section on patient safety
Eight guides in three groups, starting with the group on clinical processes
preguntas.explicacion: The set holds eight guides sorted into foundational, infrastructure and clinical process groups, and most organizations are told to start with the foundational pair and then go where their own concerns are. The high priority guide gathers sixteen recommendations pulled from the other seven.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.4 Handoff Reports
preguntas.subtema: Transitions of care · CCMA 4H k167 · CMAA 2F
preguntas.pregunta: A bedside handoff is about to start in a room where a visitor is sitting. What has to be kept in mind?
opciones: The privacy rules apply while the report is being given
Family may take part only if named as the health care agent
The report has to move out to the hallway before it starts
The report has to be written down rather than spoken aloud
preguntas.explicacion: Bedside reports are given face to face at the bedside, with the patient there and both the off-going and the oncoming staff. Privacy rules have to be kept in mind when visitors are present or the room is not private, and family may be brought in if the patient permits it, which is not the same as holding a formal appointment.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Malpractice", Issues of Concern: Documentation
preguntas.subtema: Defensible documentation · CCMA k219, k221 · NCMA 4.5 · CMAA 3A k31
preguntas.pregunta: A clinician remembers an important detail three days after the visit. How should it go into the record?
opciones: As a late entry, stating when it was recalled and when it was entered
As an edit to the original note, so the chart reads as one account
As a note in the incident report, which is filed outside the record
As an addendum signed by a witness, since the visit is already closed
preguntas.explicacion: A medical record is never changed after the fact, least of all after an adverse event. When something pertinent comes to mind later, it is entered as a late entry that states plainly when it was remembered and when it was written down. Charts should be completed on time anyway: every record system logs when the note was finished, and a late one is easy to attack.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 3, Guidelines for Using a Medical Interpreter
preguntas.subtema: Interpreters · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17
preguntas.pregunta: What should be arranged before an interview that will use an interpreter?
opciones: Extra time, and a meeting with the interpreter for background
A relative on hand in case the interpreter loses the line
A written translation of each question that will be asked
A shorter appointment so the patient is not left overtired
preguntas.explicacion: Two of the guidelines are preparatory: allow extra time for the conversation, and whenever possible meet the interpreter beforehand to give background. Asking a family member to interpret is what the same section warns against, since relatives may edit or change what is said and the patient may hold information back.

preguntas.fuente: AAMA, Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Standards for CMAs (AAMA), Principle 5; and Self-Reporting
preguntas.subtema: Unethical conduct · CCMA 7C · CMA E.7 / 2027 E.6 · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: A certified assistant is arrested for a drug offense outside work. What does the AAMA Code of Conduct require of her?
opciones: To notify the association within a reasonable period of the violation
To notify the association only once a court has entered a conviction
To notify her employer, who then decides whether the board is told
To surrender the credential immediately and reapply after the case
preguntas.explicacion: One principle requires a certificant to notify the association, inside a reasonable period, about anything capable of affecting their ability to meet the certification requirements, a violation of local, state or federal law included. Self-reporting is immediate when something calls the person's fitness to practice into question, and failing to self-report is itself grounds for discipline.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule, Required and Addressable Implementation Specifications
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics · CMAA 3B k38 safeguards · CCMA 7A k214
preguntas.pregunta: A small practice concludes that one of the Security Rule's addressable implementation specifications is not reasonable at its size. What may it do?
opciones: Adopt an alternative measure that meets the standard's purpose, and document why it did so
Skip the specification entirely, because addressable means the same thing as optional here
Adopt the specification anyway, because only the standards themselves may be substituted
Ask HHS for a written waiver before it relies on any alternative security measure at all
preguntas.explicacion: Every Security Rule standard must be met. Inside them, required specifications have to be implemented as written, while addressable ones let a regulated entity judge whether they are reasonable and appropriate for its size, resources and risks. Where one is not, the entity adopts an alternative that achieves the same purpose and documents the reasoning. Addressable never means optional.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information: Organizational Options
preguntas.subtema: Joint notice · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Several practices in an organized health care arrangement produce one joint notice. What happens when a patient is given that notice by one of them?
opciones: The distribution duty is met for every covered entity the joint notice applies to
The distribution duty is met only for the entity whose staff handed the notice over
The distribution duty is met for the visit in hand, and starts again at the next site
The distribution duty is met once the patient signs an acknowledgment at each site
preguntas.explicacion: Where entities take part in an organized health care arrangement they may issue one joint notice, provided certain conditions are met, among them that the notice say which entities and which service delivery sites it applies to. Once any one participant gives that notice to an individual, the distribution requirement is satisfied for all of them as regards that individual.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A discharge summary lists CVA in the problem list. Which event does that abbreviation record?
opciones: A cerebrovascular accident, that is, a stroke
A cardiovascular arrest, that is, a heart attack
A central venous access, that is, a line placement
A chronic valvular anomaly, that is, a valve defect
preguntas.explicacion: CVA stands for cerebrovascular accident, the event patients call a stroke or a brain attack. A smaller, temporary version is a TIA, a transient ischemic attack. A heart attack is written MI or AMI, for myocardial infarction, and the two are worth keeping apart because the treatments differ.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Nonverbal Communication
preguntas.subtema: Nonverbal cues · CCMA 6C k197 · CMAA 2C k14 · CMA F.1.d / 2027 F.1.e · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant pulls up a chair to talk with a patient who has just been given a new diagnosis. What does the SOLER mnemonic call for?
opciones: Sit with an open posture, lean in, hold eye contact and stay relaxed
Stand at eye level with the arms folded and keep the pace brisk
Stay four to ten feet away, on your feet, with the chart in hand
Sit within the patient's view and raise the voice to hold attention
preguntas.explicacion: SOLER is the mnemonic used for nonverbal communication: sitting with open posture, leaning in, good eye contact, done in a relaxed manner. Bringing a chair to the bedside helps, because initial or sensitive exchanges land better when both people are at eye level. Folded arms are listed among negative body language.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases, chapter 5: Unpacking Deliveries
preguntas.subtema: Delivery discrepancies · CCMA 5T · RMA II.B.5.a · CMAA 7D k99 · NCMA 4.13
preguntas.pregunta: The contents of a vaccine delivery do not match the packing list and a temperature excursion is suspected. What happens to those doses?
opciones: They are labeled not for use, kept apart in the storage unit, and the maker is called
They are put into stock and used first, so that no dose is wasted before it expires
They are returned to the carrier at once, since the office never took delivery of them
They are discarded on the spot and the loss is recorded in the inventory account
preguntas.explicacion: A discrepancy or a suspected excursion is reported to the manufacturer immediately. Meanwhile the doses are marked so nobody uses them, and they stay in the proper storage unit but separated from the rest until somebody decides whether they are still viable. Publicly funded stock also means a call to the state or local immunization program.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Coding Productivity
preguntas.subtema: Coding applications · CMA III.G.1 (2027 III.G.1) · CMAA 6A · CCMA 5I
preguntas.pregunta: A coding supervisor is told the target productivity rate is above ninety-five percent. What does that mean day to day?
opciones: Under five percent of the coding load should be waiting in a queue at any moment
Under five percent of the codes assigned should prove to be wrong when audited
Over ninety-five percent of claims should be paid on the first submission sent
Over ninety-five percent of charges should reach billing within two days of care
preguntas.explicacion: Coding productivity is measured against a target above ninety-five percent, which is spelled out as less than five percent of the coding load stuck in a queue at any time. Adding coders is the obvious move and may do nothing if the real cause is a faulty process or the software. Coding accuracy is a separate indicator, also above ninety-five percent and higher still for diagnosis related groups, and it is judged on audit.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: An order for a pain medication is marked PRN. What does that tell the person giving it?
opciones: It is given as needed rather than on a fixed schedule
It is given four times a day on a fixed schedule
It is given once at bedtime on a fixed schedule
It is given only by the intravenous route as ordered
preguntas.explicacion: PRN on a prescription means as needed, so the dose is tied to the patient's symptoms instead of the clock. The scheduled frequencies have their own abbreviations, such as BID, TID and QID. A route is written separately, and IV stands for intravenous while IM stands for intramuscular.

preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics · CPT D5 5H k94 distributing results · CCMA 7E k220 · NCMA 4.4 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks the laboratory for a copy of his own completed test report. How long does the Privacy Rule give the laboratory to act on that request?
opciones: No later than 30 days after receiving it, extendable once by no more than 30 days
No later than 60 days after receiving it, extendable once by no more than 30 days
No later than 30 days after receiving it, with no extension available in any case
No later than 10 days after receiving it, extendable once by no more than 20 days
preguntas.explicacion: The access clock runs 30 days from receipt of the request, and a covered entity that cannot meet it may take one extension of no more than 30 further days. CLIA was amended to match: a laboratory may give patients and their personal representatives access to completed reports it can authenticate as theirs. The 60-day figure is the breach notification deadline.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) General Information
preguntas.subtema: Procedural coding · CMA III.G.1.c (2027 III.G.1.c) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: How is a HCPCS Level II code built, and who decides on additions and deletions to it?
opciones: One letter followed by four numeric digits, with CMS maintaining the set
Five numeric digits, with the American Medical Association maintaining the set
One letter followed by six numeric digits, with the NUCC maintaining the set
Three to seven characters, with the National Center for Health Statistics in charge
preguntas.explicacion: Level II codes are alphanumeric: a single alphabetical letter followed by four numeric digits, and CMS maintains them, including additions, revisions and deletions. Level I is CPT, a numeric system of five digits kept by the American Medical Association. The three-to-seven-character structure belongs to ICD-10-CM instead.

preguntas.subtema: Integrity standard · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which risk does the integrity standard of the Security Rule address?
opciones: Information being altered or destroyed when nobody was authorized to do so
Information being unavailable to a clinician who has the right to consult it
Information being seen by a member of staff whose role does not need it
Information being sent to the wrong recipient by a mistake at the keyboard
preguntas.explicacion: Integrity is defined as the property of data not having been altered or destroyed by anyone without authorization, and the standard calls for policies protecting against exactly that. Its addressable specification is an electronic mechanism corroborating that the information is still as it was. Availability and confidentiality are the other two objectives, not this one.

preguntas.fuente: USPS, Compare Mail Services: Media Mail
preguntas.subtema: Media Mail eligibility · CCMA 5O · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7G k96 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: An office wants to post a set of training videos on memory sticks at the cheapest media rate. What does the Postal Service say about that?
opciones: Digital drives do not qualify, and disallowed contents mean a higher rate is charged
Digital drives do not qualify, and the parcel is returned to the sender unopened
Digital drives qualify where the content is educational and the parcel is under 70 lb
Digital drives qualify, and only computer games are excluded from the media rate
preguntas.explicacion: The media rate is a cheap route for books, media and educational material that qualify, but only certain kinds of media are allowed: video games are named as not qualifying, and so are computer drives and digital drives. Enclosing something that is not allowed means the sender or the recipient pays the higher postage, and these parcels may be opened and inspected.

preguntas.fuente: ISMP, List of Error-Prone Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations (2024), Doses/Measurement Units
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k10 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k8 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: Why does the Do Not Use list ban IU for international unit?
opciones: It is misread as IV or as the number 10, so unit is written out
It is misread as mL or as the number 15, so unit is written out
It is misread as IM or as the number 11, so unit is written out
It is misread as ID or as the number 12, so unit is written out
preguntas.explicacion: IU sits on the list because it gets taken either for IV, an intravenous order, or for the number 10, and either misreading changes the order completely. Write unit or units instead: an international unit can simply be called a unit. The same reasoning bans the plain U.

preguntas.fuente: ISMP, List of Error-Prone Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations (2024), Doses/Measurement Units
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k10 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k8 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: An order is handwritten as 4U of insulin. Why is that on the Do Not Use list, and what should be written?
opciones: The U can read as a zero or a four, so the word unit is spelled out
The U can read as an IV order, so the word unit is spelled out
The U can read as a liter, so the abbreviation mL is used instead
The U can read as a nanogram, so the word microgram is spelled out
preguntas.explicacion: Written by hand, the U for units is mistaken for a zero or for the number four, so 4U can be read as 40 and 4u as 44, a tenfold overdose or worse. The fix is to spell out the word unit. Reading it as an intravenous order is the hazard of IU, and the liter confusion belongs to the lowercase letter l.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, Interoperability: TEFCA
preguntas.subtema: Interoperability · CCMA 5 k179 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.c · CMAA 7 k97 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: What does TEFCA establish, according to ONC?
opciones: A nationwide floor of governance, policy and technical rules for interoperability
A federal registry listing every patient treated in the United States by name
A certification that every medical office must earn before buying an EHR system
A payment program that reimburses practices for each record they send elsewhere
preguntas.explicacion: TEFCA lays a nationwide floor of governance, policy and technical rules for interoperability, cuts down the connections an organization needs in order to exchange information securely, and gives individuals a way of gathering their own health information. ONC also runs a voluntary certification program for health IT and obliges certified products to adopt the USCDI data set.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Personal Representatives: Parents and Unemancipated Minors
preguntas.subtema: Minors and representatives · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.3.c · RMA I.C.1.a · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: A physician asks a parent whether he may speak with her sixteen-year-old confidentially, and the parent agrees. What follows under the Privacy Rule?
opciones: The parent stops being the personal representative for that care
The parent keeps full access, since minors have no separate privacy rights
The minor becomes emancipated for every purpose the rule recognizes
The physician must document the conversation on the accounting of disclosures
preguntas.explicacion: A parent is normally a minor child's personal representative, since it is normally the parent who holds the authority to decide about health care. The rule sets out three exceptions: where State law does not require parental consent for the service and the minor gives it; where somebody else is authorized by law to consent and does so; and where the parent assents to a confidential arrangement between the provider and the minor, which is exactly the conversation described.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Incidental Uses and Disclosures: Minimum Necessary
preguntas.subtema: Role-based access · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 3B k38 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Scheduling staff can open any chart in the system, including those of patients they never book. Why is that a minimum necessary problem?
opciones: Access has to be limited by role to the information each person needs to do the job
Access has to be logged in an accounting of disclosures given to the patient every six years
Access has to be reviewed case by case before any employee opens a record for any purpose
Access has to be approved in advance by each patient through a signed authorization form
preguntas.explicacion: Covered entities must adopt policies identifying who in the workforce needs PHI, which categories they need and under what conditions. Routine access does not require case-by-case review, but unimpeded access by someone whose job does not call for it means the standard is not being applied, and any incidental disclosure that follows, such as a conversation overheard, becomes an unlawful one.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.4 Transfer Reports
preguntas.subtema: Transitions of care · CCMA 4H k167 · CMAA 2F
preguntas.pregunta: What sets a transfer report apart from a bedside handoff report?
opciones: It goes into even more detail when another agency receives the patient
It leaves out assessment findings, since the receiving unit repeats them
It is given by the provider alone and never by the nursing staff
It takes the place of the checklist the agency supplies for the exchange
preguntas.explicacion: Transfer reports are given when a patient moves to another unit or to another agency. They carry information similar to a bedside handoff but are even more detailed when the receiving side is a different agency, and agencies often supply checklists so nothing is left out rather than to replace the report.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), Patient Refuses to Sign
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMAA 5 k77 · CCMA 5 k186
preguntas.pregunta: A patient will neither choose an option nor sign a properly issued advance written notice of non-coverage. What should the staff do?
opciones: Note the refusal on the original copy and keep it, and consider withholding the service
Sign the notice for the patient and enter the reason for the refusal in the record
Provide the service and bill the patient anyway, since the notice was properly issued
Reissue the notice after the service, dated the day the care was actually delivered
preguntas.explicacion: If the patient or the representative refuses to pick an option or to sign, the notifier annotates the original copy to record the refusal, may list witnesses although that is optional, and should consider not furnishing the item or service unless health, safety or civil liability make that impossible. Staff never sign for the patient, and a notice cannot be backdated to shift liability for care already given.

preguntas.subtema: Timing of advance directive information · CCMA 5D · CMA I.A.5 · RMA I.C.1.f · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: At what moment must a rural emergency hospital hand a patient the written information on advance directives?
opciones: When the patient is registered as a patient of the hospital
When the patient is admitted to the hospital as an inpatient
When the patient is first seen by the treating practitioner
When the patient is discharged, along with the follow-up plan
preguntas.explicacion: Each kind of provider has its own moment. A hospital gives the information at admission as an inpatient and a skilled nursing facility at admission as a resident; a home health agency does it before the patient comes under its care, at the latest on the first home visit and before care; a hospice at the first receipt of care; a rural emergency hospital at registration.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(2)(i) and (f)(2)(ii), Hepatitis B Vaccination
preguntas.subtema: Hepatitis B vaccination offer · CPT D1 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: A newly hired phlebotomist begins drawing blood on Monday. By when must the employer make the hepatitis B vaccine available to her?
opciones: Within 10 working days of the initial assignment, after the required training
Within 15 days of the initial assignment, the deadline for the written opinion
Within 30 days of the initial assignment, before the first annual training
Only after a prescreening antibody test shows the employee is not immune
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(2)(i) sets the clock: the vaccine and the series are offered within 10 working days of the initial assignment to a job with occupational exposure, and only after the employee has had the training on the vaccine described in (g)(2)(vii)(I). The offer is not owed if the employee already completed the series, has antibody testing showing immunity, or has a medical contraindication. Fifteen days is the deadline for the written opinion in (f)(5), and (f)(2)(ii) forbids making a prescreening program a condition of getting the vaccine.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Telehealth Systems, Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth scheduling · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient booked for a video visit says she will be staying with family in another state that day. Which question does that raise for the practice?
opciones: Whether the clinician is licensed in the state she will be in
Whether her plan pays the same rate outside her home state
Whether the platform can reach a device on another network
Whether the visit still counts as a real-time appointment
preguntas.explicacion: As a rule the clinician needs a current license issued by whichever state the patient is sitting in while the encounter takes place, which is why her location on the day matters to the booking. Compacts between states, and waivers granted for a time, have opened practice across state lines in some settings, but they do not settle the question by themselves.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), Calculating Payment
preguntas.subtema: Third-party billing · CMA III.G.3.b(1) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6 k87 · CCMA 5 k185
preguntas.pregunta: What does Medicare use to work out the size of its secondary payment on a claim?
opciones: The primary payer's payment data, plus the patient's deductible and coinsurance
The provider's full charge, less the patient's deductible and coinsurance amounts
The primary payer's allowed amount by itself, without the patient's cost sharing
The provider's contracted rate with the primary payer, less the amount it paid
preguntas.explicacion: Once the primary payer has paid, Medicare takes that information and works out what it owes as secondary payer, factoring in whatever deductible and coinsurance apply to the patient. On a hard-copy claim the calculation runs off the claim data and off the remittance advice or explanation of benefits from the primary payer, which is exactly why that document has to travel with the claim.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, I-PASS
preguntas.subtema: Transitions of care · CCMA 4H k167 · CMA F.4.c / 2027 F.2.c · CMAA 2F
preguntas.pregunta: In the I-PASS handoff, what does the receiver do in the final step?
opciones: Summarize what was heard and restate the key actions
Rate illness severity as stable, watcher or unstable
List the to-do items with their timelines and owners
Describe the events leading up to the care transition
preguntas.explicacion: I-PASS runs illness severity, patient summary, action list, situation awareness with contingency planning, and synthesis by the receiver. The last piece belongs to the person taking over: they summarize what they heard, ask questions and restate the key actions and to-do items.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Minimum Necessary Requirement
preguntas.subtema: Minimum necessary · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A hospitalist telephones the office and asks for the whole chart to treat a patient admitted overnight. How does the minimum necessary standard apply?
opciones: It does not apply, because the request comes from a provider and the purpose is treatment
It applies, so the office must send only the last progress note and withhold the rest
It applies, so the office must review the request individually against non-routine criteria
It does not apply, because a telephone request is an oral disclosure rather than a written one
preguntas.explicacion: The standard obliges covered entities to limit uses, disclosures and requests to what is needed for the purpose, but the guidance lists the situations it does not reach, and the first is a disclosure to, or request by, a provider for treatment. OCR adds that it does not apply to oral disclosures among providers for treatment either. What matters is the purpose, not the medium.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Preauthorization
preguntas.subtema: Authorizations and referrals · CCMA 5H k183 · CMA III.G.5.a · RMA II.A.4 · CMAA 4G k67 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: Before scheduling an MRI, the office calls the patient's insurer to confirm that the plan considers the study medically necessary. What is this step called?
opciones: Preauthorization
Filing a claim
Getting a referral
Checking the formulary
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov defines preauthorization as the insurer's decision that a service, treatment plan, drug or item of durable medical equipment counts as medically necessary, and gives its other names: prior authorization, prior approval and precertification. A plan may demand it before certain services, except in an emergency, and obtaining it is not a promise that the plan will pay. A claim is the request for payment sent afterwards, a referral is the primary care doctor's order to see a specialist, and the formulary is the list of covered drugs.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 3, Guidelines for Using a Medical Interpreter
preguntas.subtema: Interpreters · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.1.c(3) / 2027 F.1.d(4)
preguntas.pregunta: While a telephone interpreter is on the line, where does the assistant aim the questions?
opciones: Straight at the patient, in the first person and a normal tone
At the interpreter, who then relays each one to the patient
At the interpreter first, and then repeated to the patient
At the family member, who confirms the patient understood
preguntas.explicacion: Face and address the patient directly, keep a normal tone of voice and speak in the first person; questions aimed at the interpreter turn the patient into a spectator. Allow extra time, ask one question at a time, drop idioms and slang, and have the patient repeat the instructions back.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.b) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: An order sheet lists BUN and creatinine. Which organ is the BUN result mainly used to check?
opciones: The kidney, since blood urea nitrogen detects kidney problems
The liver, since blood urea nitrogen detects liver problems
The heart, since blood urea nitrogen detects cardiac damage
The thyroid, since blood urea nitrogen detects gland problems
preguntas.explicacion: BUN stands for blood urea nitrogen and is drawn to look for kidney trouble, alongside GFR, the glomerular filtration rate. Liver disease is followed with ALT, AST and ALP; damage to heart muscle with CPK; and the thyroid with TSH, T3 and T4.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.508(b)(5), Revocation of authorizations; 164.508(b)(2), Defective authorizations
preguntas.subtema: Revoking an authorization · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.2.b · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: A patient wants to cancel an authorization she signed to release her records to her employer. How may she revoke it under HIPAA?
opciones: In writing at any time, except for actions already taken in reliance on it
Only before the covered entity has received and acted on the request
Orally at any time, and the covered entity must recall records already sent
Not until the expiration date or event stated on the form has passed
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.508(b)(5) lets an individual revoke an authorization at any time, provided the revocation is in writing; the exceptions are actions the covered entity has already taken in reliance on the authorization, and certain insurance situations where other law gives the insurer a right to contest a claim. Records already sent cannot be recalled by the revocation, but no further disclosures may be made under it. An authorization whose expiration has passed or that is known to be revoked is defective and cannot be used.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Appeals in Original Medicare
preguntas.subtema: Denials and appeals · CMAA 6E · CCMA 5M · CMA III.G.5.b / 2027 III.G.3.b
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks how far she can push back on a Medicare denial. How many levels does the appeals process have in Original Medicare?
opciones: Five levels, and a decision at one level can usually be taken to the next
Three levels, after which the decision of the contractor becomes final
Two levels, one before the contractor and one before a federal court
Five levels, but only the first two are open to the treating provider
preguntas.explicacion: There are 5 levels of appeal, and disagreeing with the decision at one level usually allows a move to the next, with each decision letter explaining how. The first is a redetermination by the Medicare administrative contractor; the last is judicial review in federal district court, which requires the case to meet a minimum dollar amount.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0, Tool: Two-Challenge Rule
preguntas.subtema: Escalation · CCMA 6K k210 · CMAA 2B k25 · NCMA EKB 22
preguntas.pregunta: When is the Two-Challenge Rule best invoked?
opciones: When the patient or a team member is at high risk of harm
Whenever a request for clarification has been made at all
Only once the supervisor and the chain of command have failed
Only when the person being challenged outranks the challenger
preguntas.explicacion: The rule is best kept for situations in which the patient, or another member of the team, may face a high risk of harm. It empowers anyone to stop the line over an essential safety breach, which is why it is not for every request for clarification, and the chain of command is where it goes next, not a condition for starting.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Implementation and Challenges
preguntas.subtema: Backlog reduction · CMAA 4A k49 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice switching to open access is warned that working down the appointments already booked is the hard part. What does that step take?
opciones: Six to eight weeks of extra work, helped by a date beyond which nothing is booked ahead
Six to eight months of extra work, which is how long the whole change is expected to take
Two or three weeks of extra work, after which the booked schedule empties by itself
No extra work at all, because demand for appointments drops the week the model starts
preguntas.explicacion: Reducing the backlog may take six to eight weeks of seeing more patients each day, and every study of practices that made the change found this the hardest part. A useful tactic is to set a target date and agree that no visit is pre-scheduled beyond it. The literature says the whole model can be in place within a few months. Demand does fall, but not on day one.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Coordination of benefits; and Medicare.gov, How Medicare works with other insurance
preguntas.subtema: Insurance rules · CMAA 5B k75 · CCMA 5E k182
preguntas.pregunta: What is coordination of benefits?
opciones: The way of deciding which of two or more plans pays a medical claim first
The way of splitting a medical claim evenly between two plans that cover it
The way a plan divides its payment between the provider and the patient
The transfer of a patient's benefits from an old plan to a new plan
preguntas.explicacion: Coordination of benefits is how payers settle which of them pays first when two or more plans answer for the same claim. The primary payer meets the cost up to the limits of its coverage and sends what remains to the secondary payer; where that second plan does not cover the remainder, the patient may end up owing it. It is an order of payment, not an even split, and not the sharing of one plan's payment with the patient.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, SOAP Notes, Introduction
preguntas.subtema: What the SOAP structure is for · CCMA 5 k174 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA k4 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A clinician says the SOAP layout does more than store the visit. Which uses does that structure serve?
opciones: It works as a checklist, as a cognitive aid, and as an index for retrieving information
It works as a signature log, tying initials in the chart to the name of their author
It works as an indexing system, retrieving records by diagnosis and by procedure
It works as a retention schedule, fixing how long each part of the record is kept
preguntas.explicacion: Larry Weed built the layout almost fifty years ago, and its four headings do more than hold the visit: they remind the clinician of specific tasks, frame the reasoning that runs from the findings to a diagnosis, and give a way back into what was written when somebody has to look something up, or learn from an old case. Signature logs, indexing by diagnosis and retention periods answer to other rules.

preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, carcinoma and sarcoma
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k5 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: Two pathology reports arrive, one headed carcinoma and the other sarcoma. What separates the two words?
opciones: Carcinoma starts in skin or lining tissue, sarcoma in bone or soft tissue
Carcinoma starts in bone or soft tissue, sarcoma in skin or lining tissue
Carcinoma starts in blood-forming tissue, sarcoma in immune system cells
Carcinoma starts in lining tissue, sarcoma in blood-forming tissue
preguntas.explicacion: These two names say where the cancer began. A carcinoma begins in the skin or in the tissues that line or cover internal organs. A sarcoma begins in bone or in soft tissue: muscle, fat, cartilage, blood vessels and the rest of the connective or supporting tissue, which is why one that forms in bone is called an osteosarcoma.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 160.404(b)(1)-(2); 45 CFR 102.3, penalty adjustment table
preguntas.subtema: Penalty cap · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3B k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: What sets the top civil money penalty for all violations of one identical HIPAA provision in a calendar year?
opciones: A statutory ceiling, whose dollar figure is republished every year adjusted for inflation
A fixed ceiling of fifty thousand dollars, which is the same in all four culpability tiers
A ceiling of twenty-five thousand dollars, carried over from the rule as it stood before HITECH
A ceiling that binds only the top tier, willful neglect that was never corrected in time
preguntas.explicacion: HITECH set four culpability tiers and one ceiling covering every violation of an identical provision inside a calendar year. The enforcement rule still prints $1,500,000 there, and $50,000 per violation, but HHS republishes both adjusted for inflation at 45 CFR 102.3, where the calendar-year cap already stands above two million. The $25,000 cap belongs to violations occurring before February 18, 2009.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Home health services: Who's eligible
preguntas.subtema: Homebound status · CCMA 4D k162 · CMAA 2H k30
preguntas.pregunta: A home health patient asks whether attending religious services will cost her the benefit. What is true?
opciones: No, absences that are short and infrequent for non-medical reasons are allowed
No, because homebound status only concerns overnight trips away from home
Yes, leaving home for any reason other than treatment ends the benefit
Yes, unless the home health agency approves each outing in the care plan
preguntas.explicacion: Homebound means leaving home is not recommended because of the condition, or takes help such as a cane, a wheelchair, a walker, crutches, special transportation or another person, and that leaving takes a lot of effort. The patient may still leave for medical treatment, and for absences that are short and infrequent and not medical in purpose, religious services for instance, and may attend adult day care.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Service Animals (2010 requirements)
preguntas.subtema: ADAAA compliance · CMAA 3A (ADAAA)
preguntas.pregunta: Which animals are recognized as service animals in a medical office open to the public?
opciones: A dog trained individually to do work or tasks for the person
Dogs and cats individually trained to do work for the person
Any animal a licensed clinician has documented as therapeutic
Any animal wearing a harness and carrying a registered identification tag
preguntas.explicacion: From March 15, 2011 titles II and III recognize only dogs as service animals, and a service animal is a dog trained individually to do work, or to perform tasks, for someone with a disability. Guiding a person who is blind, alerting one who is deaf, pulling a wheelchair and interrupting a panic attack are the examples. Miniature horses fall under a separate provision.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Assisted Living: Summary
preguntas.subtema: Specialty resources for medical needs · CCMA 4D k165 · CMAA 2H k30
preguntas.pregunta: A daughter asks about assisted living for a father who needs help dressing but no nursing care. How is assisted living described?
opciones: Housing and services for people needing some help with daily care but not nursing care
A facility where skilled nurses and aides are on hand around the clock for every resident
A residence run by a hospice where the interdisciplinary team gives short-term respite
A rural clinic that gives primary care and preventive services in a shortage area
preguntas.explicacion: Assisted living is housing plus services, for a person needing some help with the care of daily life, dressing, bathing, taking medicines, cleaning, but not the medical care a nursing home provides. Residents usually have an apartment or a room of their own and share common areas. Services may include meals, help with medicines, housekeeping, laundry, supervision, activities and transportation.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, National Correct Coding Initiative, NCCI Implementation
preguntas.subtema: Coding applications · CMA III.G.1.a(3) (2027 III.G.1.a(1)) · CMAA 6A · CCMA 5I k184
preguntas.pregunta: A claim reports many more units of one service than a patient could receive in a day. Which set of correct coding edits catches that?
opciones: The medically unlikely edits, which look at units of service
The procedure to procedure edits, which look at code pairs
The add-on code edits, which look at the base code billed
The correct coding manual, which explains why edits exist
preguntas.explicacion: Within the national correct coding initiative, the medically unlikely edits exist to prevent improper payment where a service is reported with the wrong number of units. The procedure to procedure edits are the other half of the program and deal with pairs of codes that should not be reported together. The policy manual explains the reasoning behind both.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Common Pitfalls
preguntas.subtema: Nontherapeutic responses · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2E k21
preguntas.pregunta: Why are approving and disapproving responses treated as a pitfall?
opciones: They work as judgments of value and may feel intrusive to the patient
They offer a reassurance that the eventual outcome may not support
They move the conversation on before the patient has finished it
They repeat the patient's own words instead of exploring the feeling
preguntas.explicacion: Responses that approve or disapprove are listed as close kin to placing value judgments on the patient, and both may be felt as intrusive. False reassurance, changing the subject abruptly and unsolicited advice are other entries on the same table; reflecting the patient's words is a technique, not a pitfall.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, A Roadmap for New Physicians: Fraud & Abuse Laws; and CMS, MLN Booklet MLN4649244
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · CMA III.G.2
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory offers a practice free rent in exchange for sending it specimens. Which law does that implicate?
opciones: The Anti-Kickback Statute, which covers remuneration of any kind
The False Claims Act, which covers false statements on a claim form
The Exclusion Statute, which covers convictions for patient neglect
The Civil Monetary Penalties Law, which covers late claim filing
preguntas.explicacion: The Anti-Kickback Statute makes it a crime to offer, pay, solicit or receive remuneration knowingly and willfully so as to induce or reward a referral for items or services that federal health care programs pay for; remuneration covers anything of value, with free rent among the examples given. Penalties run to fines, imprisonment and exclusion, and under the penalties law up to three times the amount of the kickback.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Interview Techniques", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Questioning techniques · CCMA 6C k200 · CMAA 2A k15 · CMA F.5.b / 2027 F.3.b
preguntas.pregunta: At the start of an interview the clinician says how much time there is. How does that help?
opciones: It lets the patient rank concerns and feel in control of them
It shortens the history so that the examination can begin
It keeps the patient from raising more than one problem
It replaces the prompting question about other concerns
preguntas.explicacion: Expressing the time allocation at the beginning helps the patient prioritize their concerns and empowers them to feel in control of the discussion. It does not replace the prompting question about anything else, which often has to be asked more than once because the main concern is rarely the first one mentioned.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Home health services: How often
preguntas.subtema: Part-time or intermittent care · CCMA 4D k162 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: In most cases, how many hours do part-time or intermittent home health services come to?
opciones: Up to 8 hours a day combined, to a maximum of 28 hours in the week
Up to 8 hours a day combined, to a maximum of 40 hours in the week
Up to 4 hours a day combined, to a maximum of 20 hours in the week
Up to 12 hours a day combined, with no weekly maximum applied at all
preguntas.explicacion: Home health visits are unlimited in number for a patient who qualifies, but part-time or intermittent usually means skilled nursing and home health aide services together up to 8 hours a day, with a ceiling of 28 hours a week. More frequent care may be allowed for a short time, under 8 hours a day and up to 35 hours a week, when the provider decides it is necessary.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Access to Medical Care for Individuals with Mobility Disabilities: Services and Facilities
preguntas.subtema: Barrier removal · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.c · CMAA 7 k98 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: An older office building has two steps at its entrance. What does the law ask of the practice inside it?
opciones: Remove the barrier where doing so is readily achievable, and otherwise serve by other means
Remove the barrier only when the building is next altered or the lease comes up for renewal
Remove the barrier only if a patient files a written complaint about the entrance first
Leave the entrance as it stands, since buildings raised before the law are not reached by it
preguntas.explicacion: Every building is subject to the requirements for existing facilities, whatever its age. Under Title III architectural barriers are removed where removal is readily achievable, that is, easily accomplishable without much difficulty or expense; where it is not, the services still have to be made available by alternative methods that are readily achievable.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP)
preguntas.subtema: Government insurance plans · CCMA 5 k181 · CMAA 6 k74 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which children does the Children's Health Insurance Program cover?
opciones: Those in families earning too much for Medicaid but too little for private plans
Those in families earning too little for Medicaid but enough for a private plan
Those whose parents are enrolled in Medicare because of a lasting disability
Those living in a county that has a federally qualified health center nearby
preguntas.explicacion: The Children's Health Insurance Program gives health coverage to children who qualify, through Medicaid and through separate CHIP programs alike. The children who qualify are in families earning too much for Medicaid yet too little to afford private coverage. States manage the program under federal requirements, and states and the federal government fund it together.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Allowed amount
preguntas.subtema: Insurance terminology · CMAA 5C k76, 4 k61 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: What does the allowed amount of a plan represent?
opciones: The most the plan will pay for a covered service, also called the negotiated rate
The most the patient will pay for a covered service before the plan pays its share
The most the patient will pay in a plan year before coverage of benefits reaches 100%
The total the provider charges for the service before any discount is applied to it
preguntas.explicacion: The allowed amount is the ceiling a plan will pay for a covered service, and the glossary also calls it the eligible expense, the payment allowance or the negotiated rate. What the patient pays first is the deductible; the yearly ceiling on patient spending is the out-of-pocket limit; and the provider's own charge is a separate figure, which is why a charge above the allowed amount can leave a balance.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Hospice Care: Hospice Levels of Care (Respite Care); and Medicare.gov, Hospice care: Costs
preguntas.subtema: Respite for the family · CCMA 4D k165 · CMAA 2H k30
preguntas.pregunta: A caregiver needs a break from caring for a hospice patient at home. What does the respite level of care allow?
opciones: A stay of no more than 5 days in a row in a Medicare-approved facility each time
A stay of no more than 3 days in a row in a Medicare-approved facility each time
A stay of up to 30 days in each benefit period in a hospice inpatient facility
Continuous nursing at home for 8 hours a day, at least half of it given by a nurse
preguntas.explicacion: Respite is the hospice level built to relieve the caregiver. It runs no more than five consecutive days per occurrence and takes place at a facility Medicare has approved, an inpatient hospice or a nursing home for example; those patients need no skilled care. The patient may pay 5% of the approved amount for inpatient respite care.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.4 Handoff Reports
preguntas.subtema: Transitions of care · CCMA 4H k167 · CMAA 2F · CMA F.4.c / 2027 F.2.c
preguntas.pregunta: How is a handoff report defined?
opciones: A transfer and acceptance of responsibility for a patient's care
A written summary filed at the close of every nursing shift
A standing set of orders that follows the patient between units
A review of the record made before the next provider walks in
preguntas.explicacion: The definition used is a transfer and acceptance of responsibility for patient care achieved through effective communication: patient-specific information passed in real time from one caregiver, or one team, to the next, so that care stays continuous and safe. A filed summary or a set of orders is not that exchange.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule, Disclosure Accounting
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics · CMAA 3C k36 permitted disclosure · CCMA 7E k220
preguntas.pregunta: How far back may a patient's accounting of disclosures reach, and which disclosures does it leave out?
opciones: Six years back, leaving out treatment, payment and operations and those made under an authorization
Six years back, leaving out only the disclosures made to public health and law enforcement agencies
Two years back, leaving out treatment, payment and operations and those made under an authorization
Ten years back, leaving out only the disclosures the covered entity made to its business associates
preguntas.explicacion: The accounting reaches back at most six years from the request. What need not be accounted for makes a long list: health care operations, payment and treatment; disclosures to the individual or the personal representative; those made under an authorization; a limited data set; facility directories and disaster relief; national security; and disclosures incidental to a permitted use.

preguntas.fuente: USPS, Compare Mail Services: USPS Ground Advantage
preguntas.subtema: Hazardous shipments · CCMA 5O · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7D k99 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: An item classed as hazardous material cannot travel by air. Which domestic service is named as the primary option for it?
opciones: USPS Ground Advantage, the ground service that reaches most places in two to five days
Priority Mail Express, whose network is built around the fastest possible movement
First-Class Mail, whose light pieces travel with ordinary letters and small envelopes
Media Mail, whose slower schedule already allows for surface transport of the contents
preguntas.explicacion: Ground Advantage is described as the low-rate ground service with expected delivery in two to five days and as the primary option for hazardous materials that cannot go by air. Its handling fee for such items is also the only one of the three parcel services set at nothing extra.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Clinical Significance: When Can Information Be Shared?
preguntas.subtema: Where consults happen · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k213 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35
preguntas.pregunta: A clinician takes a telephone consult about a named patient from the phone in the hospital cafeteria. What is wrong with that?
opciones: The talk is allowed, but it has to happen away from the public
The talk is barred, since consults require written authorization
The talk is allowed only if the patient is on the line as well
The talk is barred, because phone lines are never encrypted
preguntas.explicacion: Consulting another provider is a permitted conversation; where it happens is what matters. Such talk belongs in a private room, out of earshot of the public, and a telephone consult taken from a cafeteria line, where anyone nearby can hear, is the example given of how not to do it. Staff may still coordinate verbally at a nurses' station, and providers may discuss a patient's status by telephone.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, A Roadmap for New Physicians: Fraud & Abuse Laws; and CMS, MLN Booklet MLN4649244
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · CMA III.G.2
preguntas.pregunta: Under the civil False Claims Act, what does the government have to prove about intent?
opciones: No specific intent to defraud is needed; reckless disregard is enough
A specific intent to defraud the program has to be shown for each claim
Only that the claim was denied by the payer after it had been reviewed
Only that the provider failed to refund an overpayment within 60 days
preguntas.explicacion: The civil False Claims Act catches anybody who knowingly presents a false or fraudulent claim, or causes one to be presented, and knowingly there takes in actual knowledge, deliberate ignorance and reckless disregard of the truth. No specific intent to defraud is required. A denial proves nothing on its own, and the 60-day overpayment rule is a separate duty whose breach can then create liability.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, HETS EDI: How to Enroll
preguntas.subtema: Eligibility verification · CMA III.G.3.a (2027 III.G.3.a) · CMAA 4 k58 · CCMA 5E
preguntas.pregunta: What does the Medicare eligibility system send a provider every month, and what is the provider expected to do with it?
opciones: A report of the eligibility transactions run under its identifier, to be reviewed
A report of the claims paid under its identifier, to be matched against postings
A list of the patients whose coverage lapsed, to be corrected before the next visit
A bill for the eligibility transactions run under its identifier, to be paid monthly
preguntas.explicacion: Providers are told to check the monthly reports detailing the eligibility transactions associated with their National Provider Identifier, and to take anything that looks wrong up with their vendor or clearinghouse directly. That is also why the enrollment has to keep a current email address: the monthly reports and the recertification contacts are sent there, and vendors are told to make sure their customers keep valid addresses.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Copayment; and Glossary: Coinsurance
preguntas.subtema: Copayment vs coinsurance · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.6.e, III.G.9.c / 2027 III.G.6.c · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: What is the difference between a copayment and coinsurance?
opciones: A copayment is a set dollar figure per service and coinsurance is a percentage of it
A copayment is a percentage of the service and coinsurance is a set dollar figure
A copayment is owed before the deductible and coinsurance replaces the deductible
A copayment is owed monthly for coverage and coinsurance is owed at each visit
preguntas.explicacion: A copayment is a fixed amount, $20 for instance, that the patient pays for a covered service. Coinsurance is a share expressed as a percentage of the allowed amount, 20% for instance, so the dollars change with the price of the service. Both are usually owed after the deductible is satisfied. The monthly amount owed for the coverage itself, used or not, is the premium.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Other Issues: Disposing of PHI
preguntas.subtema: Disposal of PHI · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k219 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.4 · CMAA 3B k39
preguntas.pregunta: How should paper records and prescription labels that contain PHI be disposed of?
opciones: Shredded or incinerated so that nobody can piece them back together
Placed in a red biohazard bag and treated as regulated waste
Handed to the person in charge of shredding to take home and destroy later
Kept in a locked cabinet indefinitely, since PHI may never be destroyed
preguntas.explicacion: Documents with PHI are shredded or incinerated so that no reconstruction is possible, computers, CDs and drives are completely erased before disposal, and the people assigned to destruction are chosen so that records are in fact destroyed rather than taken home; letting the shredding staff carry records home is exactly what that selection is meant to prevent. A red bag is the container for regulated waste under the bloodborne pathogens standard, which is about infection, not confidentiality, and HIPAA sets a retention period for its own documentation rather than a ban on destroying records.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, section 805(a)
preguntas.subtema: Collections · CMA III.G.9.f (exam through June 2027) · CMAA 6D · CCMA 5 k187
preguntas.pregunta: A patient tells the collection agency that her employer forbids calls of that kind at work. What does the statute then require?
opciones: The collector must stop telephoning her at her place of employment altogether
The collector may go on calling provided it leaves no message with a colleague
The collector may go on calling until she puts the objection down in writing
The collector must contact her only through the attorney representing her instead
preguntas.explicacion: Contacting a consumer at her place of employment is barred where the collector knows, or has reason to know, that her employer forbids her to receive such communication. A separate provision blocks contact with a consumer the collector knows is represented by an attorney whose name and address it has or can readily find, unless that attorney fails to respond or consents.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Underpayment Recoveries
preguntas.subtema: Accounts receivable · CMA III.G.6.a (exam through June 2027) · CMAA 6 k86 · CCMA 5 k187
preguntas.pregunta: How much of net patient revenue do providers fail to collect, and what is blamed for it?
opciones: Two to five percent, partly from weak billing and the effort of disputing claims
Five to ten percent, partly from weak billing and the effort of disputing claims
Ten to fifteen percent, mostly because patients never pay the balances they owe
