Under one percent, mostly because contractual write-offs get posted incorrectly
preguntas.explicacion: Underpayment recoveries measure what never comes in: between two and five percent of net patient revenue, blamed in part on inefficient revenue-cycle work and in part on the sheer effort of disputing claims, with certain insurers so notorious for wearing claimants down that practices have stopped accepting them. Five to ten percent is a different benchmark in the same material, the claim denial rate.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Public Health Activities
preguntas.subtema: Employer disclosures · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.5 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k37 · NCMA 4.10
preguntas.pregunta: An employer asks the practice for information about an employee's work-related injury. When may that be released without authorization?
opciones: When the employer needs it to comply with an occupational safety requirement
Whenever the employer is the one paying the premium for the employee's plan
Whenever the employee has already told the employer that the injury happened
Only when a court has ordered the practice to produce the medical record
preguntas.explicacion: Among the public health activities, a covered entity may disclose to an employer, at the employer's request and about its own employee, information on an illness or injury that is work- related or on medical surveillance of the workplace, because the employer needs it to satisfy the requirements of OSHA, or those of the Mine Safety and Health Administration, or of a State law that does the same job. Workers' compensation disclosures are a separate national priority purpose.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 2.1
preguntas.subtema: Interface inventory · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which list does the contingency guidance tell an organization to keep and review as part of its downtime planning?
opciones: Its system-to-system connections, marking those that must be told of an outage
Its staff members trained on paper charting, marked by the date of their training
Its patients seen during the last outage, marked by the unit that attended them
Its equipment serviced in the past year, marked by the date of the next service
preguntas.explicacion: Interfaces are the part that fails quietly. The organization keeps a comprehensive list of its system-to-system interfaces and reviews it regularly, every six months or yearly, noting which of them raise legal or regulatory duties to warn the other side, such as a state immunization registry or a prescription drug monitoring program.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Directing to a Third Party
preguntas.subtema: Directing PHI to a third party · CCMA 5 k176 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient wants her records sent straight to a research app she uses. What does the Privacy Rule require of her request?
opciones: It must be in writing, signed by her, and name the recipient and where to send the copy
It must be approved by the privacy official, who decides whether the recipient is suitable
It must come with an authorization from the app developer accepting business associate duties
It must be limited to a summary, since only summaries may be directed outside the practice
preguntas.explicacion: Beyond taking copies herself, an individual may direct the covered entity to send her PHI on to another person or entity of her choosing. The request has to be in writing, has to be signed, and has to say plainly who that designated recipient is and the address the information should go to; an electronic copy of a signed request, or one executed electronically through a secure portal, is acceptable. The same fee limits and the same form-and-format rules apply.

preguntas.subtema: Media accountability · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A practice writes down which staff member took which laptop out of the building and when it came back. Which specification does that log satisfy?
opciones: Accountability, a record of hardware movements and of the person answering for them
Maintenance records, a record of repairs made to doors, walls and locks in the office
Workstation use, which fixes what may be done at a given class of workstation
Facility security plan, which guards the premises and its equipment against theft
preguntas.explicacion: Accountability sits under device and media controls, and it is the addressable specification calling for a log of where hardware and electronic media go and of who answers for them. Maintenance records look at the building itself, not at equipment that travels.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Patient Data Verification
preguntas.subtema: Insurance verification · CMAA 5B k66, 4 k58 · CCMA 5E · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A patient hands over a new insurance card at check-in. Which step protects the claim best?
opciones: Verifying coverage and benefits with the plan before the visit is billed
Filing the card in the paper chart and billing the plan listed last year
Asking the patient to state the group number aloud instead of copying it
Waiting for the remittance advice to reveal which plan is now primary
preguntas.explicacion: Verification of patient data prevents rejections, delays and denials: insurance eligibility belongs on the list of items to confirm before the claim goes out, along with the name, the age and the billing address. Billing last year's plan invites a denial for coverage that has ended, an oral group number adds an error, and learning it from the remittance advice means the denial already happened.

preguntas.subtema: Conditioning an authorization · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.b · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient refuses to sign an authorization sending her records to her employer. May the practice make her appointment conditional on signing it?
opciones: No, treatment may not be conditioned on an authorization outside narrow exceptions
No, unless the practice notes the refusal in the record and offers a later date
Yes, a practice may set the terms on which it accepts a patient for treatment
Yes, where the employer is the source of the coverage that pays for the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Conditioning treatment, payment, enrollment in a plan or eligibility for benefits on the individual signing an authorization is forbidden to a covered entity. The exceptions are narrow: research-related treatment, a plan's own enrollment or underwriting determinations, and care provided solely in order to create information for a third party. The form itself has to state which case applies.

preguntas.fuente: NAIC, Coordination of Benefits Model Regulation (Model 120), Order of Benefit Determination Rules
preguntas.subtema: Insurance rules · CMAA 5B k75 · CCMA 5E k182
preguntas.pregunta: Both parents of a covered child were born on May 12. Which plan is primary for the child?
opciones: The plan that has covered its parent for the longer period of time
The plan that has covered its parent for the shorter period of time
The plan of the parent who carries the family coverage at work
The plan of the parent who claims the child on the tax return
preguntas.explicacion: Where the two parents share a birthday, the model rule looks to which plan has covered its parent longer, and that one becomes primary for the child. The plan with the shorter run is secondary. Which parent holds the family coverage, or claims the child as a tax dependent, plays no part in the order of benefit determination.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, Administration for Community Living: Aging and Disability Networks; and ACL, Aging and Disability Networks (Area Agencies on Aging, ADRC)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4D k164 community resources · CMAA 2H k30
preguntas.pregunta: What do senior centers funded under the aging network typically coordinate?
opciones: Community education, congregate meals, screening for health, and transportation
Congregate meals and skilled nursing care delivered inside the center
Long-term services counseling and help applying for disability programs
Legal protection and advocacy for the civil rights of older adults
preguntas.explicacion: Grants to states and territories fund multi-purpose senior centers, which pull together community education, congregate meals, health screening, transportation, and programs for exercise and health promotion. Counseling about long-term services belongs to the resource centers, and rights advocacy to the protection and advocacy systems.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Laboratory Safety Guidance (OSHA 3404), Fire safety, the PASS rule
preguntas.subtema: PASS · CPT D1 1A 1L k24 · PBT VI.G.2 · CMA I.B.8.c / 2027 I.B.7.c · RMA II.B.7.c · NCMA 2A.9 · CMAA 3A k45
preguntas.pregunta: What does the first S in PASS stand for when operating a portable fire extinguisher?
opciones: Squeeze the trigger, holding the extinguisher upright
Sweep the nozzle from side to side across the flames
Stand back 75 feet, the maximum travel distance
Shut the door behind you before discharging
preguntas.explicacion: PASS sums up how an extinguisher is worked: pull the pin, aim the nozzle at the base of the fire, then, with the extinguisher held upright, squeeze the trigger, and sweep from side to side so the spray covers the fire. Sweeping is the second S. Seventy-five feet is the maximum travel distance to a Class A extinguisher under 29 CFR 1910.157, not a stand-off distance, and shutting the door is the confine step of RACE, done before anyone tries to put the fire out.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 1.1
preguntas.subtema: Warm-site backup · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A large organization that treats patients around the clock keeps a warm-site backup that can run the whole record system. What does the guidance expect of it?
opciones: Current patient data, running within eight hours, and a test at least every quarter
Current patient data, running within eight hours, and a test at least every year
Current patient data, running within one hour, and a test at least every quarter
A weekly copy of patient data, running within eight hours, and a yearly test
preguntas.explicacion: The example given is a remote backup facility, more than fifty miles away and more than twenty miles from the coast, holding current patient data and able to be brought up in less than eight hours, with the backup computer system tested at least quarterly. A single point of failure is what the practice exists to remove.

preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, benign
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k5 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A pathology report calls a growth benign. What does that tell the patient?
opciones: It may keep growing, but it does not spread to other parts of the body
It has stopped growing, and it does not spread to other parts of the body
It is growing slowly, and it spreads only through the lymph system
It is not growing at all, and it will disappear without any treatment
preguntas.explicacion: Benign means not cancer. A benign tumor can still get larger, and its size may cause trouble by itself, but it does not invade nearby tissue or travel elsewhere. The opposite term is malignant: those cells grow in an uncontrolled way, invade nearby tissue and spread through the blood and lymph system.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Eligibility
preguntas.subtema: Financial eligibility · CMAA 6 k83 · CCMA 5E k178
preguntas.pregunta: Which method is used to decide income eligibility for Medicaid for most children, pregnant women and adults?
opciones: Modified adjusted gross income, with no asset or resource test applied
Modified adjusted gross income, with an asset test set by each state
The federal poverty guidelines applied to gross monthly wages alone
The income rules of the Supplemental Security Income program instead
preguntas.explicacion: The health care law created the modified adjusted gross income method, which works from taxable income and from the relationships declared on tax filings, and which allows no asset or resource test and no income disregards particular to a state. It also settles eligibility for CHIP and for Marketplace savings. People whose eligibility rests on being 65 or older, on blindness or on disability are exempt and are generally assessed with the income methods of the Supplemental Security Income program.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Out-of-pocket maximum/limit
preguntas.subtema: Insurance terminology · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · CMAA 5C · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: What is the out-of-pocket maximum of a health plan?
opciones: The yearly cap on what the patient pays for covered in-network care; past it, the plan pays 100%
The most the patient pays per visit for covered services; the plan pays 100% of the rest
The most the patient pays in a plan year including premiums and out-of-network care
The 2026 Marketplace cap, $10,600 per individual, which applies only to premiums
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov describes the out-of-pocket maximum, or limit, as the ceiling on what the patient spends on covered services in a plan year, not per visit. Once her deductible, her copayments and her coinsurance for care inside the network add up to that figure, the plan covers 100% of covered benefits for the rest of the year. The glossary lists what does not count toward it: monthly premiums, out-of-network care, services the plan does not cover, and charges above the allowed amount. The $10,600 figure is the 2026 Marketplace ceiling for an individual, and it caps cost sharing, never premiums.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: What should I know before my telehealth visit?
preguntas.subtema: Post-visit summary · CMAA 4E k59 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient worries she will forget what was said during a video visit. Which step does the patient guidance suggest to her?
opciones: Asking the clinician afterwards to send her a summary or notes of the appointment
Recording the appointment on her own telephone so she can play it back later
Asking the clinician for a direct mobile number she can use with any question later
Asking for the same appointment to be repeated in the office later that week
preguntas.explicacion: Feeling confident in a telehealth visit includes learning how it works, taking her time, choosing a clinician who listens, asking for anything unclear to be explained, and getting a summary: she is told to ask the clinician to send a summary or notes after the visit, which can include answers to the questions she raised. Writing a list beforehand is suggested for the same reason.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: The note mentions a condition treated years ago that no longer exists but still shapes today's treatment. How is it handled?
opciones: It is not coded as current, and a history code may be added as secondary
It is coded as current, because the note for this visit still mentions it
It is coded first, since it explains the treatment chosen for her today
It is left out entirely, since a condition that has resolved is never coded
preguntas.explicacion: Coders report the conditions that coexist at the time of the visit and that require or affect care. Conditions previously treated that no longer exist are not coded as current. Personal and family history categories may still be used as secondary codes where that history bears on the care given today or steers the treatment.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 1.3
preguntas.subtema: Downtime paper forms · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: How much paper capacity does the SAFER contingency practice expect each patient care area to hold for a downtime?
opciones: Enough forms to care for its patients for at least eight hours
Enough forms to care for its patients for at least three days
Enough forms to care for its patients for at least thirty days
Enough forms to care for one shift of scheduled visits only
preguntas.explicacion: The recommended practice is to keep paper forms on hand that can stand in for the EHR's key functions while it is down, since clinical and administrative operations have to carry on. The implementation guidance fixes the stock: enough in each patient care area to cover its patients for eight hours at least, forms for entering orders and for documenting medications, laboratory and radiology tests included.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Home health services: Coverage details
preguntas.subtema: Limits of home health · CCMA 4D k162 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: Which service does Medicare refuse to pay for under the home health benefit?
opciones: Care in the home 24 hours a day, and meals delivered to the house
Wound care for a pressure sore given by a visiting skilled nurse
Occupational therapy, physical therapy and speech-language services
Osteoporosis injections for women who meet the stated criteria
preguntas.explicacion: The benefit does not pay for care at home around the clock, for meals delivered to the house, for homemaker work such as shopping and cleaning unrelated to the care plan, or for custodial personal care when that is the only care the patient needs. It does pay for skilled nursing, the three therapies, medical social services, equipment and supplies used at home.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 413.89, reasonable collection effort
preguntas.subtema: Adjustments and write-offs · CMAA 6 k86, 6D · CCMA 5K k187
preguntas.pregunta: Before a Medicare deductible or coinsurance amount can be written off as bad debt, how long must the collection effort last?
opciones: At least 120 days from the billing that started the collection effort
At least 30 days from the billing that started the collection effort
At least 12 months from the date the service was given to the patient
Until a collection agency reports that the account cannot be collected
preguntas.explicacion: For cost reporting periods that start on or after October 1, 2020, the bill reaches the beneficiary within 120 days of the remittance advice or the secondary payer's response, and the collection effort must then continue at least 120 days before the amount is written off as uncollectible. A payment received inside that window starts a new 120-day period, and the effort has to match what the provider does for non-Medicare patients.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Introduction to the Americans with Disabilities Act (Title I)
preguntas.subtema: ADAAA compliance · CMAA 3A (ADAAA)
preguntas.pregunta: Which employers must comply with Title I of the Americans with Disabilities Act?
opciones: Those with 15 or more employees, including state and local governments
Those with 50 or more employees within 75 miles of the worksite
Those with 20 or more employees in 20 or more workweeks of the calendar year
Those that receive federal funding, at any size of payroll
preguntas.explicacion: The law is divided into five titles, each aimed at a different kind of organization. Title I covers employment and applies to employers with 15 or more employees, including labor unions, employment agencies, and state and local governments. A charge of discrimination under it goes to the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Error Prevention and Root Cause Analysis", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Incident reports and analysis · CCMA 6M k211 · CMAA 3 k44
preguntas.pregunta: What defines a sentinel event, as opposed to a preventable adverse event?
opciones: The severity of the outcome, rather than what caused it
The cause being a medical error, rather than the outcome
The event reaching a patient, rather than being a near miss
The event being reported to an accrediting organization
preguntas.explicacion: A preventable adverse event is defined by causation: harm produced by a medical error or by inaction. A sentinel event is defined by the severity of the outcome, a safety event reaching a patient and ending in death, in severe harm or in permanent harm. Wrong-site surgery is both; a medication error that resolves is only the first.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Implementation of This Model
preguntas.subtema: Appointment types · CMAA 4A k51 · CCMA 5B k173 · CMA III.H.1.a-b · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Implementing open access includes simplifying the appointment types. Which three does the improvement guide recommend a practice keep?
opciones: Personal with her own physician, team with another clinician, and unestablished
Routine, urgent and follow-up, each one holding its own block of the morning
New patient, established patient and annual wellness, each of a different length
Short, long and double, where the long one is worth about two of the short ones
preguntas.explicacion: One recommended tactic is to strip out complexity by holding the practice to three types: personal, where the patient sees her own physician; team, where she is seen by another clinician on the team; and unestablished, for patients who do not yet have a physician. Appointment length is handled apart from that, as short or long, a long visit counting for roughly two short ones.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Does your provider accept Medicare as full payment?
preguntas.subtema: Third-party billing · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 6C k87 · CCMA 5L k185 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A physician has opted out of Medicare and asks the patient to sign a private contract. What follows for her?
opciones: Medicare pays nothing for his services except in emergencies, and he stays out two years
Medicare pays its share as usual once she files her own claim for those services
Medicare pays the approved amount less the fifteen percent limiting charge for him
Medicare pays none of it for one year, after which the physician returns automatically
preguntas.explicacion: Providers who do not want to work with the program may opt out, and Medicare will not pay for what they furnish except in an emergency. Opting out lasts a minimum of two years, and at each two-year point the provider may stay out, become non-participating, or accept assignment. The patient may have to pay up front or agree a payment plan under the private contract.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 5.3 Functions of the Integumentary System, Vitamin D Synthesis
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(1) (2027 I.C.6.f(1)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12
preguntas.pregunta: Besides acting as a barrier, which vitamin does the skin synthesize when it is exposed to ultraviolet light?
opciones: Vitamin D, needed for the absorption of calcium and phosphorus
Vitamin C, needed for the absorption of calcium and phosphorus
Vitamin K, needed for the absorption of calcium and phosphorus
Vitamin A, needed for the absorption of calcium and phosphorus
preguntas.explicacion: The epidermis makes vitamin D under ultraviolet light, and the liver and kidneys then convert it to its active form. Without it calcium and phosphorus are poorly absorbed, and bones suffer: rickets in children and osteomalacia, a softening of bone, in older adults. The lack of vitamin C causes scurvy instead.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, When can I sign up for Medicare?; and Medicare costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient signed up for Part B three years after she was first eligible. How long will the late enrollment penalty last?
opciones: For as long as she holds Part B, and the longer the wait the larger it grows
For three years, one year of penalty for each year that she delayed signing up
Until the eight-month special enrollment period that follows her retirement
Until she buys a Medigap policy, which takes the penalty amount over from her
preguntas.explicacion: Someone who does not sign up for Part B when first eligible has to wait to enroll and goes months without coverage, and may pay a monthly penalty for as long as she has Part B, with the penalty rising the longer the delay ran. A similar penalty exists for Part A when it has to be bought and is not taken at the first opportunity.

preguntas.fuente: VA, CHAMPVA benefits: People who are age 65 or older or who qualify for Medicare
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74, 5B k66 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A CHAMPVA beneficiary turns 65 and becomes eligible for Medicare. What must she do to keep CHAMPVA?
opciones: Enroll in Medicare Part A and Part B, or in a Medicare Advantage plan
Enroll in Medicare Part A alone, since Part B duplicates the coverage
Drop CHAMPVA, since the two programs may not be held at the same time
Submit proof of income each year so the program can recheck her costs
preguntas.explicacion: Anyone eligible for Medicare, at 65 or at any other age, must hold Part A and Part B to get or keep CHAMPVA, and a Medicare Advantage plan satisfies that. An applicant of 65 or more who does not qualify for Medicare sends in a disallowance notice from Social Security instead. The programs coexist, and eligibility does not rest on a yearly review of income.

preguntas.fuente: NAIC, Coordination of Benefits Model Regulation (Model 120), Order of Benefit Determination Rules
preguntas.subtema: Insurance rules · CMAA 5B k75 · CCMA 5E k182
preguntas.pregunta: A child is covered by both parents' plans. The mother's birthday is March 4 and the father's is July 19. Whose plan pays first?
opciones: The mother's plan, because her birthday falls earlier in the calendar year
The father's plan, because his birthday falls later in the calendar year
The mother's plan, because she is the parent who enrolled the child first
The father's plan, because his coverage has been in force for more years
preguntas.explicacion: Where the parents of a dependent child are married or living together, the model rule gives primacy to whichever parent's birthday comes earlier in the calendar year. Length of coverage settles the tie only where both parents share a birthday, and which parent enrolled the child first plays no part. This is a model regulation the states adopt, not a federal law.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Helping patients prepare for their telehealth appointment
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth privacy · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.3.g · CMAA 4B k55 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: An upcoming telehealth visit will cover a sensitive topic. What extra step does the guidance suggest?
opciones: Helping the patient find a private spot and agreeing what a companion may hear
Moving the appointment to the office, since sensitive topics rule telehealth out
Recording the visit so that the discussion can be reviewed by a second clinician
Asking the patient to bring a relative, who can confirm what was discussed later
preguntas.explicacion: For appointments touching sensitive subjects the guidance suggests discussing whether the patient can find a private place, and offering tips for one at home, in a car or at a friend's house. It also covers other communication options such as e-mail, text or the platform's chat feature where personal safety may be an issue, and says to establish with an interpreter or caregiver present what the patient is comfortable letting them hear, and whether a release is needed.

preguntas.subtema: Media re-use · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: The office wants to hand a set of flash drives that once held claim files to another department. Which Security Rule specification governs that?
opciones: Media re-use, which has the information taken off the drive before it is handed on
Disposal, which governs the final disposition of the hardware once it leaves service
Accountability, which keeps a record of who moved the hardware and where it went
Data backup and storage, which copies the information before equipment is moved
preguntas.explicacion: Device and media controls carry four specifications. Disposal deals with hardware at the end of its life; the one that fits a drive still in service and about to be passed to someone else is media re-use, and like disposal it is required, not addressable. Both aim at the same risk: information left behind on hardware that changes hands.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Access to Medical Care for Individuals with Mobility Disabilities, Part 2
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.D Interpersonal Relations · CPT D2 2A k17 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 3A ADAAA compliance · CMA II.F.1.c(4) ADAAA
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who uses a wheelchair arrives with a friend who pushed the chair into the drawing room. How should the phlebotomist handle the conversation?
opciones: Speak to the patient directly, and ask her whether the friend should stay in the room
Speak to the friend, who can relay the answers if the patient tires during the draw
Ask the friend to step out at once, because privacy rules bar all visitors from the room
Ask the patient to sign a release before the friend may hear any of the questions
preguntas.explicacion: The rule for a patient with a disability is the rule for every patient: address her, not the companion, because a disability says nothing about her ability to speak for herself or follow the answers. Whether the companion stays is her decision, and it should be asked before the discussion starts rather than assumed either way.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), If the Primary Payer Denies the Claim
preguntas.subtema: Claim submission · CMA III.G.3.b(1) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6 k87 · CCMA 5 k185
preguntas.pregunta: On a Medicare secondary claim, why does the biller have to pick the right claim adjustment reason code?
opciones: Because Medicare may deny the claim when the code for the adjustment is wrong
Because Medicare pays interest on the claim only when the code is entered right
Because the primary payer may reopen the claim when the code for it is wrong
Because Medicare asks for it only on paper claims, where remittances are attached
preguntas.explicacion: A secondary claim has to explain why the other payer denied it, decided the benefits were exhausted, paid less than the full amount, or did not pay at all. That information sits in the claim adjustment segment of the 835 remittance advice or the 837 professional claim, and the correct claim adjustment reason code has to be identified there; if it is not, Medicare may deny the claim outright.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Common Pitfalls
preguntas.subtema: Nontherapeutic responses · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2C k14
preguntas.pregunta: Which behavior is listed as negative body language during an interview?
opciones: Standing over the patient with the arms crossed
Leaning forward while the patient is speaking
Closing the door before the interview starts
Nodding while the patient describes a symptom
preguntas.explicacion: Negative body language is described as folded arms, a distracted air, or standing over the patient. The other three appear on the list of techniques: leaning forward signifies active listening, closing the door or the curtain shows respect for privacy, and nodding is one of the cues that keeps the patient talking.

preguntas.subtema: Signature by a representative · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's son signs the release form as her personal representative. What must the form carry in addition to his signature and the date?
opciones: A description of the authority under which he acts for her
A copy of the identification he presented at the front desk
A statement that she was unable to sign the form for herself
A second signature from a member of the practice's workforce
preguntas.explicacion: The core element covering the signature says that where a personal representative signs, the form must also describe that person's authority to act for the individual. The other core elements do not change: the information, who discloses it, who receives it, the purpose and an expiration date or event all remain.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Eligibility, Financial Eligibility
preguntas.subtema: Financial eligibility · CMA III.G.4.c (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 6 k83 · CCMA 5E k178 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: Whose Medicaid income is worked out by the SSI methodologies rather than by the MAGI rules?
opciones: An applicant who is sixty-five or older, or who is blind or has a disability
An applicant who is pregnant and is applying for coverage for the first time
An applicant who is the parent of a child already enrolled in the program
An applicant who is an adult in a state that widened coverage to low earners
preguntas.explicacion: The Affordable Care Act put Modified Adjusted Gross Income at the center of financial eligibility for Medicaid, for CHIP and for Marketplace help, and it governs most adults, most parents, most pregnant women and most children. Certain people are exempt: eligibility resting on being sixty-five or over, on blindness or on disability is generally decided with the income methods of the SSI program.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Exceptions
preguntas.subtema: Breach exceptions · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3E k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: A nurse opens the wrong chart by accident, in good faith and within her duties, and closes it without using anything. What is this?
opciones: One of the three exceptions to the definition of a breach
A breach that still requires notice to the patient within sixty days
A reportable security incident that must go to the Secretary each year
A disclosure that must go on the accounting of disclosures
preguntas.explicacion: Three situations sit outside the definition. First: an unintentional acquisition, access or use by a member of the workforce who was acting in good faith and inside the authority given to her. Second: an inadvertent disclosure between two people who are both authorized to reach PHI at the same entity or organized arrangement. In both, the information may not then be used or disclosed improperly. Third: a good faith belief that whoever received it would not have been able to retain it.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3636, Hazard Communication Standard: Labels and Pictograms, Pictograms (Figure 1 note)
preguntas.subtema: Required pictograms · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: The GHS uses nine hazard pictograms. How many does OSHA enforce, and which one is optional?
opciones: Eight; only the environmental pictogram is optional
Nine; none is optional under the 2012 revision
Seven; the environmental and the health hazard ones are optional
Eight; the flame pictogram is optional for laboratory reagents
preguntas.explicacion: OSHA adopted the GHS pictograms but enforces eight of the nine: the one for the environment is not required, since environmental hazards fall to other agencies, though a label preparer may add it as supplementary information, so workers may still see it. The health hazard and the flame are among the eight required whenever the classification calls for them. The names of the eight appear in a figure of the OSHA brief; the count and the exception are what the text states.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Billing: CMS-1500 & 837P (MLN006976)
preguntas.subtema: Claim submission · CMAA 6C k87, 6 k85 · CCMA 5L k185 · CMA III.G.3.b(1)
preguntas.pregunta: What is the 837P?
opciones: The standard electronic format for professional health care claims
The standard electronic format for the plan's payment and remittance advice
The paper claim used by hospitals for inpatient services and supplies
The companion guide each contractor publishes for electronic claims
preguntas.explicacion: The 837P is the standard electronic format professionals and suppliers use to submit claims, and version 5010A1 is the current one; the P stands for the professional version. The electronic format for the plan's payment explanation is the 835 remittance advice. Companion guides are technical documents each Medicare administrative contractor publishes to accompany, not replace, the standard.

preguntas.fuente: VA, CHAMPVA benefits: Benefits you can get through CHAMPVA
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74, 6C k87 · CCMA 5L k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: How does CHAMPVA pay for the care its beneficiaries receive?
opciones: It shares the cost of certain covered services and supplies with the beneficiary
It pays the full cost of every service the beneficiary receives from any provider
It reimburses the beneficiary only after the private insurer has denied the claim
It pays a fixed amount to the beneficiary each month toward medical expenses
preguntas.explicacion: CHAMPVA is described as a cost-sharing program: once the person is enrolled, the Department of Veterans Affairs shares the cost of certain health care services and supplies with the beneficiary, so it neither covers everything nor sends a monthly allowance. Applications go in on VA Form 10-10d, online, by mail or by fax, with a copy of any other insurance or Medicare card attached.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, DESC
preguntas.subtema: Conflict management · CCMA 6J k209 · CMA F.1.f / 2027 F.1.f · RMA I.D.2.a · CMAA 2B k26
preguntas.pregunta: In the DESC script for resolving conflict, what does the final step state?
opciones: The consequences for the patient and the team's goals
The specific situation or behavior, with concrete data
How the situation makes the speaker feel about it
The alternatives on offer, while seeking agreement
preguntas.explicacion: DESC is a constructive approach to managing and resolving conflict. It describes the situation or behavior with concrete data, expresses how it makes you feel and what concerns you, suggests alternatives while seeking agreement, and closes with consequences framed as the impact on the patient and on the team goals already established.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Evacuation Plans and Procedures eTool, Emergency Action Plan: Shelter-in-Place
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.B.8.a · 2027 I.B.7.a · CMAA 3 k45 · RMA II.7.c · NCMA 2A.9 EKB 8
preguntas.pregunta: A tank car leaking chlorine derails behind the clinic and the authorities advise staying indoors. What does the office do?
opciones: Shelter in place in an interior room with no windows or few of them
Evacuate by the marked routes and gather at the outside assembly point
Send staff home in their own cars by the route furthest from the tracks
Move everyone to the room nearest the exit and keep the doors propped
preguntas.explicacion: When a chemical, biological or radiological release makes the outside air the greater danger, staying inside is safer than evacuating: an interior room, with no windows or few, is chosen and used as refuge. The signal that tells staff to shelter has to be easy to tell apart from the evacuation alarm, and staff are trained in both.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Health Care Payment and Remittance Advice (835/ERA)
preguntas.subtema: Remittance advice · CMA III.G.3.b(3) (exam through June 2027) · CMAA 5 k79 · CCMA 5 k181
preguntas.pregunta: How many payments does Medicare issue for the claims itemized on a single remittance advice?
opciones: One check or funds transfer, covering all the benefits due on that remittance
One check or funds transfer for each claim itemized on that same remittance
One check for the claims paid in full and a second for those paid in part
One funds transfer each week, however many remittances it happens to cover
preguntas.explicacion: Once a claim is processed, an electronic remittance advice or a standard paper remittance goes out with the final adjudication and payment information, and one of them usually carries decisions on several claims at once, itemized so each decision can be matched to the claim as it was submitted. When payment is due, a single check or electronic funds transfer is issued for all the benefits owed on the claims itemized there.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Specific Techniques
preguntas.subtema: Therapeutic techniques · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2A k21 · CMA F.2 / 2027 F.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: While a patient tells a long history the assistant nods and says “go on.” What is that doing?
opciones: Encouraging the patient to keep going and showing she is heard
Repeating the patient's words back to show she is being followed
Putting the patient's account into the listener's own words
Offering guiding statements so the patient makes a point clearer
preguntas.explicacion: Nodding and small phrases such as “Uh-huh”, “I see” or “Go on” are listed as verbal and nonverbal cues that keep the conversation going and show the patient is being listened to. Repeating the words back is reflecting, restating the account in your own words is summarizing, and guiding statements are clarifying.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 6A, 5 k68 · CCMA 5I k184 · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: After an ambulatory surgery the postoperative diagnosis turns out to differ from the preoperative one by the time the chart is coded. Which one is used?
opciones: The postoperative diagnosis, as the more definitive of the two
The preoperative diagnosis, which is what justified the surgery
Both of them, with the preoperative one sequenced first
The one the surgeon dictated first in the operative report
preguntas.explicacion: For ambulatory surgery the diagnosis coded is the one the surgery was performed for. When the postoperative diagnosis is known to differ from the preoperative one at the time the diagnosis is confirmed, the postoperative one is selected because it is the most definitive. The preoperative impression is what was believed beforehand, not what was established.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Promoting Interoperability Programs
preguntas.subtema: MACRA and MIPS · CCMA 5 k179 · CMA III.G.4 (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.B.6.c · CMAA 7 k90 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: What did MACRA do in 2015 to the incentive program that had paid clinicians for meaningful use of certified EHRs?
opciones: It sunset that program and folded similar requirements into MIPS as one of four categories
It doubled the payments available under that program and extended it through 2027
It replaced that program with a penalty applied to every practice using paper charts
It moved that program from CMS to the Office for Civil Rights for enforcement
preguntas.explicacion: The EHR Incentive Programs were established in 2011 under the HITECH Act. In 2015 the Medicare Access and CHIP Reauthorization Act sunset the Medicare program for eligible professionals and built similar requirements into the Merit-based Incentive Payment System as one of its four performance categories, Promoting Interoperability. The hospital program continues; the Medicaid one ended on December 31, 2021.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 482.13(a), Standard: Notice of rights; 482.13(h), Patient visitation rights
preguntas.subtema: Notice of patient rights · CPT D1 k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7A k215 · CMA II.E.1.d · RMA I.C.1.e · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32
preguntas.pregunta: Under the Medicare Conditions of Participation, 42 CFR 482.13, when must a hospital inform patients of their rights?
opciones: In advance of furnishing or discontinuing care, whenever possible
Within 30 days of admission, in a written notice signed by the patient
Only when the patient or a representative files a formal grievance
At discharge, together with the billing statement and visitation policy
preguntas.explicacion: The first standard of 482.13, notice of rights, has the hospital tell each patient, or the representative where state law allows one, what their rights are before care is given or withdrawn, whenever that can be done. The same standard calls for a grievance process: a clear procedure for grievances written or spoken, time frames for the review, and a written decision naming the contact person, the steps taken and the outcome. Visitation rights are explained along with the rest, not at discharge.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: The Intervention
preguntas.subtema: Open access principles · CMAA 4A k51 · CCMA 5C k171 · CMA III.H.1.c · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A front desk moving to open access is told its single rule is to do today's work today. Which habit does that ask the staff to drop?
opciones: Sorting callers by clinical urgency, since demand is now sorted by clinician instead
Booking the follow-up visits a clinician asked for, since those slots are needed today
Offering a caller a later day, since under this model nobody may decline the same-day slot
Tracking the calls patients make, since demand is read from the count of past appointments
preguntas.explicacion: The model breaks with the traditional split between urgent and routine, which is what pushes routine care back. Instead of triaging callers by urgency, reception simply sorts the demand by clinician. Clinically necessary follow-ups are still booked ahead, patients may still choose a later day, and the practice has to measure both supply and demand as precisely as it can.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, FAQ: What is a patient portal?
preguntas.subtema: Portal functions · CMAA 4E k56 · CCMA 5U k172 · CMA III.H.3.a (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.B.6.c · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether she has to telephone the office to settle her balance and confirm what her plan covers. What does ONC say some portals allow?
opciones: Checking benefits and coverage and making payments through the portal itself
Filing the claim with her insurer once the appointment has been completed
Reading the explanation of benefits her insurer prepared for the last visit
Setting the allowed amount her plan will pay for the appointment she booked
preguntas.explicacion: On top of secure messaging, refill requests and booking non-urgent appointments, some portals let the patient look up her benefits and coverage, correct her contact details, pay what she owes, pull down forms and fill them in, and read educational material. Filing the claim and setting an allowed amount are done by the practice and the plan, not by the patient at her portal.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Mandatory & Optional Medicaid Benefits
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.c (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A mother asks whether her child's Medicaid covers a screening and whatever the screening turns up. What does the mandatory benefit list say?
opciones: The early and periodic screening benefit, with diagnosis and treatment, is mandatory
Screening is mandatory in every state, but the treatment it leads to is left optional
Screening for children is one of the optional benefits a state may add if it chooses
Screening is mandatory only in the states that widened Medicaid to low-income adults
preguntas.explicacion: The early and periodic screening benefit, taking in diagnosis and treatment, appears on the federal list of mandatory Medicaid state plan benefits that every state must provide, and it is named as one benefit rather than split between the screening and what follows. The optional list is where a state chooses what to add through its state plan.

preguntas.subtema: Required specifications · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice argues that its risk analysis found little need for an emergency access procedure, so it will not build one. Is that allowed?
opciones: No, that specification is required, so it has to be implemented as the rule states
Yes, if the reason is documented and an equivalent alternative measure is put in place
Yes, provided the automatic logoff is shortened to make up for the missing measure
No, but a small practice may write a note in the contingency plan in place of it
preguntas.explicacion: The document-and-substitute route belongs to addressable specifications only. The emergency access procedure, which lets staff obtain the information they need during an emergency, is marked required, and a required specification must be implemented whatever the size of the practice.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Administrative Requirements, Privacy Personnel; 45 CFR 164.530(a)
preguntas.subtema: HIPAA personnel designations · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which two roles must a practice name to satisfy the personnel designations of the Privacy Rule?
opciones: A privacy official who builds and runs the policies, and a contact who takes in complaints
A privacy official who builds and runs the policies, and a records custodian who releases charts
A compliance officer who audits the billing, and a contact who takes in privacy complaints
A privacy official who builds and runs the policies, and a trainer for every new workforce member
preguntas.explicacion: Two names go on the wall, not one. The privacy official owns the policies and procedures: writing them and putting them to work. The contact person, or a contact office, is the door for the public — complaints arrive there, and so do questions about how the practice handles information, which is why the notice has to say who that is and add that a complaint may also go to the Secretary of HHS. Training, sanctions and mitigation are separate administrative duties of the same section, and they do not have to be handed to a designated person.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases, chapter 5: Unpacking Deliveries
preguntas.subtema: Cold chain monitor · CCMA 5T · RMA II.B.5.a · CMAA 7D k99 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A cold chain monitor is included in the shipping container. What does the receiving staff member do with it?
opciones: Read it for any excursion during transit and then discard it, since it is single use
Read it for any excursion during transit and place it inside the storage unit
File it with the packing list as the record of the temperature during transit
Return it to the distributor with the shipping container for its next journey
preguntas.explicacion: The monitor's job ends when the box is opened: it is checked for a temperature excursion during transit and then thrown away, because it is made for one trip only. It is not the storage unit's monitoring device, which is a continuous digital data logger that stays with the unit.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 21: Make Referrals Easy
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k168 referral processes · CMAA 4 referrals
preguntas.pregunta: What does a formal referral agreement between a practice and a specialist group spell out?
opciones: Which patients to refer, what information is shared, and each side's role afterward
The fee the specialist will charge and how the two practices split the payment
The number of patients the practice promises to send in a calendar year
Which insurance plans the specialist agrees to accept from those patients
preguntas.explicacion: Referral agreements set out mutual expectations: which patients are appropriate to refer, how the referral is transmitted, what information travels before and after it, appointments held open for urgent referrals, and what each side does once the referral is made. Making the process easy raises the odds the patient follows through.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, "Talking With Your Older Patients", Sensitive topics
preguntas.subtema: Questioning techniques · CCMA 6C k200 · CMAA 2A k15
preguntas.pregunta: A clinician needs to raise alcohol use with an older patient who seems reluctant. Which opening is recommended?
opciones: Framing it as something many people in her situation face
Asking a direct yes-or-no question early in the interview
Handing her a brochure instead of raising it out loud
Asking the companion about it while she is out of the room
preguntas.explicacion: The technique offered for broaching sensitive subjects is a universal, nonthreatening approach that presents the topic as a common concern among older patients, with openings such as many people experience this. Informative brochures left in the exam room are the fallback for patients who still avoid the subject, not the opening move.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Healthcare Professional Burnout", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Professional presence · CCMA 6M k213 · CMAA 2I k24 · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Burnout among health care professionals is described as which three-part response?
opciones: Emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, low accomplishment
Emotional exhaustion, anxiety, and impaired concentration
Irritability, absenteeism, and reduced clinical competence
Fatigue, compassion for patients, and a heavier workload
preguntas.explicacion: Burnout is a job-related stress syndrome built out of exhaustion that is emotional, depersonalization, and a sense of personal accomplishment that has shrunk; it comes of responding over a long stretch to occupational stressors that are chronic. National surveys have repeatedly put prevalence near or above 50 percent, which frames it as a system problem.

preguntas.fuente: VA, CHAMPVA benefits: Eligibility for CHAMPVA
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.d / 2027 III.G.4 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Who may qualify for CHAMPVA?
opciones: The spouse or child of a veteran whose service disability is permanent and total
The veteran herself, whose service disability is rated permanent and total
The spouse or child of a service member who is currently on active-duty status
The parent of a veteran who died while serving in the uniformed services abroad
preguntas.explicacion: CHAMPVA covers the spouse or the dependent child of a veteran whose service-connected disability is rated permanent and total, and the surviving spouse or child of a veteran who died from such a disability or held that rating at death. The veteran's own care comes through the health system for veterans, and families of active-duty members are served by the military program instead.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, HITECH Act Enforcement Interim Final Rule
preguntas.subtema: HIPAA penalties · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3B k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: How many culpability categories does the civil money penalty scheme for HIPAA violations use?
opciones: Four, running from not knowing up to willful neglect that was never corrected
Three, running from an honest mistake up to a deliberate sale of patient records
Two, one for covered entities and a separate one for their business associates
Six, one for each of the circumstances in which records may go to law enforcement
preguntas.explicacion: HITECH set four categories of violation reflecting rising culpability, matched by four tiers of penalty. In order: the entity did not know and would not have known with reasonable diligence; there was reasonable cause but no willful neglect; there was willful neglect but the violation was corrected inside 30 days; and there was willful neglect and no correction.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: When may a three-character code be reported on a claim?
opciones: Only when that category is not subdivided any further
Only when the record supports no more specific code
Only when its index entry ends with a dash after it
Only when the index lists it as the default for the term
preguntas.explicacion: All categories in the tabular list are three characters, and a three-character category with nothing subdivided under it is itself a code. A three-character code is therefore used only when it is not subdivided; where fourth, fifth or sixth characters exist, a code that stops short of them is invalid, and so is one missing an applicable seventh character. A dash at the end of an index entry says the opposite of what the answer offers: that more characters are still required.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication, Use of Accompanying Adults or Children as Interpreters
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.F Laboratory Regulations, ADA · CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA II.F.1.c(2) interpreter · CMAA 3A ADAAA compliance
preguntas.pregunta: A deaf patient asks for a sign language interpreter for a long pre-test discussion. May the laboratory tell him to bring a family member instead?
opciones: No, responsibility for effective communication rests on the covered entity itself
Yes, if that family member signs and agrees to interpret for him on the day
Yes, if hiring an interpreter would be an undue burden for the laboratory
No, unless the laboratory offers video remote interpreting as the alternative
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity may not oblige anyone to bring along a person to interpret. An accompanying adult may interpret in two narrow cases only: an emergency with an imminent threat where no qualified interpreter is at hand, and a non-emergency where the individual asks for it, the adult agrees and it is appropriate. Undue burden does not erase the duty either; it shifts it onto another effective aid.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Defining the PCMH: 3. Coordinated Care
preguntas.subtema: Transition of care · CCMA 4H · CMA II.F.4.a / 2027 II.F.2.a · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: A medical home patient is being discharged from the hospital. Which of the five functions is most in play?
opciones: Coordinated care, which the model calls critical during transitions
Comprehensive care, which makes the practice accountable for most health needs
Accessible services, which shorten waiting times when a need is urgent
Quality and safety, shown by measuring and acting on patient experience
preguntas.explicacion: Coordinated care means the medical home organizes care across the whole health care system: specialty care, hospitals, home health, and the services and supports of the community. The model singles out transitions between sites of care, a hospital discharge for instance, as the moment coordination matters most, and asks for open communication among patient, family and care team.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Communication Styles
preguntas.subtema: Assertive communication · CCMA 6K k203 · CMAA 2A k13 · CMA F.1.e / 2027 F.1.f · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: A coworker keeps leaving exam rooms cluttered for the next shift. Which reply is assertive rather than aggressive?
opciones: "I feel frustrated tidying rooms each shift. Help me understand."
"Why is your area always such a mess? I dread following you."
"It is fine. I will just clean them myself and keep quiet."
"You never think about the next shift when you leave a room."
preguntas.explicacion: Assertive communication states the facts and what the sender feels, with no disrespect toward the receiver, and it leans on "I" messages. "You" messages attack the person instead of the issue and read as aggressive. Absorbing the problem in silence and putting the other person's rights first is the passive style.

preguntas.subtema: Scope of practice · RMA I.C.6 · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k48
preguntas.pregunta: As a general rule, what level of supervision does auxiliary personnel need for services billed as incident to?
opciones: Direct supervision from the physician, or from whoever bills the service
General supervision, with the physician's overall direction only
Personal supervision, with the physician inside the treatment room
No supervision, provided the state license allows the task itself
preguntas.explicacion: Auxiliary personnel are individuals acting under the supervision of a physician or other practitioner, whether employed, leased or contracted, who are not excluded from federal health programs and who meet any state licensure requirements for the service. The general rule is direct supervision, which for some services may be met through real-time audio and video presence, never audio alone. Two named groups drop to general supervision: designated care management services and behavioral health services.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN: NPI - What You Need to Know
preguntas.subtema: NPI entity types · CCMA 5 k183 · CMA III.H.2 · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 6 k89 · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: A group practice and each of its physicians are enrolling. Which NPI entity types apply?
opciones: Type 2 for the organization and Type 1 for each individual provider
Type 1 for the organization and Type 2 for each individual provider
Type 2 for both, since everyone in a group enrolls under the group number
Type 1 for both, since the number always belongs to a licensed human being
preguntas.explicacion: There are two enumeration categories. Entity Type 1 covers individual health care providers, sole proprietors included, and a sole proprietor applies with a Social Security Number rather than an employer identification number even if one exists. Entity Type 2 covers organizations. Students, interns and residents are eligible and must apply. Billing services, clearinghouses and health plans may not obtain one at all.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Administrative Simplification: Code Sets Overview; and MLN Booklet MLN006976, Procedure Coding
preguntas.subtema: Code sets · CMA III.G.1 (2027 III.G.1) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which code set did HIPAA adopt for reporting dental procedures?
opciones: The Code on Dental Procedures and Nomenclature
The national drug codes used for medicines
HCPCS Level II, for supplies and equipment
ICD-10-PCS, for procedures done in facilities
preguntas.explicacion: The code sets named in the HIPAA rules are ICD-10, HCPCS, CPT, the dental procedure code set and the national drug codes. CMS maintains HCPCS Level II but not the dental set, which is why a dental office works from its own list. Drug codes name medicines, not the work done in the operatory.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 18: Attend to Social Needs
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k164 community resources · CMAA 2H k30 · CMA 2027 I.A.6.g(1) barriers
preguntas.pregunta: A patient says she cannot follow the eating plan because there is not enough money for food. What is the practice's role?
opciones: Screen for social needs and link her to community resources, then follow up
Repeat the eating plan in simpler language and check with teach-back
Record the refusal in the chart and revisit the plan at the annual visit
Refer her to a dietitian, who is the only role that handles food access
preguntas.explicacion: Unmet social needs damage health, and food, housing and transportation are the common priorities practices screen for. The work is to learn what the community offers, ask about needs with care, point the patient to the resources, and then follow up to confirm the connection was actually made.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Numbers and Amounts
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A pulse of 48 beats per minute is documented as bradycardia. Which two word parts build that term?
opciones: A prefix meaning slow plus a root meaning heart
A prefix meaning fast plus a root meaning heart
A prefix meaning slow plus a root meaning artery
A prefix meaning half plus a root meaning muscle
preguntas.explicacion: Brady- means slow and tachy- means fast; cardi- and cardio- name the heart. So bradycardia is a slow heart and tachycardia a fast one. The root for artery is arterio-, and my- or myo- names muscle, which is why a heart attack is a myocardial infarction rather than an arterial one.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), Table 1
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMAA 5B k75, 5 k74 · CCMA 5E k182 · CMA III.G.4.d / 2027 III.G.4
preguntas.pregunta: An active-duty service member with both TRICARE and Medicare is treated. Which pays first?
opciones: TRICARE pays first and Medicare pays second for that patient
Medicare pays first and TRICARE pays second for that patient
Medicare pays first for inpatient care and TRICARE for outpatient care
The patient pays first and both programs reimburse him afterward
preguntas.explicacion: In the table of common Medicare Secondary Payer situations, a service member on active-duty status has TRICARE paying first and Medicare second. The order flips for inactive-status members seen by civilian providers, where Medicare pays first; should that inactive member be seen at a military hospital, or by another federal provider, TRICARE pays first again. The split turns on status and setting, not on the type of service.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Administrative Simplification: Health Care Payment and Remittance Advice and EFT; and CMS, Health Care Payment and Remittance Advice
preguntas.subtema: Electronic remittance advice · CMAA 5 k79, 6E · CCMA 5M k182
preguntas.pregunta: A remittance advice arrives with an adjustment the biller does not recognize. Which codes must every payer use to explain an adjustment?
opciones: Claim adjustment reason codes and remittance advice remark codes approved by X12
Claim adjustment reason codes and remark codes each payer designs for its own use
Diagnosis codes and procedure codes copied from the claim that was submitted
Place of service codes and provider level balance codes assigned by the contractor
preguntas.explicacion: Under HIPAA every payer, Medicare included, must use claim adjustment reason codes and remittance advice remark codes approved by the X12 code set maintainers, and proprietary codes of their own are not allowed. The reason code gives the overall explanation of the adjustment and the remark code adds detail. Provider level balance codes explain adjustments not tied to a single claim, a narrower use.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), Repetitive or Continuous Non-covered Care
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMA III.G.3.c (2027 III.G.3.c) · CMAA 5 k77 · CCMA 5 k186
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is midway through a repeated non-covered treatment and nothing about it has changed. Does each session need its own advance written notice?
opciones: No, the first notice holds while the care, her health and the rules stay put
Yes, a fresh notice has to be signed before every session of the course
Yes, but only where the patient asks for another one to be issued
No, and that first notice holds for the rest of her life as a patient
preguntas.explicacion: A notice stays effective after delivery as long as three things hold: the care described on it, the patient's health status, and the coverage rules for those items or services. If any of them changes during treatment, a new notice goes out. For repetitive or continuous care the provider may issue another notice after a year, though nothing requires it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Common Pitfalls
preguntas.subtema: Nontherapeutic responses · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2E k22 · CMA F.2 / 2027 F.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: A patient describes a hard week at home and the assistant begins telling her what to do. Why is unsolicited advice a pitfall?
opciones: The patient may feel it as intrusive and lacking in empathy
It commits the office to a plan no provider has ordered
It counts as practicing outside the assistant's own scope
It shortens the visit and leaves the history incomplete
preguntas.explicacion: Advice the patient never asked for is listed among the approaches with negative therapeutic value: unless she specifically asked, she may feel it as intrusive and lacking in empathy. It sits in the same table as value judgments, negative body language and false reassurance.

preguntas.subtema: Event notifications · CCMA 5 k179 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 7 k90 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital's electronic system sends an event notification when a patient is admitted. Which three items must the message carry at a minimum?
opciones: The patient's name, the treating practitioner's name and the sending institution
The patient's name, the admitting diagnosis and the expected date of discharge
The patient's record number, the insurance plan and the treating practitioner
The patient's name, the reason for the visit and the telephone of the unit
preguntas.explicacion: Where a hospital runs a system meeting the adopted content exchange standard, its notification capacity has to be switched on, and every message has to carry at least three items: who the patient is, which practitioner is treating him, and which institution is sending it. Diagnosis and coverage are outside that minimum.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 9: Assess language preferences
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k166 barriers to care · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.1.c · 2027 F.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: Which question does the toolkit tell staff to ask about language, and why that one?
opciones: What language the patient wants to be spoken to in, since illness erodes English
How well the patient speaks English, since that decides if an interpreter is needed
Whether the patient has a relative who can interpret at the next appointment
What country the patient was born in, since that identifies the language needed
preguntas.explicacion: Every patient is asked what language they want spoken and what language they want written material in, and the answers go in the medical record. Asking preference rather than proficiency matters because people who normally handle English well can lose it when sick, tired or frightened, and because admitting limited English is embarrassing.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Eligibility, Third Party Liability
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMA III.G.4.c (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5B k75 · CCMA 5E k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicaid patient also holds coverage through her husband's employer. Which plan does the practice bill first?
opciones: The employer plan, since Medicaid pays only the portion no third party owes
Medicaid, since a state program always pays ahead of a commercial plan
Whichever plan the patient names, since she may choose the order of payers
Both together, since the two share the bill in proportion to their benefits
preguntas.explicacion: Third party liability means a third party has a legal obligation to pay part or all of the cost of services given to a Medicaid beneficiary, and the examples named are other programs such as Medicare and any other health insurance the person holds. Where such an obligation exists Medicaid pays only its own portion, which is why the other coverage is billed first.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Hospice care: How often; and StatPearls, Hospice Care: Hospice Benefit Periods
preguntas.subtema: Hospice benefit periods · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: A hospice patient is nearing the end of her second 90-day period and the family asks what comes next. How are the periods arranged?
opciones: Two 90-day periods, then an unlimited number of 60-day periods with recertification
Two 60-day periods, then an unlimited number of 90-day periods with recertification
Three 30-day periods, then one final 90-day period that cannot be renewed again
One single 100-day period, the same ceiling that applies inside a skilled nursing facility
preguntas.explicacion: Hospice runs in benefit periods: two of 90 days, followed by an unlimited number of 60-day periods. Before each new period the team re-evaluates the patient and recertifies a terminal illness with a prognosis under 6 months, and each 60-day period also calls for a face-to-face visit by a hospice physician or nurse practitioner. The patient may change hospice once per period.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 2.4
preguntas.subtema: Ransomware prevention · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7H k97 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: An e-mail marked urgent asks a receptionist to open an attachment and confirm her log-in. Which trained response does the guidance describe?
opciones: Hover over the link to read where it goes and check the sender by another route
Open the attachment only if the sender's address matches the practice's domain
Forward it to the whole staff so that everyone recognizes the message on sight
Reply to the same message asking the sender to confirm that it is legitimate
preguntas.explicacion: Malicious attachments and callers asking for log-in details are the usual first step of a ransomware attack. Users are trained to hover first and read the destination address, to weigh the sender, the urgency and the spelling, and, when in doubt, to confirm through a separate channel. Replying in the same thread confirms nothing, since the sender may be the attacker.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(b); StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Selective Access
preguntas.subtema: Minimum necessary in practice · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k36
preguntas.pregunta: A billing clerk asks a phlebotomist for a patient's full medical history to process a claim. Which HIPAA standard is at stake?
opciones: Minimum necessary: limit the PHI to what the payment purpose requires
Right of access: the clerk may see all records that the patient could see herself
Treatment exception: payment staff are exempt from all limits
De-identification: the clerk must receive only coded data
preguntas.explicacion: Payment is a permitted purpose, yet it is not among the exceptions to the minimum necessary standard, so the entity has to make a reasonable effort to hold what the clerk receives down to what processing the claim requires. The treatment exception covers providers treating the patient, not billing. De-identified data would not serve payment, and the right of access belongs to the individual rather than to workforce members. The same principle turns up in guidance that access should match the employee's role, so a laboratory technologist sees laboratory records and not the whole history.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), Issuing a Notice
preguntas.subtema: Documentation for billing · CMAA 6A, 5 k69 · CCMA 5J k180
preguntas.pregunta: Why does every billed service have to point to a sign, symptom or complaint in the record?
opciones: Because the documentation is what shows the service was reasonable and necessary
Because the payer needs the symptom to decide which fee schedule amount applies
Because the diagnosis code determines the place of service reported on the claim
Because the coding guidelines require a symptom code on every claim submitted
preguntas.explicacion: Each service billed has to point to the particular sign, the symptom or the complaint from the patient that makes it reasonable and necessary; that is how the record supports coverage under the national or local policy for the service. The fee schedule amount follows the procedure reported, the place of service is a separate two-digit code, and symptom codes come in when no diagnosis is confirmed, not on every claim.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Administrative Simplification: Health Care Payment and Remittance Advice and EFT
preguntas.subtema: Electronic funds transfer · CMAA 5 k79, 6B · CCMA 5K k182
preguntas.pregunta: What is an electronic funds transfer in health care payment?
opciones: The message a plan sends a bank to move the payment into the provider's account
The message a plan sends a provider listing the adjustments made on each claim
The message a provider sends a plan asking for payment for services delivered
The message a clearinghouse sends a provider confirming that claims were accepted
preguntas.explicacion: An electronic funds transfer is the message a health plan uses to order a financial institution to move funds electronically into the provider's account, carrying the amount, the payer and payee identification, the bank accounts, routing numbers and payment date. The explanation of the adjustments is the remittance advice, and the request for payment is the claim itself.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.6 Anatomical Terminology, Anatomical Position
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k36 · CMA I.C.6.e (2027 I.C.6.d) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k11 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A scar is documented as being in the anterior carpal region. Which surface of the wrist does that describe?
opciones: The palm side, because anterior is defined from anatomical position
The back side, because anterior is defined from the resting hand
The thumb side, because anterior is defined from the midline
The little finger side, because anterior follows the ulnar edge
preguntas.explicacion: Every directional term is read as if the body were in anatomical position: standing upright, feet forward, arms out to the sides and palms facing forward. In that position the palm faces front, so an anterior carpal scar is on the palm side, and it keeps that name even when the hand is lying palm down on a table.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Bloodborne Pathogens and Needlestick Prevention: Standards
preguntas.subtema: Laws and regulations · CCMA 7A k214 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: What did the Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act lead to?
opciones: A revision of the bloodborne pathogens standard, with a sharps injury log
A new federal agency dedicated to investigating percutaneous injuries
A requirement that every needlestick be reported to the state health board
A ban on all needle devices that are not fitted with a retracting sheath
preguntas.explicacion: The act became public law on November 6, 2000, and in 2001 the bloodborne pathogens standard was revised in response. Among other things the revised standard calls for engineering and work practice controls to remove or reduce exposure to blood and to other material that is potentially infectious, and it requires employers to keep a sharps injury log recording every percutaneous injury caused by a contaminated sharp.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, How Medicare works with other insurance; and CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), Paid Promptly
preguntas.subtema: Claim follow-up · CMA III.G.3.b(5) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6 k87 · CCMA 5M
