preguntas.pregunta: An insurer that should pay before Medicare has sat on a claim for four months. What may happen next?
opciones: The provider may bill Medicare, which can pay conditionally and recover it later
The provider may bill the patient, who then goes after the insurer for the money
The provider may bill Medicare, which pays and closes the matter with the insurer
The provider may bill the insurer again and wait a second 120 days for an answer
preguntas.explicacion: Where the insurance company does not pay promptly, which usually means inside 120 days, the bill may go to Medicare from the doctor or other provider. A conditional payment can then be made so the bill is settled, and Medicare recovers afterwards whatever the primary payer should have paid. For no-fault and workers' compensation claims with no ongoing responsibility, promptness is measured as 120 days from the day that insurer received the claim.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Body Parts and Disorders
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k12 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient points to the breastbone and asks for its medical name. Which root names that bone?
opciones: Stern-, for the sternum
Cost-, for the ribs
Spondyl-, for a vertebra
Phalang-, for a finger bone
preguntas.explicacion: Stern- names the sternum, the bone people call the breastbone. Several roots in this vocabulary come with their plain-language gloss attached, which is what makes them useful at the bedside: cost- is a rib, spondyl- a vertebra of the spine and phalang- any bone in the fingers or toes.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Requests for Access
preguntas.subtema: Access requests · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks for his records and refuses to say what he wants them for. How should the office respond?
opciones: Process the request, because a covered entity may not require a reason for wanting access
Hold the request until he states a purpose the office can record on its own access form
Deny the request, since a stated purpose is one of the elements of a valid access request
Refer him to the privacy official, who alone may waive the requirement to state a purpose
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity may require that access requests be in writing and may use its own form, but only if that does not become a barrier or an unreasonable delay. OCR states plainly that the entity may not require the individual to give a reason, and that a rationale volunteered or already known is not a permitted ground for denying access.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting started with telehealth, Finding a telehealth vendor
preguntas.subtema: Choosing a platform · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice is comparing telehealth platforms and wants the scheduling desk's questions on the list. Which questions belong to that desk's concerns?
opciones: Whether there is a waiting room feature and whether staff or patients can book visits on the platform
Whether there is a waiting room feature and whether the vendor will train the practice's clinicians
Whether the product is compliant with privacy law and whether a written contract is required
Whether patients must download an application and whether the vendor stores the recordings
preguntas.explicacion: The questions suggested for researching a platform include whether it is compliant with privacy law, whether a contract is required, whether it integrates with the record system, whether it will be easy for patients, whether there is a waiting room feature, whether staff or patients can schedule visits through the platform itself, and whether patients can give consent on it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Specific Techniques
preguntas.subtema: Therapeutic techniques · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2A k13 · CMA F.1.c(7)(a) / 2027 F.1.d(7)(b)
preguntas.pregunta: A new patient in her seventies is being roomed for the first time. How should the assistant introduce themselves and address her?
opciones: By first and last name, addressing the patient formally
By first name only, addressing the patient by first name
By role only, addressing the patient by the room number
By last name only, addressing the patient as dear or honey
preguntas.explicacion: Introducing yourself with first and last names and addressing the patient by a title and last name shows respect for their dignity and autonomy; gender-neutral wording and chosen pronouns belong here too. Older patients in particular may expect formal address, and terms such as dear can land as disrespect.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Competency and Capacity", Issues of Concern: Ethical Principles Involved; and StatPearls, "Medical Ethics" (NBK535361)
preguntas.subtema: Unbiased care · CCMA 7G · CMA E.7 / 2027 E.6 · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: An uninsured patient and an insured patient need the same limited resource. What does the ethical framework require?
opciones: Fair distribution regardless of insurance status or social standing
Priority for the insured patient, because the cost is already covered
Priority for the uninsured patient, to correct the existing imbalance
A decision by the business manager, who is accountable for the budget
preguntas.explicacion: The principle of justice tells the practitioner to distribute medical resources fairly and equitably, whatever the patient's demographics, insurance, socioeconomic position or mental disability. At the bedside that means rationing the good that can be done evenly and equitably among the patients involved, rather than sorting them by who pays.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: The Intervention
preguntas.subtema: Open access, the two meanings · CMAA 4A k51 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A manager reads that her group is moving to open access and assumes patients will now be able to go straight to a specialist. Why is she mistaken?
opciones: In the scheduling literature the phrase means same-day appointments, not direct specialist access
In the scheduling literature the phrase means direct specialist access, not same-day appointments
In the scheduling literature the phrase means dropping referrals for established patients only
In the scheduling literature the phrase means open enrollment, so any patient may join the panel
preguntas.explicacion: The phrase carries two meanings. In managed care it is sometimes used for removing the gatekeeper so that patients reach specialists directly. In the appointment literature, where it is also called advanced access or same-day scheduling, it means only that every patient can be given a slot on the day she calls, almost always with her own physician.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Documentation for billing · CMAA 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · CMA III.G.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: Where should the search for a diagnosis code always begin?
opciones: In the alphabetic index, before the entry is verified in the tabular list
In the tabular list, before the entry is checked against the alphabetic index
In the payer's coverage policy for the service that was performed that day
In the previous claim for the patient, so the coding stays consistent over time
preguntas.explicacion: The guidelines call it the most critical rule: begin the search for the correct code in the alphabetic index and never start in the tabular list, because starting there leads to coding errors. Coverage policies decide payment, not code selection, and copying a code from an earlier claim skips the documentation of this encounter.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Medicare Advantage Plan (Part C) costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient in a Medicare Advantage Plan asks whether joining it ends her monthly Part B bill.
opciones: No, she must keep Part B and go on paying that premium to stay in the plan
Yes, the plan takes the place of Part B and of the premium that goes with it
Yes, provided the plan she joined also includes prescription drug coverage
No, but the Part B premium is refunded to her each year by the plan itself
preguntas.explicacion: Premiums, deductibles, copayments and coinsurance under a Medicare Advantage Plan vary by plan and can change every year, and the condition Medicare states plainly is that the enrollee must have Part B and keep paying the Part B premium in order to stay in the plan. Some plans do help pay that premium, but the requirement to hold Part B does not disappear.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Confidential Communications Requirements
preguntas.subtema: Confidential communications · CCMA 6 k204 · CMA II.F.4 · RMA II.B.3.g · CMAA 4 k62 · NCMA 3.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks that appointment calls go to her work number rather than her home. What must the office do?
opciones: Accommodate her reasonable request that confidential communications go to another number
Refuse, because the number in the demographic record is the only one the office may dial
Require a signed authorization naming the workplace as a permitted disclosure location
Send the reminder by postcard instead, since written notice avoids the problem entirely
preguntas.explicacion: Health plans and covered providers have to let individuals ask that communications reach them by some other means or at some other location. The rule's example is a patient asking to be telephoned at her office instead of her home, and a provider must accommodate such a request where it is reasonable. The parallel example for written mail is asking for a closed envelope in place of a postcard.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information: Providing the Notice
preguntas.subtema: Electronic delivery of the notice · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks the desk to e-mail her the notice of privacy practices rather than take a paper copy home. May the office do that?
opciones: Yes, once she has said she will take the notice electronically rather than on paper
Yes, once the message has been encrypted and a read receipt has been returned
No, a direct treatment provider always hands the notice over on paper at the first visit
No, unless her first contact with the practice was made over the internet or by e-mail
preguntas.explicacion: The rule lets a covered entity e-mail the notice to an individual who has agreed to that form of delivery. That is a separate matter from the online-intake rule, under which a provider whose first service arrives electronically sends the notice automatically with the first request for service and tries for a return receipt.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 1.2
preguntas.subtema: Backup power · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: What does the contingency guidance expect of the power arrangements behind the record system?
opciones: An uninterrupted supply for at least ten minutes and a generator with fuel for two days
An uninterrupted supply for at least one hour and a generator with fuel for one day
A generator alone, tested each year, since the record system restarts by itself after a cut
A second electricity contract with another company, switched over by the building's staff
preguntas.explicacion: Two layers are described. A battery or flywheel supply carries the record system instantly for at least ten minutes, and it is tested regularly, optimally monthly. Behind it sits an on-site generator able to keep the functions critical to operations running, with two days of fuel held on site, tested monthly and kept where flooding is unlikely.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Helping patients prepare for their telehealth appointment
preguntas.subtema: Appointment setup instructions · CMAA 4E k59 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: The clinician will need to look at a rash on the patient's shoulder by video. Which instruction does the setup guidance give her beforehand?
opciones: To wear loose clothing, so that she can show the part of the body in question
To sit with the window behind her, so that the strongest light falls on the camera
To hold the device in her hand and move it about as the clinician asks her to
To sit far enough back that her whole body stays inside the picture throughout
preguntas.explicacion: The advice on getting set up is to choose a spot with plenty of light and avoid sitting with the back towards a window, since that makes the face harder to see; to keep the camera steady and at eye level with head and shoulders in view; to wear loose clothing where the clinician needs to see skin or a particular part of the body; and to cut background noise and distractions.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Conflict Management", Issues of Concern: Conflict Management Styles
preguntas.subtema: Conflict management · CCMA 6J k209 · CMAA 2B k26 · CMA F.1.f / 2027 F.1.f
preguntas.pregunta: When is a competing style the appropriate way to handle a conflict?
opciones: In a real emergency, or to stop behavior that is unethical
When feelings need to cool or the stakes are trivial anyway
When the working relationship matters more than the issue
When two parties of equal power are short of time to decide
preguntas.explicacion: Competing is high on assertiveness and low on cooperativeness, and it fits genuine emergencies, decisions that are unpopular but necessary, and standing against unethical behavior. Making a habit of it damages psychological safety. The other three options are the situations that suit avoiding, accommodating and compromising.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Health Savings Account (HSA)
preguntas.subtema: Commercial plan types · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what a health savings account can be used for. Which answer is correct?
opciones: Untaxed dollars for qualified medical expenses, but generally not for premiums
Untaxed dollars for premiums, but generally not for deductibles or copayments
Employer dollars that are lost in full if they are not spent by the plan year end
Plan dollars that pay the provider directly once the out-of-pocket limit is reached
preguntas.explicacion: A health savings account lets a person set money aside before taxes and spend it on qualified medical costs such as deductibles, copayments and coinsurance; the funds generally may not go toward premiums, and only someone with an HSA-eligible plan may contribute. The use-it-or-lose-it design with an employer-set limit describes a flexible spending arrangement instead, and no savings account pays providers on the plan's behalf.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Health Topic: Patient Rights, Where can I get help; StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Who Monitors; 45 CFR 164.530(d) and (g)
preguntas.subtema: Privacy complaints · CPT D1 k13 k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33
preguntas.pregunta: Where can a patient file a complaint about a violation of their health information privacy rights?
opciones: With the HHS Office for Civil Rights
With the state insurance oversight agency
With the hospital's patient advocate only
With the long-term care ombudsman office
preguntas.explicacion: The Office for Civil Rights, at the federal Department of Health and Human Services, takes complaints from people who believe their health information privacy rights were violated, or who were discriminated against in their medical care; it investigates, audits, and may pass criminal matters to the Department of Justice. Patient advocates, state health departments, insurance oversight agencies and long-term care ombudsman offices handle other kinds of problem. A covered entity must also run its own complaint process and may not retaliate against anyone who files.

preguntas.fuente: Child Welfare Information Gateway, Mandatory Reporting of Child Abuse and Neglect (May 2023), Reporting by Other Persons; and Child Welfare Information Gateway, Mandatory Reporting of Child Abuse and Neglect - State Statutes
preguntas.subtema: Mandatory reporting · CCMA 7F k222 · CMA E.6.c / 2027 E.5.b · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k43
preguntas.pregunta: A receptionist with no clinical role suspects a child in the waiting room is being abused. May she report it?
opciones: Yes: every jurisdiction permits any person to report a suspicion
Yes, but only in the 17 states where all persons must report
No: reports from staff outside clinical roles are not accepted
No: the report has to come from the child's treating clinician
preguntas.explicacion: Every state, every territory and the District of Columbia permits any person to report where there is reason to believe a child has been abused or neglected; such voluntary reporters are called permissive reporters. Roughly 17 states and Puerto Rico go further and require any person to report, and four of them list no professions at all.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medicare: Summary; and Medicare.gov, Parts of Medicare
preguntas.subtema: Government insurance plans · CCMA 5 k181 · CMAA 6 k74 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A 62-year-old patient with permanent kidney failure asks whether she can have Medicare. Who is the program for?
opciones: People age 65 or older, and some under 65 with a disability or kidney failure
People with low income, under the rules that each state writes for itself
Children in families that earn too much to qualify for the state plan
Workers whose employer purchases the coverage as a benefit of the job
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare is the health insurance program the government runs for people aged 65 or over. Some people under 65 qualify too: those with disabilities, with permanent kidney failure or with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. It helps with the cost of care without covering every medical expense, and it has four parts: A for hospital insurance, B for medical services, C for Advantage plans and D for prescription drugs.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 1.4
preguntas.subtema: Backup practice · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: What backup arrangement does the contingency guidance describe for patient data?
opciones: A daily, complete, encrypted copy held off site and restored as a test regularly
A weekly complete copy kept on a second drive inside the same server cabinet
A monthly copy of the day's new entries stored with the software developer
A copy made each time the system is upgraded and kept until the next upgrade
preguntas.explicacion: What is recommended is a complete backup, encrypted and taken off site, every day, with the most critical data copied as near to real time as can be managed. Restoring the whole system and the patient data is tested regularly, monthly at best, and the media are kept physically apart from the working data, air-gapped ideally, so ransomware cannot reach them.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Error Reduction and Prevention", Function: Near miss event
preguntas.subtema: Incident reporting · CCMA 7F · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3E k44
preguntas.pregunta: A wrong medication is caught by the pharmacist before it reaches the patient. What is that called, and what should follow?
opciones: A near miss, and it deserves the same scrutiny as an event that caused harm
A near miss, and no report is needed at all because the patient was not harmed
An adverse event, and the patient must be told before the shift is over
A sentinel event, and the accrediting body must be notified immediately
preguntas.explicacion: A near miss is an error that could have harmed the patient but did not, because someone intervened or because of chance. It is identical to an adverse event except for the outcome, which is exactly why it should get the same scrutiny: it shows the weakness without the cost. An adverse event means the patient was actually injured.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Interview Techniques", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Questioning techniques · CCMA 6C k200 · CMAA 2A k15
preguntas.pregunta: Before asking about drinking, the interviewer remarks that many people drink more under stress. What is that meant to do?
opciones: Lower the patient's defensiveness so more is shared
Confirm the diagnosis the interviewer already suspects
Give the patient permission to skip over the question
Meet the duty to say why the information is needed
preguntas.explicacion: Meaningful, positive questions reduce defensiveness during the interview, and one way of doing that is to suggest a behavior commonly associated with the patient's situation, such as people drinking when under stress, before asking whether it applies. The patient may then feel enough trust to share what matters.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, HCAHPS: Patients' Perspectives of Care Survey, HCAHPS Overview
preguntas.subtema: Patient satisfaction surveys · CCMA 6J k207 · CMAA 2B k16
preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about the HCAHPS survey is accurate?
opciones: It was the first national, standardized, public hospital survey
It was the first survey of experience with private health plans
It is the ambulatory survey about the patient's most recent visit
It is the survey administered only to Medicare beneficiaries
preguntas.explicacion: HCAHPS was the first survey of patients' perspectives on hospital care to be national, standardized and publicly reported, and that is what makes valid comparisons between hospitals possible. It reaches a random sample of adult patients somewhere between 48 hours and six weeks after they leave, and is not restricted to Medicare beneficiaries.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow, Preparing for telehealth visits
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth access route · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5U k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice is deciding how patients will reach the video visits it books. Which route does the workflow guidance name?
opciones: Through the patient portal, with an e-mail or text reminder sent before the appointment
Through a link the clinician reads out over the telephone as the appointment begins
Through whichever public video service the patient already has on her own telephone
Through an address on the practice web site that any visitor is able to join
preguntas.explicacion: Among the technology questions to settle in advance is how patients will reach a telehealth appointment, and the example given is through a patient portal, with an e-mail or text reminder. The same guidance asks whether the platform is easy to use and whether it merges with the electronic health record, and the platform itself has to meet the HIPAA Rules.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Personal Health Records
preguntas.subtema: Personal health record · CCMA 5 k172 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.a · CMAA k3 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what a personal health record is. Which description fits?
opciones: A record the patient keeps herself, pulling together what several offices hold about her
The legal chart the practice maintains, printed and handed to the patient once a year
The set of records a health plan keeps to adjudicate the claims it has received
The archive a hospital keeps of records for patients who have moved out of the area
preguntas.explicacion: A patient may have charts at several doctors' offices and another at a hospital, on paper or electronically, and those charts are the medical records. Keeping track of all of it is the reason for a personal health record, which starts with items such as name, birth date, blood type, emergency contact and a list of medicines and supplements with doses and how long they have been taken.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Drug plan coverage rules: Step therapy
preguntas.subtema: Medication authorization · CMA III.G.5.a(2) (2027 III.G.5.a(2)) · CMAA 4G k67 · CCMA 5H k183 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: The office is gathering what the prescriber must send to win a step therapy exception. What has to be in his supporting statement?
opciones: That the costlier drug is medically necessary, or the cheaper one would harm her or fail
That the cheaper drug on the plan's list is beyond what the patient can afford to pay
That the cheaper drug is out of stock at the pharmacy the patient normally uses
That the plan itself covered the costlier drug for this patient in an earlier year
preguntas.explicacion: Step therapy is a form of prior authorization that makes the patient try a cheaper drug proven effective for most people with her condition first. The prescriber may ask for an exception with a statement supporting his belief that the costlier drug is medically necessary for her condition, that the cheaper one would have adverse effects, or that it would be less effective.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Hospice Care: Hospice Interprofessional Team
preguntas.subtema: Team-based care in hospice · CCMA 4G k167 · CMA II.F.4.c / 2027 II.F.2.c · CMAA 1 k1 · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which staff make up the core hospice team that Medicare requires the agency itself to employ?
opciones: The hospice nurse, the social worker and the chaplain, plus the medical director
The home health aide, the physical therapist and the dietitian who visit the home
The attending clinician, the consultant subspecialist and the pharmacist on call
The case manager, the patient navigator and the volunteer coordinator on staff
preguntas.explicacion: The core hospice team is the nurse, the social worker and the chaplain, and those members must be employed by the hospice agency. The hospice medical director also belongs to the interdisciplinary team. Together they build an individual plan of care for each patient and family, covering physical needs and psychological, social and spiritual ones, with the nurse coordinating.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A triage note reads: patient reports SOB on climbing stairs. What is the patient describing?
opciones: Shortness of breath during exertion
Soreness of the back during exertion
Swelling of both legs during exertion
Stiffness of both knees during exertion
preguntas.explicacion: SOB is the charted shorthand for shortness of breath, a symptom the patient reports rather than a sign anyone can observe. Written out it belongs with the respiratory complaints, and it is one of the entries that should be spelled out in anything the patient will read at home.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Burden of Proof
preguntas.subtema: Breach documentation · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3E k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: After deciding an impermissible disclosure was not a breach, what does the practice have to be able to show?
opciones: Documentation of the risk assessment or of the exception it relied on
A signed statement from the patient agreeing that no harm was done
A letter from the Office for Civil Rights closing the matter without action
A note in the chart of every patient the practice treated on the same day
preguntas.explicacion: Proving that every required notification went out, or that a use or disclosure was not a breach at all, falls on the covered entity or the business associate. It should hold on to either the risk assessment showing a low probability that PHI was compromised, or evidence that one of the exceptions applied. Entities also have to keep written breach policies, train staff on them, and sanction workforce members who do not comply.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN006903 Medicare Secondary Payer
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.b / 2027 III.G.4 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: What does a Medigap policy do?
opciones: It helps pay the patient's share of costs left by Original Medicare
It helps pay the patient's share of costs left by a Medicare drug plan
It replaces Part A and Part B with benefits from a private insurer
It pays the Part B premium for beneficiaries with limited resources
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare Supplement Insurance, or Medigap, is bought from a private company to help with copayments, coinsurance and deductibles in Original Medicare, and a person must have Part A and Part B to buy it. Coverage that stands in for Part A and Part B is Medicare Advantage. Paying the Part B premium for people with limited income and resources is what Medicaid does for dually eligible patients.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.3 Active Listening and Attending Behaviors
preguntas.subtema: Active listening · CCMA 6C k202 · CMAA 2A k21 · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: During a report a coworker keeps steering the exchange back to his own view of the case. Which type of listening is that?
opciones: Competitive listening
Reflective listening
Attending behavior
Passive listening
preguntas.explicacion: Three types of listening are described. Competitive listening is being focused on putting your own point of view across instead of hearing the other person. Passive listening is a lack of interest plus the assumption that you understood without checking. Active listening shows interest and verifies understanding with the speaker, and reflecting is one of its techniques.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Home health services: Coverage details
preguntas.subtema: Resources for clinical services · CCMA 4D k162 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: Which service belongs to Medicare-covered home health care?
opciones: Medical social services, alongside skilled nursing and therapy visits
Homemaker services such as shopping and cleaning, ordered by the family
Around-the-clock nursing coverage in the home, ordered by the provider
Custodial personal care alone, when no skilled service is being given
preguntas.explicacion: Covered home health takes in medically necessary skilled nursing on a part-time or intermittent basis, therapy that is physical or occupational, speech-language pathology services, medical social services, part-time aide care, injectable drugs for osteoporosis where the woman meets the criteria, durable medical equipment, and supplies for use at home.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Appeals in Original Medicare
preguntas.subtema: Denials and appeals · CMAA 6E · CCMA 5M · CMA III.G.5.b / 2027 III.G.3.b
preguntas.pregunta: The first-level Medicare appeal was decided against the patient. How long does she have to ask for the second level?
opciones: 180 days from the decision letter, to request a reconsideration by a QIC
60 days from the decision letter, to request a reconsideration by a QIC
30 days from the decision letter, to request a hearing before a judge
12 months from the date of service, the same limit that applies to claims
preguntas.explicacion: After the redetermination, the patient has 180 days from the decision letter or the summary notice to ask a qualified independent contractor for a reconsideration, which is level 2. The 60-day figure is the window for moving from level 2 to level 3 and from level 3 to level 4, and 12 months is the deadline for filing the claim itself, not for appealing.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Issues of Concern: Medical Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Emergency treatment · CPT D1 1D k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 1A k2 · CMA II.E.3 · RMA I.C.2 · NCMA 4.2 · CMAA 3B k34
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with no insurance arrives at an emergency department in crisis. Which federal law applies?
opciones: The one requiring an attempt to stabilize, whatever the ability to pay
The one requiring a written estimate before any care is given
The one requiring transfer to a public hospital within the hour
The one requiring the plan to be billed before treatment begins
preguntas.explicacion: The Emergency Medical Treatment and Active Labor Act, passed inside a budget reconciliation law, obliges an organization that devotes at least a third of its services to emergency care to attempt to stabilize an emergency condition whether or not the person is able to pay for it. It exists because patients known or suspected to be unable to pay were being turned away. What counts as an emergency, and when a patient is stable enough to stop, is left to each organization to interpret.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Interview Techniques", Issues of Concern: Common Interview Mistakes
preguntas.subtema: Questioning techniques · CCMA 6C k200 · CMAA 2A k15 · CMA F.5.b / 2027 F.3.b
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is listed as a common mistake in a medical interview?
opciones: Settling on a diagnosis too early in the interview
Going back to the patient for further clarification
Opening with a question that has no fixed answer
Assessing the patient's emotions early in the process
preguntas.explicacion: The mistakes listed are asking too many focused questions, passing over what the patient feels, narrowing the differential or landing on a diagnosis too early, refusing to go back for clarification, skipping introductions and relationship building, asking no open-ended questions, and interrupting. The other three options are what the article recommends.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Designated Record Set
preguntas.subtema: Designated record set · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which category of information is expressly excluded from the individual's right of access?
opciones: Psychotherapy notes kept separate from the rest of the patient's medical record
Laboratory results, which the patient obtains from the testing laboratory instead
Billing and payment records, which belong to the revenue cycle rather than the chart
Medical images such as X-rays, because they are not readily producible on paper
preguntas.explicacion: Two categories are excluded outright: psychotherapy notes, meaning a mental health provider's own notes on a counseling session kept apart from the record, and information gathered because a legal proceeding is expected or under way. Otherwise the right of access is broad; it expressly reaches insurance information, billing and payment records, laboratory results, and medical images like X-rays.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Business Associate Defined
preguntas.subtema: Business associates · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3B k33 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: The practice hires an outside company to process its claims. Under the Privacy Rule, what is that company?
opciones: A business associate, because it performs a function for the practice that uses patient information
A member of the practice workforce, because it handles the same records the front desk handles
A health care clearinghouse, because any outside company that touches claims fits that definition
An ordinary supplier outside the rule, since only entities that treat patients are regulated
preguntas.explicacion: A business associate is a person or an organization outside the workforce that performs functions or supplies services for a covered entity where the work involves using or disclosing health information that identifies an individual. Processing claims, analyzing data, reviewing utilization and doing the billing are the functions named. Someone whose work never touches PHI is not one.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: COBRA
preguntas.subtema: Coverage continuation · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's job ended last month and he kept his employer coverage under COBRA. What changed for him?
opciones: He now pays the full premium, including the employer's old share, plus a small fee
He now pays the same share of the premium he paid while he was still employed
He now pays no premium, and the plan bills the former employer for the coverage
He now pays a premium set by the Marketplace, based on his household income
preguntas.explicacion: COBRA is the federal law that lets a person keep employer coverage for a time after the job ends, after losing dependent status, or after another qualifying event. Whoever elects it pays 100% of the premium, the portion the employer used to cover included, plus a small administrative charge. Nothing shifts the cost back to the employer, and income-based premiums belong to Marketplace coverage instead.

preguntas.fuente: NAIC, Coordination of Benefits Model Regulation (Model 120), Order of Benefit Determination Rules
preguntas.subtema: Insurance rules · CMAA 5B k75 · CCMA 5E k182
preguntas.pregunta: A patient kept coverage through COBRA and is also a dependent on her spouse's active employer plan. Which plan is primary?
opciones: The spouse's employer plan, with the continuation coverage paying second
The continuation coverage, with the spouse's employer plan paying second
The plan whose subscriber has the earlier birthday in the calendar year
The plan that has covered the patient for the shorter period of time
preguntas.explicacion: When someone holds continuation coverage under COBRA or a state law and is also covered under another plan as an employee, member, subscriber, retiree or their dependent, that other plan is primary and the continuation coverage is secondary. The rule is ignored if the other plan lacks it and the two disagree, and it does not apply when the non-dependent or dependent rule already decides.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, I-PASS; and Team Performance Observation Tool
preguntas.subtema: Transitions of care · CCMA 4H k167 · CMAA 2F
preguntas.pregunta: Which tool is named the preferred handoff for patient transitions in care?
opciones: I-PASS, running illness severity through synthesis
SBAR, running situation through the recommendation
DESC, running describe through to consequences
STEP, running status through progress toward a goal
preguntas.explicacion: I-PASS is the handoff tool named for transitions in care. SBAR carries critical information that needs immediate attention, DESC is the constructive script for resolving conflict, and STEP is the situation-monitoring tool covering the status of the patient, team members, environment and progress toward the goal.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3636, Hazard Communication Standard: Labels and Pictograms, Pictograms; and OSHA, 29 CFR 1910.1030 (texto oficial en osha.gov)
preguntas.subtema: Pictogram design · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.a / 2027 I.B.6.a · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: How is a GHS hazard pictogram drawn on a shipped chemical label?
opciones: A black symbol on a white background inside a red square frame set on a point
A black symbol on a fluorescent orange background with the legend BIOHAZARD
A red symbol on a white background inside a black diamond used for transport
A black symbol inside a red square frame that may be left empty as a design element
preguntas.explicacion: A pictogram on a shipped container is a red square frame standing on one point, with a black symbol for the hazard set on white inside it, drawn wide enough to be seen clearly. A red frame left empty, with no symbol in it, is not a pictogram and has no place on the label. The fluorescent orange label carrying the BIOHAZARD legend belongs to the bloodborne pathogens standard, and the diamond-shaped transport labels are what the Department of Transportation requires for shipping, which the OSHA pictograms do not replace.

preguntas.fuente: HRSA, Health Center Program Compliance Manual, Chapter 9: Sliding Fee Discount Program
preguntas.subtema: Financial considerations · CMA III.G.6.e (exam from July 2027) · CMAA 6 k83 · CCMA 5E k178
preguntas.pregunta: A health center gives a patient below the poverty guidelines a full discount but still asks her for a small fixed amount. Is that allowed?
opciones: Yes, a nominal charge may be kept for those patients
No, a full discount rules out any charge at all
Yes, but only where the patient holds other insurance
No, unless the state has approved that fixed amount
preguntas.explicacion: The schedule of discounts has to discount in full for anyone whose family income sits at or below the federal poverty guidelines, except that the center may collect a nominal charge. The charge has to be nominal from the patient's point of view, must not reflect what the service costs, and stays below the fee of the first pay class above that line.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Utilize standardized notification procedures
preguntas.subtema: Patient-initiated ending · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.b · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient writes that she is leaving the practice for a clinician nearer her home. Does the office owe her a termination notice?
opciones: No, though a letter confirming her decision is wise and cuts the risk of a later claim
Yes, and the same thirty days of care and medication refills still have to be offered
Yes, and it has to travel by certified mail with a return receipt like any other notice
No, and no letter should go out either, since the record closes with her last visit
preguntas.explicacion: When it is the patient who has ended the relationship, no termination notice is owed by the physician. Putting her decision on paper in a short letter is still the prudent move: it removes the ambiguity and lowers the exposure to a legal claim. The thirty days that are usually deemed reasonable, and the certified mail, attach to a termination the practice itself starts.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, General Compliance Program Guidance (2023), Compliance Programs for Small Entities
preguntas.subtema: Auditing and compliance · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: A two-physician practice cannot support a compliance officer even part-time. What does the OIG guidance suggest?
opciones: Naming a compliance contact, kept clear of billing and coding
Naming the office manager who runs the billing and the coding
Hiring an outside auditor to act as the compliance officer
Leaving the seven elements aside until the practice grows
preguntas.explicacion: A small entity still works through the seven elements, scaled to what it can carry. Where no compliance officer is possible, one person is designated as the compliance contact and made responsible for seeing the compliance work done; that person should be kept out of legal services and, wherever possible, out of billing, coding and claim submission.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Accountable care organization
preguntas.subtema: Delivery models · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: Which description matches an accountable care organization?
opciones: A group of providers giving coordinated care and chronic disease management
A plan that contracts with a network and limits care to providers inside it
A clinic funded by the federal government to serve an underserved population
A center certified to give surgery to patients who go home the same day
preguntas.explicacion: An accountable care organization is a group of health care providers who deliver coordinated care and chronic disease management, improving the quality of care patients get. Its payment is tied to reaching quality goals and outcomes that produce cost savings. Managed care networks, health centers and surgical centers are different arrangements altogether.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Access to Medical Care for Individuals with Mobility Disabilities: Services and Facilities
preguntas.subtema: Reasonable modifications · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.c · CMAA 7 k98 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks for a change in how the office usually does things so that she can be seen. What is the limit on that duty?
opciones: The change is made unless it would alter the essential nature of the service
The change is made unless another patient objects to the way it affects his visit
The change is made unless it costs the practice more than a routine visit is paid
The change is made unless the practice has already made one for her this year
preguntas.explicacion: Providers owe full and equal access, and along with it modifications to policies, to practices and to procedures that are reasonable, whenever such a change is what makes the service fully available to a person with a disability. The single boundary written into the duty is a change that would alter the essential nature of what the practice does.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · CMA III.G.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: An Excludes1 note appears under a diagnosis code. What does it tell the coder?
opciones: The excluded code is never reported at the same time as the code above the note
The excluded code may be reported with it whenever the record supports both
The excluded code replaces the one above the note for outpatient encounters
The excluded code is reported first, with the code above it sequenced second
preguntas.explicacion: Excludes1 is a pure excludes note meaning not coded here: the two conditions cannot occur together, as with a congenital and an acquired form of the same problem, so the codes are not reported for the same encounter. The exception is when the two conditions are clearly unrelated, and when that is unclear the provider should be queried. Excludes2 is the note that allows both codes together.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Other Issues
preguntas.subtema: De-escalation · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k26 · CMA F.1.f / 2027 F.1.f
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant is verbally de-escalating an agitated patient in an exam room. What does the guidance say about the room itself?
opciones: Keep an awareness of the exits and let the patient leave easily
Stand between the patient and the door leading to the hallway
Close the door and the curtain to protect the patient's privacy
Sit right beside the patient so the room does not feel isolating
preguntas.explicacion: Verbal de-escalation techniques overlap with therapeutic communication and add a few of their own: a moderate distance without looking guarded, calm and open body language and tone, standing at a right angle to the person, and keeping an awareness of the exits so the person can walk out. Closing the door is a privacy technique for an ordinary interview.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, What Is Health Literacy? Overview
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k166 barriers to care · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.3.a · 2027 F.1.h · RMA I.D.1.c communication methods
preguntas.pregunta: How is personal health literacy defined since the 2020 update?
opciones: How far a person can locate health information and services, grasp them and use them
How far a person can read and pronounce common medical words correctly
How far a person can obtain and process basic information about a diagnosis
How many years of formal schooling a person has completed before adulthood
preguntas.explicacion: The definition was rewritten in August 2020 with Healthy People 2030. Personal health literacy measures how far someone can locate information and services, grasp them, and put them to use in making health decisions for herself and for others. The wording deliberately moved from merely understanding information to being able to act on it.

preguntas.fuente: plainlanguage.gov, Federal plain language guidelines
preguntas.subtema: Plain language · CCMA 6 k206 · CMA II.F.2 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7G k95 · NCMA 3.2
preguntas.pregunta: Which federal statute requires that content written for the public be written for its specific audience?
opciones: The Plain Writing Act of 2010
The 21st Century Cures Act of 2016
The HITECH Act of 2009, part of ARRA
The Privacy Rule, published in 2000
preguntas.explicacion: Plain language means content that is clear and easy to grasp; the guidance presents it as more efficient and more effective, and as a legal duty besides. It was the Plain Writing Act of 2010 that laid down the requirement: whatever is written for the public has to be written for the particular audience it addresses. That is why pinning down the audience comes before drafting the letter or the handout.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, Exclusions Program
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: An excluded provider's period of exclusion has now run its course. What happens to her standing with the federal programs?
opciones: Reinstatement is not automatic; she has to apply for it once the period ends
Reinstatement is automatic on the day the stated period of exclusion runs out
Reinstatement follows as soon as a state Medicaid agency enrolls her once more
Reinstatement follows as soon as a practice checks the list and cannot find her
preguntas.explicacion: The exclusions program is explicit that an excluded individual or entity does not get reinstated automatically when the specified period runs out; an application has to be made. That is why the list gets checked month by month rather than counted forward: a period that has expired does not by itself put anyone back into the federal programs.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse (MLN4649244); and CMS, National Correct Coding Initiative
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMAA 3 k46, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · CMA III.G.1.a(3), III.G.2
preguntas.pregunta: A practice bills separately for services that belong in a single comprehensive code. What is that called?
opciones: Unbundling, which the correct coding edits are designed to detect and prevent
Upcoding, which reports a level of complexity higher than the care delivered
Balance billing, which charges the patient the amount above the allowed rate
Downgrading, which reports a level of service lower than the one documented
preguntas.explicacion: Splitting a service into its parts to bill them separately is unbundling, and the procedure-to-procedure edits exist to catch code pairs reported that way. Upcoding is the related abuse of billing a higher level of complexity than was provided or documented. Balance billing is charging the patient the difference between a charge and the allowed amount, which concerns the patient's bill rather than the codes chosen.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, Office of Minority Health, National CLAS Standards, Communication and Language Assistance
preguntas.subtema: Interpreters · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.1.c(3) / 2027 F.1.d(4) · RMA I.D.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: A woman with limited English brings her teenage son to interpret for her visit. What should the assistant do?
opciones: Bring in a trained medical interpreter for the encounter
Let the son interpret, since the patient chose him herself
Have the son interpret the history but not the consent
Reschedule the visit until an adult relative can come along
preguntas.explicacion: Organizations are asked to ensure the competence of anyone providing language assistance and to avoid untrained people and minors as interpreters. A relative may edit or soften what is said, and a patient may hold back sensitive details in front of family. Interpreters may be on site, by video or by telephone.

preguntas.subtema: Security incident · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: The firewall blocks a log-in attempt from outside the practice that never reached any record. Does the Security Rule count that as a security incident?
opciones: Yes, the definition takes in attempted as well as successful unauthorized access
No, an incident starts only once information has actually been reached or altered
No, unless the attempt is later shown to have exposed unsecured information
Yes, but only where the attempt interferes with how the information system runs
preguntas.explicacion: The wording is deliberately wide. It reaches unauthorized access, use, modification, disclosure or destruction of information whether the attempt succeeded or not, and it reaches interference with the way the system operates as well. Interference is one branch of the definition, not the whole of it, and the practice has to identify these events, respond to them, mitigate them and write them down.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Clinical Significance: When Can Information Be Shared?; Issues of Concern: Selective Access
preguntas.subtema: How much to tell a colleague · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k213 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35
preguntas.pregunta: A physician asks a phlebotomist to place an IV line for a patient's chemotherapy. How much of the history should the request carry?
opciones: Only what the task needs; the reason for the therapy is not required
The full oncology history, so the phlebotomist can judge the vein
The diagnosis and the stage, since both work for the same employer
No history at all, since treatment details may not be shared
preguntas.explicacion: Providers are not restricted from talking to one another about treatment, and a patient's care would stall if they were. The caution is about how much: asking someone to place a line does not require telling them why the therapy was prescribed. That is the same minimum necessary thinking behind selective access to records, where a laboratory worker needs the laboratory record and not the whole medical history.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, Office of Minority Health, National CLAS Standards
preguntas.subtema: CLAS standards · CCMA 6A k193 · CMAA 2C k17
preguntas.pregunta: How many National CLAS Standards are there, and how are they arranged?
opciones: Fifteen: one principal standard and three themed groups
Fifteen: five on governance, five on language, five on data
Fourteen: two principal standards and four themed groups
Twelve: one principal standard and two themed groups
preguntas.explicacion: The National CLAS Standards are 15 action steps. One is the principal standard, on care that is effective, understandable and respectful. The rest fall into three themes: Governance, Leadership and Workforce; Communication and Language Assistance; and a last group on engagement, accountability and continuous improvement.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, section 809
preguntas.subtema: Collections · CMAA 6D · CCMA 5 k187 · CMA III.G.9.f (exam through June 2027)
preguntas.pregunta: A collection agency contacts a patient about a medical debt. What must it send within five days of that first contact?
opciones: A written notice with the amount, the creditor, and the right to dispute
A written notice with the itemized services and the dates of each visit
A copy of the remittance advice showing what the health plan paid on it
A payment plan proposal that spreads the balance over the coming months
preguntas.explicacion: Within five days of the initial communication the debt collector must send written notice of the amount of the debt, the name of the creditor, and a statement that the debt will be assumed valid unless the consumer disputes it within 30 days, along with what happens if the consumer does dispute it or asks who the original creditor was. Itemized bills, remittance advices and payment plans are not part of that notice.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, National Provider Identifiers Standard, Administrative Simplification
preguntas.subtema: Third-party billing requirements · CMAA 6C k87, 6 k85 · CCMA 5L k185
preguntas.pregunta: A provider moves the practice to another state and changes her married name. What happens to her National Provider Identifier?
opciones: It stays the same, since the number never changes once it is assigned
It is reissued, since the number reflects the state where she practices
It is reissued, since the enrollment record has to match the legal name
It is suspended until the payer confirms the new address on the claim
preguntas.explicacion: Once assigned, the identifier remains the same even when the provider changes name, address or other information, because it carries no geographic or specialty meaning. Every HIPAA-covered provider, whether an individual or an organization, obtains one and uses it in all standard transactions, and a health plan may not require a provider who already has one to obtain an additional number.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms, entry Preauthorization; and CMS, Medicare Program Integrity Manual, Chapter 3 (documentación, enmiendas y correcciones del registro)
preguntas.subtema: Authorizations · CMAA 4G k67, 6E · CCMA 5H k183 · CMA III.G.5.a · RMA II.A.4 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: The plan approved the preauthorization for a scheduled procedure. What has the office actually obtained?
opciones: A decision that the service is medically necessary, with payment still not promised
A decision that the service is medically necessary, and a guarantee it will be paid
A decision that the patient has met the deductible for the plan year in question
A decision that the provider may bill the patient if the plan denies the claim
preguntas.explicacion: Preauthorization is the plan's finding that a service, a treatment plan, a drug or an item of durable medical equipment counts as medically necessary. The glossary is explicit that it is no promise the plan will cover the cost, since eligibility, benefits and coding still come into play when the claim is adjudicated. It says nothing about the deductible, and shifting liability to the patient is what an advance written notice of non-coverage does in Medicare.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Medicare and Medicaid Accreditation and Deemed Status: Definitions (Deemed status)
preguntas.subtema: Compliance with regulators · CMAA 3A k42
preguntas.pregunta: What does deemed status give a facility accredited by an approved organization?
opciones: It skips a separate survey by CMS in order to take part in the programs
It skips the state license requirement for operating the facility at all
It skips the yearly review of its own quality assurance program
It skips the requirement to meet the standards on patient rights
preguntas.explicacion: Deemed status is a designation granted to a facility that an approved accrediting organization has accredited and that the agency recognizes as meeting the participation requirements. A facility holding it needs no separate survey to be eligible for Medicare and Medicaid, because the accrediting organization has already measured it against those standards.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 1.5
preguntas.subtema: Downtime registration · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.2.a · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A new patient walks in while the record system is down. What does the contingency guidance expect the practice to have arranged?
opciones: Temporary record numbers to assign now and reconcile once the system returns
A paper chart opened under the patient's name and filed as a permanent record
A wait until the system returns, since a record cannot be opened without it
Registration in the read-only backup system, which accepts new patients too
preguntas.explicacion: Patient identification is one of the required practices for downtimes. There has to be a way to register a new patient while the system is unavailable, including assigning unique temporary record numbers, plus a process for reconciling those identifiers once the record system comes back. A read-only system, by definition, cannot take a new registration.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicare Program Integrity Manual, chapter 3, section 3.3.2.5
preguntas.subtema: Corrections and late entries · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 7A · NCMA 4.5
preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant realizes she charted a blood pressure in the wrong patient's record. How is the correction made?
opciones: The change is clearly and permanently marked, with its date and author identifiable
The wrong reading is erased or covered so that the record shows only accurate data
The entry is deleted from the system and re-entered under the correct patient name
The entry stays as it is, and a note about it goes into the practice incident log
preguntas.explicacion: CMS expects services to be documented when they are rendered, and accepts that entries sometimes have to be amended, corrected or added late. The date and the author of any amendment, correction or delayed entry must be identifiable, and the change or addendum must be clearly and permanently denoted. Reviewers examine such entries against the signature requirements of the same chapter.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Prospective Payment Systems - General Information
preguntas.subtema: Payment models · CMAA 6 k82 · CCMA 1 k6
preguntas.pregunta: What is a prospective payment system?
opciones: Payment of a fixed predetermined amount set by a classification of the service
Payment of the provider's billed charges once the claim has been adjudicated
Payment of a fixed amount per enrolled member for each month of coverage
Payment of a bonus when quality measures for the reporting year are met
preguntas.explicacion: Under a prospective payment system Medicare pays a predetermined, fixed amount, and the amount for a given service comes from the classification system for that service, diagnosis-related groups in the inpatient hospital case. CMS runs separate systems for acute inpatient, home health, hospice, hospital outpatient, psychiatric, rehabilitation, long-term care and skilled nursing care. Per-member monthly payment is capitation, and quality bonuses belong to value-based programs.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guides
preguntas.subtema: Downtime resources · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: The EHR will be down for a planned upgrade. Which resource is written specifically for that situation?
opciones: The Contingency Planning guide, on planned and unplanned EHR unavailability
The Patient Identification guide, on identifying patients reliably in the record
The Test Results Reporting and Follow-Up guide, on managing results electronically
The Clinician Communication guide, on messaging between care teams and patients
preguntas.explicacion: The 2025 SAFER guides come in eight titles across three groups, and each one names its own subject. Contingency Planning covers the safety practices tied to planned or unplanned EHR unavailability, meaning any time clinicians or other users cannot reach all or part of the system. The other three guides listed cover patient identification, test result follow-up and communication among clinicians and patients.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, What Part A covers; and Parts of Medicare
preguntas.subtema: Insurance types · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether Medicare Part A will pay for her care at the small critical access hospital in her county. What is the accurate answer?
opciones: It pays for an inpatient stay there, as it does in any hospital
It pays for an outpatient visit there, but not for an admission
It pays for neither, since those hospitals bill only under Part B
It pays for both, since those hospitals bill only under Part A
preguntas.explicacion: Part A helps pay for inpatient care in hospitals, in critical access hospitals and in skilled nursing facilities, and it also helps with hospice care, some home health services, nursing home care and inpatient behavioral and mental health care. Outpatient care, office visits with providers and the equipment ordered at them sit under Part B instead.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: respondeat superior (Exceptions: Independent Contractors)
preguntas.subtema: Legal doctrines · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.c(3) · RMA I.C.3 · CMAA 3A k31
preguntas.pregunta: A practice uses an independent contractor for weekend coverage. Does respondeat superior reach the practice for that person's acts?
opciones: No: the doctrine covers employees and agents, not independent contractors
No: the doctrine covers only acts committed inside the employer's premises
Yes: the doctrine covers every clinician the practice pays to see patients
Yes: the doctrine covers any clinician working under the practice's name
preguntas.explicacion: The doctrine makes an employer or principal answer for whatever wrongful acts an employee or an agent commits inside the scope of that employment or agency, and the plaintiff usually sues both. It does not extend to independent contractors, and courts weigh factors such as how much control was agreed, who supplies the tools, how the person is paid and whether the work forms part of the regular business the principal runs.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 416.2; and Medicare.gov, Ambulatory surgical centers: Description
preguntas.subtema: Ambulatory surgical center · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1 · RMA II.B.2.e
preguntas.pregunta: A freestanding center performs only surgery and sends every patient home the same day. Which Medicare facility definition fits it?
opciones: An ambulatory surgical center, an entity operating only for surgery without a hospital stay
A critical access hospital, which keeps a small number of inpatient beds in a rural county
An inpatient rehabilitation facility, which gives intensive therapy under physician supervision
A hospital outpatient department, which charges a facility copayment for each service given
preguntas.explicacion: The regulation describes an ambulatory surgical center as a distinct entity operating only to furnish surgery to patients who do not need to be hospitalized, with the expected duration of services no longer than 24 hours after admission. It must hold an agreement with CMS. Part B pays the facility fee for approved procedures there.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A blood count report uses the word leukopenia. What does the ending of that term indicate?
opciones: A deficiency or lack of the cells named by the root
A blood condition involving the cells named by the root
An enlargement of the structure named by the root
An abnormal softening of the tissue named by the root
preguntas.explicacion: The ending -penia means a deficiency or lack, so leukopenia is too few white cells. The endings around it name other things: -emia is a blood condition, -megaly an enlargement, and -malacia a softening. Leukocytosis, with -osis for an abnormal condition, points the other way.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Common Pitfalls
preguntas.subtema: Nontherapeutic responses · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2E k21 · CMA F.2 / 2027 F.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: A patient waiting on a biopsy result says she is frightened, and the assistant answers “I am sure it will be fine.” What is the risk?
opciones: A severe rupture in the relationship if that outcome does not arrive
The patient reads it as a value judgment placed on her situation
The patient hears it as a piece of advice that she never asked for
The subject moves on abruptly and she is left feeling dismissed
preguntas.explicacion: False reassurance is listed among the pitfalls precisely because of what happens when the promised outcome does not come: the relationship can be severely and significantly damaged. The other three options are also named pitfalls, but they describe value judgments, unsolicited advice and an abrupt change of subject, not a promise about the future.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting started with telehealth, Types of telehealth
preguntas.subtema: Audio-only telehealth · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient booked for a video visit has no working camera and asks whether the appointment is off. What do the categories of telehealth allow?
opciones: An audio-only call still counts as synchronous care when a video visit is not an option
An audio-only call counts as asynchronous care, since no picture is shared between them
The visit must be rebooked in person, because synchronous care requires live video
The visit must become a secure message exchange, which is the audio-only equivalent
preguntas.explicacion: Synchronous care means provider and patient interacting live, with a caregiver joining where that makes sense. The video call is the familiar shape of it, but audio-only calls are listed as synchronous as well, for occasions when a video visit is not possible, and so is secure text messaging used to answer a patient's questions.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), Collecting Patient Payment
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMA III.G.3.c (2027 III.G.3.c) · CMAA 5 k77, 6D · CCMA 5 k186
preguntas.pregunta: A patient paid after signing an advance written notice, appealed, and the appeal went her way. How soon does the refund have to reach her?
opciones: Within fifteen days of the appeal decision, to count as timely
Within thirty days of the appeal decision, to count as timely
Within sixty days of the appeal decision, to count as timely
Within ninety days of the appeal decision, to count as timely
preguntas.explicacion: Once the notice has been issued and signed, the provider may seek payment from the patient. If Medicare then pays all or part of the claim and the patient has also paid, the money goes back to her promptly: within thirty days of the remittance advice, or within fifteen days of an appeal determination where an appeal was filed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Common Pitfalls
preguntas.subtema: Nontherapeutic responses · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2B k16 · CMA F.2 / 2027 F.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: A patient says angrily that the office lost her paperwork. Why should the reply not be defensive?
opciones: It leaves her room to voice the frustration and find a fix with you
It keeps the exchange from moving to another subject too abruptly
It stops her from reading approval or disapproval into the answer
It avoids handing her a piece of advice that she has not asked for
preguntas.explicacion: Responding defensively is named as a pitfall and is admitted to be a hard one to avoid. Holding back the defense gives the patient room to express the frustration and to work out a solution together with the provider rather than against them. Abrupt subject changes, approving responses and unsolicited advice are separate pitfalls with separate reasons.

preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, in situ
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k5 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A biopsy report reads carcinoma in situ. What do those last two words add?
opciones: The abnormal cells are still only where they first formed
The abnormal cells have reached one nearby lymph node only
The abnormal cells have already settled in a second organ
The abnormal cells are not cancer and will not spread at all
preguntas.explicacion: In situ means in its original place, so in a carcinoma in situ the abnormal cells are found only where they first formed and have not spread. That is a different statement from benign, which means the growth is not cancer, and from metastasis, where cells break away and start a new tumor somewhere else.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, General Compliance Program Guidance
preguntas.subtema: Auditing and compliance · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A
preguntas.pregunta: Is a small practice required by law to follow the OIG's general compliance program guidance?
opciones: No, the guidance is voluntary and not binding on any person or entity
No, but only practices with fewer than 10 employees are exempt from it
Yes, every practice that bills a federal program must follow it in full
Yes, and a contractor reviews compliance with it at each record audit
preguntas.explicacion: The general compliance program guidance is a reference for the health care compliance community that discusses federal laws, compliance infrastructure and risks. It is voluntary and not binding on any individual or entity, and the office signals that by using the word should throughout. Its adaptations for small entities are suggestions, not an exemption from a requirement that does not exist.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 3186, Model Exposure Control Plan, Recordkeeping: Sharps Injury Log; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(h)(5)(i) and (h)(5)(iii)
preguntas.subtema: Keeping the sharps log · CPT D1 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA II.B.5.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: How long is the sharps injury log kept, and what happens when someone asks for a copy of it?
opciones: At least five years after the end of the year it covers, with identifiers removed
Three years after the training it documents, with the trainer's name removed
Thirty years after the employee leaves, with the device brand taken out
Five years, and copies go only to the Assistant Secretary who asks for them
preguntas.explicacion: The standard sends the log's retention to 29 CFR 1904.33, and the model plan spells out what that comes to: five years at minimum, counted from the close of the calendar year the log covers. The model adds that any copy handed out has the personal identifiers stripped, which matches the demand in (h)(5)(i) that the record keep the injured worker's identity confidential. Three years is the training record; employment plus thirty years is the medical record.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Challenges of This Model
preguntas.subtema: Limits of the model · CMAA 4A k49 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic receives far more appointment requests every single day than its clinicians could ever see. What can open access do for it?
opciones: Nothing lasting, because no scheduling system works if demand always exceeds capacity
Solve it, because the model assumes the trouble is never a real shortage of capacity
Solve it, once the backlog has been worked down over six to eight weeks of longer days
Solve it, by going back to triaging the callers whose problems sound the most urgent
preguntas.explicacion: The model rests on the supposition that the problem is usually an imbalance between supply and demand rather than a shortage of capacity, and it can absorb excess demand on a given day. But the guide states the limit plainly: where demand is permanently greater than capacity, no scheduling system works. Clearing a backlog does not change that.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 7: Improve how well clinicians and staff communicate on the phone
preguntas.subtema: Telephone etiquette · CCMA 6C k196 · CMAA 2A k27
preguntas.pregunta: A patient calls with questions the assistant has answered before. What does the toolkit suggest for consistency?
opciones: Written scripts with the answers to frequent questions
A recording of the answer played back to the caller
A note telling the caller to book a visit for the answer
A rule that only the clinician may answer such calls
preguntas.explicacion: Practices are told to develop and use written scripts for frequently asked questions, so answers come out clear and consistent, and to close the call by inviting questions and using teach-back to confirm that whatever was said over the phone has been understood. Sending routine questions to a visit or to the clinician is not what is advised.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026, Section I.A.14
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A subcategory is titled tuberculosis of bones and joints. How does the coder read the word and in that title?
opciones: As either and or or, so bones alone, joints alone or both all belong there
As and alone, so both sites have to be documented before the code may be used
As or alone, so the code may not be used when both sites are documented
As a nonessential modifier, so the whole phrase may be present or absent
preguntas.explicacion: The word and in a title is read as meaning either and or or. The guidelines use this very subcategory as their example: tuberculosis of the bones alone, of the joints alone, and of bones and joints together all classify to it. Nonessential modifiers are a different convention, the terms sitting inside parentheses.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 3.1
preguntas.subtema: Monitoring response time · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: The guidance asks a practice to monitor how quickly the record system answers on important clinical tasks. What figure does it give as the optimum?
opciones: Under two seconds
Under five seconds
Under ten seconds
Under thirty seconds
preguntas.explicacion: A monitoring and auditing strategy is expected to cover downtime events, access to patient information and system response time for tasks such as reviewing results, entering orders and looking a patient up, with under two seconds named as the optimum. A log of all downtime testing is kept, and leadership watches the unplanned outages.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Skilled nursing facility (SNF) care: Coverage details and Who's eligible
preguntas.subtema: Transition of care to a SNF · CCMA 4H · CMAA 1 k1 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A hospitalized patient will need daily physical therapy after discharge. What must have happened for Part A to cover a skilled nursing facility stay?
opciones: An inpatient hospital stay, medically necessary, of at least 3 days running beforehand
An inpatient hospital stay, medically necessary, of at least 7 days running beforehand
A face-to-face assessment by a nurse practitioner within 30 days after the discharge
A certification by two doctors that the patient's life expectancy is 6 months or less
preguntas.explicacion: Coverage in a skilled nursing facility rests on a qualifying inpatient hospital stay: at least three days in a row, counted from the day of admission as an inpatient but not the day of discharge. The patient must also enter the facility generally within 30 days of leaving and need daily skilled care. The face-to-face visit belongs to home health, the six-month prognosis to hospice.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practices for Domain 2
preguntas.subtema: Downtime communication · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Why must the communication strategy for an EHR downtime not run on the EHR's own computing infrastructure?
