opciones: Because it has to keep working when that infrastructure is the thing that has failed
Because messages about a downtime are protected health information under the rule
Because staff are trained on ransomware prevention through a separate channel entirely
Because the vendor rather than the practice owns the messaging tools inside the system
preguntas.explicacion: Among the recommended practices for using health IT safely, the guide wants the strategy for communicating during downtime and recovery to run on something other than the computing infrastructure that keeps the EHR up. Related practices cover training and testing staff on downtime and recovery procedures, written policies that keep patient care and critical business operations going, and an orderly restart of data exchange across the interfaces.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", HIPAA and Communication With Patients, Contents and Authorizations; StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", Relative disclosure
preguntas.subtema: Family and caregivers · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: May a phlebotomist tell a patient's spouse, who is present and involved in the patient's care, about the draw and the follow-up?
opciones: Yes, if the patient is informed and does not object; ask when others are present
No; disclosure to any family member requires a signed written authorization
Yes, and the same applies to any relative who telephones the clinic asking about results
No, unless the spouse holds a medical power of attorney on file at the clinic
preguntas.explicacion: The Privacy Rule lets information reach a spouse, a parent, a guardian or another caregiver who takes part in looking after the patient, and no formal agreement is needed for it. The practical move is to ask the patient whether they mind before discussing something specific with others in the room. Patients may also put limits on that sharing, for instance asking that no relative collect medications or be told about their condition. A relative on the telephone is a different case: a hospital may not disclose over the phone to a caller who says they are family.

preguntas.fuente: USPS, Compare Mail Services: Priority Mail
preguntas.subtema: Priority Mail · CCMA 5O · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7G k96 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A practice mails a heavy set of imaging discs to a specialist and wants tracking and cover for loss included in the price. Which service fits?
opciones: Priority Mail, delivered in two to three days with tracking and cover included
First-Class Mail, delivered in one to five days at the lowest price per piece
Media Mail, delivered in two to eight days for recorded and printed materials
Priority Mail Express, delivered in one to three days with a money-back promise
preguntas.explicacion: Priority Mail is the everyday parcel service: two to three days, tracking and up to $100 of insurance built into the price, free flat rate packaging and a 70 lb ceiling. Express is faster but is bought for speed, and First-Class carries no tracking of its own.

preguntas.fuente: NHA Candidate Handbook (2026), Code of Ethics
preguntas.subtema: Codes of ethics · CPT D1 k26 · CCMA 7C · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: Which duty does the code of ethics for NHA-certified professionals state?
opciones: To respect and safeguard every patient's dignity, privacy and safety
To report any colleague suspected of an error to the state licensing board
To accept any assignment the employer gives while the shift is under way
To keep patient information from the patient's own family in every case
preguntas.explicacion: The code lists six duties a certified professional takes on, and one is safeguarding every patient's dignity, privacy and safety. The others cover working for the betterment of society and the profession, professionalism and honesty, continued learning, taking part in activities that improve health and the allied health field, and acting in the public's best interest.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, FAQ: What are the advantages of electronic health records?
preguntas.subtema: EHR advantages · CCMA 5 k172 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.c · CMAA k3 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which benefit does ONC attribute to electronic health records?
opciones: Less duplicate testing, and legible documentation that supports accurate coding and billing
An automatic release of records to any provider who asks, without further authorization
A guarantee that no unauthorized person will ever reach the information they contain
An exemption from the Security Rule, since certified systems already meet its standards
preguntas.explicacion: The advantages ONC lists include having information that is accurate, current and complete right at the point of care; quicker access, so care is better coordinated; secure sharing with patients and with other clinicians; fewer medical errors; safer prescribing; documentation that is legible and complete, with coding and billing streamlined; better privacy and security for patient data; and lower costs through less paperwork and less duplicated testing.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, introduction and Sections 12-15
preguntas.subtema: SDS structure · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: How many sections does a GHS-format Safety Data Sheet have, and which of them does OSHA not enforce?
opciones: 16 sections; OSHA does not enforce sections 12 through 15
16 sections; OSHA does not enforce sections 9 through 11 and 16
12 sections; OSHA does not enforce the last two, transport and regulatory
8 sections, one per required pictogram; all are enforced by OSHA
preguntas.explicacion: A safety data sheet under the Hazard Communication standard has 16 numbered sections in a fixed order. Sections 12 through 15, ecological information, disposal, transport and regulatory information, must be present to match the GHS, but OSHA does not enforce their content because other agencies handle those matters. Sections 9 through 11 and 16 hold technical data such as physical properties, reactivity, toxicology and the date of preparation, and they are enforced. Eight is the number of pictograms OSHA requires, not of SDS sections.

preguntas.subtema: Uses described in the notice · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice is drafting the part of its notice that deals with use for treatment, for payment and for health care operations. What does the rule require of that description?
opciones: A description of each of the three purposes, with at least one example of its own
A description of each of the three purposes, with the patient's consent alongside
A description of the three purposes together, with a single example covering them
A description of each of the three purposes, with the legal citation for each one
preguntas.explicacion: The notice must describe, and give at least one example of, the kinds of use and disclosure the entity may make for treatment, for payment and for health care operations. It must also cover the other purposes for which information may go out without written authorization, in enough detail for the reader to know what is permitted.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, Office of Minority Health, National CLAS Standards, Communication and Language Assistance
preguntas.subtema: CLAS standards · CCMA 6A k193 · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.1.c(3) / 2027 F.1.d(4)
preguntas.pregunta: Under the National CLAS Standards, what is owed to a patient with limited English proficiency?
opciones: Language assistance at no cost, announced in writing and out loud
Language assistance at cost, once the patient asks for it in writing
A translated consent form only, since the rest is spoken anyway
A bilingual staff member who has had no interpreter training
preguntas.explicacion: One standard tells organizations to offer language assistance at no cost to the person, so care is not delayed. Another tells them to inform everyone, in writing and orally, that the service exists. A third requires competent interpreters, which rules out grabbing whoever happens to be bilingual.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: consent
preguntas.subtema: Consent · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a-b · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7 · CMAA 3D k40
preguntas.pregunta: What has to be true for consent to be valid?
opciones: Enough mental capacity, and no coercion, fraud or mistake behind it
A signature on the practice's own form, witnessed by a staff member
A relative present at the time the person agrees to the procedure
A note in the record showing the person was told the likely outcome
preguntas.explicacion: Consent means the person voluntarily and willingly agrees to what is proposed. The person consenting must have sufficient mental capacity, and the agreement must be free of coercion, fraud or error. It divides into express consent, given directly in speech or writing, and implied consent, inferred from actions, signs, facts or even silence.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Piaget", Issues of Concern; and Enhancing Healthcare Team Outcomes
preguntas.subtema: Developmental stages · CCMA 1E k29 · CMA F.1.c(7)(b) / 2027 F.1.d(7)(a) · CMAA 2D k17
preguntas.pregunta: Why should an explanation given to a six-year-old stay away from abstract ideas?
opciones: Logic at that age is applied to concrete, tangible things
Symbolic play and make-believe are beyond that age group
Language is not yet used to recall events already past
Object permanence has not been established at that age
preguntas.explicacion: In the concrete operational period the child brings logical rules to bear on objects that are concrete or tangible and can mentally transform what is seen and heard; abstraction waits for formal operations around 11. Symbolic play, drawing and the verbal recall of past events all arrive earlier, in the preoperational period.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Essential health benefits
preguntas.subtema: Affordable Care Act protections · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: What are essential health benefits?
opciones: Ten categories of service that plans must cover under the health care law
Ten categories of service that plans may add to lower the monthly premium
The list of covered prescription drugs that each plan updates every year
The preventive screenings that plans must provide without any cost sharing
preguntas.explicacion: Essential health benefits are the ten service categories the health care law obliges plans to cover, among them prescription drugs, doctors' services, hospital care both inpatient and outpatient, pregnancy and childbirth, and mental health care. Dental cover has to be offered for children; for adults it is optional. The list of covered drugs is the formulary, and free preventive care is one protection among several, not the whole set of categories.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms: Out-of-pocket Limit
preguntas.subtema: Financial calculations · CMA III.G.8, III.G.6.e (2027 III.G.6.c-d) · CMAA 5C k76, 6B · CCMA 5K k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reached her out-of-pocket limit in September. What does she pay for covered in-network care in October?
opciones: No more cost sharing, since the plan pays the allowed amount
Her copayment only, because copays sit outside of that limit
Her coinsurance only, because it is a share and not a fixed sum
Her premium and her coinsurance, as she did before September
preguntas.explicacion: The out-of-pocket limit is the most a member pays for her share of covered services in the coverage period; once she meets it the plan usually pays the whole allowed amount. The premium is never part of that limit, so she goes on paying it, and neither the copayment nor the coinsurance survives the limit as a separate charge.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Medically necessary; and Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms
preguntas.subtema: Medical necessity · CMAA 5 k69 · CCMA 5J k182 · CMA III.G.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: What does medically necessary mean?
opciones: Care or supplies needed to diagnose or to treat a condition, meeting accepted standards
Services or supplies the patient requests and the provider is willing to deliver
Services or supplies listed in the plan's contract as covered benefits for the year
Services or supplies the plan authorized in advance, whether or not they were given
preguntas.explicacion: Medically necessary is the label for care or supplies needed in order to prevent, to diagnose or to treat an illness, an injury, a condition, a disease or the symptoms of one, and that come up to the accepted standards of medicine. Patient preference does not establish it; the benefit list answers a different question, what is covered; and preauthorization is the plan's own finding of necessity, not the definition.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability
preguntas.subtema: Security objectives · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Under the Security Rule, what does the word integrity mean?
opciones: Data has not been altered or destroyed in a manner that was not authorized
Data is accessible and usable on demand by a person who is authorized
Data is withheld from persons or processes that lack authorization
Data is stored on equipment the practice owns rather than on a vendor's servers
preguntas.explicacion: The rule sets out three objectives and gives each a definition. Confidentiality is the property of not being handed over or disclosed to persons or processes lacking authorization, which is what backs the Privacy Rule's limits on use and disclosure. Integrity is the property of not having been altered or destroyed without authorization. Availability is being reachable and usable on demand by a person who is authorized.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Common Pitfalls
preguntas.subtema: Nontherapeutic responses · CCMA 6C k199 · CMA F.2 / 2027 F.1.d · CMAA 2E k21
preguntas.pregunta: Why do interviewers generally hold back from agreeing or disagreeing with a patient?
opciones: It leaves more room for the patient's own views to come out
It keeps the office from a position it may have to undo later
It leads the patient to trim the history to what gets accepted
It takes away the chance to ask a clarifying question later on
preguntas.explicacion: Agreeing now and then can be useful because it validates the patient, but as a habit both agreeing and disagreeing crowd out the patient's own views. Approving and disapproving responses sit beside them in the same list, close to placing value judgments on what the patient says.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Days to Pay
preguntas.subtema: Revenue cycle KPIs · CMA III.G.3.b(5) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6 k81 · CCMA 5 k181 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A biller is uneasy because a Medicare claim has still not paid twenty-two days after it was sent. What do the benchmarks for time to payment say?
opciones: Medicare pays in 18 to 30 days, so this claim is still inside the payment benchmark
Medicare pays in 12 to 20 days, so this claim is already past the payment benchmark
Medicare pays in 55 to 75 days, so this claim is nowhere near the payment benchmark
Medicare pays in 2 to 5 days, so this claim is far beyond the payment benchmark
preguntas.explicacion: Time to payment is benchmarked payer by payer: 12 to 20 days for private insurance, 18 to 30 for Medicare, and 55 to 75 for workers' compensation. Twenty-two days therefore sits comfortably inside the Medicare span. What stretches the wait is errors in billing, demographic data that is wrong, documentation missing or incomplete, and submission on paper rather than electronically.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, HIPAA Compliance, Introduction
preguntas.subtema: HIPAA titles · CCMA 1 k2 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.c · CMAA 3B k33 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: HIPAA is organized into how many titles, and which one contains administrative simplification?
opciones: Five titles, and administrative simplification sits in Title II
Five titles, and administrative simplification sits in Title I
Three titles, and administrative simplification sits in Title III
Seven titles, and administrative simplification sits in Title IV
preguntas.explicacion: The 1996 statute, also known as the Kennedy-Kassebaum Act, has five titles. Title I protects insurance coverage for workers changing or losing jobs. Title II is the one that addresses health care fraud and abuse and promotes administrative simplification through national standards for electronic transactions and national identifiers. Titles III, IV and V deal with medical spending accounts, group plans and company-owned life insurance.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Eligibility, Effective Date of Coverage
preguntas.subtema: Financial eligibility · CMA III.G.4.c (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 6 k83 · CCMA 5E k178 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is found eligible for Medicaid in June and still owes the practice for visits in April. What may the program allow?
opciones: Coverage reaching back up to three months before the month of application
Coverage reaching back up to six months before the month of application
Coverage starting on the date of the determination and never any earlier
Coverage reaching back to the first day of the year the application was made
preguntas.explicacion: Once eligibility is established, coverage starts either on the date of the application or on the first day of the month it was made in. Benefits may also reach back as far as three months before that month, provided the person would have qualified during that stretch had she applied then. Coverage generally ends with the month in which she stops qualifying.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information: Providing the Notice
preguntas.subtema: Revised notice from a plan · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA II.A.1 · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A health plan makes a material revision to its notice of privacy practices. Within what period must the people it covers receive the revised notice?
opciones: Within 60 days of the revision, to the individuals then covered by the plan
Within 30 days of the revision, to the individuals then covered by the plan
Within 90 days of the revision, to every individual enrolled in the last year
Within 60 days of the revision, to new enrollees only, at the time of enrollment
preguntas.explicacion: Health plans carry delivery duties of their own. When a revision is material, the revised notice has to reach whoever the plan covers at that moment inside 60 days; someone who enrolls later gets the notice when the enrollment happens. And any covered entity, plan or not, has to revise its notice and put it out promptly whenever it changes a privacy practice materially.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Introduction to the Skeletal System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(2) (2027 I.C.6.f(2)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12
preguntas.pregunta: Where does hematopoiesis take place, and which mineral does bone store more of than any other organ?
opciones: In the red marrow, and the mineral is calcium
In the yellow marrow, and the mineral is calcium
In the red marrow, and the mineral is potassium
In the compact bone, and the mineral is sodium
preguntas.explicacion: Blood cell formation happens mostly in the red marrow, which fills the bone cavities in infants and in adults is limited to spongy bone: the pelvis and vertebrae, the clavicles and sternum, the ribs and the skull. Yellow marrow stores fat. Bone also holds more calcium than any other organ and releases it when blood levels drop.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases, chapter 5: Vaccine Inventory Management
preguntas.subtema: Inventory assessment · CCMA 5T · RMA II.B.5.a · CMAA 7E k99 · NCMA 4.13
preguntas.pregunta: How often should a practice take stock of what it holds, and what does it weigh when deciding how much to order?
opciones: Monthly and before each order, weighing expected demand, storage room and stock
Weekly and after each order, weighing the price offered and the delivery times
Yearly and before each order, weighing last year's use and the budget approved
Monthly and after each order, weighing the number of patients seen that month
preguntas.explicacion: An inventory assessment is done at least once a month, and again before an order goes out, so that the practice knows what is really on the shelf. The quantity ordered is set by projected demand, by how much storage capacity there is, and by the current supply on hand.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, Office of Minority Health, National CLAS Standards, Engagement, Continuous Improvement, and Accountability
preguntas.subtema: CLAS standards · CCMA 6A k193 · CMAA 2B k16
preguntas.pregunta: A patient files a grievance about how an interpreter request was handled. Which National CLAS Standard covers how the organization should respond?
opciones: Building culturally appropriate ways to resolve complaints
Collecting demographic data to monitor the impact of CLAS
Partnering with the community to design and evaluate services
Reporting the organization's CLAS progress to the public
preguntas.explicacion: The standard on conflicts and complaints sits in the group on engagement and accountability, which also covers continuous improvement: it asks the organization to build processes, appropriate culturally and linguistically, to spot, head off and settle conflicts, complaints and grievances. The other three are real CLAS Standards too, but they cover something else: collecting demographic data, partnering with the community and reporting progress to the public.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), Issuing a Notice
preguntas.subtema: Medical necessity · CMA III.G.1.d, III.G.3.c (2027 III.G.1.d, III.G.3.c) · CMAA 5 k69, 5 k77 · CCMA 5J k180
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is scheduled for a service that the local coverage determination in the area does not cover for her diagnosis. What does the notice guidance draw from that?
opciones: That the practice knew, or should have known, of the likely denial
That a national determination has to be issued before any denial
That the notice may be given after the service has been provided
That the patient may be billed even with no notice on the record
preguntas.explicacion: Every service billed has to point to the sign, symptom or complaint that makes it reasonable and necessary, and coverage may be limited by a national determination or, where none exists or where one needs defining for an area, by a local one issued by the contractor. Once such a policy is public, the guidance treats the provider as knowing the denial was coming.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Muscular System: Muscle Types
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(2) (2027 I.C.6.f(2)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which three types of muscle tissue does the body contain, and which of them is both striated and involuntary?
opciones: Skeletal, smooth and cardiac; cardiac is striated and involuntary
Skeletal, smooth and cardiac; smooth is striated and involuntary
Skeletal, smooth and cardiac; skeletal is striated and involuntary
Striated, spindle and rectangular; spindle is striated and involuntary
preguntas.explicacion: Skeletal muscle attaches to bone, is striated and is under voluntary control. Smooth muscle lines the hollow organs, is not striated and works involuntarily under the autonomic nervous system. Cardiac muscle sits in the heart wall and takes one feature from each: striated like skeletal, involuntary like smooth.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Malpractice", Functional Elements of a Lawsuit
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, malpractice and negligence · CCMA 7A k221 · CMA II.E.4.a professional liability torts · RMA I.C.3 legal terminology · CMAA 3 k31
preguntas.pregunta: A patient sues after an injury during a draw. Which four elements must the plaintiff prove for a medical malpractice claim to succeed?
opciones: A duty to the patient, a breach of that duty, causation, and damages
A duty to the patient, a written complaint, an apology refused, and damages
A duty to the patient, a breach of that duty, an intent to harm, and damages
A duty to the patient, a breach of that duty, causation, and a policy in force
preguntas.explicacion: A mistake on its own is not malpractice. The plaintiff has to establish that the clinician owed this patient a duty, that the duty was breached measured against the standard of care, that the poor outcome came from the act or the omission and not from the underlying disease, and that damages followed. Intent is not on the list, which is what separates negligence from a deliberate wrong.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Situation Monitoring Process
preguntas.subtema: Teamwork · CCMA 6L k202 · CMAA 2F k21 · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: What is the team outcome in which everyone ends up on the same page?
opciones: Shared mental model
Situation awareness
Situation monitoring
Cross-monitoring
preguntas.explicacion: Situation monitoring is the individual skill of scanning and assessing what is going on; situation awareness is what that produces in the individual, the state of knowing how things stand; and the shared mental model is the team outcome arising when every member keeps that awareness and communicates it. Cross-monitoring is watching each other for slips.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, What's the difference between Medicare and Medicaid?
preguntas.subtema: Medicare vs Medicaid · CMAA 6 k84, 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.c / 2027 III.G.4 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: What is the basic difference between Medicare and Medicaid?
opciones: Medicare is federal and age or disability based; Medicaid is federal-state and income based
Medicare is federal and income based; Medicaid is federal-state and age or disability based
Both are federal, but Medicare covers hospital care and Medicaid covers office visits
Both are state run, but Medicare follows federal rules and Medicaid follows state rules
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare is federal health insurance, administered by CMS, for people 65 and older and for some younger people with disabilities or certain conditions, so its costs and coverage are the same in every state. Medicaid is a joint federal-state program serving people whose income and resources are limited; general rules come from the federal government and each state runs its own version, so eligibility and benefits differ from state to state.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), Table 1 and Table 2
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMAA 5B k75 · CCMA 5E k182
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has Medicare because of end-stage renal disease and also has a group health plan. What happens during the first 30 months?
opciones: The group health plan pays first and Medicare pays second during that period
Medicare pays first and the group health plan pays second during that period
The group health plan pays first for dialysis and Medicare for everything else
Medicare pays first, and the 30 months apply only to a COBRA continuation plan
preguntas.explicacion: End-stage renal disease brings a coordination period of 30 months. While it runs, the group health plan coverage that had been primary before eligibility began pays first and Medicare pays second; once the 30 months are up, Medicare becomes primary. The same 30-month clock applies where the other coverage is COBRA, so it is not peculiar to that situation, and the rule is not split by type of service.

preguntas.subtema: Rescinding an authorization · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA E.2.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: A patient revokes his consent to share his substance use disorder records. What about what was already sent?
opciones: The revocation does not undo disclosures already acted on in reliance
The revocation obliges the recipient to return or destroy the records
The revocation is only valid if it is given before the expiration event
The revocation must be approved by the program before it takes effect
preguntas.explicacion: The consent form has to tell the patient how to revoke it in writing, and that the right to revoke does not reach back over what the program or another lawful holder has already done in reliance on the consent. The program does not get to approve or refuse the revocation, and revoking is not tied to the expiration date the form carries.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A main term in the alphabetic index carries a see instruction. What does the coder do with it?
opciones: Go to the term the note names, since that is where the code is
Use the code beside the main term and read the other term later
Look at the other term only if the first gives no useful code
Verify the main term in the tabular list without looking further
preguntas.explicacion: A see note after a main term means the coder has to go to the term it points at in order to find the right code. That is different from a see also note, which offers another main term that may hold useful entries but need not be followed when the original main term already gives the code that is needed.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A patient treated for pneumonia has the cough and fever that illness routinely brings. Are those coded as well?
opciones: No, symptoms routinely tied to a disease process are not coded on their own
Yes, every symptom the provider documents is coded along with the disease
Yes, but only as secondary codes placed after the code for the disease
No, unless the provider states in the note that they are unrelated to it
preguntas.explicacion: Signs and symptoms that go with a disease process as a matter of course are not assigned as additional codes, unless the classification instructs otherwise. Additional signs and symptoms that are not routinely associated with the disease are coded when they are present. So the test is whether the finding is part of the illness or beyond it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Conflict Management", Issues of Concern: Conflict Management Styles
preguntas.subtema: Conflict management · CCMA 6J k209 · CMAA 2B k26
preguntas.pregunta: What happens when the accommodating style is used too often?
opciones: It breeds resentment and comes across as weakness
It lets disagreements fester into team dysfunction
It damages psychological safety and stifles speaking up
It costs more effort than any of the other four styles
preguntas.explicacion: Accommodating means giving way, either to keep the relationship intact or because the issue weighs more with the other side; it earns its place when relational capital counts or when you were in the wrong, but overuse breeds resentment and reads as weakness. Festering disagreement belongs to habitual avoiding, harm to psychological safety to competing, and high effort to collaborating.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: For Notification and Other Purposes
preguntas.subtema: Family involvement · CCMA 6 k204 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA II.B.3.g · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's adult daughter is helping with his care and asks about the medication list. What does the Privacy Rule permit?
opciones: Sharing what is directly relevant to her involvement in his care, on his informal permission
Sharing the entire record with her, since a relative helping with care stands in for the patient
Withholding the list unless she is appointed as his personal representative by a court
Sharing only after she signs an authorization form on the patient's behalf at the front desk
preguntas.explicacion: On informal permission a covered entity may give family, relatives, friends or anyone else the patient names whatever bears directly on that person's part in the care or in paying for it. That is narrower than a personal representative, who stands in the patient's shoes for every purpose. The same provision lets a pharmacist hand filled prescriptions to somebody acting for the patient.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Telehealth Systems, Asynchronous Telehealth
preguntas.subtema: Asynchronous telehealth · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A primary care clinician sends a focused question to a specialist and receives the answer two days later. Which telehealth service is that?
opciones: An electronic consultation, which is one of the asynchronous arrangements
A facilitated virtual visit, where an assistant gathers the objective data
A teletriage visit, used to sort symptoms quickly in an urgent setting
A remote critical care consultation, which guides a team at the bedside
preguntas.explicacion: The asynchronous, store-and-forward route collects history, images and diagnostic data and passes them to a specialist who reads them later. An e-consult, in which the primary care clinician puts a focused question to a specialist, sits in that group, together with portal messaging, teledermatology, off-site reading of images and digital intake questionnaires.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicare Coverage Determination Process; and CMS, MLN Booklet MLN006976
preguntas.subtema: Medical necessity · CMAA 5 k69, 6 k85 · CCMA 5J k180 · CMA III.G.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: What standard limits Medicare coverage of an item or service?
opciones: It must sit in a benefit category and be needed and reasonable for diagnosis or treatment
It must be ordered by a specialist and delivered in a hospital outpatient department
It must be listed in the fee schedule with a payment amount for the current year
It must be approved in advance by the contractor for each individual patient
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare covers an item or a service where it is reasonable and necessary in order to diagnose or treat an illness or an injury, falls inside a benefit category and is not excluded. National coverage determinations settle the question nationally through an evidence-based process, and where no national policy exists the contractors may issue local coverage determinations. Appearing on a fee schedule, or being ordered by a specialist, decides nothing by itself.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Hospice care: Coverage details and Costs
preguntas.subtema: What the hospice benefit changes · CCMA 4D k165 · CMAA 2H k30
preguntas.pregunta: A family asks what changes once a patient enrolls in hospice. Which service does Medicare stop covering?
opciones: Treatment intended to cure the terminal illness, and drugs meant to cure it
Nursing visits and the medical equipment that the hospice plan of care calls for
Short-term inpatient care the hospice team arranges when symptoms get out of hand
Care for a health problem that is unrelated to the terminal illness itself
preguntas.explicacion: Once the benefit starts, Medicare no longer pays for treatment aimed at curing the terminal illness or its related conditions, nor for prescription drugs meant to cure rather than to control symptoms or relieve pain. It also stops paying for care from a hospice the team did not set up, and for room and board. Original Medicare still covers unrelated health problems.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Yearly "Wellness" visits, Coverage details
preguntas.subtema: Pre-appointment screening · CMAA 4H k62 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient booked for a yearly Wellness visit asks what the questionnaire the office sent her ahead of the appointment is for. What is it?
opciones: A Health Risk Assessment, which feeds her prevention plan
A financial responsibility form, which sets her share of the cost
A notice of privacy practices, which records her acknowledgement
An advance directive, which records her wishes about treatment
preguntas.explicacion: Part of the visit is a questionnaire the provider hands out, the Health Risk Assessment, whose answers are used to build or update the personalised prevention plan for that patient. Advance directives do come up at that visit, but as an offer to talk about them, and they are a different document altogether.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Definition of Breach
preguntas.subtema: Breach presumption · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3E k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: A staff member e-mails a lab result to the wrong patient. How does the Breach Notification Rule treat that event at the outset?
opciones: As a breach, unless a risk assessment shows a low probability that the information was compromised
As a breach only after the Office for Civil Rights investigates and reaches that conclusion
As an incidental disclosure, since a misdirected message cannot reasonably be prevented
As a security incident rather than a breach, because e-mail systems are technical safeguards
preguntas.explicacion: Any use or disclosure that the Privacy Rule does not permit is presumed to be a breach. The presumption only falls where the covered entity or business associate demonstrates, through a risk assessment, a low probability that the PHI was compromised. An entity may also skip the assessment entirely and simply notify.

preguntas.fuente: NHA Candidate Handbook (2026), Code of Ethics; and Maintaining your Certification
preguntas.subtema: Professional development · CPT D1 k26 · CCMA 7C · RMA I.C.4.e · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: What does that code say about a certified professional's knowledge over time?
opciones: That learning continues and that the person keeps up with current research
That the original training is sufficient until the credential is renewed
That new techniques are learned only through the employer's own program
That research is followed only when the employer pays for the coursework
preguntas.explicacion: One of the six duties is to keep learning, applying and advancing knowledge and skills, practical and scientific alike, and to stay current with the latest research and how it is used in practice. Nothing ties that duty to who pays or who provides the course, and the very purpose of renewing the credential is to show that the holder stays current.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Business Associate Notice
preguntas.subtema: Business associate breach · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3E k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: The practice's billing vendor suffers a breach of unsecured PHI. What does the vendor owe the practice?
opciones: Notice straight away, and in any event within 60 days of the vendor discovering it
Notice within 30 days, together with the individual notices already mailed on its own
No more than its yearly report to the Secretary, which the practice can look up
Notice only once the practice asks, since the duty to notify patients rests with the practice
preguntas.explicacion: A business associate that suffers a breach has to tell the covered entity straight away, and in any event within 60 days of discovery; it should also identify each affected individual and hand over what the entity needs to write its own notices. Responsibility for notifying the individuals stays with the covered entity, though it may delegate the job to the business associate where that makes more sense.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Implementation of This Model
preguntas.subtema: Max packing · CMAA 4A k49 · CCMA 5C k171 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: While a practice works down its backlog it is told to apply max packing. What does that mean in the appointment book?
opciones: Handling any upcoming preventive or screening need at whatever visit brings the patient in
Booking the patient's next preventive and screening visits before she leaves the office
Replacing one-to-one visits for a chronic condition with a single group visit
Using the telephone and e-mail for concerns that do not really need a visit at all
preguntas.explicacion: Max packing reduces the demand for future visits by dealing with preventive and screening needs whenever the patient is already there, whatever the reason for that visit. Group visits for patients who share a chronic condition, and using phone and e-mail for concerns that need no visit, are two other tactics the same section lists for reducing demand.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: What should I know before my telehealth visit?
preguntas.subtema: Asking for accommodations · CMAA 4H k62 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A deaf patient is being booked for her first video visit. Should she tell the practice about her need for captioning before the day of the visit?
opciones: Yes: she should tell the provider if she needs support such as closed captioning or a screen reader
Yes, but only where the platform the practice uses has no captioning already built into it
No: accommodations are arranged by the clinician once the visit begins and the need is plain
No: a video visit will not suit her, and an office appointment should be booked in its place
preguntas.explicacion: The preparation list for patients includes asking for help where it is needed: the provider is to be told if the patient needs support such as a screen reader, closed captioning or anything else. The same list has her check the visit details in the reminder she is sent, find a quiet place with good internet access, and test the device she will use, with help from the team if she wants it.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth barriers · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.2.a · CMAA 4B k55 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient says her video appointments freeze constantly. Which barrier does HHS name as the biggest one for telehealth?
opciones: No access to an internet service fast enough to carry video reliably
Lack of a telephone line at the address where the patient normally lives
Lack of a signed consent form covering the use of video technology
Lack of a printer at home for the visit summary the clinician sends
preguntas.explicacion: The barrier named as the biggest of all is having no access to an internet service fast enough to carry video. The suggestions offered are that the patient may qualify for federal help through the Lifeline program, that plenty of fast food restaurants push free Wi-Fi out into the parking lot, and that most public libraries offer high-speed internet and often a private room.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.4 Reports to Health Care Team Members
preguntas.subtema: Structured communication · CCMA 6F k198 · CMAA 2E k23
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant is calling a provider about a patient whose incision has turned red. Which detail belongs in the Background section?
opciones: The admitting diagnosis, the code status and known allergies
The abnormal findings and your own read of the situation
The patient's name and location and the recent vital signs
What you want the provider to order, change or reassess
preguntas.explicacion: Background carries the pertinent history: the diagnoses on admission, the code status, allergies, and any recent laboratory or diagnostic result that matters. The abnormal findings and your evaluation go in Assessment, the name, location and vital signs go in Situation, and what you want done goes in Request or Recommendation.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0, Tool: Two-Challenge Rule
preguntas.subtema: Escalation · CCMA 6K k210 · CMAA 2B k25 · NCMA EKB 22
preguntas.pregunta: The safety problem is still unresolved after the concern has been voiced twice. What comes next?
opciones: A stronger course: bring in others and go up the chain
A repeat of the same concern in exactly the same words
A note in the chart that the concern was not accepted
A pause until the next shift takes over the patient
preguntas.explicacion: Where the outcome is still unacceptable, a stronger course falls to the challenger: bring in other team members, then go to the supervisor and up the chain of command. Once the chain is invoked it is essential to tell the whole team that additional input has been sought.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 3, Guidelines for Using a Medical Interpreter
preguntas.subtema: Interpreters · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17 · RMA I.D.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: What has the use of a trained medical interpreter been linked to?
opciones: Fewer communication errors and shorter stays in hospital
Longer visits that patients go on to rate as less satisfying
More readmissions, because instructions have to be repeated
Fewer forms, since consent can then be taken out loud
preguntas.explicacion: Facilities are required by the accrediting body to provide qualified medical interpreters, and using one is tied to hospital stays that are shorter, communication errors that are fewer, fewer readmissions within thirty days and better patient satisfaction. The distractors reverse each of those findings.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Evacuation Plans and Procedures eTool, Emergency Action Plan: Minimum Requirements [29 CFR 1910.38(c)]
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.B.8.a · 2027 I.B.7.a · CMAA 3 k45 · RMA II.7.c · NCMA 2A.9 EKB 8
preguntas.pregunta: Under OSHA's emergency action plan rule, which element must the plan contain?
opciones: A way to account for all employees once the evacuation is finished
A list of the medicines kept in the office emergency supplies
A copy of the safety data sheet for every product in the building
A record of the annual training given to each employee by name
preguntas.explicacion: The rule sets a floor of six elements: a way to report fires and other emergencies, the evacuation procedures with escape routes assigned, procedures for employees who stay to run critical operations, accounting for everyone after the evacuation, rescue and medical duties for those who perform them, and names or job titles to contact.

preguntas.subtema: Charting standards · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 7A · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which five attributes must every patient medical record entry carry under the Medicare conditions of participation?
opciones: Dated, timed, legible, complete and authenticated by the person responsible
Typed, countersigned, numbered, indexed and filed by the medical record service
Dated, timed, legible, complete and witnessed by a second member of the staff
Handwritten, dated, timed, initialed and stamped with the practice identifier
preguntas.explicacion: Every entry has to be authenticated, dated and timed, and it must be legible and complete; the person who provided or evaluated the service is the one who signs it, on paper or electronically, in line with the facility's own policies. The same condition of participation asks the hospital to run a system that identifies authors and keeps records so that the authentication stays trustworthy and every entry stays secure.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Challenges of This Model
preguntas.subtema: Measuring demand · CMAA 4A k49 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice plans to estimate how many same-day slots it will need from last year's appointment counts. What is wrong with that?
opciones: Past appointments reflect the clinical time that was on offer more than the demand there was
Past appointments reflect the demand there was, though not the urgency behind any of it
Past appointments cannot be used because the practice has since changed its appointment types
Past appointments reflect demand well, but the count has to be adjusted for the no-show rate
preguntas.explicacion: The model needs accurate figures for the size of each doctor's panel, for the level of demand and for the slots free each day. Demand is hard to read backwards: how many appointments were held in the past says more about the clinical time on offer than about what patients wanted. It has to be gathered going forward, by tracking the calls patients make and the follow-ups clinicians ask for.

preguntas.subtema: Inpatient procedure code set · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · CMA III.G.1 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital reports the operations it performed on its own inpatients. Which standard code set does the regulation adopt for those procedures?
opciones: The tenth revision procedure coding system for hospital inpatients
The tenth revision clinical modification used for the conditions treated
The combination of the common procedure system and the physician code set
The common procedure coding system used for supplies and equipment
preguntas.explicacion: For procedures and other actions taken on hospital inpatients and reported by hospitals, the standard is the tenth revision procedure coding system, covering prevention, diagnosis, treatment and management. The clinical modification of the same revision is the standard for diseases, injuries, impairments and their causes.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Remittance Processing
preguntas.subtema: Charge reconciliation · CMAA 6B · CCMA 5K k187 · CMA III.G.7.c / 2027 III.G.6.b
preguntas.pregunta: A contracted plan allows $80 for a service the office charges $120 at. How is the $40 handled at posting?
opciones: It is posted as a contractual adjustment, since the contract sets the allowed amount
It is posted as a patient balance, since the plan paid less than the amount charged
It is posted as a bad debt, since the office will not collect that money at all
It is posted as a denial, and an appeal is filed to recover the difference later
preguntas.explicacion: During remittance processing the payments are posted and the difference between the charge and the agreed fee schedule is written off; defining contractual and noncontractual write-offs clearly is part of resolving denials. A provider inside the network has accepted the allowed amount, so the gap cannot be billed to the patient. Bad debt is uncollected patient money, and no denial occurred here.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: One note in a chart says dysphagia and another says dysphasia. Which contrast between the two endings is correct?
opciones: The first is about swallowing and the second is about speech
The first is about speech and the second is about swallowing
The first is about breathing and the second is about swallowing
The first is about swallowing and the second is about breathing
preguntas.explicacion: A single letter separates them. The part -phagia, also written -phagy, is eating or swallowing, and -phasia is speech; dys- in front of either means difficult or abnormal. Breathing is -pnea, which is the ending in apnea and in dyspnea, so it belongs to neither of these two words.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, STEP
preguntas.subtema: Teamwork · CCMA 6L k202 · CMAA 2F k21
preguntas.pregunta: In the STEP tool, what falls under Environment?
opciones: Facility and administrative information, triage acuity and equipment
Fatigue, workload, task performance, skill level and stress level
History, vital signs, medications, plan of care and preferences
The team's goals, the tasks under way and whether the plan fits
preguntas.explicacion: STEP helps a person monitor the critical elements of a situation. Status of the patient covers history, vital signs, medications, exam, plan of care and psychosocial concerns; Team members covers fatigue, workload, performance, skill and stress; Environment covers information about the facility and its administration, the human resources, the acuity at triage and the equipment; Progress covers the goals.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medigap (Medicare Supplement Insurance)
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient enrolled in a Medicare Advantage Plan asks the office to help her buy a Medigap policy. What is the obstacle?
opciones: Medigap is sold only to people who have Original Medicare, both Part A and Part B
Medigap is sold only during the Medicare Open Enrollment Period held every year
Medigap is sold only to people who also carry a separate Part D drug plan
Medigap is sold only to people who paid Medicare taxes for at least ten years
preguntas.explicacion: Medigap is extra insurance bought from a private company to help with the enrollee's share of costs in Original Medicare, such as copayments, coinsurance and deductibles. It can only be bought by someone who has Original Medicare, which generally means signing up for Part A and Part B before a Medigap policy can be purchased at all.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Uses and Disclosures for Treatment, Payment, and Health Care Operations
preguntas.subtema: Health care operations · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which activity is a health care operation under the Privacy Rule?
opciones: Reviewing the competence and qualifications of health care professionals
Sending a chart to the specialist who will see the patient next month
Submitting a claim to the health plan for the visit performed yesterday
Releasing records to a life insurer weighing an application for a policy
preguntas.explicacion: Health care operations are the administrative, legal, financial and quality-improvement work that keeps the business running and supports treatment and payment. The list takes in quality assessment and improvement; care coordination and case management; reviews of how competent and how qualified the professionals are and how they perform; training; accreditation, licensing and credentialing; medical review and auditing; fraud detection; and compliance programs.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, "Talking With Your Older Patients", Compensating for hearing deficits
preguntas.subtema: Hearing impairment · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with hearing loss mixes up letters and numbers at the front desk. What helps?
opciones: Giving context, such as reading the digits one by one
Writing down only the first letter of each spoken word
Speaking faster so the whole phrase arrives together
Repeating the same number in a higher pitched voice
preguntas.explicacion: Give context for letters and numbers that sound alike: name a word beginning with the letter, or read a two-digit number out as its separate digits. Letters that sound similar call for extra care. Raising the pitch works against the patient, since a high-pitched voice is harder to hear.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.524(b)(1) and (b)(2), Requests for access and timely action
preguntas.subtema: Right of access deadline · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks for a copy of her lab results. Under HIPAA, how long does the covered entity have to act on the request?
opciones: No later than 30 days after receipt, with one possible 30-day extension explained in writing
No later than 60 days after receipt, the same limit as breach notification
No later than 15 days after receipt, the same limit as the OSHA written opinion after exposure
No later than 10 working days, with unlimited extensions if the record is large or on paper
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.524(b)(2) requires action on an access request no later than 30 days after receipt, either granting access or giving a written denial; if the entity cannot act in time it may take one extension of no more than 30 days, provided it tells the individual in writing, within the original period, the reason and the date it will finish. The entity may require requests in writing if it says so. Sixty days is the breach notification limit and 15 days the OSHA written opinion; neither governs access.

preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.D Interpersonal Relations · CCMA 6G k204 telephone under HIPAA · CMAA 3B k33 · RMA I.C.1.b disclosure laws
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks that laboratory results be mailed to a post office box instead of her home, and never left on the home voicemail. How must the practice respond?
opciones: It must let her ask for an alternative means or location for these communications
It must refuse, because the address of record is the only lawful place to send them
It must obtain a written authorization from her before using any other address at all
It must ask her to explain why the usual address would put her in any kind of danger
preguntas.explicacion: Health plans and covered providers have to let people ask that communications come by some other means, or to some other place, than the entity normally uses: a chosen address or phone number, a sealed envelope instead of a postcard. A provider may make compliance conditional on being given a workable alternative and on knowing how payment will be handled. Only health plans face the endangerment test.

preguntas.subtema: Sanction policy · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A receptionist is found opening a neighbour's chart out of curiosity. Which required specification should already have been in place for that?
opciones: A sanction policy for workforce members who break the security policies
A termination procedure that ends access when a person leaves the practice
A workforce clearance procedure that decides whether the access was proper
A log-in monitoring procedure that watches attempts and reports differences
preguntas.explicacion: The security management process calls for sanctions, appropriate to the case, against any member of the workforce who does not follow the security policies and procedures. Clearance, termination and log-in monitoring are addressable specifications that decide on access or watch it; only the sanction policy answers what happens to the person afterwards.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Cost sharing
preguntas.subtema: Insurance terminology · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: Which costs are included in the term cost sharing?
opciones: Deductibles, copayments and coinsurance for the services a plan covers
Premiums, deductibles and the charges for services a plan does not cover
Premiums and any amount a non-network provider bills above the allowed rate
Only the copayment collected at the desk on the day of the covered service
preguntas.explicacion: Cost sharing is the part of covered costs the patient pays personally, and the glossary names deductibles, coinsurance and copayments as the examples. It leaves out premiums, amounts balance billed by providers outside the network, and services the plan does not cover. Medicaid and CHIP are the exception where premiums are counted as cost sharing. The copayment alone is only one piece of it.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Service Animals (inquiries, exclusions, charges)
preguntas.subtema: ADAAA compliance · CMAA 3A (ADAAA)
preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives with a dog and it is not obvious what the dog does. What may the front desk ask?
opciones: Whether the dog is required for a disability and what task it performs
Whether the dog is required for a disability and to see its certificate
What the person's disability is and how long the dog has been trained
To see the dog demonstrate the task and to show its vaccination card
preguntas.explicacion: Only two questions are allowed: whether a disability is the reason the dog is required as a service animal, and what work or task it has been trained to perform. Staff may not ask about the disability itself, require medical documentation, demand a special identification card or training papers, or ask the dog to demonstrate anything.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) General Information
preguntas.subtema: Procedural coding · CMA III.G.1.c (2027 III.G.1.c) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: A supplier wants a new HCPCS Level II code created for a product it sells. Who is allowed to ask for it?
opciones: Anyone may ask CMS to change the national code set
Only the manufacturer that holds the product license
Only a Medicare contractor may put the request in
Only the association that maintains Level I may do it
preguntas.explicacion: CMS decides on additions, revisions and deletions to HCPCS Level II, and anyone may submit a request to modify the national code set through its electronic application system. Drug and biological applications are due at the start of each quarter, and applications for other items twice a year.

preguntas.fuente: TRICARE, Health Plans
preguntas.subtema: Insurance types · CMA III.G.4.d (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182
preguntas.pregunta: A TRICARE beneficiary at the front desk is not sure which of the program's plans she is enrolled in. Where can she find out?
opciones: In the enrollment system for the uniformed services, or from her regional contractor
In her yearly explanation of benefits, or from the pharmacy that fills her drugs
In the plan comparison tool, or from the military treatment facility nearest her
In the health insurance Marketplace, or from her former unit's personnel office
preguntas.explicacion: A beneficiary who does not know which plan she holds can log into her DEERS account through the milConnect portal, or telephone her regional contractor. The plan finder and the side-by-side comparison tool are there for choosing among plans, which is a different question from looking up the plan already held.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A chart note lists tonsillitis as the reason for the visit. What does the ending of that term tell you?
opciones: That the structure named by the root is inflamed
That the structure named by the root has been removed
That the structure named by the root has been cut into
That the structure named by the root is drooping down
preguntas.explicacion: The ending -itis means inflammation, so tonsillitis is inflamed tonsils. The endings that get mixed up with it point elsewhere: -ectomy is cutting a part out, -otomy is an incision, and -ptosis is a falling or drooping. Reading the ending first tells you what is happening to whatever the root names.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology
preguntas.subtema: Pre-appointment screening · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · CMAA 4H k62 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A first-time telehealth patient is being screened before her appointment. Which question belongs in that screening?
opciones: Whether she has a device with a camera and microphone that works with the platform
Whether she prefers the practice to bill her insurer before or after the appointment
Whether she would rather receive her visit summary by letter or by facsimile
Whether she agrees to have the encounter recorded for the practice training file
preguntas.explicacion: The checklist for learning about a patient's technology asks whether she has a camera and a microphone on a computer, a tablet or a mobile device, and whether those work with the platform; whether her internet connection carries enough bandwidth for video; whether she has a secure place with internet from which to take the appointment; and whether she needs a hand setting up an e-mail account where the platform requires one.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Uncompensated care; and PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Remittance Processing
preguntas.subtema: Collections · CMA III.G.9.c (2027 III.G.6.e) · CMAA 6 k83, 6D · CCMA 5K k187
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital reports the care it gave that was never reimbursed. What is the term for that?
opciones: Uncompensated care, which nobody ever pays the provider for
A contractual adjustment, agreed with the plan beforehand
A balance bill, sent to the patient for what is left over
An underpayment, where the payer paid less than the contract
preguntas.explicacion: Uncompensated care is health care or services that hospitals or providers give without being reimbursed, and it often arises where people have no insurance and cannot afford to pay. A contractual adjustment is the difference the contract itself gives up, and an underpayment is what a payer still owes under that contract.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Incidental Uses and Disclosures: General Provision
preguntas.subtema: Incidental disclosures · CCMA 6 k204 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA II.B.3.g · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A visitor in the waiting room glimpses another patient's name on the sign-in sheet. Is that a violation?
opciones: No, it is an incidental disclosure, permitted where safeguards and minimum necessary are in place
No, because sign-in sheets are excluded from the definition of protected health information
Yes, because the rule requires that every risk of an unintended disclosure be eliminated first
Yes, unless each patient signed an authorization allowing the office to use a sign-in sheet
preguntas.explicacion: OCR treats the glimpse of a sign-in sheet, or a conversation overheard at a nursing station, as an incidental disclosure: a secondary one that no reasonable step could have prevented, that is limited in nature, and that flows from something the rule already allows. It is permitted as long as reasonable safeguards and the minimum necessary policies are applied to the underlying use.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Helping patients prepare for their telehealth appointment
preguntas.subtema: Information to provide beforehand · CMAA 4E k59 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A video visit is booked to review a patient's medicines. Which item does the guidance tell the office to ask her to have ready?
opciones: The bottles themselves or a list of them, plus the pharmacy's contact details
The claim forms the pharmacy sent after the last two prescriptions were filled
The plan's drug list, so the tier of each medicine can be checked on screen
The explanation of benefits the insurer mailed after her last prescription
preguntas.explicacion: Depending on the nature of the appointment, the office may ask the patient to prepare a list of her current medicines or gather the actual bottles, her medical history, the symptoms and questions she wants to raise, her pharmacy's contact information, measurements such as weight and temperature, and a flashlight or phone light if her throat will be examined.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Abandonment", Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Abandonment · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a(4) · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.9 · CMAA 3A k31
preguntas.pregunta: What is patient abandonment?
opciones: Ending the relationship one-sidedly without notice enough to find other care
Ending the relationship after the patient has missed several appointments
Refusing to treat a person who has never been seen at the practice before
Transferring a patient to a specialist without telling the primary clinician
preguntas.explicacion: Abandonment is a breach of duty: the clinician terminates the relationship one-sidedly and without giving the patient adequate notice to arrange substitute medical care. It presupposes that a clinician-patient relationship existed, which starts when the clinician acts on the patient's diagnosis or treatment, or agrees to. Someone never seen at the practice is not yet in that relationship.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Filing an appeal
preguntas.subtema: Denials and appeals · CMA III.G.5.b (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6E · CCMA 5M
preguntas.pregunta: Which decision may a person with Medicare take to appeal?
opciones: The amount she is required to pay for a service, supply, item or drug
The provider her plan assigned for a service she has not yet received
The pharmacy her plan asked her to use for a drug it already covers
The appointment time the office offered her for a covered procedure
preguntas.explicacion: An appeal can ask for five things: that a service, supply, item or drug be covered; that one already received be paid for; that the amount the patient owes be changed; that coverage not stop for something she still needs; and a review of an at-risk label under the plan's drug management program. Scheduling, and the choice of provider or pharmacy, are not on that list.

preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.1.c restrict access · CMAA 3D patient's bill of rights
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks the practice not to share his information with a particular specialist. What does the Privacy Rule require of the practice?
opciones: Only weigh the request, because this is not one of the restrictions it is obliged to accept
It must agree, because a restriction request binds the covered entity once it is written down
It must agree unless the specialist is inside the same organized health care arrangement
It must agree for one year, after which the restriction lapses unless the patient renews it
preguntas.explicacion: Individuals may ask that information be restricted for treatment, payment or operations, or towards people involved in their care, and the practice is free to say no to a request like this one. Only one restriction has to be granted: when the patient has paid in full out of pocket, that item may be kept from the health plan. Once a restriction is accepted it binds, except for emergency treatment.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, HHS Agencies & Offices: Health Resources and Services Administration
preguntas.subtema: Community resources · CCMA 4D k164 · CMAA 2H k30
preguntas.pregunta: Which agency serves people who are isolated geographically, or vulnerable economically or medically?
opciones: HRSA, the health resources agency, inside the Public Health Service
The Administration for Community Living, which widens access to local support
The Indian Health Service, which serves American Indians and Alaska Natives
SAMHSA, the administration for substance abuse and mental health services
preguntas.explicacion: HRSA belongs to the Public Health Service, and it delivers health care to people who are isolated geographically or vulnerable economically or medically; the Health Center Program a patient can be referred to is one of its programs. The Administration for Community Living is the one widening access to support for older adults and for people with disabilities.

preguntas.subtema: Advance directive information · CCMA 5D · CMA I.A.5 · RMA I.C.1.f · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital admits an adult patient. What does the advance directive regulation require the facility to do?
opciones: Give written information about the patient's rights to make care decisions
Require the patient to sign an advance directive before treatment can begin
Contact the patient's next of kin to obtain an advance directive on her behalf
File a copy of any directive with the State agency within ninety days of admission
preguntas.explicacion: The regulation reaches hospitals, critical access hospitals, skilled nursing and nursing facilities, home health agencies, hospices, and those religious institutions providing nonmedical health care alike: each keeps written policies on advance directives for every adult in its care, and each hands the adult written information about the rights State law gives her over decisions about her care, the right to accept or refuse treatment included, and about drawing up a directive should she wish to.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Days to Pay
preguntas.subtema: Tracking unpaid claims · CMA III.G.3.b(5) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6 k81 · CCMA 5 k181 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: Two weeks after a batch of claims went out, nothing has come back from the payer. What does the guidance on tracking submitted claims advise?
opciones: Set a reminder to check on every claim within twenty-one days of submission
Wait for the remittance advice, which every payer owes within thirty days
Send the whole batch again on paper so the payer cannot say it never arrived
Write the balances off and bill the patients once ninety days have gone by
preguntas.explicacion: Among the remedies for slow payment are gathering demographic data accurately, billing accurately, cross-checking entries before submission, confirming that the claims sent were actually received and processed, and setting reminders to follow up on every claim within twenty-one days of submission. Paper is the opposite of a remedy: it always takes longer and hands the payer the excuse that the claim never arrived or is still being processed.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Individual Notice
preguntas.subtema: Individual breach notice · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3E k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: A breach of unsecured PHI is discovered on June 1. When and how must the affected patients be told?
opciones: Without unreasonable delay and within sixty days, in writing by first-class mail
Without unreasonable delay and within thirty days, by telephone call to each patient
Within sixty days of the end of the calendar year, in a single written summary
Within ten working days, by a notice posted at the front desk of the practice
preguntas.explicacion: Individual notice has to go without unreasonable delay, and 60 days after the discovery of the breach is the outer limit. It has to be written and sent by first-class mail, or by e-mail where the person agreed to electronic notices. It describes the breach, the kinds of information involved, the steps the person ought to take, what the entity is doing about it, and how to get in touch.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, Who is eligible for Medicare?; and HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Medicare
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74, 6 k84 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Who is generally eligible for Medicare?
opciones: People 65 or older, and younger people with certain disabilities, ESRD or ALS
People 65 or older, and younger people whose income falls below the poverty level
People 65 or older who worked at least 10 years, and no one under that age
People of any age enrolled in a state program that pays their hospital costs
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare is the federal program for people 65 and older; it also reaches younger people who have a disability, end-stage renal disease, or ALS. The 10 years of Medicare taxes decide whether Part A comes without a premium, not whether the person is eligible at all. Coverage based on low income is Medicaid, which the states run jointly with the federal government.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 3, 3.2 Cultural Diversity and Cultural Humility
preguntas.subtema: Bias and stereotypes · CCMA 6B k193 · CMA F.2.b / 2027 F.1.c · RMA I.D.1.d · CMAA 2C k17
preguntas.pregunta: How should staff treat what they know about a patient's cultural group?
opciones: As background, since beliefs vary inside every culture
As the plan, since group practice predicts the person
As a script, applied the same way to every member
As a warning, since some beliefs will delay the care
preguntas.explicacion: Knowing the traits of a culture or subculture is useful, but each person is unique and beliefs vary within every group, so assumptions about the values of members are to be avoided. Treating culture as static and uniform is stereotyping; asking the patient is what turns background into care.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Handoff
preguntas.subtema: Transitions of care · CCMA 4H k167 · CMA F.4.c / 2027 F.2.c · CMAA 2F
preguntas.pregunta: Which element does a proper handoff have to include?
opciones: Acknowledgment by the receiver, with a chance to ask
A written summary signed by both of the team members
A supervisor present in the room to witness it happen
A copy filed with the risk management office that day
preguntas.explicacion: A handoff is the standardized way of passing information, and with it authority and responsibility, at a transition in care. A proper one carries accountability and responsibility across, clear information, that information spoken aloud, acknowledgment by the receiver, and room to ask and to review.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Mandatory & Optional Medicaid Benefits
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.c (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicaid patient says she has no way of getting to her appointment. What does the federal list of state plan benefits say about that?
opciones: Transportation to medical care is a benefit every state Medicaid program must cover
Dental services are a benefit that every state Medicaid program is obliged to cover
Physical therapy is a benefit that every state Medicaid program is obliged to cover
Private duty nursing is a benefit every state Medicaid program is obliged to cover
preguntas.explicacion: Federal law obliges states to provide the mandatory state plan benefits, and transportation to medical care is one of them, alongside hospital services inpatient and outpatient, laboratory and X-ray, physician services, nursing facility care, home health and family planning. Dental care, physical therapy and private duty nursing sit on the optional list instead.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Telehealth Systems, Function
preguntas.subtema: Synchronous telehealth · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.2.a · CMAA 4B k54 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which service is an example of synchronous telehealth?
opciones: A live video visit between a patient at home and a clinician elsewhere
A digital intake questionnaire the patient completes before the appointment
A continuous glucose monitor transmitting readings to the clinician's dashboard
A secure portal message asking for a refill that the office answers next week
preguntas.explicacion: Synchronous telehealth delivers health information in real time, patient and clinician talking live. The forms listed are video visits direct to the consumer at home from a smartphone or a computer, consultations run clinic-to-clinic and clinician-to-clinician, teletriage in urgent settings, behavioral health encounters by live video, and remote critical care consultations.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.508(b)(4), Prohibition on conditioning of authorizations; 164.508(a)(3)
