preguntas.subtema: Conditioning treatment on authorization · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: May a clinic refuse to draw a patient's blood unless she signs an authorization releasing her results to a marketing company?
opciones: No: treatment may not be conditioned on an authorization, with narrow exceptions
Yes: a covered entity may set any condition it discloses in its notice
Yes, if the marketing company has signed a business associate agreement
No, unless the patient pays out of pocket and in full, which removes the restriction
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.508(b)(4) forbids making treatment, payment, enrollment or the eligibility for benefits hang on the individual signing an authorization. The exceptions are narrow: research-related treatment conditioned on a research authorization, a health plan's enrollment or underwriting authorization sought before enrollment, and care given solely to create PHI for a third party. Marketing needs an authorization of its own under 164.508(a)(3), and a business associate agreement covers services performed for the covered entity, not marketing by an outside company.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare Summary Notice (MSN)
preguntas.subtema: Electronic summary notice · CMAA 5 k78 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.3.b(3) · RMA II.A.2 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with Original Medicare would rather not wait for her summary notice to arrive by post. What does Medicare offer her?
opciones: An e-mail with a link to the notice for any month in which a claim was processed
An e-mail with a link to the notice on the same schedule as the posted version
An e-mail with the notice attached, sent each time a provider submits a claim
An e-mail alert whenever the claim total for the period passes her deductible
preguntas.explicacion: Electronic delivery is an option: choosing it brings an e-mail carrying a link to the notice for any month in which a claim has been processed, without waiting for paper. The posted version arrives at least twice a year, every six months, and only for a period in which services or supplies were actually received.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.3 Adapting Your Communication
preguntas.subtema: Adolescent communication · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(7)(b) / 2027 F.1.d(7)(a) · RMA I.D.1.a · CMAA 2D k17
preguntas.pregunta: Which approach fits an adolescent patient during a visit?
opciones: Give freedom to make choices inside set limits
Give the same play-based demonstration on a doll
Give the whole explanation to the parent present
Give the schedule of the visit without any choices
preguntas.explicacion: For adolescents the guidance is to allow choices to be made freely inside limits that have been established. Play and demonstration on a toy belong to younger children, and handing the explanation to the parent sidelines a patient who is developing abstract thinking and a strong need for privacy.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule, Notice Distribution
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics · CMAA 3B k33 HIPAA guidelines
preguntas.pregunta: An independent laboratory has no waiting room and never meets its patients. What does the Privacy Rule say about its notice of privacy practices?
opciones: It must supply the notice to anyone who asks, and post it on any customer service web site
It is exempt from the notice requirement because it has no direct treatment relationship
It must mail the notice to every patient whose specimen it receives, before it reports out
It must obtain a written acknowledgement of the notice from each patient before testing
preguntas.explicacion: A laboratory is an indirect treatment provider, and the notice obligation still applies: it has to hand the notice to anyone who asks and make it available electronically on any web site it runs to provide customer service or benefits information. Stricter duties fall on providers with a direct treatment relationship: delivery at the first encounter, plus a good-faith attempt at getting the acknowledgement in writing.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse: Prevent, Detect, Report (MLN4649244), Free Samples
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: A drug company leaves free samples at the practice. What may the office do with them?
opciones: Give them to patients free of charge, but never sell them
Sell them at cost to patients who cannot afford the drug
Bill the plan for them at the price a pharmacy charges
Bill Medicare for them once the patient takes the first dose
preguntas.explicacion: Handing free samples to patients at no charge is lawful; selling them is not, and physicians have been prosecuted for billing Medicare for samples they were given. A practice that keeps samples should store them safely and apart from the stock it has bought.

preguntas.fuente: USPS, Compare Mail Services
preguntas.subtema: Mail classes · CCMA 5O · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7G k96 · NCMA 3.6
preguntas.pregunta: Records must reach a hospital across the country by the fastest domestic service the Postal Service offers. Which is it?
opciones: Priority Mail Express, delivered seven days a week
Priority Mail, delivered in two to three days
USPS Ground Advantage, delivered in two to five days
First-Class Mail, the service used for ordinary letters
preguntas.explicacion: Priority Mail Express is described as the fastest domestic shipping service; it runs every day of the week and every day of the year, with limited exceptions, and reaches most United States addresses and post office boxes in one to three days under a money-back guarantee. Priority Mail arrives in two to three days and Ground Advantage in two to five.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, Information Blocking
preguntas.subtema: Information blocking · CCMA 5 k179 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 7 k90 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: A practice delays sending records to a competing clinic in the hope of keeping the patient. What is that practice at risk of being?
opciones: Information blocking, a practice likely to interfere with the use of electronic health information
A breach of unsecured PHI that obliges the practice to give notice inside sixty days
A minimum necessary violation, since the records were not limited to what was needed
An impermissible marketing communication, since the aim was to keep the patient enrolled
preguntas.explicacion: Information blocking names a practice by an actor that would probably get in the way of accessing, exchanging or using electronic health information, unless the law demands it or one of the exceptions covers it. The actors reached are health care providers, health information networks and exchanges, and the developers of certified health IT. For a provider the test is whether it knows the practice is unreasonable and likely to interfere.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Cross-Monitoring
preguntas.subtema: Teamwork · CCMA 6L k202 · CMAA 2F k21 · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: What does cross-monitoring involve?
opciones: Watching the actions and the stress of teammates to catch slips
Scanning the whole situation to keep track of what is going on
Helping a colleague with tasks when the workload gets heavy
Checking that a message was received the way it was intended
preguntas.explicacion: Cross-monitoring is a harm reduction strategy: keeping an eye on what other team members are doing and on the stress they are carrying, providing a safety net, and catching mistakes or oversights early. It is described as watching each other's back. Scanning the situation is situation monitoring, covering someone's work is task assistance, and confirming a message is a check-back.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A problem list records a TIA two years before the CVA the patient was admitted with. What separates those two entries?
opciones: A TIA is a small stroke, and a CVA is the stroke itself
A TIA is a small stroke, and a CVA is a clot in a deep vein
A TIA is a heart attack, and a CVA is a stroke of the brain
A TIA is a brief seizure, and a CVA is a stroke of the brain
preguntas.explicacion: TIA stands for transient ischemic attack, listed as a small stroke, while CVA is a cerebrovascular accident, the stroke or brain attack itself. The abbreviations that get swapped in belong to other organs: AMI and MI are the heart attack, and DVT is the clot in a deep vein.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Body Parts and Disorders
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A referral is addressed to a nephrologist. Which organ does the root of that specialty name?
opciones: The kidney, which is also named by the root ren-
The liver, which is also named by the root hepat-
The bladder, which is also named by the root cyst-
The stomach, which is also named by the root gastr-
preguntas.explicacion: Nephr- and ren- both name the kidney, which is why the same organ gives us nephrology and renal failure. The other roots belong to their own organs: hepat- the liver, cyst- a bladder or sac, gastr- the stomach. Two roots for one organ is common in this vocabulary, one from Greek and one from Latin.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Communication Styles
preguntas.subtema: Communication styles · CCMA 6K k203 · CMAA 2A k13 · CMA F.1.e / 2027 F.1.f · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which description matches a passive communicator?
opciones: One who puts the rights of others first and sounds tentative or apologetic
One who defends their own rights even at the cost of the rights of others
One who respects the rights of others while standing up for their own ideas
One who assumes the message was understood without ever verifying it
preguntas.explicacion: Three styles are described. The passive communicator places everyone else's rights above their own, sounds apologetic or unsure, and stays quiet even when wronged. Defending your own rights at the expense of others is the aggressive style, and balancing both is the assertive one. Assuming understanding without checking describes passive listening, not the passive style.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Does your provider accept Medicare as full payment?
preguntas.subtema: Third-party billing · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 6C k87 · CCMA 5L k185 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: The office accepts assignment for a Medicare patient. What does that oblige it to do about her bill?
opciones: Charge her only the deductible and coinsurance, and file the claim at no charge
Collect the whole charge at the visit and let her seek reimbursement afterwards
Charge up to fifteen percent above the approved amount for each service given
Decide service by service whether the approved amount will be accepted as payment
preguntas.explicacion: Accepting assignment means treating the amount Medicare approves as payment in full, and it holds for every Part A and Part B service the provider gives. Such a provider agrees to charge only the deductible and the coinsurance, usually waits for Medicare to pay its share first, and has to send the claim to Medicare without charging the patient for doing it.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Defining the PCMH
preguntas.subtema: Delivery models · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: Which statement best describes what a patient-centered medical home is?
opciones: A model for organizing primary care that delivers its core functions
A building where several specialties share one waiting room and one chart room
A group of providers whose payment is tied to quality goals and cost savings
A plan that pays a fixed amount per patient no matter what services follow
preguntas.explicacion: The medical home is understood not simply as a place but as a model for organizing primary care so that the core functions of primary health care get delivered. Five functions and attributes define it: comprehensive care, patient-centered care, coordinated care, accessible services, and a commitment to quality and safety.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 6A, 5 k68 · CCMA 5I k184 · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: An outpatient X-ray has been interpreted and the final report is on the chart when the coder works it. What is done with the symptoms that prompted it?
opciones: The confirmed diagnosis is coded and the related symptoms are left off
The related symptoms are coded first and the confirmed diagnosis second
The confirmed diagnosis is coded and the related symptoms follow it
Only the symptoms are coded, since a radiologist read the study
preguntas.explicacion: Where an outpatient diagnostic test has been read by a physician and the report is on the chart when the coding is done, any confirmed or definitive diagnosis in that reading is coded, and related signs and symptoms are not added. The guidelines flag this as different from the inpatient practice with abnormal test findings.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Error Prevention and Root Cause Analysis", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Incident reports and analysis · CCMA 6M k211 · CMAA 3 k44
preguntas.pregunta: Within what period must an accredited organization finish its analysis and action plan after a sentinel event?
opciones: Within 45 business days of recognizing the event
Within 30 business days of recognizing the event
Within 60 business days of recognizing the event
Within 10 business days of recognizing the event
preguntas.explicacion: An accredited organization has to keep a formal process for spotting sentinel events, running an analysis that is timely and credible, and then putting in place a corrective action and risk-reduction plan, documented, that measures whether the improvements worked. The whole process has to be complete within 45 business days of the event being recognized.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), Table 1; and CMS, Coordination of Benefits & Recovery Overview
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMA III.G.4.f (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k72 · CCMA 5B
preguntas.pregunta: Which coverages make up what Medicare calls a non-group health plan?
opciones: No-fault insurance, workers' compensation, and liability cover with self-insurance
Retiree coverage, employer group coverage and coverage bought on the Marketplace
Medigap policies, employer supplemental plans and the state Medicaid programs
Medigap policies, the Marketplace, and liability cover with self-insurance
preguntas.explicacion: A non-group health plan means liability insurance, self-insured entities included, together with no-fault insurers and workers' compensation, and all such claims go to that insurer before they go to Medicare. Medigap, employer supplemental plans and Medicaid sit on the other side of the picture: they receive Medicare-paid claims through the crossover agreement, with Medicare usually paying first.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Introduction to the Americans with Disabilities Act: Title V
preguntas.subtema: Declining an accommodation · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.c · CMAA 7 k98 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with low vision declines the large-print forms the office offers her. What does the law say about that refusal?
opciones: She is free to decline an aid or accommodation she does not want to accept
She must accept it once it has been prepared, or sign a waiver of her rights
She may decline it only if she brings a companion who will read the forms
She may decline it, but the office must then record the refusal in her chart
preguntas.explicacion: The last title of the law collects the rules on how the rest of it operates, and one of them says outright that nobody with a disability has to accept an aid, a service or an accommodation that is offered. The same title bars retaliation against anyone who has asserted these rights.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), Your Responsibilities
preguntas.subtema: Insurance verification · CMA III.G.3.a (2027 III.G.3.a) · CMAA 5B k66 · CCMA 5B
preguntas.pregunta: An institutional provider asks what to do with the eligibility response once the Medicare Secondary Payer questions have been asked.
opciones: Both the patient's answers and the eligibility response go into the health record
Only the patient's answers go in; the eligibility response stays with the biller
Only the eligibility response goes in; the patient's answers stay at registration
Both go on the claim instead of the record, as condition and value code entries
preguntas.explicacion: Institutional providers are told to have patients update their insurance profile at every visit before services are given, to administer the secondary payer questions each time they treat or admit the patient, and to bring the patient's answers together with the verification from the 271 eligibility response into their health records. Condition, occurrence and value codes belong on the claim and do not replace what the record has to hold.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Effective Team Event Tools
preguntas.subtema: Teamwork · CCMA 6L k202 · CMAA 2F k21 · CMA F.4.c / 2027 F.2.c · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: The team meets before the clinic session opens to share the plan, hand out roles and set expectations. Which tool is that?
opciones: A brief, held before the work starts
A huddle, called during the session
A debrief, once the session is over
A handoff, as responsibility passes
preguntas.explicacion: Sharing the plan is the brief: a short session before the start that covers team formation, roles and responsibilities, expectations, climate and likely contingencies. The huddle is the ad hoc meeting that monitors and modifies the plan along the way, the debrief reviews performance afterwards, and a handoff transfers responsibility for a patient.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Error Prevention and Root Cause Analysis", Function
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.B Quality Improvement · CCMA 6 k211 incident and event reports · CMAA 3E k44
preguntas.pregunta: What distinguishes a sentinel event from a preventable adverse event?
opciones: The sentinel event is defined by how severe the outcome is; the other is defined by being caused by an error
The preventable adverse event is defined by how severe the outcome is; the other one by being caused by an error
The sentinel event reaches the patient, while the preventable adverse event is stopped before it does
The sentinel event is reported to the state agency, while the preventable adverse event stays internal
preguntas.explicacion: What divides them is the defining criterion, not the setting. A preventable adverse event is harm to a patient traced back to an error or to a clinician's inaction, so causation is what defines it. A sentinel event is defined by how severe the outcome was: death, severe harm or permanent harm reaching a patient. Wrong-site surgery is both; where a medication error does temporary harm, only the first applies. An error caught before it reaches the patient is a near miss.

preguntas.fuente: USPS, Compare Mail Services
preguntas.subtema: Proof of delivery · CCMA 5O · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7G k96 · NCMA 3.6
preguntas.pregunta: The office needs proof that a letter of withdrawal from care reached the patient. What does First-Class Mail alone provide?
opciones: No delivery confirmation, unless a service such as Certified Mail is added
Delivery confirmation on every letter, included in the price of the stamp
A money-back guarantee if the letter arrives later than the date promised
Insurance up to one hundred dollars, included at no additional charge
preguntas.explicacion: First-Class Mail covers standard-sized single-piece envelopes up to 3.5 ounces and large envelopes up to 13 ounces. The comparison table shows no delivery confirmation for it, with the note that confirmation becomes available once a service such as Certified Mail is added. The money-back guarantee belongs to Priority Mail Express, and the hundred dollars of included insurance to Ground Advantage.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms: Cost-sharing Reductions
preguntas.subtema: Cost sharing · CMA III.G.6.e (2027 III.G.6.d) · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5E k178 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A Marketplace shopper with a low income asks how to get the extra discounts on what she will pay at the doctor. What does she need to choose?
opciones: A silver level plan, which is where those discounts sit
A premium tax credit, which lowers what she pays monthly
A grandfathered plan, bought before the law took effect
A high deductible plan paired with a savings account
preguntas.explicacion: Cost-sharing reductions are discounts on what the member pays for covered services in an individual Marketplace plan. They are available where income is below a certain level and the member picks a silver level plan, or where the member belongs to a federally recognized tribe. The premium tax credit is the separate help that lowers the monthly premium.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026, Section I.B.7
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A code tells the coder to code any causal condition first, if one applies, and none is known here. What follows?
opciones: That code may itself be the first-listed diagnosis
That code may not be reported at all at this encounter
The symptom code takes the first-listed position instead
An unspecified code from the category is listed first
preguntas.explicacion: A note that asks for the causal condition first, if any applies, means the code it sits under may be assigned as the principal diagnosis, or listed first, where that cause is unknown or does not apply here. Where the cause is known, that condition is what goes first, in the same way as the etiology in a code first note.

preguntas.fuente: Child Welfare Information Gateway, Mandatory Reporting of Child Abuse and Neglect (May 2023), Disclosure of the Reporter's Identity
preguntas.subtema: Mandatory reporting · CCMA 7F k222 · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k43
preguntas.pregunta: What protection does a reporter's identity normally have?
opciones: It is shielded from the alleged perpetrator in most jurisdictions
It is shielded from the investigating agency until a case is opened
It is published with the report once the investigation has closed
It is shielded only when the report turns out to be substantiated
preguntas.explicacion: Every jurisdiction keeps abuse and neglect records confidential, and in 44 states plus the District of Columbia and several territories the identity of the reporter is specifically shielded from being disclosed to the alleged perpetrator, even where other information from the report comes out. Some places release the name in narrow circumstances, such as a finding that the report was knowingly false.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Helping patients prepare for their telehealth appointment
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth scheduling detail · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.2.a · CMAA 4B k54 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A telehealth appointment has been booked for a nine-year-old. What should the office confirm with the family in advance?
opciones: Who needs to be available, since the minor must be present and the parent may be too
That the child will hold the device alone, so the clinician can assess her unaided
That the parent will complete the visit while the child stays out of the room
That the school nurse will join the call to act as the telehealth facilitator
preguntas.explicacion: Among the topics to discuss with a patient before a first virtual visit, the guidance lists treating the appointment as one would an in-person visit, how the patient will connect, and who needs to be available: for a minor, it says to make clear that the minor needs to be present and whether the parent should or should not also be there. It also covers what to do if the appointment cannot be kept or the connection fails.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Effective Team Event Tools
preguntas.subtema: Teamwork · CCMA 6L k202 · CMAA 2F k21 · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: What is a debrief for?
opciones: Reviewing how the team performed and drawing out the lessons
Sharing the plan and handing out roles before the work starts
Re-establishing awareness partway through and adjusting the plan
Passing responsibility and accountability on to the next person
preguntas.explicacion: The debrief reviews the team's performance: a structured, intentional but informal and quick exchange meant to improve performance through lessons learned and by reinforcing what went well. Sharing the plan up front is the brief, re-establishing situational awareness in the middle is the huddle, and passing responsibility is a handoff.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Procedures, Diagnosis and Surgery
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.c (2027 I.A.2.c) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: An operative report is titled appendectomy. Which ending would have been used instead if the surgeon had only cut into the appendix?
opciones: -otomy, the ending that names an incision
-ostomy, the ending that names an opening
-plasty, the ending for a reconstruction
-pexy, the ending for a surgical fixation
preguntas.explicacion: The four surgical endings are close cousins and each names a different act: -ectomy cuts the part out, -otomy only cuts into it, -ostomy makes an opening, -plasty rebuilds and -pexy anchors a part in place. An appendectomy removes the appendix, so an incision alone would have carried -otomy.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Nonverbal Communication
preguntas.subtema: Nonverbal cues · CCMA 6C k197 · CMAA 2C k14 · CMA F.1.d / 2027 F.1.e
preguntas.pregunta: A patient seated in the exam room is about to hear sensitive results. Where should the assistant place themselves?
opciones: At the patient's eye level, seated, facing them and leaning in
Standing beside the chair so both can watch the computer screen
Behind the desk, facing the chart, with the door left open
At a right angle to the patient, with an eye on the exit
preguntas.explicacion: Initial and sensitive exchanges land better when both people are at eye level, and bringing a chair over helps. Facing the patient, making eye contact and leaning a little forward signal full attention. Standing at a right angle with an awareness of the exits is the posture kept for a patient who may become aggressive.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), If the Primary Payer Denies the Claim
preguntas.subtema: Third-party billing · CMA III.G.3.b(4) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6 k87 · CCMA 5 k185
preguntas.pregunta: A workers' compensation carrier denied the bill and the office now wants Medicare to pay it. What has to go with the Medicare claim?
opciones: The reason the compensation insurer gave for denying, taken from its remittance
A letter from the patient's attorney saying the case is still being contested
A copy of the compensation policy showing the condition is excluded from it
A statement that the compensation carrier was billed first and made no payment
preguntas.explicacion: The claim always goes to the primary payer first. When a liability, no-fault or workers' compensation insurer denies on liability grounds, that insurer has to put the reason for the denial on the claim; the provider finds it on the remittance advice it received and sends it on to Medicare. Without that reason Medicare denies the claim. In an electronic remittance the reason lives in the claim adjustment segment.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Non-preferred provider; and Glossary: Preferred provider
preguntas.subtema: In-network and out-of-network coverage · CMAA 4 k61 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: What is a non-preferred provider?
opciones: A provider with no contract with the plan, whom the patient pays more to see
A provider with a contract with the plan whose discount is smaller than usual
A provider the plan removed from its network after a quality review of the care
A provider the patient may see only when the primary care doctor refers her there
preguntas.explicacion: The non-preferred provider is simply one who has no contract with the insurer or plan, so the patient pays more for that care. A contracted provider whose discount is smaller is described in the glossary as a participating provider inside a tiered network. Removal after a quality review and referral requirements are separate matters; the definition turns on the contract alone.

preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, remission
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k5 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is told the disease is in complete remission. What does that phrase mean?
opciones: Every sign and symptom has gone, though cancer may still be present
Every sign and symptom has gone, so the cancer is considered cured
Some of the signs and symptoms have gone and the others have not
The signs have gone but the tests still show the disease clearly
preguntas.explicacion: Remission means the signs and symptoms of a cancer have lessened or gone. Partial remission is when some of them have gone; complete remission is when all of them have, although cancer may still be in the body. That last clause is why complete remission and cure are not the same word.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Defining the PCMH: 1. Comprehensive Care
preguntas.subtema: Delivery models · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: Which function of the medical home makes the practice accountable for most of a patient's physical and mental health needs?
opciones: Comprehensive care, which calls for a team of care providers to meet those needs
Coordinated care, which links the practice with hospitals and the community services
Accessible services, which shorten waits and extend hours for urgent problems
Patient-centered care, which treats the family as a core member of the team
preguntas.explicacion: Comprehensive care makes the primary care medical home accountable for the bulk of each patient's health needs, physical and mental alike: prevention, wellness, care that is acute and care that is chronic. Delivering that takes a team, which may bring together nurses and physicians, pharmacists, physician assistants, advanced practice nurses, nutritionists, care coordinators, social workers and educators.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease", Introduction and Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(6) (2027 I.C.6.g(6)) · RMA I.A.2.a · CMAA 1 k10 · NCMA 1.10
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports heartburn and regurgitation after meals. Which structure normally prevents that, and what is the diagnosis?
opciones: The lower esophageal sphincter; the diagnosis is gastroesophageal reflux disease
The lower esophageal sphincter; the diagnosis is peptic ulcer disease
The pyloric sphincter; the diagnosis is gastroesophageal reflux disease
The upper esophageal sphincter; the diagnosis is irritable bowel syndrome
preguntas.explicacion: The usual complaints in gastroesophageal reflux disease are heartburn, regurgitation, and chest pain that is not cardiac; with symptoms as typical as those the diagnosis can be made presumptively. What normally holds the contents down is the lower esophageal sphincter, a physiological sphincter three to five centimeters long whose high resting tone keeps stomach contents out of the esophagus.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Home Care Services: Summary
preguntas.subtema: Non-clinical community resources · CCMA 4D k164 · CMAA 2H k30
preguntas.pregunta: Which help falls under home care services rather than under the Medicare home health benefit?
opciones: Housework, cooking or meal delivery, and help keeping the bills paid on time
Wound care for a pressure sore, given by a skilled nurse who visits her at home
Intravenous or nutrition therapy given at home by a skilled visiting nurse
Occupational therapy at home for a patient recovering from a serious stroke
preguntas.explicacion: Home care lets a person with special needs stay at home, whether through aging in place, chronic illness, recovery from surgery or disability. It covers personal care such as bathing or dressing; chores such as laundry, cleaning and yard work; cooking or delivered meals; help with forms and bills; and health care from an aide or through telehealth. Many of these are paid privately.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse (MLN4649244), Physician Self-Referral Law
preguntas.subtema: Compliance · CMAA 3 k46, 6 k85 · CCMA 7A
preguntas.pregunta: A practice discovers it was overpaid by Medicare. How soon must the money be reported and returned?
opciones: Within 60 days of identifying the overpayment, to avoid liability
Within 120 days of identifying the overpayment, to avoid liability
Within 12 months, the same deadline that applies to filing a claim
When the contractor requests it after its next scheduled record review
preguntas.explicacion: An overpayment is money paid by Medicare that the recipient is not entitled to, and it must be reported and returned within 60 days of being identified; missing that window can create False Claims Act liability and whistleblower exposure. The 120-day figures belong to the bad debt collection rules, and 12 months is the timely filing limit for claims, so neither governs a refund.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Part A (Hospital Insurance) costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74, 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient's inpatient stay runs to sixty-eight days. What does she pay for days sixty-one to sixty-eight in 2026?
opciones: $434 for each of those days, on top of the deductible she has already paid
$868 for each of those days, which is the rate that starts at day ninety-one
$217 for each of those days, which is the rate for a skilled nursing stay
No charge for those days, because the deductible already covers the whole stay
preguntas.explicacion: Under Part A in 2026 an inpatient stay costs nothing for days one to sixty once the deductible is paid, then $434 a day for days sixty-one to ninety, then $868 a day for days ninety-one to a hundred and fifty while the sixty lifetime reserve days last. After day a hundred and fifty the patient pays everything.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Utilize standardized notification procedures
preguntas.subtema: Termination notice · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.3.f · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: How is a written termination notice sent, and what does the practice keep afterwards?
opciones: By certified mail, return receipt requested, keeping the receipt and a copy in the chart
By First-Class Mail, keeping a note of the date the envelope went to the post office
By a portal message, which is now the preferred way of sending these notices
By telephone, with the caller writing the date care ends into the progress note
preguntas.explicacion: Termination notices always go out in writing, and many states demand certified mail, return receipt requested, addressed to the latest address the file holds; the receipt and a copy of the letter then live in the medical record. At least one state now blesses HIPAA-compliant portal messages that report back whether the message has been viewed, and that route may take over, but for now the preferred means is still certified mail.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 3, Guidelines for Using a Medical Interpreter
preguntas.subtema: Interpreters · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.1.c(3) / 2027 F.1.d(4)
preguntas.pregunta: A telephone interpreter was used for a visit. What has to be entered in the progress note?
opciones: The name of the medical interpreter who took part in the visit
The account number of the language line that handled the call
The consent the patient gave before the interpreter was called
The reason a family member was not used to interpret instead
preguntas.explicacion: One of the guidelines for medical interpreters is that the interpreter's name goes into the progress note. Interpreters may be on site or reached by video or telephone. Nothing in the guidance calls for recording an account number, a separate consent or a justification for not using a relative.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Uncomplicated Urinary Tract Infections", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(7) (2027 I.C.6.g(7)) · RMA I.A.2.a · CMAA 1 k10 · NCMA 1.10
preguntas.pregunta: A woman reports urinary frequency, urgency, burning on urination and suprapubic discomfort. Which organism most often causes this?
opciones: Escherichia coli, responsible for the majority of these infections
Klebsiella species, responsible for the majority of these infections
Staphylococcus aureus, responsible for the majority of these infections
Neisseria gonorrhoeae, responsible for the majority of these infections
preguntas.explicacion: Dysuria, urgency, frequency and discomfort above the pubic bone are the typical symptoms of an uncomplicated urinary tract infection, and Escherichia coli causes most of them, with Klebsiella next and Proteus, Enterobacter and Enterococcus behind. Bacteria without symptoms are not a urinary tract infection.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Rights & protections under the health care law
preguntas.subtema: Insurance types · CMA III.G.4.a (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with a costly chronic illness fears her plan will stop paying once she reaches a yearly ceiling. What does the health care law say?
opciones: Yearly and lifetime dollar caps on essential benefits are over
Yearly caps are over, and each state sets the lifetime ones
Caps are allowed once she goes outside her plan's own network
Caps stay in force until her plan renews at the end of the year
preguntas.explicacion: Among the protections of the health care law is the end of lifetime and yearly dollar limits on the coverage of essential health benefits. The same law bars insurers from refusing to cover a pre-existing condition or charging more for it, and gives the member the right to appeal a plan decision. Grandfathered plans may fall outside some of this.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Public Interest and Benefit Activities
preguntas.subtema: Public interest disclosures · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.5 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k37 · NCMA 4.10
preguntas.pregunta: Public interest and benefit activities let a covered entity release information without authorization. How many such purposes does the rule list?
opciones: Twelve national priority purposes, each with its own conditions and limitations
Six national priority purposes, all of them limited to law enforcement requests
Four national priority purposes, all of them requiring a court order beforehand
Eighteen national priority purposes, one for each identifier the rule names
preguntas.explicacion: OCR groups the disclosures that need no authorization or permission into twelve national priority purposes, each with specific conditions: required by law, public health activities, victims of abuse or neglect, health oversight, judicial and administrative proceedings, law enforcement, decedents, organ donation, research, serious threat to health or safety, essential government functions, and workers' compensation. The six-circumstance list belongs to law enforcement alone.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 482.13(e), Standard: Restraint or seclusion, paragraphs (e)(2)-(e)(9) and (e)(12)
preguntas.subtema: Restraint orders · CPT D1 k14 · CCMA 7A k215 · CMA II.E.1.d · RMA I.C.1.e · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32
preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about restraint or seclusion orders is correct under the CMS patient-rights condition?
opciones: They may never be written as standing or as-needed (PRN) orders
They may be written PRN for patients with a history of falls
They may be renewed indefinitely without a new assessment
They may be issued by any staff member trained in restraint use
preguntas.explicacion: Restraint or seclusion may be used only to secure the patient's immediate physical safety, or that of staff or of others, never as coercion, as discipline, for the convenience of staff or as payback, and only once less restrictive measures have failed, on the order of a physician or another licensed practitioner responsible for that patient. Such an order is never written as a standing order, nor on a PRN basis. For violent behavior each order runs at most 4 hours for adults, 2 hours from ages 9 to 17 and 1 hour under 9, to a total of 24 hours, with a face-to-face evaluation inside 1 hour, and the intervention stops as soon as it can.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Worker's compensation
preguntas.subtema: Workers' compensation · CMAA 5 k72 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.f / 2027 III.G.4 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: What is workers' compensation insurance?
opciones: Coverage employers must carry for workers who get sick or hurt on the job
Coverage employers may buy to replace the group health plan for their workers
Coverage the state buys for workers whose employer offers no health plan
Coverage that pays the deductible of the group plan after a workplace injury
preguntas.explicacion: Workers' compensation is the insurance an employer is obliged to carry for employees who fall ill or are injured because of their work. It does not stand in for the group health plan, is not bought by the state for uninsured workers, and does not merely pay a deductible: for care related to the job injury it is the payer, which is why those claims go to it first.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Deductible; and Glossary: Coinsurance
preguntas.subtema: Financial calculations · CMA III.G.8, III.G.6.e (2027 III.G.6.c-d) · CMAA 5C k76, 6B · CCMA 5K k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has met $400 of her $1,000 deductible. Today's visit is allowed at $250 and her coinsurance is 20%. What does she owe today?
opciones: $250, since the whole allowed amount still goes to the deductible
$50, which is twenty percent of the amount the plan allows
$350, which is what is left on the deductible after today
$300, the amount of the visit plus her twenty percent share
preguntas.explicacion: A plan begins to pay only after the deductible has been met, so with $600 still outstanding the whole $250 allowed for the visit is applied to the deductible and the patient pays it. Coinsurance is her percentage share of the allowed amount, and it starts to apply on the services that come after the deductible is satisfied.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Billing: CMS-1500 & 837P (MLN006976), Coding & Billing Dates of Service
preguntas.subtema: Claim submission · CMA III.G.3.b(1) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6C k87, 6 k85 · CCMA 5L k185
preguntas.pregunta: A walker was ordered in March, delivered to the patient in April and paid for in May. Which is the date of service?
opciones: April, when the patient received the item
March, when the provider ordered the item
May, when the payment for it was made
March, since the order opens the benefit
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare counts the expense from the day the patient actually received the item or the service, whatever the day it was ordered on or paid for. Services that run across two calendar dates start on one day and finish the next, and either day may be used, but no claim goes out until the service is complete.

preguntas.subtema: Flexibility of approach · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A two-physician office and a large group implement the same security standard in very different ways. Which factors does the rule let them weigh?
opciones: Their size and capabilities, their technical infrastructure, cost, and the risks
The number of patients seen each year and the volume of claims they send out
Whether the state they work in has passed security legislation of its own
How many staff members hold a formal certification in privacy and security
preguntas.explicacion: Flexibility of approach lets a covered entity pick whatever security measures implement the standards reasonably and appropriately, weighing how big it is, how complex and how capable, what its technical infrastructure amounts to and what the security capabilities of its hardware and software amount to, what the measures cost, and how probable and how critical the risks are.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Required Disclosures
preguntas.subtema: Required disclosures · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: In which two situations does the Privacy Rule REQUIRE a covered entity to disclose protected health information?
opciones: To the individual asking for access or an accounting, and to HHS for a compliance review
To the individual asking for access, and to any provider who requests records for treatment
To HHS for a compliance review, and to the health plan whenever it asks to audit a claim
To a law enforcement official with a badge, and to the patient's closest living relative
preguntas.explicacion: Almost everything in the rule is permissive: the entity may use or disclose PHI in the situations listed but is not obliged to. Only two disclosures are compulsory, namely to the individual herself, or to her personal representative, when access or an accounting of disclosures is requested, and to HHS when it is conducting an investigation, a compliance review or an enforcement action.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Nursing Homes: Summary
preguntas.subtema: Specialty resources for medical needs · CCMA 4D k165 · CMAA 2H k30
preguntas.pregunta: A family asks what a nursing home offers that home care cannot. What is the defining feature?
opciones: Skilled nurses and nursing aides available around the clock, for people not needing a hospital
A private apartment with meals, housekeeping and social activities for independent residents
Surgery on patients who are expected to go home within 24 hours after the procedure
An interdisciplinary team that manages pain for a patient in the last stage of illness
preguntas.explicacion: A nursing home serves people who do not need to be in hospital but cannot be cared for at home, and most keep skilled nurses and nursing aides available around the clock. Some are laid out like a hospital, with therapy staff and a nurses' station on each floor; others aim to feel like a neighborhood. They are not only for older adults: anyone needing 24-hour care may live there.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), If the Primary Payer Denies the Claim
preguntas.subtema: Denials and appeals · CMA III.G.5.b (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6E · CCMA 5M
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with an open workers' compensation record is treated for something unrelated, and the contractor denies the claim anyway. What should the office do?
opciones: Appeal with evidence that the care had nothing to do with the injury, and keep treating
Stop treating the patient until the workers' compensation record has been closed
Rebill the compensation carrier, since the open record makes it the primary payer
Write the balance off, since a claim denied on an open record cannot be reopened
preguntas.explicacion: Contractors sometimes deny claims because the diagnosis codes fall within the family of codes attached to a liability, no-fault or workers' compensation record in the patient's eligibility file, even when the care had nothing to do with the accident. Those denials can be appealed with information proving the services were unrelated, and care must go on during the appeal period while the record stays open.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Appeals in Original Medicare, Level 5; and Medicare.gov, Filing an appeal
preguntas.subtema: Denials and appeals · CMA III.G.5.b (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6E · CCMA 5M
preguntas.pregunta: A patient wants to take her Medicare appeal all the way to federal district court in 2026. What has to be true of the amount in dispute?
opciones: It has to reach $1,960, and she may combine claims to get to that figure
It has to reach $1,960, and only one claim at a time may be counted for it
It has to reach $1,000, and she may combine claims to get to that figure
It has to reach $5,000, and only one claim at a time may be counted for it
preguntas.explicacion: Judicial review in federal district court is the last of the five levels of Medicare appeal, and it is the only one with a minimum amount in controversy: $1,960 for 2026. Claims may be combined to reach that figure, and the decision letter from the fourth level carries the directions for filing, as every level's letter carries the directions for the next.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 2.5
preguntas.subtema: Stopping system interfaces · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: The record system's link to the laboratory has to be stopped for maintenance. What does the contingency guidance want checked before it is halted or restarted?
opciones: That the buffers holding data on the interface have been emptied first
That the laboratory has agreed the window and confirmed it in writing
That the read-only backup system has been switched on for the interval
That the last day of results has been printed and filed in the charts
preguntas.explicacion: Stopping or restarting an interface badly can lose or corrupt data in transit with no warning to anyone. The guidance therefore asks that all interface buffers be empty before the system is stopped or restarted, that buffers be large enough where the sending system keeps producing data, and that users be told when an interface is not working.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A condition is documented on both sides and the classification offers no bilateral code for it. What is assigned?
opciones: Separate codes for the left side and for the right side
The code for the unspecified side, just for this encounter
One code, for the side that was treated at this encounter
The same code reported twice, once for each side treated
preguntas.explicacion: Some codes specify left, right or bilateral. Where the condition is bilateral and no bilateral code exists, separate codes are assigned for the left and the right side. Reporting one code twice is not an option, since a given code goes on an encounter a single time, and the unspecified side is kept for records that never say which side.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Specific Techniques
preguntas.subtema: Therapeutic techniques · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2E k21 · CMA F.2 / 2027 F.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's account of when the pain started keeps contradicting itself. Which technique fits?
opciones: Clarifying, with guiding statements that draw out more detail
Reflecting, by repeating the account back almost word for word
Providing rationale, by saying up front why the detail is needed
Using silence, by waiting without interrupting until she stops
preguntas.explicacion: Clarifying is the listed technique for guiding a patient to make a statement clearer and to obtain additional information. Reflecting repeats what was said, sometimes word for word; providing rationale explains why the information or the recommendation is needed; and silence is about attentiveness and not interrupting. All four are techniques, but only one fits a confused account.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Health Care Payment and Remittance Advice (835/ERA)
preguntas.subtema: Electronic remittance advice · CMAA 5 k79, 6D · CCMA 5K k182
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare remittance advice shows an adjustment with group code PR. What does that mean for the office?
opciones: The amount is patient responsibility, so the beneficiary may be billed for it
The amount is a provider obligation, so the beneficiary may not be billed for it
The amount is under review, so the office should resubmit the claim as corrected
The amount is a payment for interest owed for a late payment on a clean claim
preguntas.explicacion: Group codes assign responsibility for the unpaid part of the claim balance: CO marks a contractual obligation that belongs to the provider, and PR marks patient responsibility. Beneficiaries may be billed only when the adjustment carries the PR group code. Interest for a late payment on a clean claim appears instead as a provider level adjustment on the remittance.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicare Shared Savings Program - About the Program
preguntas.subtema: Delivery models · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: How do providers join the Medicare Shared Savings Program?
opciones: Voluntarily, by coming together as an ACO accountable for quality and cost
Automatically, once the practice bills Medicare for fee-for-service claims
By state assignment, when the state designates a necessary provider region
By accreditation, once an approved organization grants the group deemed status
preguntas.explicacion: The Shared Savings Program is voluntary: it encourages doctors, hospitals and other providers to group together as an ACO and deliver coordinated care to their Medicare patients. In return the ACO accepts accountability for the cost, the quality and the experience of care given to an assigned fee-for-service population, and picks among participation tracks.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 9: Let patients know about language access services
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k166 barriers to care · CMAA 2D
preguntas.pregunta: Which sign belongs in the waiting and reception areas under the toolkit's language guidance?
opciones: A poster announcing that interpreter services are available at no charge
A poster listing the fee schedule for interpreter services by language
A poster asking patients to bring a bilingual relative to every visit
A poster stating that visits are conducted in English unless arranged early
preguntas.explicacion: Interpretive services posters go up in waiting and reception areas so patients learn that free interpreter services exist, and directories list which languages the bilingual clinicians speak. A practice taking Medicare or Medicaid is required to provide language access, and failing to use acceptable services exposes it to liability.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information: Providing the Notice
preguntas.subtema: Triennial reminder from a plan · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA II.A.1 · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: How often must a health plan remind the individuals it covers that its notice of privacy practices exists and how to obtain it?
opciones: At least once every three years, to the individuals then covered by the plan
At least once every year, to the individuals then covered by the plan
At least once every five years, to the individuals then covered by the plan
At least once every three years, and again whenever a claim is denied
preguntas.explicacion: Among the duties that fall on health plans rather than on providers, the plan must notify the individuals it then covers of the availability of the notice and of how to obtain it at least once every three years. A separate duty sends a revised notice within 60 days when the plan makes a material revision.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Positions and Directions
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: An order calls for an intramuscular injection, and the same note mentions an intercostal muscle. Which pair of meanings is right?
opciones: Intra- is within and inter- is between
Intra- is between and inter- is within
Intra- is within and inter- is beneath
Intra- is beyond and inter- is between
preguntas.explicacion: Intra- means within, so an intramuscular injection is placed inside the muscle. Inter- means between, so an intercostal muscle lies between the ribs. Two more from the same group are easy to confuse with them: infra- is beneath or below, and ex- and extra- carry the sense of beyond.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology
preguntas.subtema: Technology screening · CMAA 4H k62 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which question belongs to the check on what technology a telehealth patient already has, rather than to another part of the preparation?
opciones: Whether she needs help opening an e-mail account, if the platform calls for one
Whether she has somewhere quiet and private in which to take the appointment
Whether she is able to raise the camera so that it sits at the level of her eyes
Whether she has the bottles of her current medicines within reach of the screen
preguntas.explicacion: Working out what technology a patient already has means asking whether her computer, tablet or mobile device carries a camera and microphone that suit the platform; whether her internet connection has the bandwidth video needs; whether she has somewhere with secure internet; and whether she needs help opening an e-mail account. Privacy, camera position and having the medicines ready sit on other lists.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Telehealth
preguntas.subtema: Medicare telehealth coverage · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.G.4 · RMA II.A.1 · CMAA 4B k54 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient asks whether she can have a telehealth visit from her own home. What is the current answer?
opciones: Yes, Medicare covers telehealth from anywhere in the country through December 31, 2027
Yes, but only if she travels to a clinic in a rural area that acts as the originating site
No, Medicare stopped covering telehealth when the public health emergency was declared over
Yes, but only for the brief virtual check-ins that last ten minutes or less
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare covers telehealth services obtained from anywhere in the United States, the patient's own home included, through December 31, 2027. Telehealth there means care from a provider in another location over audio and video, or over audio alone in some cases, and it takes in office visits, psychotherapy and consultations. E-visits through a portal and short virtual check-ins are extra ways of communicating, not the only ones.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Billing: CMS-1500 & 837P (MLN006976), Key Terms
preguntas.subtema: Claim submission · CMA III.G.3.b(1) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6C k87, 6 k85 · CCMA 5L k185
preguntas.pregunta: A payer asks the office to send its claims as an 837P, version 5010A1. What has it asked for?
opciones: The current electronic standard for professional claims
The paper claim form that a national committee designs
The electronic standard for institutional facility claims
The remittance standard the payer sends back afterwards
preguntas.explicacion: In that string the 837 is the standard format for sending claims electronically, the P marks the professional version used by health care professionals and suppliers, and 5010A1 is the current version of the electronic transaction standards. The paper alternative is the claim form the national uniform claim committee designs and maintains.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, SBAR
preguntas.subtema: Structured communication · CCMA 6F k198 · CMAA 2E k23 · CMA F.4.c / 2027 F.2.c · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant calls a provider about a patient whose catheter has stopped draining. In SBAR, which part says what the caller thinks is wrong?
opciones: The assessment, naming what the caller believes is wrong
The situation, naming what is going on with the patient
The background, giving the clinical context of the case
The recommendation, saying what should be done about it
preguntas.explicacion: SBAR carries critical information that needs attention and action right away. Situation says what is happening with the patient, background gives the clinical context, assessment states what the caller thinks the problem is, and recommendation or request says what should be done to correct it.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 6: Choose the ways your office will follow up
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4F facilitate compliance · CMAA 2A · NCMA F.23
preguntas.pregunta: The office plans to follow up with all its patients by text message. What does the toolkit warn about?
opciones: Ask each patient how they want to be contacted; do not rely on electronic means alone
Text everyone, since owning a mobile phone shows the patient accepts texting
Use secure email for everyone instead, since it is part of the patient portal
Use postal mail for everyone instead, since it reaches patients without devices
preguntas.explicacion: Follow-up means contacting patients at a set later date to check on progress, catch misunderstandings and answer questions. Patients are asked how they want to be reached, because owning a phone does not mean wanting texts, some are charged to receive them, and not everyone checks their devices. Phone, secure email, texting and mail all serve.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Emancipated Minor", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Consent exceptions · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7 · CMAA 3D k40
preguntas.pregunta: A 16-year-old comes to the office alone and asks to be treated without her parents being told. What decides whether she can consent for herself?
opciones: Whether she is emancipated or her state lets minors consent to that service
Whether she is able to pay for the visit herself on the day of the appointment
Whether the clinician judges that she is mature enough during the encounter
Whether a parent can be reached by telephone before the visit starts
preguntas.explicacion: Minors under 18 usually cannot consent, and the parent gives permission instead. The openings are emancipation — marriage, active military duty, or living apart and managing one's own money — and the services a state lets minors seek alone, such as contraception, care for a sexually transmitted infection, or prenatal care. Paying for a visit does not emancipate anyone, and the mature minor doctrine exists in very few states.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Rights & protections under the health care law
preguntas.subtema: Insurance types · CMA III.G.4.a (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: May an insurance company cancel a member's coverage because she has fallen ill?
opciones: No, the health care law makes that cancellation illegal
Yes, where the illness is a pre-existing condition
Yes, once she passes the yearly dollar limit of the plan
No, unless the plan was bought through the Marketplace
preguntas.explicacion: The law makes it illegal for an insurance company to cancel someone's health insurance just because that person gets sick. It also requires plans to cover a person who has a pre-existing condition, pregnancy included, and to charge her no more for it, and it has ended the yearly dollar limits that the other answers lean on.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Health Topic: Patient Rights, Summary; 42 CFR 482.13(b)(2)
preguntas.subtema: Federal patient rights · CPT D1 k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k215 · CMA II.E.1.d · RMA I.C.1.e · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32
preguntas.pregunta: Which patient right is guaranteed by federal law, as opposed to a facility's own bill of rights?
opciones: The right to a copy of one's medical records and to keep them private
The right to receive any treatment the patient requests, regardless of medical necessity
The right to free care in any hospital that accepts Medicare
The right to choose which staff member performs each procedure
preguntas.explicacion: Some patient rights are guaranteed by federal law, notably the right to get a copy of one's medical records and to have them kept private and secure; many states add protections, and insurers, medical organizations and facilities publish their own non-enforceable bills of rights. Other common rights are respectful treatment, freedom from discrimination, the right to refuse treatment and informed consent. The CMS condition adds that the right to make informed decisions is not a mechanism to demand treatment that is medically unnecessary.

preguntas.subtema: Records access · CCMA k215, k219 · NCMA 4.4 · CMAA 3D k32
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks orally for an electronic copy of their current hospital records. What is required?
opciones: The records in the form requested, if readily producible, within a reasonable time
A written and notarized request before any copy of the record can be released
A paper copy only, since electronic release is limited to other treating providers
A copy of everything except the current admission, which stays open until discharge
preguntas.explicacion: The right of access covers current records, on an oral or a written request, in the form and format asked for when that is readily producible — including electronic format when the records are kept electronically — and otherwise in readable hard copy or another agreed format, within a reasonable time. The hospital must not frustrate that right.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Utilize standardized notification procedures
preguntas.subtema: Missed appointments and dismissal · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.b · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: The dismissed patient never signed for the certified letter and appears at the desk two months later asking to be booked. What is the guidance?
opciones: Hand her a copy of the letter or say it was mailed, and that care ended on its date
Book her, because a return receipt nobody signed leaves the notice without effect
Start the thirty days again from today, since she has only now learned of the decision
Send a second certified letter and keep seeing her until that new period runs out
preguntas.explicacion: The situation is anticipated: the patient does not sign the return receipt and then contacts the office or turns up after the period in the letter has run. She should be given a copy of the letter, or told by telephone that a letter was sent, and politely told that care ended on the date it named. Nothing in the guidance restarts the clock because the receipt came back unsigned.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Medicaid; and Glossary: Open Enrollment Period
preguntas.subtema: Financial eligibility · CMAA 6 k83 · CCMA 5E k178
preguntas.pregunta: When can a person apply for Medicaid or CHIP coverage?
opciones: At any time of year, since these programs have no yearly enrollment window
Only from November 1 to January 15, the Marketplace enrollment window
Only within 60 days of a qualifying life event such as a birth or a move
Only during the seven months around the applicant's sixty-fifth birthday
preguntas.explicacion: Applications for Medicaid and CHIP are taken all year, and coverage can begin immediately for those who qualify. The window from November 1 to January 15 is Marketplace open enrollment; the 60-day rule belongs to Special Enrollment Periods for Marketplace plans; and the 7-month period around the 65th birthday is the Initial Enrollment Period for Medicare.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Expert Witness", Introduction: Standard of Care
preguntas.subtema: Standard of care · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.b · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3A k31
preguntas.pregunta: How is the standard of care described when a malpractice claim is judged?
opciones: The care a reasonable clinician of similar training would give in like cases
The care described in the manufacturer's instructions for the device used
The care the best specialist in the state would have given the same patient
The care the patient expected after reading the practice's own brochures
preguntas.explicacion: The defendant's actions are measured against the standard of care for that diagnosis and that situation: the care, skill and diligence, ordinary and reasonable, that clinicians in good standing in the same general line of practice usually exercise in like cases. National boards have flattened much of the old regional variation, though access in rural or underserved areas is the occasional exception.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Administrative Simplification: Transactions; and CMS, Administrative Simplification: Health Care Payment and Remittance Advice and EFT
preguntas.subtema: Claim submission · CMA III.G.3.b(1) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6 k87 · CCMA 5 k185
preguntas.pregunta: A payer is refusing to accept the adopted electronic claim format. Where can a practice report that?
opciones: To the enforcement and testing tool that takes administrative simplification complaints
To the clearinghouse, which is obliged to report the payer to the standards body
To the code set maintainer, which decides whether the payer's format is acceptable
To the state insurance department, which enforces the electronic transaction rules
preguntas.explicacion: Complaints about possible violations of the transaction standards go through the enforcement and testing tool for administrative simplification, and the same route takes complaints about the standards for payment, remittance advice and funds transfer. Requests for new or revised codes go to the code set maintainers rather than to enforcement, and the standards themselves are federal, not a state matter.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow, Preparing for telehealth visits
preguntas.subtema: Supporting a caregiver · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A frail patient will have her son working the tablet for her at every video visit. Which item does the workflow guidance put on the practice's list because of him?
opciones: How the practice will support a caregiver or other person assisting the patient during the visit
How the practice will bill for the extra time a caregiver's presence adds to each visit
How the practice will record the caregiver's own contact details in the appointment book
How the practice will limit the caregiver's involvement to the opening minutes of the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Under meeting patient needs the guidance asks the practice to settle four things: how it will learn what accommodations a patient may need; how and when appointment reminders go out; how it will support a patient whose disability is a hearing loss or a visual impairment; and how it will support a caregiver, or anyone else who will be assisting the patient through the visit.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 11: Assess, Select, and Create Easy-to-Understand Materials
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k160 education methods · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.3.a · 2027 F.1.h
preguntas.pregunta: What is the average reading level of adults in the United States?
opciones: About 8th or 9th grade
About 5th or 6th grade
About 11th or 12th grade
About 3rd or 4th grade
preguntas.explicacion: Adults in the United States read on average at an 8th or 9th grade level, and nearly a quarter have low literacy while a third have low numeracy. Health education material is often written well above that average, which leaves half of adults struggling with it.

preguntas.fuente: The Joint Commission, 2026 Ambulatory Health Care National Patient Safety Goals, NPSG.03.06.01
preguntas.subtema: Medicine information at check-out · CCMA 4 · CMA I.A.1 · RMA II.B.4.a · CMAA 5H · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is leaving at the end of her visit. What does the 2026 ambulatory safety goal on medicines expect her to be given and told?
opciones: Written information on what she is to take, and to bring an up-to-date list to every visit
Written information on what she is to take, and to bring the bottles themselves each visit
A printed note of the changes made today, and to ring the office before her next refill
Written information on what she is to take, and to leave the list on file at her pharmacy
preguntas.explicacion: The goal on using medicines safely asks that a patient's medicines be found out and compared with anything new she is given, that correct information about them be recorded and passed on, that she leave with something written about what she needs to take, and that she be told it matters to carry a current list to every appointment with a doctor.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), Financial Liability
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMA III.G.3.c (2027 III.G.3.c) · CMAA 5 k77, 6D · CCMA 5 k186
preguntas.pregunta: The required advance written notice never went out, and Medicare denies the claim as not medically necessary. Who ends up carrying the cost?
opciones: The provider, who may not collect that amount from the patient
The patient, who signed the general consent form at check-in
The patient, as soon as the practice sends her the remittance
Medicare, which pays the claim where no notice was given at all
preguntas.explicacion: Where the provider fails to issue a required notice, or the contractor finds the notice invalid, the provider may be held financially liable and cannot seek the money from the patient. Medicare does not pay for an item or service the provider knew or should have known was not reasonable and necessary for that patient. A general consent form is not a notice.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026, Section I.B.14
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 6A, 5 k68 · CCMA 5I k184 · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: The dietitian recorded the body mass index and the physician documented the obesity. What may the coder take from each note?
opciones: The index may be coded from the dietitian, but the diagnosis has to come from the provider
Both codes may be taken from the dietitian, since she may document in the medical record
Neither may be taken from the dietitian, so the index cannot be coded from her entry at all
The index may be coded from the dietitian, and it may be listed as the first diagnosis
preguntas.explicacion: Code assignment normally rests on the documentation of the patient's own provider. A short list of items may be taken from other clinicians who may write in the record, and the body mass index is one of them; the associated diagnosis, such as obesity, still has to be documented by the provider. The index code is reported only as a secondary diagnosis.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Empathy and compassion · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2A k22 · CMA F.2 / 2027 F.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: Staff say there is no time to answer a patient's emotional concerns. What have studies found about that?
opciones: Consultation time changes only marginally when empathy is shown
Consultation time roughly doubles once emotions are addressed
Consultations run long enough to need a second appointment
Consultation time drops because patients then say much less
preguntas.explicacion: The worry about time is not supported. Physicians giving an empathic response showed only a marginal change in consultation length, and better communication skills were not associated with longer consultations; one observational study put the difference at about 21 seconds. Patients rate communication ability as no less important than technical competence.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fighting Identity Theft with the Red Flags Rule: Detect Red Flags
preguntas.subtema: Verifying identity · CMAA 4C · CCMA 5F k190 · CMA III.H.2.b · RMA II.B.1 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: Staff verify a returning patient online by asking for her date of birth and her mother's maiden name. What does the FTC say about that choice?
opciones: Those details make poor authenticators, since they are so easily obtained
Those details are the two identifiers the safety goal asks for before a procedure
Those details satisfy the rule, because they were collected on the intake form
Those details may be used once the patient has signed the privacy acknowledgment
preguntas.explicacion: For accounts that already exist, the program may take in reasonable steps for confirming who it is dealing with, watching transactions and checking that a change of address is genuine; for authenticating online the guidance points to multi-factor techniques built on PINs, passwords, tokens, smart cards and biometrics. What it rules out as reliable authenticators is exactly the easy stuff: a mailing address, a date of birth, a mother's maiden name, a Social Security number.

preguntas.fuente: AAMA, Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Standards for CMAs (AAMA), Expired Credentials
preguntas.subtema: Unethical conduct · CCMA 7C · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant's certification lapsed last year but she still signs her name with the initials. What is that?
opciones: Unethical, and a misrepresentation of a credential she no longer holds
Acceptable, as long as she is working toward reinstating the credential
Acceptable, because the exam she passed years ago cannot be undone
Unethical, but permitted while the reinstatement application is pending
preguntas.explicacion: Publicly displaying the certification title, or using the initials after one's name, once the credential has expired is treated as unethical and as a misrepresentation. Misrepresenting one's credentials or education is also listed among the matters the certifying board can investigate and discipline.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Preauthorization
preguntas.subtema: Prior authorization · CCMA 5 k183 · CMA III.H.1.d · RMA II.B.2.c · CMAA 4G k67 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: Before booking an imaging study, staff contact the insurer for its decision on medical necessity. What limits does that decision carry?
opciones: It is not a promise that the plan will pay the cost of the service
It removes the need for a referral from the patient's primary care doctor
It fixes the amount the patient will owe once the study has been performed
It obliges the imaging center to accept the amount the plan decides to pay
preguntas.explicacion: Preauthorization is the insurer's decision that a service, a treatment plan, a prescription drug or a piece of durable medical equipment counts as medically necessary.
