A plan may demand it before certain services, emergencies aside; other names for the same thing are precertification, prior approval and prior authorization. The glossary states plainly that having it is no promise that the plan will pay.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pay for Performance and Value-Based Care", Summary
preguntas.subtema: Payment models · CMAA 6 k82 · CCMA 1 k6
preguntas.pregunta: Under a diagnosis-related group payment, what does a hospital receive for two patients with the same diagnosis but different lengths of stay?
opciones: The same payment, since the amount follows the diagnosis rather than the days
A larger payment for the longer stay, since each extra day is billed separately
A payment adjusted daily, since the group sets a rate for each day of care
A payment set after discharge from the charges the hospital actually billed
preguntas.explicacion: The diagnosis-related group pays a single amount for the hospitalization, built from the average cost of treating that condition and adjusted for factors such as teaching hospitals or a large uninsured caseload. Patients with the same diagnosis bring the same payment whether the stay is long or short, which was designed to push efficiency and remove the incentive to over-treat.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), Table 1
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMAA 5B k75, 5B k66 · CCMA 5E k182
preguntas.pregunta: A patient under 65 has Medicare because of a disability and works for an employer with 60 employees. Who pays first?
opciones: Medicare pays first, since the employer has fewer than 100 employees
The group health plan pays first, since the employer has 20 or more employees
Medicare pays first, since entitlement based on disability always comes first
The group health plan pays first, since the patient is younger than 65 years
preguntas.explicacion: When Medicare entitlement rests on disability, the group health plan pays first only if the employer has 100 or more employees; below that number Medicare is primary. The 20-employee threshold is the one used for patients 65 or older. Disability by itself does not settle the order, and neither does age: the size of the employer is what decides it in both rules.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Claim Denial Rate
preguntas.subtema: Denials · CMA III.G.5.b (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6E · CCMA 5M · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: Nine percent of a practice's claims were denied last quarter, and the manager wants to know whether that is out of line.
opciones: It is inside the usual range, which runs from five to ten percent of claims
It is above the usual range, which runs from two to five percent of claims
It is below the usual range, which runs from ten to fifteen percent of claims
It is above the usual range, which runs from one to three percent of claims
preguntas.explicacion: The benchmark for the claim denial rate is five to ten percent, so nine percent sits at the top of the normal band rather than outside it. Denial rates climb with errors in demographic, coding, documentation or billing data, and with missed invoices, unclear preauthorization or services billed on medical necessity. Two to five percent is a different figure: the share of net patient revenue providers never manage to collect.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · CMA III.G.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: A manifestation code carries a code first note. How are the two codes sequenced?
opciones: The underlying condition is sequenced first and the manifestation second
The manifestation is sequenced first and the underlying condition second
Either order is acceptable as long as both codes appear on the claim
Only the manifestation is reported, since it names the condition treated
preguntas.explicacion: In the etiology and manifestation convention, the underlying condition is sequenced first and the manifestation follows. The etiology code carries a use additional code note and the manifestation code a code first note; manifestation titles usually end in diseases classified elsewhere, and such codes are never allowed as the first-listed or principal diagnosis, so they cannot stand alone.

preguntas.fuente: NIH, NIDDK: Eating, Diet, & Nutrition for Celiac Disease — Cross-contact
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k161 nutrition education · CMA I.A.6.g(3)(e) · 2027 I.A.6.g(3)(e) · CMAA 2G
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with celiac disease keeps having symptoms even though she buys only gluten-free products. What should be explored first?
opciones: Cross-contact, where gluten reaches her food during storage or preparation
Cross-reaction, where gluten-free grains trigger the same immune response
Tolerance, which builds up so that gluten-free products stop working
Lactase deficiency, which is what actually causes celiac symptoms
preguntas.explicacion: Cross-contact happens when foods or products holding gluten touch gluten-free food, which makes that food unsafe for her. It can occur while food is grown, processed, stored, prepared or served, so gluten-free items are kept and cooked apart from the rest of the household's food.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Incidental Uses and Disclosures: Reasonable Safeguards
preguntas.subtema: Reasonable safeguards · CCMA 6 k204 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA II.B.3.g · CMAA 3B k38 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which practice is named by OCR as a reasonable safeguard a health care office can adopt?
opciones: Speaking quietly when discussing a condition with relatives in a public area of the office
Guaranteeing that no visitor can ever overhear or glimpse any patient information at all
Requiring every workforce member to obtain the patient's consent before each chart entry
Sending all internal messages about patients through unencrypted e-mail to speed up care
preguntas.explicacion: The Privacy Rule expects safeguards of the administrative, technical and physical kinds, and OCR says outright that they are not meant to guarantee privacy against every conceivable risk. What is reasonable varies with the size and the nature of the entity; the examples given are dropping one's voice in public areas, keeping names out of conversations in hallways and elevators, posting reminder signs, and password-protecting the computers.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 6A, 5 k68 · CCMA 5I k184 · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A coder believes the test values on the chart do not support the diagnosis the provider wrote down. What do the coding guidelines say?
opciones: The provider's statement that the condition exists is what the code rests on
The clinical criteria decide, so the code has to follow the values on file
The code is held back until the values and the diagnosis agree with each other
The coder assigns the unspecified code for that condition and moves on
preguntas.explicacion: What the code rests on is the provider stating that the patient has the condition, not the clinical criteria the provider used to get there. What the guidelines ask for when the record itself is contradictory is a query to the provider, not a code chosen by the coder from the numbers.

preguntas.fuente: Child Welfare Information Gateway, Mandatory Reporting of Child Abuse and Neglect (May 2023), Standards for Making a Report
preguntas.subtema: Mandatory reporting · CCMA 7F k222 · CMA E.6.c / 2027 E.5.b · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k43
preguntas.pregunta: What does a mandatory reporter have to have before filing a report?
opciones: The facts and circumstances that raised the suspicion, not proof
A photograph or an X-ray documenting the suspected injury
Proof that abuse or neglect occurred, by a preponderance of the evidence
A second staff member willing to sign the report as a witness
preguntas.explicacion: Reporters are asked for the facts, and the circumstances, that brought them to suspect a child has been abused or neglected; the burden of proving that it happened is not theirs. The usual trigger is suspecting, or having reason to believe, in one's official capacity, that a child has been abused or neglected. Permissive reporters follow the same standard when they choose to report.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Verbal Communication
preguntas.subtema: Communication cycle · CCMA 6F k198 · CMAA 2C k17 · CMA F.3.a / 2027 F.1.h
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant gives postsurgical instructions to a child and then to an adult with the same procedure. What should differ?
opciones: The way the information is delivered, not its substance
The substance of the information, not the way it is given
The person who receives it, and no other element
The record it is charted in, and not the wording used
preguntas.explicacion: The requirements on signs of infection, pain management and the rest may be much the same, but the way the information is provided can be quite different depending on developmental level. Whatever adaptation is made, the sender still has to verify that the patient understood.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: Physical Safeguards
preguntas.subtema: Workstation security · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 3B k38 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: The check-in monitor faces the waiting room and shows the day's schedule with patient names. Which safeguard is at issue?
opciones: Workstation use and security, a physical safeguard covering how workstations are placed and used
Security awareness and training, the administrative standard for teaching staff the policies
Contingency planning, the administrative standard for keeping care going during a system failure
Evaluation, the administrative standard for periodically testing how well the policies work
preguntas.explicacion: The physical safeguards include workstation use and security, which call for policies setting out the proper use of workstations that can reach ePHI and the physical protections around them. The other three options are administrative safeguards: training the workforce, planning for emergencies that damage the systems, and assessing the policies periodically, on technical and on non-technical grounds.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Billing: CMS-1500 & 837P (MLN006976), ASCA Exceptions
preguntas.subtema: Claim submission · CMA III.G.3.b(1) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6C k87, 6 k85 · CCMA 5L k185
preguntas.pregunta: A mass immunizer gives flu shots at a community center. What does roster billing let it do?
opciones: Send one paper claim with a list of the patients who got the shot
Send one paper claim for each patient, signed by the immunizer
Send claims on paper only where the site has no internet line
Send one claim a month covering every shot given in that month
preguntas.explicacion: Roster billing is one of the exceptions to electronic filing. The mass immunizer completes a single paper claim form for the covid, flu or pneumonia shot and attaches a roster naming the patients who received it, instead of a separate form for each one. It is a way of billing, not a way of grouping a month's work together.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", Clinical Significance; and StatPearls, "Emancipated Minor"
preguntas.subtema: Implied consent · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.b-c · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7 · CMAA 3D k40
preguntas.pregunta: An unconscious patient needs an urgent procedure and no surrogate is present. Which doctrine lets the team proceed?
opciones: Implied consent, on the assumption a reasonable person would agree
Expressed consent, obtained afterwards and dated to the time of care
Informed permission, given by the admitting service on arrival
Waived consent, recorded once the patient wakes up and agrees
preguntas.explicacion: Consent may be waived in an emergency where the patient cannot communicate and there is no surrogate decision-maker to be found. For an unaccompanied child the same reasoning goes by the emergency exception rule, or the doctrine of implied consent, on the assumption that a reasonable parent would agree. Permission is what a parent gives for a minor, and consent obtained afterwards is not what authorized the care.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Ethics", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Ethical principles · CCMA 7C · CMA E.7 / 2027 E.6 · RMA I.C.4.a · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: Four principles dominate the ethics codes: beneficence, nonmaleficence, distributive justice and autonomy. Which one governs sharing one scarce treatment among several patients?
opciones: Distributive justice, used when more than one patient is involved
Beneficence, the one about advocating for the patient's best interests
Nonmaleficence, the one that draws the boundary against causing harm
Autonomy, the one about the patient deciding free of outside control
preguntas.explicacion: In the four-principle heuristic that most code-writing bodies use, distributive justice is the principle that applies equal or equitable treatment when the matter involves more than one patient. Beneficence is advocating for the patient's best interest, nonmaleficence is not harming the patient, and autonomy is preserving the patient's ability to decide independently of outside control.

preguntas.subtema: Patient rights · CCMA k215 · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32
preguntas.pregunta: A patient files a written grievance about the quality of care. What must the hospital give back?
opciones: Written notice naming the contact person, the steps taken, the result and the date
Written notice that the complaint was received and then forwarded to the state agency
Verbal notice from the department manager once the review has been completed
Written notice of the outcome only if the grievance is found to have merit
preguntas.explicacion: A hospital must run a process for resolving grievances promptly and tell each patient whom to contact in order to file one. Resolving it means giving the patient written notice of the decision, naming the hospital's contact person, describing the steps taken to investigate, the results, and the date the process closed. The governing body owns the process.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Authorization
preguntas.subtema: Authorization elements · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.a-b · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which feature must appear on a valid HIPAA authorization form?
opciones: An expiration and a statement of the right to revoke it in writing, all in plain language
A witness signature from a workforce member who watched the patient sign the document
A cost estimate of the copies, since the fee has to be agreed before the release is signed
A clause making treatment conditional on the patient granting the authorization requested
preguntas.explicacion: An authorization has to be written in specific terms and in plain language, and it has to state what information is involved, who is disclosing it, who is receiving it, when it runs out, and that it can be revoked in writing. Conditioning treatment, payment, enrollment or benefits on the patient signing one is forbidden to a covered entity, save in the limited circumstances the rule spells out.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, EMR vs EHR - What is the Difference?
preguntas.subtema: EHR versus EMR · CCMA 5 k172 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.c · CMAA k3 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: What distinguishes an electronic health record from an electronic medical record?
opciones: The EHR is built to be shared with other organizations involved in the patient's care
The EHR is the version the patient keeps at home, while the EMR belongs to the practice
The EHR holds only billing and demographic data, while the EMR holds the clinical notes
The EHR is a scanned copy of the paper chart, while the EMR is entered directly by staff
preguntas.explicacion: An EMR is the digital version of the paper chart in one clinician's office: it tracks data over time, flags who is due for screening and supports quality work inside that practice, but the information does not travel easily beyond it. An EHR is designed to reach past the organization that collected the data, so the record follows the patient to the specialist, the hospital or the next state.

preguntas.fuente: ISMP, List of Error-Prone Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations (2024), Doses/Measurement Units
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k10 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k8 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A handwritten order reads QD. Which misreading put that abbreviation on the Do Not Use list?
opciones: It is read as QID, four times daily, instead of every day
It is read as QOD, every other day, instead of every day
It is read as QHS, nightly at bedtime, instead of every day
It is read as PRN, only as needed, instead of every day
preguntas.explicacion: QD means every day, but a handwritten q that trails off, or the period that follows it, gets taken for the letter i, and the order turns into QID, four doses a day. Write daily instead. QOD has its own entry on the list, where the badly written o is the problem.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Network; and Glossary: Out-of-pocket maximum/limit
preguntas.subtema: Insurance terminology · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.e (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.A.1 · CMAA 4 k61 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: What does a health plan's "network" consist of?
opciones: The providers, facilities and suppliers under contract with the insurer
The list of prescription drugs the plan covers, also called its drug list
The providers the patient may see without a referral from the primary care doctor
The services that count toward the out-of-pocket limit, including out-of-network care
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov defines the network as the set of facilities, providers and suppliers that have a contract with the insurer or plan to deliver health care services. Being in the network is a matter of contract, not of whether a referral is needed: in many HMOs even in-network specialists require one. The glossary's entry on the out-of-pocket limit shows the other side of the coin: care received out of network does not count toward that limit. The list of covered drugs is the formulary, a separate entry.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Billing: CMS-1500 & 837P (MLN006976), ASCA Exceptions
preguntas.subtema: Claim submission · CMA III.G.3.b(1) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6C k87, 6 k85 · CCMA 5L k185
preguntas.pregunta: A practice never answers the contractor's request for the papers behind its paper claim exception. What follows?
opciones: Its paper claims are denied from the ninety-first day, with no appeal
Its paper claims are denied from the sixty-first day, with no appeal
Its paper claims are denied from the ninety-first day, and it may appeal
Its paper claims are held back until the papers reach the contractor
preguntas.explicacion: A practice that sends its justification for a paper claim exception is told by mail whether the exception was approved. Where it does not respond to the request for the documentation, the paper claims are denied with effect from the ninety-first calendar day after the date of the first letter, and those denials carry no right of appeal.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Rights & protections under the health care law; and Glossary: Preventive services
preguntas.subtema: Insurance coverage · CMA III.G.3 (2027 III.G.3) · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is surprised that the screening her plan covers as preventive care cost her nothing. Why is that?
opciones: The health care law provides preventive care free to members
The screening counts against her deductible for the year
The provider writes the charge off under the plan contract
The plan pays it as an out-of-network service in full
preguntas.explicacion: Free preventive care is one of the protections the health care law sets out, and preventive services are the routine screenings, check-ups and counseling that head off illness or catch it early. Writing a charge off and applying a deductible are things that happen to services the member does have to share the cost of.

preguntas.subtema: Verbal orders · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 7A · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A provider gives a verbal order during a procedure. What does the record have to show afterwards?
opciones: That the order was dated, timed and authenticated promptly by a responsible practitioner
That the order was witnessed by two members of staff before it was carried out
That the order was entered as a standing order approved by the medical staff earlier
That the order was repeated back and then filed in the practice correspondence log
preguntas.explicacion: Orders of every kind, spoken ones included, have to carry a date, a time and prompt authentication from the practitioner who gave the order, or from another practitioner who is responsible for the patient where State scope-of-practice law, the facility's policy and the medical staff rules permit it. Preprinted and electronic standing orders run on a separate mechanism, with their own approval and review requirements.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), Collecting Patient Health Insurance Information
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMA III.G.3.a (2027 III.G.3.a) · CMAA 5 k75 · CCMA 5B
preguntas.pregunta: How do a Medigap insurer and a state Medicaid agency get the Medicare-paid claims data they need to pay their share?
opciones: Through the crossover agreement, a national contract for exchanging that claims data
Through the provider, which rebills each of them once Medicare's payment is posted
Through the patient, who forwards the summary notice Medicare mails to her at home
Through the clearinghouse, which splits the claim between payers before sending it
preguntas.explicacion: The coordination of benefits agreement program lays down a national standard contract between the secondary payer contractor and other insurers, for the sending of eligibility data on enrollees and of paid claims data from Original Medicare. Employer supplemental plans, Medicaid, Medigap plans and the rest draw on that national repository, each with a unique identifier, so paid claims cross over to them. Medicare is usually the primary payer on claims exchanged this way.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Access to Medical Care for Individuals with Mobility Disabilities, Part 2
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.F Laboratory Regulations, ADA · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA II.F.1.c(4) ADAAA · CMAA 3D ADA compliance
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who uses a wheelchair calls to book a draw and is told to bring someone who can help her transfer. Is that acceptable?
opciones: No, the provider must give reasonable assistance so she can be seen on her own
Yes, as long as staff offer to help when the companion cannot manage the transfer
Yes, if the practice can show that lifting would risk injuring its own staff
No, unless she is offered an appointment when the accessible room happens to be free
preguntas.explicacion: A patient with a disability may come to an appointment alone, like anyone else, and the provider has to give the reasonable assistance that lets her receive the care: help undressing, transferring, and being positioned. Protecting staff backs is answered with accessible equipment and training in patient handling, not with a refusal, and the accessible room should be reserved for her appointment in advance.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Urgent care; and Glossary: Emergency services
preguntas.subtema: Urgent care vs emergency · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A caller with no regular provider has a painful ear infection that began last night. Where should the front desk steer her first?
opciones: To an urgent care center, since the problem needs prompt care but is not emergency severe
To the hospital emergency department, where a sudden illness is always evaluated first
To an ambulatory surgical center, the outpatient site that handles same-day procedures
To a skilled nursing facility, where licensed nurses treat and observe a condition daily
preguntas.explicacion: Urgent care is meant for a problem serious enough that a person would want care without delay, yet not so severe that the emergency room is required. Emergency services mean evaluating an emergency condition and treating it so it does not worsen. For someone with no primary care provider, urgent care usually saves time and money over the emergency room.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Definition of Breach
preguntas.subtema: Breach risk assessment · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3E k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which factor is part of the risk assessment used to decide whether an impermissible disclosure is a breach?
opciones: The identity of the unauthorized person who used or received the information
The number of years the practice has operated without a previous incident
Whether the workforce member involved had completed the yearly privacy training
Whether the patient complained to the practice about the disclosure afterwards
preguntas.explicacion: At least four things go into the assessment: what PHI was involved and how much of it, taking in which identifiers appear and how likely re-identification would be; who the unauthorized person using or receiving it was; whether the PHI was in fact acquired or viewed; and how far the risk has been mitigated. Training records and complaints do not figure.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Hospital-wide Hazards: Recordkeeping, 29 CFR Part 1904; govinfo, Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act, sec. 2(9)
preguntas.subtema: OSHA 300, 301 and 300A · CPT D1 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.11.c / 2027 I.B.10.c · RMA II.B.7.e · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3E k44
preguntas.pregunta: Under OSHA's recordkeeping rule, 29 CFR part 1904, which forms record work-related injuries and illnesses?
opciones: The OSHA 300 log, the 301 incident report and the 300A summary posted each year
The sharps injury log, the training record and the employee medical record
The OSHA 200 log, which the Needlestick Act found sufficient for exposure tracking
The exposure determination, the written opinion and the Appendix A declination
preguntas.explicacion: Covered employers record each recordable injury and illness on the OSHA Form 300 log, prepare a Form 301 incident report with details of each case, and at the end of the year prepare the Form 300A summary and post it in a visible place. The sharps injury log, training records and medical records are kept under the bloodborne pathogens standard; the exposure determination, written opinion and declination are other documents of that same standard. Congress found the old OSHA 200 log insufficient, which is why the sharps log was added.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 1.4
preguntas.subtema: Read-only backup · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: What is a read-only backup record system able to do for a practice during an outage?
opciones: Show and print the information already recorded, from a copy refreshed often
Accept new orders and notes that are merged into the record after the outage
Run the scheduling module so that the day's appointments can still be moved
Send the claims already prepared, since billing does not alter clinical data
preguntas.explicacion: A read-only backup is a copy of what is already in the record system, kept up to date as often as possible, optimally hourly, and tested regularly. Users can look things up and print from it, but nothing new goes in, which is why paper forms and temporary record numbers are still needed for what happens during the outage.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Care Coordination: definition
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4E k163 coordinate care · CMAA 1 health care delivery
preguntas.pregunta: How is care coordination defined?
opciones: Organizing the activities of care on purpose and sharing information with everyone involved
Deliberately assigning one clinician to make every decision about a patient's care
Deliberately limiting the number of specialists a patient is allowed to see
Deliberately scheduling all of a patient's appointments on the same calendar day
preguntas.explicacion: Care coordination means organizing a patient's care activities on purpose and sharing information among everyone involved, so care comes out safer and more effective. What the patient needs and prefers is known in advance and reaches the right people at the right time, and that information then guides the care delivered.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, HETS EDI: How to Enroll
preguntas.subtema: Eligibility verification · CMA III.G.3.a (2027 III.G.3.a) · CMAA 4 k58 · CCMA 5E
preguntas.pregunta: A practice that stopped sending Medicare claims electronically has lost its access to the eligibility system. What is still open to it?
opciones: Its contractor's secure internet portal, which can still be used to check eligibility
Its clearinghouse's enrollment, which covers eligibility checks for all its providers
A paper eligibility request to the contractor, which has to be answered in 30 days
A telephone request to the contractor, which takes the place of the lost enrollment
preguntas.explicacion: Access to the eligibility system rests on an electronic claims enrollment with a contractor, and a provider that does not follow the enrollment steps or stops submitting electronic Original Medicare claims loses it. What remains open is registering with the contractor to use its secure portal for eligibility checks. The contractor verifies the claims enrollment before it approves eligibility access in the first place.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(c)(1)(iv), Exposure Control Plan
preguntas.subtema: Exposure Control Plan · CPT D1 1H k31 · PBT VI.G · CCMA 3C k109 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: How often does OSHA require an employer's written Exposure Control Plan to be reviewed and updated?
opciones: At least once a year, and whenever the tasks, procedures or positions with occupational exposure change
Within 10 working days of each new hire with occupational exposure, and otherwise every three years
Once a year together with the annual employee training, and at no other time even if tasks change
Every time an exposure incident is reported, and kept for the duration of employment plus 30 years
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (c)(1)(iv) sets two triggers: a review at least every year, plus a review whenever new or changed tasks, procedures or job positions alter who is exposed and how. The same review has to take in new technology that cuts exposure and document, each year, which safer medical devices were considered and adopted. The other periods belong to other rules of the same standard: 10 working days is the deadline for offering the hepatitis B vaccine, three years is how long training records are kept, and employment plus 30 years is the retention of medical records. An exposure incident triggers follow-up for the employee, not a rewrite of the plan.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, Office of Disease Prevention and Health Promotion, Healthy People 2030: Social Determinants of Health
preguntas.subtema: Social determinants · CCMA 4D k166 · CMAA 2H k30
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is one of the five domains of the social determinants of health?
opciones: Neighborhood and built environment
Family history and inherited disease risk
Body mass index and nutrition status
Vaccination record and screening history
preguntas.explicacion: Social determinants are the conditions in which people are born and live, learn and work, play and worship and grow old. Five domains are named: stability in economic terms; access to education and its quality; access to health care and its quality; the neighborhood and the built environment; and the social and community context.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Evacuation Plans and Procedures eTool, Emergency Action Plan: Evacuation Elements
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.B.8.a · 2027 I.B.7.a · CMAA 3 k45 · RMA II.7.c
preguntas.pregunta: Which item belongs on the evacuation map an office posts for its staff?
opciones: The exits, the assembly points and where the extinguishers and kits are
The names of the patients scheduled in each room of that hallway
The floor's electrical panels and the phone number of the landlord
The exits and the seating chart of the staff assigned to each desk
preguntas.explicacion: Most employers draw the routes on a floor diagram with arrows, and the map shows exits, assembly points and the equipment that may be needed in an emergency, such as fire extinguishers, first aid kits and spill kits. The plan also names who may order an evacuation and says how visitors and people with disabilities will be helped out.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, HETS EDI - How to Enroll, Enrollment Information for Providers and After You Enroll
preguntas.subtema: Medicare eligibility verification · CMAA 4C k58 · CCMA 5 k181 · CMA III.G.3 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: The clearinghouse reports that Medicare eligibility checks for one of the practice's providers are coming back rejected. What is the likeliest cause?
opciones: That provider's NPI has no active HETS EDI enrollment on file, which is now required
That provider's NPI has no active claims EDI enrollment, which is checked in its place
The clearinghouse has not linked its unique identifier to the beneficiary's Medicare number
The beneficiary's Medicare card was issued before the current numbering system took effect
preguntas.explicacion: Providers and suppliers check Medicare beneficiary eligibility through HETS, and since 11 May 2026 every National Provider Identifier submitted for eligibility verification has to have a valid HETS EDI enrollment on file. Where that enrollment is not active, the eligibility request is rejected. The electronic claims enrollment is a separate thing, verified by the contractor before it approves HETS access.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology
preguntas.subtema: Technology support · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.2.a · CMAA 4B k55 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: What does the telehealth guidance recommend a practice do with a patient before the first virtual appointment?
opciones: Walk her through the platform, or run a brief practice appointment with her
Ask her to install the software without help, to test whether she can manage
Send her the login details only, since written instructions overwhelm most patients
Have her come to the office once so that staff can configure her own device there
preguntas.explicacion: The guidance asks for written instructions that take the patient step by step through the whole process, and it says frustration and time lost to troubleshooting both drop when a telehealth coordinator, a nurse, an administrative staff member or a community health worker walks the patient through it directly. Where it can be arranged, someone on the team should run a short practice appointment so the patient rehearses every step.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms, cost-sharing example
preguntas.subtema: Financial calculations · CMAA 5C k76, 6B · CCMA 5K k182 · CMA III.G.8, III.G.6.e / 2027 III.G.6.c · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with a $1,500 deductible and 20% coinsurance has paid nothing yet this year. The office visit is allowed at $125. What does he pay today?
opciones: $125, the whole allowed amount, because the deductible has not been met
$25, the coinsurance share, because the deductible applies only to hospital care
$100, the plan's share, with the remaining amount billed to him later
$0, because the plan pays first and bills him after the year is closed
preguntas.explicacion: Until the deductible is satisfied, the plan pays nothing toward covered services, so the patient owes the full allowed amount of the visit. The $25 figure is what he would owe on a $125 visit after the deductible, when the 20% coinsurance begins. Deductibles are not limited to hospital services, and the plan's share is what the plan pays, never something the patient is billed for.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicare Coverage Determination Process
preguntas.subtema: Medical necessity · CMA III.G.1.d (2027 III.G.1.d) · CMAA 5 k69 · CCMA 5J k180
preguntas.pregunta: A proposed national coverage decision is posted for public comment. How long is that window, and when does the final decision follow?
opciones: Thirty days of comment, with the final decision inside sixty days after
Sixty days of comment, with the final decision inside thirty days after
Thirty days of comment, with the final decision inside six months after
Ninety days of comment, with the final decision inside ninety days after
preguntas.explicacion: The proposed decision is published for the public at the end of the six or nine month period, the comment period lasts thirty days, and the final decision is issued no later than sixty days after that period closes. A summary of the comments and the responses to them goes into the final determination, which is what makes the process an open one.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: In-network coinsurance; and Glossary: Out-of-network coinsurance
preguntas.subtema: In-network and out-of-network coverage · CMAA 4 k61 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A plan lists in-network coinsurance of 20% and out-of-network coinsurance of 40%. What does that tell the patient?
opciones: Her share of the allowed amount doubles when she uses a provider without a contract
Her share of the allowed amount doubles once she has used up the plan's yearly limit
The provider without a contract is paid twice as much by the plan for the same service
The provider without a contract must accept the plan's allowed amount as full payment
preguntas.explicacion: In-network coinsurance is the percentage owed when the provider has a contract with the plan, and it is normally lower than the out-of-network percentage; here the patient's share rises from a fifth to two fifths of the allowed amount. The figures describe what the patient owes, not extra payment to the provider, and a provider without a contract has agreed to nothing, which is why balance billing shows up outside the network.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Helping patients prepare for their telehealth appointment
preguntas.subtema: Setting up the picture · CMAA 4E k59 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks how to sit for her video appointment so the clinician can see her properly. What does the setup guidance tell her?
opciones: Plenty of light in front, camera steady at eye level, head and shoulders in the frame
Plenty of light behind her, camera steady at chest level, the whole room in the frame
Plenty of light in front, camera held in the hand, and the face filling the whole frame
Plenty of light behind her, camera steady at eye level, head and shoulders in the frame
preguntas.explicacion: The patient is told to choose a spot with plenty of light and to avoid sitting with her back to a window, which makes her face harder to see. The camera should be steady, at eye level, and framed so that head and shoulders are in view. She is also asked to find a quiet place and to close other applications so they do not slow the connection or distract her.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Reasons for Termination
preguntas.subtema: What follows a dismissal · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.b · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: A committee asks what becomes of patients after a practice dismisses them. What did the review of 536 terminations find?
opciones: Of those who re-established care in the same network, only a quarter were seen within six months
Of those who re-established care in the same network, three quarters were seen within one month
Of those who re-established care in the same network, nearly all were seen within six months
Of those who re-established care in the same network, only a quarter were seen within two years
preguntas.explicacion: Of the patients who left and later re-established care inside that same network, only a quarter, 25%, obtained a primary care appointment in the six months that followed, which the authors raise as a possible discontinuity of care. The same study found race, age and employment status to be independent predictors of who ends up dismissed.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: fraud
preguntas.subtema: Torts · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a · RMA I.C.3 · CMAA 3A k31
preguntas.pregunta: What separates an intentional misrepresentation from a negligent one in a fraud claim?
opciones: The speaker knew the statement was false or was reckless about its truth
The speaker put the statement in writing rather than saying it out loud
The speaker gained money from the statement rather than only goodwill
The speaker made the statement to a group rather than to a single person
preguntas.explicacion: For an intentional misrepresentation the speaker has to have known the statement was false, or to have been reckless about whether it was true, and to have intended the hearer to rely on it; the hearer then has to have relied reasonably and been harmed by relying. In a negligent misrepresentation the speaker may have believed the statement, but had no reasonable grounds for the belief.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 482.13(e)(8), (e)(9) and (e)(12), Standard: Restraint or seclusion
preguntas.subtema: Restraint time limits · CPT D1 k14 · CCMA 7A k215 · CMA II.E.1.d · RMA I.C.1.e · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32
preguntas.pregunta: For violent or self-destructive behavior, how long may a single restraint order last for an adult before it must be renewed?
opciones: 4 hours for adults 18 and older
2 hours for adults 18 and older
1 hour for adults 18 and older
8 hours for adults 18 and older
preguntas.explicacion: Unless state law is stricter, an order aimed at violent or self-destructive behavior may be renewed only within these limits, to a total of 24 hours: 4 hours for adults 18 or older, 2 hours for children and adolescents from 9 to 17, and 1 hour for children under 9. Past 24 hours a physician or other authorized practitioner has to see and assess the patient before a new order, and the patient is seen face to face within 1 hour of the intervention starting. Restraint for non-violent patients may be renewed as hospital policy allows.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", What healthcare information is protected; StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Introduction and Definition of PHI
preguntas.subtema: What counts as PHI · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35
preguntas.pregunta: What makes a laboratory result protected health information under HIPAA?
opciones: Any identifier tying the result to one patient: name, phone number or email
Only the patient's Social Security number or medical record number, not the name
Only the result itself, regardless of whether a name is attached
Only electronic storage; a printed result with a name attached is not PHI under the rule
preguntas.explicacion: Health information turns into protected health information once it carries an identifier tying it to one particular patient: a name, a telephone or email address, a street address, a Social Security number. The Privacy Rule lists 18 such elements, and information about relatives, employers or the people who share a patient's household is covered as well. PHI may be written, spoken, on paper or electronic, of any size, inside the facility or outside it. Strip every identifier under the de-identification standard and what is left is no longer PHI.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse (MLN4649244), Exclusion: Reinstatement
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: OIG turns down an excluded provider's application for reinstatement. When may she apply again?
opciones: After a year, which is the wait a refusal opens up
After five years, the floor for a mandatory exclusion
After sixty days, the deadline that runs on overpayments
At any moment, since a refusal sets no waiting time
preguntas.explicacion: Reinstatement is not automatic when the exclusion period ends: the excluded party has to apply and receive written notice from OIG granting it. Where OIG denies the application, the party may re-apply after one year. The five-year figure is the minimum length of a mandatory exclusion, not a waiting time after a refusal.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Administrative Simplification: Transactions
preguntas.subtema: Claim submission · CMA III.G.3.b(1) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6C k87 · CCMA 5L k185
preguntas.pregunta: Which standard does a covered entity use for the pharmacy transactions that HIPAA adopted?
opciones: The one set by the prescription drug program council
The one set by the X12 committee for all transactions
The one set by the committee that designs the paper form
The one set by the dental association for its own codes
preguntas.explicacion: Covered entities that carry out any of the adopted transactions electronically have to use an adopted standard, and the rules name two sources: the insurance section of the X12 committee, and, for certain pharmacy transactions, the national council that sets prescription drug standards. The paper claim form and the dental code set are separate matters.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", Other Issues: Criminal violations; StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Criminal Violation of HIPAA Rules
preguntas.subtema: Criminal penalties · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k34
preguntas.pregunta: Which HIPAA violation carries a criminal penalty of up to $100,000 and up to 5 years in prison?
opciones: Obtaining or disclosing identifiable health information under false pretenses
Knowingly obtaining or disclosing identifiable health information
Selling identifiable health information for gain or to cause malicious harm
Failing to correct a violation due to willful neglect within the required period
preguntas.explicacion: The criminal side has three tiers. Knowingly obtaining identifiable health information, or disclosing it, reaches $50,000 and 1 year. Doing so under false pretenses reaches $100,000 and 5 years. Doing so while intending to sell, transfer or use the information for commercial advantage, for personal gain, or to do malicious harm reaches $250,000 and 10 years. These cases belong to the Department of Justice, and they can land on nurses, secretaries, telephone operators and other employees, not only on institutions. Willful neglect left uncorrected is the highest civil tier, not a criminal one.

preguntas.subtema: Treatment disclosures · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.2.a(5) · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist faxes a patient's lab results to the physician who ordered them. Does HIPAA require the patient's written authorization first?
opciones: No: disclosures for treatment are permitted without authorization
Yes: any disclosure outside the facility requires a signed authorization
Yes, unless the patient signed the notice of privacy practices acknowledgment
No, but only because fax transmissions are outside the Privacy Rule
preguntas.explicacion: No authorization is needed for a covered entity to use or disclose PHI in its own treatment, in payment or in health care operations, nor to disclose it so that any other provider can treat the patient; 45 CFR 164.506 sets that out and 164.502(a)(1)(ii) lists it among the permitted uses. Authorization under 164.508 is needed for uses outside those categories, such as marketing or sale of PHI. The acknowledgment of the notice is a separate duty and does not create or remove permissions, and faxes carry PHI like any other medium.

preguntas.subtema: Form of retained records · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: An employer wants to scan its employee medical files and shred the paper. Which item may not be handled that way?
opciones: Chest X-ray films, which the standard has preserved in their original state
Exposure monitoring worksheets, which the standard keeps for thirty years
Any record whose author has left, because nobody can authenticate the entry
Any record older than five years, which has to stay in the form first used
preguntas.explicacion: The standard does not dictate the form or the process by which a record is preserved, so long as the information stays intact and can be retrieved. It makes one exception in that sentence: chest X-ray films are kept in their original state.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Media Notice
preguntas.subtema: Media notice · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3E k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: At what point does a breach also require notice to prominent media outlets?
opciones: When it affects more than 500 residents of one State or jurisdiction
When it affects more than 500 individuals nationwide, counted across all States
When it affects any number of individuals and involves an electronic device
When it affects fewer than 500 individuals but the entity cannot reach them by mail
preguntas.explicacion: Where a breach touches more than 500 residents of one State or jurisdiction, the entity has to notify prominent media outlets serving that area as well as the individuals, usually by press release. The media notice runs on the individual notice's clock: no unreasonable delay, and 60 days from discovery at the outside. The content is the same.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Billing: CMS-1500 & 837P (MLN006976), Implementation & Companion Guides
preguntas.subtema: Claim submission · CMA III.G.3.b(1) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6C k87, 6 k85 · CCMA 5L k185
preguntas.pregunta: Why does each Medicare contractor publish its own companion guide for the electronic professional claim?
opciones: To spell out its data content needs alongside the standard
To replace the standard with a claim format of its own
To set the fees it will pay for each professional service
To list the codes it accepts on a paper claim form instead
preguntas.explicacion: The implementation guide gives the technical instructions for the adopted transaction itself. Each contractor then publishes a companion guide, approved by CMS, that defines the data content its own fee-for-service claims require. The companion guide is used with the standard and never in place of it.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 7: Improve secure email exchanges
preguntas.subtema: Email etiquette · CCMA 6C k196 · CMAA 2A k27 · CMA F.5 / 2027 F.3
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant is answering a patient's secure message about her results. How should that message be written?
opciones: Short and simple, in plain words that are not medical
Detailed, so that every question is settled in one message
In the same wording that went into the clinical note
With a request that the patient not reply by telephone
preguntas.explicacion: Emails are kept short and simple, in plain non-medical language, and checked against what the patient actually asked; patients are also told they may call with questions. Where understanding really matters, the advice is to telephone the patient and use teach-back rather than rely on the message.

preguntas.fuente: AAMA, Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Standards for CMAs (AAMA), Principle 7; and Grounds for Discipline I
preguntas.subtema: Unethical conduct · CCMA 7C · CMA E.7 / 2027 E.6 · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: What does the AAMA Code of Conduct say about working while impaired?
opciones: Certificants shall not practice while impaired by drugs or alcohol
Certificants shall not practice while impaired unless supervised closely
Certificants shall report impairment to the employer before each shift
Certificants shall be tested whenever a supervisor suspects impairment
preguntas.explicacion: One of the principles states plainly that certificants must not practice medical assisting while their ability to do so is impaired by chemical substances, drugs or alcohol. A related ground for discipline covers possessing, using or distributing controlled substances for anything other than legitimate or therapeutic purposes, addiction, diversion, and breaking any drug law.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Access to Medical Care for Individuals with Mobility Disabilities
preguntas.subtema: ADAAA compliance · CMAA 3A (ADAAA)
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who uses a wheelchair needs a full examination. Is examining her in the chair acceptable?
opciones: Generally no: an accessible table, lift or trained staff should be used
Generally yes, provided the findings are documented as a limited examination
Generally yes, as long as the patient consents to being seen that way
Generally no, unless the practice has fewer than fifteen employees
preguntas.explicacion: Examining a patient in a wheelchair is usually less thorough than on the table and does not deliver equal medical services. Options include a table that lowers to roughly 17 to 19 inches from the floor, an accessible stretcher, a patient lift, or enough trained staff to help with the transfer. Care cannot be refused because the visit takes longer.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse: Prevent, Detect, Report (MLN4649244), Program Integrity
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: CMS sorts the causes of improper payments into four groups. Which result does bending the rules produce?
opciones: Abuse, as in improper billing practices such as upcoding
Fraud, as in billing for services that were never given
Waste, as in ordering more diagnostic tests than needed
Error, as in a contract with a physician left unsigned
preguntas.explicacion: The figure CMS uses runs from mistakes, which produce errors such as an unsigned physician contract, through inefficiencies, which produce waste such as excessive testing, to bending the rules, which produces abuse, and intentional deception, which produces fraud. How any single improper payment is finally characterised depends on its own facts.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Telehealth Systems, Function
preguntas.subtema: Remote monitoring · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.2.a · CMAA 4B k54 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which telehealth arrangement is remote patient monitoring?
opciones: A wearable device sending the patient's readings to the clinician between visits
A live video call in which the clinician watches the patient walk across the room
A specialist reading an image the primary care clinician uploaded the previous day
A brief telephone call in which the clinician asks about new symptoms since Monday
preguntas.explicacion: Remote patient monitoring follows a patient's clinical status between visits, either without interruption or at intervals, using devices or digital platforms; the readings travel in from equipment kept at home or are keyed in by the patient. Continuous glucose monitors are one named example; cardiac rhythm monitors are the other. It stands beside the synchronous and the asynchronous arrangement as the third type of telemedicine service.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fighting Identity Theft with the Red Flags Rule: Covered Accounts
preguntas.subtema: Covered accounts · CMAA 4C · CCMA 5F k190 · CMA III.H.2.b · RMA II.B.1 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A practice works out that it holds no covered accounts at all this year. What does the FTC advise it to do about the Red Flags Rule?
opciones: Repeat the risk assessment periodically, since a change in the business can create them
Write the program anyway, since every medical office holds covered accounts in practice
Send the Commission a statement recording that the Rule does not reach the practice
Destroy the identification documents on file, which are no longer needed for the Rule
preguntas.explicacion: A financial institution or creditor first has to work out whether it holds covered accounts, looking at the ones it has and the ones it opens, and only then does a written program become compulsory. Holding none means no program is needed, but business models shift and so do services, and accounts can appear through a change of structure, of process or of organization, which is why the assessment is repeated periodically.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, National Provider Identifier Standard (NPI)
preguntas.subtema: Third-party billing requirements · CMAA 6 k85, 6C k87 · CCMA 5L k180 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: What is the National Provider Identifier?
opciones: A 10-digit number that identifies a covered provider and carries no other data
A 10-digit number that identifies a covered provider and encodes the specialty
A 9-digit number the payer assigns to each provider it contracts with
A number that replaces the provider's state license in clinical records
preguntas.explicacion: The National Provider Identifier is a HIPAA administrative simplification standard: covered health care providers get a unique identification number, ten positions long, numeric and intelligence-free, so that the digits give away nothing about the state where the provider lives or the specialty practiced. Payers do not assign it, and in standard transactions it replaces legacy identifiers, not licenses in the record.

preguntas.fuente: NAIC, Coordination of Benefits Model Regulation (Model 120), Order of Benefit Determination Rules
preguntas.subtema: Insurance rules · CMAA 5B k75 · CCMA 5E k182
preguntas.pregunta: One plan covers a woman because she still works for the employer; another covers her because she retired from a different one. Which is primary?
opciones: The plan covering the person as an active employee is the primary one
The plan covering the person as a retired employee is the primary one
The plan with the earlier effective date is the primary one for the claim
The plan whose subscriber has the earlier birthday is the primary one
preguntas.explicacion: The plan covering a person as an active employee, meaning one who is neither laid off nor retired, is primary, and the plan covering that same person as retired or laid off is secondary; the same holds for a dependent of each. The rule is skipped when the non-dependent or dependent rule already settles the order, and it is ignored when the other plan has no such rule.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: The provider documents a borderline condition at the end of the visit. How is it coded?
opciones: As confirmed, unless the classification has an entry for the borderline form
As uncertain, so only the signs and symptoms are coded for that visit
As confirmed, but only for inpatients and never in an outpatient office
As uncertain, unless the provider repeats it at the following visit
preguntas.explicacion: A borderline diagnosis is treated as confirmed unless the classification carries its own entry for the borderline form of that condition, as it does for borderline diabetes. A borderline condition is not an uncertain diagnosis, so the inpatient and the outpatient setting are treated alike here. Unclear documentation is a reason to query.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Remittance Processing and Patient Collections
preguntas.subtema: Charge reconciliation · CMAA 6B, 6 k81 · CCMA 5K k181 · CMA III.G.7.a / 2027 III.G.6.a-c
preguntas.pregunta: In what order are these steps done after the payer adjudicates a claim?
opciones: The remittance arrives, payments are posted, adjustments are recorded, balances are billed
Payments are posted, the remittance arrives, balances are billed, adjustments are recorded
Balances are billed, payments are posted, the remittance arrives, adjustments are recorded
Adjustments are recorded, balances are billed, payments are posted, the remittance arrives
preguntas.explicacion: Once the payer approves the claim, an explanation of benefits or an electronic remittance advice goes out listing the covered services and the reasons anything went unpaid; payments are then posted and the write-offs applied, contractual and noncontractual alike. Collecting the patient's portion comes last, at the patient collections step, once the office knows what the plan left unpaid.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: Organizational Requirements
preguntas.subtema: Business associate agreements · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA I.C.5 · CMAA 3B k33 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Before a transcription vendor may start receiving electronic protected health information, what must the practice have in place?
opciones: A written business associate agreement obligating the vendor to safeguard the information
A signed authorization from every patient whose dictation the vendor is going to transcribe
A notice of privacy practices addressed to the vendor and acknowledged by its privacy official
An accounting of disclosures listing each record the vendor is expected to receive that year
preguntas.explicacion: The Security Rule lets a covered entity put ePHI in a business associate's hands, to be created, received, kept or transmitted on the entity's behalf, only once satisfactory assurances have been obtained in a contract or another written arrangement. That agreement also obliges the business associate to demand the same of any subcontractor and to report security incidents, breaches included, back to the practice.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Clinical Significance: Patient Rights under HIPAA
preguntas.subtema: How results are communicated · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks that results never be left as a message on his home phone, only mailed to his address. How is that request treated?
opciones: As a right: patients may say how information reaches them
As a courtesy the clinic may grant if its system allows it
As a restriction that needs the privacy officer's approval
As impossible, since results go out the way the system sends
preguntas.explicacion: The list of patient rights includes stating how one's information is to be handled and communicated to others; the example given is a patient who wants any message from the pharmacy or the hospital mailed to his home rather than left on his telephone. It sits beside the right to ask that disclosures be restricted and the right to receive an accounting of the disclosures that were made.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Interview Techniques", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Questioning techniques · CCMA 6C k200 · CMAA 2A k15 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which opening question invites a patient to lay out their own concerns?
opciones: "What is the main reason you are seeking care today?"
"Has this pain been present for more than three days?"
"Would you rather have the lab drawn before the visit?"
"Did the last provider already start you on a medicine?"
preguntas.explicacion: The first question posed is usually open-ended, inviting the patient to share what brought them in and showing that someone is listening without judgment. The other three are focused questions: they gather a specific detail with a yes-or-no answer and belong later in the encounter.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, How Medicare works with other insurance
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k75 · CCMA 5B
preguntas.pregunta: A retiree's former employer plan pays after Medicare and is paying nothing at all. What does the coordination guidance suggest checking first?
opciones: Whether she signed up for Part B, which a secondary group plan may require of her
Whether she signed up for Part D, which a secondary group plan may require of her
Whether she bought a Medigap policy, which a secondary group plan may require
Whether she met the Part A deductible, which a secondary group plan may require
preguntas.explicacion: Where the secondary payer is a group health plan or retiree coverage, the patient may have to sign up for Medicare Part B before that plan pays anything. It is the usual reason a retiree plan that looks like real coverage pays nothing. Changes in coverage should be reported to the doctor and to the provider at the time of care, and questions about who pays first go to the coordination center.

preguntas.subtema: Hospital retention · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: Under the Medicare conditions of participation, how long must a hospital keep its medical records?
opciones: At least five years, either in the original form or a legal reproduction
At least seven years, matching the rule for orders and certifications
At least ten years, matching the rule for Medicare Advantage organizations
For the duration of care plus thirty years, matching the OSHA employee rule
preguntas.explicacion: The medical record service condition wants records written accurately, completed promptly, filed and retained properly, and kept accessible, and it fixes a floor of five years, in original form or a legal reproduction. Seven, ten and thirty years belong elsewhere: documentation of ordered and certified services, Medicare Advantage contracts, and OSHA employee medical records.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: The Intervention
preguntas.subtema: Open access, shape of the day · CMAA 4A k51 · CCMA 5C k171 · CMA III.H.1.a-b · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Under open access, how is a physician's day laid out in the appointment book?
opciones: About half the day is left open, the rest for necessary follow-ups and patients who declined a same-day slot
About a quarter of the day is left open, and the remainder is booked ahead as in the traditional system
The day is booked as usual, but a quarter of the slots are held back for callers with an urgent problem
About half the day is left open, and the remainder is kept for callers the front desk triages as urgent
preguntas.explicacion: Instead of filling a physician's time weeks or months in advance, the model leaves roughly half the day open. Booked ahead are the clinically necessary follow-ups and the visits of those who, having called, preferred not to be seen that same day, a group that usually stays under a quarter. Triaging callers by clinical urgency is exactly what the model does away with.

preguntas.subtema: Patient rights · CCMA k215 · CMA E.1.d · RMA I.C.1.e · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32
preguntas.pregunta: Which right does a hospitalized patient have over the plan of care?
opciones: To be informed of their status, take part in planning, and refuse treatment
To be informed of their status and to demand any treatment they have read about
To take part in planning only when a family representative is at the bedside
To refuse treatment only after a second physician has documented agreement
preguntas.explicacion: The patient, or their representative where state law allows one, has the right to make informed decisions: to be told their health status, to take part in planning the care and the treatment, and to request or refuse treatment. That right explicitly does not become a way to demand services judged medically unnecessary or inappropriate, and no second signature is needed to refuse.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient in acute kidney failure has produced no urine at all. Which term names that finding, and how is it built?
opciones: Anuria: a prefix meaning without plus an ending meaning in the urine
Dysuria: a prefix meaning without plus an ending meaning in the urine
Polyuria: a prefix meaning without plus an ending meaning in the urine
Nocturia: a prefix meaning without plus an ending meaning in the urine
preguntas.explicacion: The prefix a- or an- means without or lacking, and the ending -uria means in the urine, so anuria is the absence of urine. The distractors reuse the same ending with other prefixes: dys- is difficult or abnormal, and poly- is many or excessive, which is why polyuria is a large output rather than none.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Body Parts and Disorders
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: Which set of roots would you expect to see in the terms used by a cardiology practice?
opciones: cardi/o for the heart, angi/o for a vessel, phleb/o for a vein
cardi/o for the heart, aden/o for a vessel, hepat/o for a vein
coron/o for the heart, arthr/o for a vessel, nephr/o for a vein
my/o for the heart, thromb/o for a vessel, splen/o for a vein
preguntas.explicacion: Cardi- and coron- both name the heart, angi- and vasculo- name a blood vessel, and phleb- and ven- name a vein. The roots in the wrong answers belong elsewhere: aden- is a gland, hepat- the liver, arthr- a joint, nephr- the kidney, thromb- a clot and splen- the spleen.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Common Barriers to Communication
preguntas.subtema: Barriers to communication · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.3.b / 2027 F.1.i
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with no health care background looks lost while an assistant explains a procedure. Which barrier fits best?
opciones: Jargon the receiver does not share with the sender
Physiological pain that blocks what the patient recalls
Hallway noise, a loud television and overhead paging
A stress response running in the sender and the receiver
preguntas.explicacion: Medical terminology, complicated words and slang build a barrier the sender creates without noticing; the fix is plain language a person outside health care can follow. Noise, pain and the stress response are barriers too, but none of them is what the scenario describes.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Service Animals (inquiries, exclusions, charges)
preguntas.subtema: ADAAA compliance · CMAA 3A (ADAAA)
preguntas.pregunta: When may a service animal be asked to leave the office?
opciones: When it is out of control and the handler will not control it
When another patient in the waiting room is allergic to dogs
When the state health code bars animals from the premises
When staff have no time to supervise or care for the animal
preguntas.explicacion: There are two grounds: the dog is out of control and its handler takes no effective action, or the dog is not housebroken. Even then the person has to be offered the goods or services with the animal absent. Neither an allergy nor a fear of dogs is a valid reason, food premises must generally admit them anyway, and staff are never required to supervise or care for the animal.

preguntas.fuente: plainlanguage.gov, Plain language guides: Writing for understanding, Use the active voice
preguntas.subtema: Written communication · CCMA 6C k196 · CMAA 2C k19 · CMA F.5 / 2027 F.3
preguntas.pregunta: An instruction sheet reads “The form must be returned before the visit.” What does plain language guidance advise?
opciones: Name who acts: “You must return the form before the visit”
Add a heading above it so the section is easier to scan
Move it to the future tense so the deadline reads as clearer
Turn the verb into a noun: “Return of the form is required”
preguntas.explicacion: Active voice makes clear who does what and removes any doubt about who is responsible; passive sentences often hide the actor and are called one of the biggest problems in government writing. Short sections help, but they do not fix the sentence. The future tense and nouns made out of verbs are the two habits the same guidance tells writers to drop.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Administrative Simplification: Transactions
preguntas.subtema: Claim submission · CMA III.G.3.b(1) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6 k87 · CCMA 5 k185
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is on the list of standard transactions adopted under HIPAA?
opciones: Coordination of benefits between one health plan and another
Correction of a diagnosis code after the claim has been paid
Notification that a payer has changed its own fee schedule
Certification that a provider's state license is still current
preguntas.explicacion: The adopted transactions run to claims and encounter information; eligibility; claim status; referrals and authorizations; enrollment and disenrollment; coordination of benefits; premium payment; and payment together with remittance advice. Any covered entity carrying out one of them electronically must use the adopted ASC X12N standard, or NCPDP for certain pharmacy transactions.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Hospital-wide Hazards: Recordkeeping, Updates to OSHA's Recordkeeping Rule
preguntas.subtema: Reporting severe injuries to OSHA · CPT D1 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.11.c / 2027 I.B.10.c · RMA II.B.7.d III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3E k44
preguntas.pregunta: How quickly must an employer report a work-related fatality, and a work-related inpatient hospitalization, to OSHA?
opciones: A fatality within 8 hours; a hospitalization within 24 hours
A fatality within 24 hours; a hospitalization within 8 hours
Both within 72 hours, by telephone to the area office
Both within 60 days, on the OSHA 300A summary
preguntas.explicacion: Under the recordkeeping rule updated in 2015, as summarized in OSHA's Hospitals eTool, employers report every work-related fatality within 8 hours of learning of it, and every work-related inpatient hospitalization, amputation or loss of an eye within 24 hours. Reports can be made by phone to the nearest area office, to the 24-hour OSHA hotline at 1-800-321-6742, or through the online serious event form. The 300A summary is an annual posting, not a reporting channel, and 60 days is the HIPAA breach notification limit.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Part A (Hospital Insurance) costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74, 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient is admitted to hospital in February and again in September. How often may she owe the 2026 Part A deductible?
opciones: Twice, since $1,736 falls due for each benefit period and there is no yearly cap
Once, since $1,736 is a yearly deductible in the way the Part B deductible is
Twice, but at $283 each time, which is the figure the yearly deductible uses
Not at all, since days one to sixty of an inpatient stay carry no charge
preguntas.explicacion: The 2026 Part A deductible is $1,736 for each inpatient benefit period before Original Medicare begins to pay, and there is no limit on how many benefit periods a person may have in one year, so the deductible can fall due more than once. Days one to sixty cost nothing only after that deductible has been paid.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Administrative Simplification: Health Care Payment and Remittance Advice and EFT
preguntas.subtema: Remittance advice · CMA III.G.3.b(3) (exam through June 2027) · CMAA 5 k79 · CCMA 5 k181
preguntas.pregunta: To which transmissions do the electronic funds transfer standards apply?
opciones: Only to those sent over the Automated Clearing House network
Only to those sent between a health plan and a clearinghouse
To every transfer of funds a health plan makes to a provider
To every transfer a provider's own financial institution makes
preguntas.explicacion: The funds transfer standards reach only data sent over the Automated Clearing House network, the processing and delivery system that carries these transfers over nationwide telecommunications networks. The transfer itself is the message a health plan uses to order a financial institution to move money into a provider's account, and it carries the amount, the payer and payee and their identification, the bank accounts, routing numbers and payment date.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A prescription is written for one tablet BID. How often should the patient take it?
opciones: Two doses a day
One dose a day
Three doses a day
Four doses a day
preguntas.explicacion: The frequency abbreviations on a prescription run in a family that is easy to confuse: BID is twice a day, TID three times a day and QID four times a day, while PRN means the patient takes it only as needed. Reading BID as TID or QID hands the patient an extra dose every day.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Coinsurance
preguntas.subtema: Financial calculations · CMAA 5C k76, 6B · CCMA 5K k182 · CMA III.G.8, III.G.6.e / 2027 III.G.6.c · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: An office visit has an allowed amount of $100 and the plan's coinsurance is 20%. The patient has already met the deductible. What does she owe?
opciones: $20, and the plan pays the rest of the allowed amount for that visit
$80, and the plan pays the rest of the allowed amount for that visit
$100, because coinsurance applies only after the visit has been billed
$120, because the coinsurance is added on top of the allowed amount
preguntas.explicacion: Coinsurance is the patient's percentage of the allowed amount once the deductible is satisfied: 20% of $100 comes to $20, and the plan covers the remainder. The $80 figure inverts the shares. Paying the whole $100 is what happens before the deductible is met, not after. Nothing is added above the allowed amount by a contracted provider, since that ceiling is the negotiated price.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Inappropriate Medical Abbreviations", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k10 · CMAA 1 k7 · RMA I.B.3.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which documents must be kept free of abbreviations because the patient and family receive them?
opciones: Consent forms, discharge instructions and patient rights documents
Handwritten drug orders, preprinted forms and progress notes
Laboratory requisitions, referral letters and imaging reports
Staff schedules, inventory records and equipment logs
preguntas.explicacion: Abbreviations are banned from anything the patient or family will read, including documents on patient rights, informed consent forms and discharge instructions. The point is that people should not have to guess: a patient too embarrassed to ask what an entry means may go home and follow it wrong.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Email Communications and Faxes
preguntas.subtema: Email safeguards · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k38
