preguntas.fuente: CMS, HETS EDI - How to Enroll, Enrollment Information for Vendors & Clearinghouses
preguntas.subtema: Who enrols for eligibility checks · CMAA 4C k58 · CCMA 5 k181 · CMA III.G.3 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: A vendor offers to complete the practice's HETS enrollment on its behalf so that nobody at the office has to deal with it. What does CMS say?
opciones: The provider itself must acknowledge the rules of behavior and name its relationship with the vendor
The vendor may enroll the provider once it holds a signed trading partner agreement on file
The provider must enroll separately with each contractor whose jurisdiction it bills into
The vendor may enroll the provider, but only for the jurisdiction where the practice sits
preguntas.explicacion: Vendors and clearinghouses are asked to support enrollment, encouraging providers to enroll and sharing their unique identifier, but they are told not to enroll providers themselves. It is the provider who has to read the HETS Rules of Behavior, acknowledge them, and state what its relationship with the vendor is. Enrolling once with a single contractor is enough; there is no need to repeat it with each one.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicare Coverage Determination Process
preguntas.subtema: Medical necessity · CMAA 5 k69 · CCMA 5J k180 · CMA III.G.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: What is the difference between a national coverage determination and a local coverage determination?
opciones: The national one binds the whole program; the local one is issued by a contractor for its area
The national one binds the whole program; the local one is issued by the state insurance office
The national one applies to hospitals and the local one applies to physician offices
The national one is advisory and the local one decides payment for the claim at hand
preguntas.explicacion: National coverage determinations limit coverage of a service, procedure or technology across the program, and HHS decides them through an evidence-based process that may include an outside technology assessment or the advisory committee. Where no national policy exists, a Medicare administrative contractor may cover an item at its discretion through a local coverage determination for its geographic area, and it may also further define a national one.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Notice to the Secretary
preguntas.subtema: Notice to the Secretary · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3E k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: A breach affects 40 patients. When must the Secretary be notified?
opciones: Annually, within 60 days of the close of the calendar year in which it was discovered
Straight away, and in any event within 60 days of discovering the breach
Annually, within 90 days of the close of the calendar year in which it was discovered
Only if the affected patients ask the practice in writing to make the report
preguntas.explicacion: Notice to the Secretary travels through a breach report form filed electronically on the HHS site. When 500 or more individuals are affected the report goes in straight away and in any event within 60 days of the breach. Where fewer than 500 are affected the practice may report annually, and those reports fall due within 60 days of the close of the calendar year in which the breaches were discovered.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, FAQ 570: E-mail with patients
preguntas.subtema: E-mail with patients · CCMA 6 k204 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.3.g · CMAA 7H k97 · NCMA 3.2
preguntas.pregunta: May a practice discuss treatment with a patient by ordinary e-mail?
opciones: Yes, provided the practice applies reasonable safeguards when it does so
No, unencrypted e-mail is forbidden for messages that touch on treatment
Yes, but only after the patient signs an authorization for each message
No, unless the practice first files a security incident report with the Secretary
preguntas.explicacion: The Privacy Rule lets covered providers communicate electronically with patients so long as reasonable safeguards go with it. The precautions given as examples are verifying that the address is right before anything is sent, and sending an alert first to confirm it. Unencrypted e-mail is not forbidden for treatment-related messages, though other safeguards should be used, such as limiting how much the message carries.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: Safeguards
preguntas.subtema: Security safeguards · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Into which three categories does the Security Rule sort the safeguards a practice must put in place?
opciones: Administrative, physical and technical
Preventive, detective and corrective controls
Required, addressable and optional measures
Confidentiality, integrity and availability
preguntas.explicacion: Regulated entities have to put in place safeguards that are reasonable and appropriate, and the rule sorts them into three families: administrative, physical and technical, which is the skeleton of the rule itself. Confidentiality, integrity and availability are the goals those safeguards serve, not the families; required and addressable describe how each implementation specification inside a standard is designated.

preguntas.fuente: plainlanguage.gov, Identify and write for your audience
preguntas.subtema: Writing for the audience · CCMA 6 k206 · CMA II.F.2 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7G k95 · NCMA 3.2
preguntas.pregunta: Before drafting a letter that will go to patients, what does the federal plain language guidance say to do first?
opciones: Identify the audience the letter is going to be written for
Choose the template and the letterhead the practice prefers
Decide which class of mail will carry the finished letter
Check the reading level of the last letter the practice sent
preguntas.explicacion: The guidance is built on a set of principles: plain language itself, writing so as to be understood, designing so as to be understood, and testing whether the content really is understandable. Identifying the audience and writing for it is the first of them, because the statutory requirement is that content aimed at the public be written for the specific audience that will read it.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Drug plan coverage rules
preguntas.subtema: Medication authorization · CMA III.G.5.a(2) (2027 III.G.5.a(2)) · CMAA 4G k67 · CCMA 5H k183 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: A new plan member finds her long-standing medicine is not on the plan's drug list. What may the plan give her while that is sorted out?
opciones: A transition fill, a one-time thirty-day supply of the drug she has been taking
A quantity limit exception, which covers the drug for the remainder of the year
A step therapy exception, granted once she has tried the cheaper drug on the list
A formulary exception, granted automatically for any drug she was already taking
preguntas.explicacion: When drug coverage begins, the member may get a transition fill: a one-time thirty-day supply of a drug she has been taking that the plan either does not cover or subjects to prior authorization or step therapy. An exception, by contrast, is a decision the plan makes on request to cover a drug off its list or to waive one of its coverage rules.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 20: Assess interest
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4D k165 specialty resources · CMAA 2H k30
preguntas.pregunta: How should a practice find out which patients would benefit from adult literacy or math classes?
opciones: Ask every patient whether they want to improve their reading or math skills
Watch for patients who leave the intake forms partly blank and ask only them
Add a question about reading skills to the intake form and read the answers
Have the clinician judge during the visit which patients seem to struggle
preguntas.explicacion: Research shows clinicians are poor at spotting who has limited literacy, so the guesswork is removed by asking everyone the same open offer. Putting the question on the intake form is not enough, since patients with literacy trouble may leave forms unfinished, and patients rarely raise the subject unless someone else starts it.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Food Safety — Summary
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k169 disease prevention education · CMAA 2G · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient shopping for canned goods asks what to look out for. Which advice is correct?
opciones: Skip bulging cans and jars with cracks or loose lids, and check the date
Skip dented cans only, since bulging is caused by normal temperature change
Skip cans past the date only, since packaging damage does not reach the food
Skip glass jars altogether, since only cans can be checked for damage
preguntas.explicacion: In the grocery store the advice is to avoid cans that bulge and jars whose lids are loose or whose glass is cracked, and to look at the package so the food has not passed its expiration date. That check happens before the food ever reaches the four home steps of cleaning, separating, cooking and chilling.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Reproductive System: Female Reproductive System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(8) (2027 I.C.6.f(8)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12
preguntas.pregunta: Which organs make up the female reproductive system?
opciones: Vagina, uterus, Fallopian tubes, ovaries, accessory glands and external genitals
Vagina, uterus, ureters, ovaries, accessory glands and external genitals
Ovaries, Fallopian tubes, bladder, urethra, accessory glands and mammary glands
Ovaries, Fallopian tubes, uterus, rectum, seminal vesicles and external genitals
preguntas.explicacion: The female reproductive organs produce and sustain the egg cells, carry them to where fertilization can happen, house a developing fetus, deliver it, and make the female sex hormones. The list is the ovaries, the Fallopian tubes, the uterus, the vagina, the accessory glands and the external genital organs.

preguntas.subtema: Rights stated in the notice · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: The notice tells patients they may ask the practice to restrict certain uses of their information. What must the notice say alongside that right?
opciones: That the practice is not obliged to agree to a restriction a patient requests
That the practice will answer any request for a restriction within thirty days
That a restriction once agreed binds every provider the patient later attends
That a request for a restriction has to be renewed at each new plan year
preguntas.explicacion: The statement of individual rights in the notice covers the right to ask for restrictions on uses and disclosures, and it has to say alongside that the entity need not agree, apart from one restriction the rule does make binding. The same statement covers confidential communications, access, amendment and an accounting of disclosures.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", What are physical safeguards and How do you protect electronic information; StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Storage of PHI Data and Computers
preguntas.subtema: Physical safeguards · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k38
preguntas.pregunta: Which physical safeguard for PHI applies to the computer at a phlebotomy station?
opciones: Point the screen away from public view and log off when stepping away
Leave the session open so the next phlebotomist can chart without delay
Store the patient list on a personal flash drive as an unencrypted backup
Print the day's schedule and post it at the check-in window
preguntas.explicacion: Physical safeguards regulate access to equipment that holds PHI: computer screens are turned away from public view, privacy barriers are used at reception, PHI is never left unattended, and workstations are logged off whenever the user leaves, even for a few minutes. Portable devices are a known source of breaches, so patient data is not stored on personal laptops or flash drives, and if it must be, it is encrypted. A posted schedule and an open session both expose identifiable information to people not involved in care.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Verification
preguntas.subtema: Access barriers · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks that her records be mailed to her home. The office tells her to come in person with photo identification. What is wrong with that?
opciones: Requiring a personal visit is an unreasonable barrier when the patient asked for mail delivery
Requiring photo identification is forbidden, since the rule bars verifying who is asking
Requiring mail delivery is forbidden, since mail is not a readily producible means of transfer
Requiring a visit is allowed only if the office also offers the same records through its portal
preguntas.explicacion: Verification of the requester's identity is required, and the rule leaves its manner to the entity's judgment, but it may not become a barrier or an unreasonable delay. OCR gives this exact example: a doctor may not make someone who wants her record mailed home come to the office to request access and prove identity in person. Mail and e-mail are treated as readily producible by all covered entities.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, SOAP Notes, Objective
preguntas.subtema: SOAP structure · CCMA 5 k174 · CMA III.H.3.a · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA k4 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A patient says her stomach hurts, and the clinician finds tenderness on palpation. Where does each item belong in a SOAP note?
opciones: The reported pain is subjective and the tenderness found on examination is objective
Both belong under objective, since the clinician wrote them down during the same visit
Both belong under subjective, since abdominal complaints cannot be measured directly
The reported pain is objective and the tenderness found on examination is subjective
preguntas.explicacion: A common documentation mistake is blurring symptoms and signs. Symptoms are what the patient describes and go under subjective; signs are the objective findings related to the reported symptom and go under objective. The article uses this very pair as its illustration: a report of stomach pain against tenderness found on palpation.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Patient Data Verification
preguntas.subtema: Revenue cycle · CMA III.G.3.a (2027 III.G.3.a) · CMAA 6 k81 · CCMA 5 k181 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A claim sits unpaid for weeks and the payer finally reports that the member cannot be matched. The patient's surname was mistyped at registration. Which phase of the revenue cycle should have caught it?
opciones: Patient data verification, which checks the name, age, eligibility and billing address
Charge capture, which assembles the documented visit, the services and the facility fees
Claim scrubbing, which searches the outgoing claim for coding and formatting errors
Remittance processing, which posts the payment and sorts the contractual write-offs
preguntas.explicacion: Verification is the phase whose whole job is to keep claims from being rejected, delayed or denied, and the data it checks are the full name, the age, insurance eligibility, the billing address and, above all, preauthorizations. Insurers have been known to let a claim languish over a misspelled name rather than report the failed match. Charge capture, scrubbing and posting all happen later and none of them compares the patient's identity against the plan.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Nervous System: The Central Nervous System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(3) (2027 I.C.6.f(3)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which structures form the central nervous system, and which form the peripheral nervous system?
opciones: Brain and spinal cord centrally; the nerves branching from them peripherally
Brain and cranial nerves centrally; the spinal cord and its nerves peripherally
Spinal cord and ganglia centrally; the brain and its coverings peripherally
Brain and meninges centrally; the spinal cord and the ganglia peripherally
preguntas.explicacion: The central nervous system is the brain and the spinal cord, both inside the dorsal body cavity and both wrapped in bone, meninges and cerebrospinal fluid. The peripheral system is everything that branches out from them, and it forms the communication network between the center and the rest of the body.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Malpractice", Introduction and Negligence or breach of duty
preguntas.subtema: Standard of care · CPT D1 1D · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7A k221 · CMA II.E.4.b · RMA I.C.1.c · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k31
preguntas.pregunta: How is the standard of care defined when negligence is alleged?
opciones: The care a similarly trained peer in the same community would reasonably give
The care described in the facility's written policies, as approved by its governing body
The best care available anywhere in the country at the time of the event
The care the patient expected when consenting, as recorded on the consent form
preguntas.explicacion: Negligence is measured against the standard of care, which the law describes as what a reasonable physician in that community, holding comparable training and experience, would have done for this patient. Perfection is not the yardstick, and some states use the term gross negligence instead. Malpractice is care that falls short of what a colleague in the same post, with the same credentials, would have given, with injury resulting. Written policies and a patient's expectations may serve as evidence, but the legal measure is the reasonable, similarly trained clinician.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Telehealth
preguntas.subtema: Virtual check-ins · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.2.a · CMAA 4B k54 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient describes a brief real-time exchange with her doctor that lasted under ten minutes. What is that called?
opciones: A virtual check-in
An online e-visit
A monitoring session
A telephone triage call
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare describes several ways of using telehealth. E-visits are exchanges that are not face to face and that usually run through an online patient portal. Virtual check-ins are short live exchanges, generally ten minutes or less. Both sit alongside the fuller telehealth visits that stand in for services normally given in person, such as office visits and psychotherapy.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Hospice care: Coverage details and Costs
preguntas.subtema: Hospice in a facility · CCMA 4D k165 · CMAA 2H k30
preguntas.pregunta: A patient living in a nursing home elects hospice. What should the family be told about room and board?
opciones: Medicare does not cover it, so the family may still have to pay the facility
Medicare covers it in full once the hospice election statement is signed
Medicare covers it only during the first two 90-day benefit periods of care
Medicare covers it whenever the nursing home also accepts Medicare assignment
preguntas.explicacion: Room and board is not covered when hospice care is given at home, in a nursing home or in a hospice inpatient facility, so a person living in a facility may still owe that cost. If the hospice team decides short-term inpatient or respite care is needed and arranges it, Medicare pays for the stay. A stay the team did not arrange can leave the patient owing the whole bill.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Billing: CMS-1500 & 837P (MLN006976), Coding
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · CMA III.G.1.b · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which code set is used to report the patient's diagnosis on a claim?
opciones: ICD-10-CM, the clinical modification used for diagnostic information
ICD-10-PCS, the procedure system used for inpatient facility claims
HCPCS Level II, the system used for supplies, equipment and ambulance
The national drug codes, used for the drugs and biologics dispensed
preguntas.explicacion: Diagnostic information is coded with ICD-10-CM, the clinical modification maintained on the CDC side. The procedure coding system, ICD-10-PCS, is used for procedures on inpatient facility claims under Part A. HCPCS Level II names products, supplies, ambulance services and equipment, and national drug codes identify drugs and biologics, so none of the three carries the diagnosis.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has two conditions whose codes carry an Excludes1 note, and the two look unrelated to each other. What do the guidelines allow?
opciones: Reporting both, and querying where the link is unclear
Reporting neither, until the provider rewrites the note
Reporting only the code above the note, in every case
Reporting both, with the excluded code sequenced first
preguntas.explicacion: An Excludes1 note normally means the excluded code is never used at the same time as the code it sits under, because the two conditions cannot occur together. The exception is where the two are unrelated in that patient, and then both may be reported. Where it is not clear whether they are related, the provider is queried.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) General Information
preguntas.subtema: Procedural coding · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · CMA III.G.1.c · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: An office needs to bill for a wheelchair supplied to a patient at home. Which code set covers that item?
opciones: HCPCS Level II, which names durable medical equipment and similar supplies
HCPCS Level I, which names the professional services physicians perform
ICD-10-PCS, which names procedures reported on inpatient facility claims
The code on dental procedures, which names items dispensed to patients
preguntas.explicacion: HCPCS Level II exists precisely because insurers cover services, supplies and equipment that Level I codes do not identify: it names products, supplies, ambulance services, and the durable medical equipment, the prosthetics, the orthotics and the supplies used outside a physician's office. Level I is where procedures in medicine and professional services live, and dental nomenclature covers dental services.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Medicare Advantage Plan (Part C) costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74, 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient weighing a Medicare Advantage Plan against Original Medicare asks which one caps what she can spend in a year.
opciones: The plan does, through a yearly limit after which it pays all covered services
The plan does not, and neither does Original Medicare without extra coverage
Original Medicare does, through the deductible she pays once each calendar year
Neither does, since a yearly limit belongs to Medigap policies alone
preguntas.explicacion: Original Medicare sets no yearly limit on what a person pays out of pocket unless she adds supplemental coverage such as a Medigap policy or joins a Medicare Advantage Plan. Advantage plans carry an out-of-pocket limit that varies by plan; once it is reached the plan pays the whole cost of covered services for the rest of the calendar year.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Conflict Management", Function: Types of Conflict in Healthcare
preguntas.subtema: Conflict management · CCMA 6J k209 · CMAA 2B k26
preguntas.pregunta: Two departments argue over which of them should admit a patient. Which type of conflict is that?
opciones: Intergroup conflict
Intragroup conflict
Interpersonal conflict
Organizational conflict
preguntas.explicacion: Intergroup conflict is disagreement between departments, teams or professional groups, and a dispute between intensive care and surgery over admission criteria is the example used. Intragroup conflict stays inside one unit, interpersonal conflict is between two individuals, and organizational conflict is structural, about policy, pay, staffing or governance.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Specific Techniques
preguntas.subtema: Adapting communication · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17
preguntas.pregunta: For which patients can eye contact and sitting close be destabilizing?
opciones: Patients with a psychotic disorder or with paranoia
Patients with hearing loss who are reading your lips
Patients with expressive aphasia after a recent stroke
Patients with low vision who cannot make out the room
preguntas.explicacion: The table of techniques carries a warning: for some people, those with paranoia and those with psychotic disorders among them, eye contact and sitting close can destabilize, and where staff safety is uncertain the advice is to sit at a safe distance without leaving the patient feeling isolated. Hearing loss calls for the opposite, facing the patient directly.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: An intake form is marked NKDA. What has the patient reported?
opciones: The patient has no known drug allergies
The patient has no known dietary allergy
The patient has no known kidney disease
The patient has no known cardiac history
preguntas.explicacion: NKDA means no known drug allergies, and it belongs on the intake form before any medication is given. It records the absence of a known allergy, not the absence of any reaction ever, so a new reaction is still possible and the entry has to be checked at every visit.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), Collecting Patient Payment
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice and refunds · CMAA 5 k77, 6D · CCMA 5 k186
preguntas.pregunta: An advance written notice was signed, the patient paid, and Medicare later paid the claim after all. What must the provider do?
opciones: Refund the patient within 30 days of receiving the remittance advice for that claim
Refund the patient within 90 days of receiving the remittance advice for that claim
Keep the payment, since the signed notice made the patient liable for the charge
Credit the amount to the patient's account for future services at the practice
preguntas.explicacion: After a properly issued notice the provider may seek payment from the patient, but if Medicare pays all or part of the claim and the patient has also paid, the refund must be timely: within 30 days of getting the remittance advice, or within 15 days of an appeal determination when one was filed. A signed notice does not entitle the provider to keep both payments.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 4: Communicate Clearly
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k160 education methods · CMA F.3.a · 2027 F.1.h · CMAA 2G · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant has a long list of instructions to give. How much should be covered in one visit?
opciones: Between one and three need-to-know or need-to-do points, each repeated
One to three need-to-know points, each mentioned exactly one time
Five to seven need-to-know points, prioritized by the assistant beforehand
Everything on the list, since leaving items out risks a safety problem
preguntas.explicacion: Content is limited so the patient is not swamped: what needs discussing is prioritized with her, held to between one and three points she needs to know or to do, and each of those is emphasized more than once. Repetition is part of the technique, not padding, because most of what is said in a visit is forgotten right away.

preguntas.fuente: NAIC, Coordination of Benefits Model Regulation (Model 120), Order of Benefit Determination Rules and Definitions
preguntas.subtema: Insurance rules · CMAA 5B k75 · CCMA 5E k182
preguntas.pregunta: A child's parents are divorced with no court decree about health care expenses. Which plan does the model rule place first?
opciones: The plan covering the custodial parent, then that parent's spouse
The plan covering the non-custodial parent, then that parent's spouse
The plan of the parent with the earlier birthday within the calendar year
The plan that has covered the child for the longer period of time
preguntas.explicacion: Without a decree allocating responsibility, the order runs through four plans: the one covering the custodial parent, then the one covering that parent's spouse, then the non-custodial parent's plan, and last the plan of the non-custodial parent's spouse. The custodial parent is the one given custody by a court or, absent a decree, the one the child lives with more than half the year.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, HETS EDI: How to Enroll
preguntas.subtema: Eligibility verification · CMA III.G.3.a (2027 III.G.3.a) · CMAA 4 k58 · CCMA 5E · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A clearinghouse sends an electronic eligibility request for a provider who has no active enrollment in the Medicare eligibility system. What happens to it?
opciones: It is rejected, because every identifier submitted needs an enrollment on file
It is answered, because the clearinghouse's own enrollment covers its providers
It is held back until the provider's enrollment has been approved by a contractor
It is answered, because enrollment matters only when claims are being submitted
preguntas.explicacion: Since 11 May 2026 every National Provider Identifier a vendor or clearinghouse submits needs an active eligibility enrollment on file, and without one the eligibility request is rejected. The vendor's identifier does not stand in for the provider's: each provider has to read and acknowledge the rules of behavior and name its relationship with the vendor, and vendors are told not to enroll providers themselves.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", AR more than 90 days
preguntas.subtema: Aging of accounts · CMA III.G.9.b (exam through June 2027) · CMAA 6 k86 · CCMA 5 k187
preguntas.pregunta: A quarter of a practice's receivables are older than ninety days. Which remedies does the guidance name for exactly that problem?
opciones: Tracking at twenty-one days and getting missing documents in within forty-eight hours
Tracking at ninety days and getting missing documents in within thirty days of a denial
Tracking at sixty days and holding every claim until the whole record has been signed
Tracking at thirty days and rebilling each unpaid claim once a month from then on
preguntas.explicacion: Receivables past ninety days come from errors in claim submission, from appeals that are slow or never filed, and from the insurer processing late; the benchmark is that under fifteen percent of accounts should be sitting there. The remedies listed are tracking on a twenty-one-day cycle, spotting missing documents early and getting them in within forty-eight hours, and working denials at once, the incomplete material behind them included.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.6 Anatomical Terminology, Body Planes; and SEER Training Modules, Anatomical Terminology, Planes of the Body
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k13 · CMA I.C.6.f (2027 I.C.6.e) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k11 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A scan is cut horizontally, dividing the body into an upper and a lower portion. Which plane was used?
opciones: The transverse plane, also called the axial plane
The frontal plane, also called the coronal plane
The sagittal plane, also called the lateral plane
The oblique plane, which meets the body at an angle
preguntas.explicacion: The transverse or axial plane is the horizontal one, and it separates upper from lower; the images it produces are called cross sections. The frontal or coronal plane runs from side to side and separates front from back, the sagittal runs from front to back and separates right from left, and an oblique plane cuts at an angle to all three.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Poisoning first aid", Poison Control
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.h · 2027 I.B.8.h · RMA III.I.1.b · CMAA 3 k45
preguntas.pregunta: Which number reaches poison control from anywhere in the United States?
opciones: The national toll-free Poison Help line, 1-800-222-1222
The state health department line printed on the label
The manufacturer's hotline printed on the product container
The nearest hospital switchboard, which routes the call on
preguntas.explicacion: One national toll-free line, 1-800-222-1222, reaches the local poison control center from anywhere in the country, free and confidential, 24 hours a day and 7 days a week, and it takes questions that are not emergencies as well. If the patient is taken to the hospital, the container of the substance goes along.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: TRICARE; and VA, .gov: CHAMPVA benefits
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.d / 2027 III.G.4 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Who is covered by TRICARE?
opciones: Uniformed services members, serving or retired, together with their families
Veterans with a service-connected disability rated permanent and total
Civilian employees of the Department of Defense and their dependents
Members of the National Guard only while they are not on active orders
preguntas.explicacion: TRICARE covers uniformed services members, serving or retired, and their families, as their health care program. Cover tied to a veteran rated permanently and totally disabled by a service-connected condition, or to that veteran's survivors, belongs instead to the Department of Veterans Affairs program, and being eligible for TRICARE actually rules that program out. Civilian federal employees have a health benefits program of their own.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fighting Identity Theft with the Red Flags Rule: FAQs
preguntas.subtema: Identity theft program · CMAA 4C · CCMA 5F k190 · CMA III.H.2.b · RMA II.B.1 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A small practice decides its risk of identity theft is low but agrees that it does hold covered accounts. What does the Rule still require of it?
opciones: A written program, approved by its board or by an appropriate senior employee
A written program, filed with the Commission before the practice may rely on it
A written program, reviewed each year by the insurer that carries its liability cover
No written program, since the Rule reaches only businesses that face a high risk
preguntas.explicacion: The Rule is deliberately flexible: a business facing a high risk of identity theft may need a comprehensive program while one facing a low risk may need only a streamlined one, and where the risk is low the program might focus on how to respond when someone reports that an identity was misused. Even a low-risk business needs a written program approved at that level.

preguntas.subtema: PSDA · CCMA 7D k217 · CMA E.8.d / 2027 E.7.c · NCMA 4.2 · CMAA 3D k32
preguntas.pregunta: Under the Patient Self-Determination Act rules, what must a Medicare hospital do when an adult is admitted?
opciones: Give written information on the right to accept or refuse treatment
Give the patient a state advance directive form already filled out
Give the patient's family a copy of any directive within 90 days
Give the admitting physician a signed directive before care starts
preguntas.explicacion: Providers that take Medicare or Medicaid must hand adult patients written information about their rights under state law to decide about their own care, the right to refuse or accept treatment included, and to draw up an advance directive, plus the provider's own written policies on honoring one. A hospital does that at admission. The 90 days is the deadline for circulating updates when state law changes.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Interview Techniques", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Questioning techniques · CCMA 6C k200 · CMAA 2A k15 · CMA F.5.b / 2027 F.3.b
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant sits down to take a new patient history. How should open-ended and closed-ended questions be sequenced?
opciones: Open questions first, then closed ones for the details
Closed questions first, then open ones for the feelings
Closed questions only, so the visit stays on schedule
Open questions only, since closed ones feel like a test
preguntas.explicacion: Begin with open-ended questions and let the account flow before moving to closed-ended questioning. Focused yes-or-no questions gather detail efficiently, but a very high number of them makes the person feel interrogated and costs rapport. Having no open questions at all is itself a listed interview mistake.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), MSP Provision Exceptions
preguntas.subtema: Patient financial responsibility · CMA III.G.6 (2027 III.G.6.b) · CMAA 5C · CCMA 5 k182
preguntas.pregunta: A patient whose employer plan pays before Medicare offers to hand over her coinsurance at check-in. What should the office do?
opciones: Decline it, because a participating provider may not take that money in this case
Take it and post it, then refund her share once the primary payer has paid
Take it and leave it unapplied until the primary payer's remittance has arrived
Decline it, because coinsurance is never collected before the visit takes place
preguntas.explicacion: There are no exceptions to the Medicare Secondary Payer provisions. Federal law forbids accepting a patient's payment on admission when another insurer is primary, and participating providers must not take a copayment, coinsurance or any other payment while an employer group plan or an employer managed care plan pays first. The remittance advice later shows what may be collected, and money already taken has to be given back.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Eligibility, Financial Eligibility
preguntas.subtema: Financial eligibility · CMA III.G.4.c (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 6 k83 · CCMA 5E k178 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A patient applying for Medicaid worries that the savings in her bank account will disqualify her. What do the MAGI rules do?
opciones: They weigh taxable income and tax relationships, and allow no asset or resource test
They weigh income and assets, with each state setting its own limit on resources
They weigh assets alone, because income is verified through the Marketplace instead
They weigh income after disregards that vary by state and by eligibility group
preguntas.explicacion: The MAGI-based method looks at taxable income and at tax filing relationships in order to settle financial eligibility. It replaced the older calculation inherited from the AFDC program, and it deliberately allows neither income disregards varying by state or by eligibility group nor any test of assets or resources.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 3, 3.2 Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity
preguntas.subtema: Gender identity and pronouns · CCMA 6A k194 · CMAA 2C k18
preguntas.pregunta: Which term names a person's outward demonstration of gender, such as dress or hairstyle?
opciones: Gender expression, shown in dress, hair and mannerisms
Gender identity, the inner sense of being a man or a woman
Sexual orientation, the physical and emotional interest
Cisgender, an identity matching the sex assigned at birth
preguntas.explicacion: Gender expression is the outward demonstration of gender against societal norms — style of dress, hairstyle, mannerisms. Gender identity is the inner sensibility of being a man, a woman or perhaps neither, sexual orientation is interest or desire for others, and cisgender describes identity matching the sex assigned at birth.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Interview Techniques", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Questioning techniques · CCMA 6C k200 · CMA F.5.b / 2027 F.3.b · CMAA 2A k15
preguntas.pregunta: What is the cost of leaning on too many focused, yes-or-no questions?
opciones: The patient can feel interrogated and rapport is lost
The interview runs longer than an open-ended one does
The answers cannot be entered into the medical record
The patient gives the answer the office expects to hear
preguntas.explicacion: Focused questions are efficient for details, but too many of them is listed among the common interview mistakes: the person feels interrogated and the interviewer loses rapport. Mixing them with open questions is what keeps the encounter productive. Focused questions shorten the interview rather than lengthen it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Conflict Management", Function: Types of Conflict in Healthcare
preguntas.subtema: Conflict management · CCMA 6J k209 · CMAA 2B k26
preguntas.pregunta: Which category of conflict is reported most often in hospital settings?
opciones: Interpersonal conflict, including disputes with patients
Organizational conflict over policy, pay and staffing
Intergroup conflict between departments and professions
Intrapersonal conflict between a person's competing goals
preguntas.explicacion: Interpersonal conflict, the category covering disputes between clinicians, between a clinician and a nurse, and between a clinician and a patient, is the one hospitals report most often. Organizational conflicts usually surface as collective grievances, intergroup conflicts sit between services, and intrapersonal conflict never leaves the person who has it.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Billing: CMS-1500 & 837P (MLN006976), ASCA Exceptions
preguntas.subtema: Claim submission · CMA III.G.3.b(1) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6C k87, 6 k85 · CCMA 5L k185
preguntas.pregunta: Which practice may send Medicare a claim on paper without having to ask for a waiver first?
opciones: One with fewer than ten full-time equivalent employees
One with fewer than twenty full-time equivalent employees
One with fewer than fifty full-time equivalent employees
One that files fewer than ten Medicare claims each month
preguntas.explicacion: The exceptions that let a professional or supplier bill Medicare on paper include having fewer than ten full-time equivalent employees, roster billing for mass immunization, paper claims under a demonstration project, and secondary payer claims with more than one primary payer. Meeting an exception excuses the practice from any waiver request. The practice that files under ten claims a month is on the separate list of unusual circumstance waivers, which do have to be requested.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Malpractice", Issues of Concern: Referrals
preguntas.subtema: Legal doctrines · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.c(3) · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3A k31
preguntas.pregunta: A physician assistant working under a physician's license is sued over care given in the office. Which doctrine pulls the physician into the case?
opciones: Respondeat superior
Res ipsa loquitur
Proximate causation
Standard of care
preguntas.explicacion: Midlevel providers are an integral part of medicine but practice under a physician's license, and the physician answers for the care they deliver. When a suit comes, the plaintiff aims at the supervising physician under respondeat superior. Causation and the standard of care are elements the plaintiff must prove, not the doctrine that reaches the supervisor.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fighting Identity Theft with the Red Flags Rule: Identify Relevant Red Flags
preguntas.subtema: Registration red flags · CMAA 4C · CCMA 5F k190 · CMA III.H.2.b · RMA II.B.1 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A new patient registering by telephone gives an address that does not match the one on the report the office pulled. Under the Red Flags Rule, what is that?
opciones: A red flag among personal identifying information, which the program must answer
A covered account, because the practice will bill him after the service is given
A creditor test, since the office is deciding whether to let him pay in instalments
A reportable breach, since his information may already have been misused by someone
preguntas.explicacion: Red flags are the patterns, practices or activities that point to possible identity theft, and the categories to consider include alerts from a credit reporting company, suspicious documents such as identification that looks altered, and personal identifying information that does not hold together, with an address that fails to match the credit report given as the first example.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Part B (Medical Insurance) costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74, 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: What does a patient with Original Medicare pay each month, and what does she pay before Part B starts to pay, in 2026?
opciones: A premium of $202.90 a month, and a deductible of $283 once each year
A premium of $202.90 a month, and a deductible of $1,736 for each benefit period
A premium of $311 a month, and a deductible of $283 once during each year
No premium for most people, and a deductible of $434 once during each year
preguntas.explicacion: The Part B premium in 2026 is $202.90 a month, higher for some incomes, and it is owed every month whether or not any covered service is used. The Part B deductible is $283 and is paid once a year. The $1,736 figure is the Part A deductible, which is owed for each hospital benefit period rather than once a year.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Medicare and Medicaid Accreditation and Deemed Status: Definitions
preguntas.subtema: Compliance with regulators · CMAA 3A k42
preguntas.pregunta: What happens to a facility that has neither accreditation nor deemed status but wants to join Medicare?
opciones: A separate survey by CMS is mandatory before it can take part
A state fire inspection replaces the survey and settles the matter
It may take part for one year while it applies for accreditation
It may take part if a hospital in its system holds deemed status
preguntas.explicacion: For a facility lacking accreditation or deemed status, a separate survey by the agency is mandatory before it may take part in Medicare and Medicaid. That survey looks at how the facility follows the criteria on patient care, safety, the physical environment and administration, among other areas. Accreditation stays voluntary but is required for participation.

preguntas.fuente: AAMA, Medical Assisting Creed
preguntas.subtema: Codes of ethics · CCMA 7C · CMA E.7 / 2027 E.6 · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: What is the Medical Assisting Creed of the AAMA?
opciones: A set of statements of belief, including protecting confidences entrusted
A set of enforceable rules whose breach is grounds for losing the credential
A list of the tasks a medical assistant may perform without supervision
A summary of the disciplinary sanctions the certifying board may impose
preguntas.explicacion: The creed is a series of statements of belief rather than a rulebook: belief in the profession's principles and purposes, striving to be more effective, aspiring to render greater service, protecting confidences entrusted, dedication to the care and well-being of all people, loyalty to the employer, faithfulness to professional ethics, and being strengthened by courage, by compassion and by faith.

preguntas.subtema: Culpability terms · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.3 · CMAA 3B k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: How does the enforcement regulation define willful neglect?
opciones: Reckless indifference toward the duty to comply, or a conscious and intentional failure
An act or omission the entity would have caught by exercising reasonable diligence
The business care and prudence expected of someone trying to satisfy a legal requirement
Any violation that the entity failed to correct inside the thirty day period allowed
preguntas.explicacion: The enforcement subpart lines up three defined terms. Willful neglect is reckless indifference toward the duty to comply, or a failure to comply that is conscious and intentional. Reasonable cause is an act or omission the entity knew of, or would have known of with reasonable diligence, that nonetheless falls short of willful neglect. Reasonable diligence itself is the business care and prudence expected in similar circumstances.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare Advantage Plans (Part C); and Parts of Medicare
preguntas.subtema: Insurance types · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Besides a Medicare Advantage plan, which of these delivers Part A and Part B benefits through a private plan?
opciones: PACE, the Program of All-inclusive Care for elderly people
A Medigap policy sold by a private insurance company
A stand-alone Medicare drug plan approved by Medicare
A state Medicaid program covering dual eligible people
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare health plans deliver Part A and Part B benefits and generally come from private companies under contract with Medicare. Besides Medicare Advantage they take in Medicare Cost Plans, demonstrations and pilots, and PACE, the Program of All-inclusive Care for elderly people. Medigap helps pay the patient's share of costs in Original Medicare rather than delivering the benefits, a drug plan covers Part D, and Medicaid is a joint federal-state program.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Workplace Violence", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Difficult situations · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k16
preguntas.pregunta: Which set of behaviors is given as psychological workplace violence?
opciones: Sexual harassment, bullying and intimidation of a coworker
Shouting, swearing and threatening language toward staff
Pushing, grabbing and striking a member of the staff
Theft and other criminal acts committed on the premises
preguntas.explicacion: One way of sorting workplace violence is by the nature of the aggression: physical, verbal or psychological. Harassment, bullying and intimidation are the examples given for the psychological form. Shouting and threats fall under verbal abuse, which is the most common form of all; hitting is physical; theft belongs to the criminal type I.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Workplace Violence", Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: De-escalation · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k26 · NCMA EKB 22 · CMA F.1.f / 2027 F.1.f
preguntas.pregunta: A man raises his voice at the front desk because he has waited an hour. What is the trained response?
opciones: Listen, acknowledge the concern, then guide him to a goal
Tell him the wait is exactly the same for everyone there
Ask him to step outside and return once he has calmed
Recite the office policy on wait times before he says more
preguntas.explicacion: Risk drops when patients are approached calmly and staff make an effort to connect. The trained sequence is to listen to the person, to acknowledge what worries him, and to steer him respectfully toward a goal, repeated as often as it takes. Openings to defuse, such as moving him into an open room sooner, are taken as they appear.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Common Pitfalls
preguntas.subtema: Nontherapeutic responses · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2E k21
preguntas.pregunta: An interviewer needs to move to a different topic in the middle of a visit. What keeps that from feeling dismissive?
opciones: Asking permission with a transition phrase before the change
Waiting until the patient has run out of things to say first
Summarizing the encounter and ending the interview right there
Providing the rationale for every question asked from then on
preguntas.explicacion: Changing the subject abruptly can be perceived as dismissive; the suggested repair is a transition phrase that asks whether it is all right to move on to another topic. Summarizing does close an interview, and providing rationale explains why information is being gathered, but neither one solves an abrupt turn.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule, Media Notice
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics · CMAA 3E k44 security breach · CCMA 7F reportable incidents
preguntas.pregunta: When must a breach involving unsecured protected health information also be reported to prominent media outlets?
opciones: When it affects more than 500 residents of one state or jurisdiction
When it affects 500 or more individuals anywhere in the whole country
When it affects more than 500 residents of one hospital's service area
When it affects any number of residents, if the information was unencrypted
preguntas.explicacion: Media notice is triggered by geography, not by a national tally: where more than 500 residents of one state or jurisdiction are affected, the breach must also be announced to prominent media serving that area, usually by press release, on the same 60-day clock and with the same content as the individual notice. The separate threshold of 500 or more individuals governs how fast the Secretary is told.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Nonverbal Communication
preguntas.subtema: Nonverbal cues · CCMA 6C k197 · CMAA 2C k14 · CMA F.1.d / 2027 F.1.e · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: One well-known account splits a message into 55, 38 and 7 percent. What does the 38 percent stand for?
opciones: The tone of voice the sender uses
The actual words the sender speaks
The body language the sender shows
The pace at which the two people talk
preguntas.explicacion: In that account body language carries 55 percent, tone of voice 38 percent, and the spoken words only 7 percent. A separate figure often taught is that 80 percent of communication is nonverbal. Pace of the conversation belongs to nonverbal signals but has no percentage attached.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Implementation and Challenges
preguntas.subtema: Measuring access · CMAA 4A k49 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Same-day slots are now available and the manager wants to know whether the change is holding. Which measure does the guide name?
opciones: Appointment availability checked daily, such as the third next available appointment
The number of visits each clinician completed daily, compared with the year before
The count of appointments booked in past months, which shows how demand has moved
The share of calls the front desk answers before the telephone rings a third time
preguntas.explicacion: Once same-day appointments are possible, the practice is told to gauge whether the change works by tracking, day by day, how available appointments are; the example given is the third next available appointment. Counting appointments already held will not serve: the guide warns that the number of visits completed reflects the supply of clinical time more than the demand for it.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Personal Space
preguntas.subtema: Personal space · CCMA 6C k197 · CMAA 2I k24 · RMA I.D.1.c
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant leans in about two feet from a seated patient to check a dressing. Which space zone has been entered?
opciones: The personal zone, the space usually kept for friends and family
The social zone, the one used in social and business exchanges
The public zone, which generally keeps any physical contact out
The zone under eighteen inches, kept for close relationships
preguntas.explicacion: Proxemics puts the personal zone at eighteen inches to four feet, the social zone at four to ten feet, and the public zone beyond ten feet. Staff normally talk with patients in the social zone to hold professional boundaries, but assessing and doing procedures moves them into the personal zone, where the patient may feel psychological discomfort.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Abandonment, Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Inadvertent abandonment · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.4.d(2) · RMA I.C.1.c · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: A physician leaves on a three-month sabbatical without telling patients or arranging emergency coverage. How is that treated?
opciones: As inadvertent abandonment, since care stopped with no notice and no substitute clinician
As intentional abandonment, since an absence of that length is planned months beforehand
As no abandonment, because nobody was ever told the relationship had come to an end
As an ending chosen by the patients, who were free to find another clinician meanwhile
preguntas.explicacion: Liability for abandonment does not depend on intending to end the relationship. The example given is precisely this one: a healthcare professional who neither notifies patients nor sets up emergency coverage before a long vacation or sabbatical has abandoned them inadvertently. Leaving a patient's calls or e-mails unanswered, and failing to follow up after surgery or after a new medication is started, are treated the same way.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.530(j)(1) and (j)(2), Documentation and retention period
preguntas.subtema: HIPAA documentation retention · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k219 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.4 · CMAA 3B k39
preguntas.pregunta: How long must a covered entity retain its HIPAA policies, procedures and other required documentation?
opciones: Six years from creation or last effective date, whichever is later
Three years from creation, matching OSHA training records
Thirty years, matching OSHA employee medical records
Ten years from creation, matching the period for Medicare claims documentation
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.530(j) requires policies and procedures to be kept in written or electronic form, together with every communication the rule requires in writing and every action, activity or designation it requires to be documented, for six years from the date of creation or the date it was last in effect, whichever is later. The same section requires a privacy official, a complaints contact, workforce training, safeguards, a complaint process, sanctions, mitigation and no retaliation. Three and thirty years are OSHA periods, not HIPAA ones.

preguntas.fuente: USPS, Compare Mail Services: Priority Mail Express
preguntas.subtema: Express delivery days · CCMA 5O · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7G k96 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A transplant center needs a package on a Sunday. Which feature of Priority Mail Express answers that need?
opciones: It delivers seven days a week, all year, with limited exceptions to that rule
It delivers on weekdays and adds a Saturday run when the label is bought online
It delivers seven days a week only to post office box addresses in large markets
It delivers on any day agreed with the receiving office when the package is sent
preguntas.explicacion: Express is the fastest domestic service, and it runs on every day of the week and every day of the year, limited exceptions aside. Most addresses see it in one to three days, and that delivery time carries a money-back guarantee, which the two-to-three-day estimate for Priority Mail does not.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Minimum essential coverage; and Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms
preguntas.subtema: Affordable Care Act protections · CMAA 5 k73, 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: Which coverage counts as minimum essential coverage?
opciones: A job-based plan, a Marketplace plan, Medicare, Medicaid or CHIP coverage
A job-based plan or a Marketplace plan, but not a public program coverage
A grandfathered policy bought before March 23, 2010, and no other coverage
Any policy that pays cash benefits toward hospital stays and lost earnings
preguntas.explicacion: Minimum essential coverage is any plan meeting the health care law's coverage requirement; the examples given are job-based plans, Marketplace plans, Medicaid with CHIP, and Medicare, and TRICARE and certain other coverage qualify too. Public programs are therefore included. Grandfathered policies are individual plans bought on or before March 23, 2010, a category of their own, and a cash indemnity policy is not health coverage in this sense.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: Administrative Safeguards
preguntas.subtema: Contingency plan · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: What must a practice's contingency plan under the Security Rule provide for?
opciones: Backing up ePHI, restoring lost data and running critical processes in emergency mode
Buying a second electronic health record from a different vendor as a permanent standby
Printing the whole record of every active patient at the close of each business day
Notifying the Secretary of any system failure that lasts longer than a single work shift
preguntas.explicacion: The contingency plan is the administrative safeguard for responding to emergencies or other events that damage the systems holding ePHI. It has to include plans for backing the information up, restoring whatever is lost, and continuing the critical business processes that protect the security of ePHI while the entity operates in emergency mode.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), Gathering Accurate Data
preguntas.subtema: CMS documentation requirements · CMAA 6 k85 · CCMA 5J k180
preguntas.pregunta: How long must a provider keep the patient's answers to the Medicare Secondary Payer questions?
opciones: 10 years after the date of service, on paper or stored electronically
5 years after the date of service, on paper or stored electronically
Only until the claim is paid, since the answers live on the claim itself
7 years, but only when the answers show another payer is primary
preguntas.explicacion: Responses to the secondary payer questions, along with other information gathered, must be kept for 10 years after the date of service, in hard copy or electronically, and both positive and negative answers are kept. Five years is the retention period for a signed advance beneficiary notice, and Medicare enrollment records carry a 7-year rule; neither applies here.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Appeals in Original Medicare
preguntas.subtema: Denials and appeals · CMAA 6E · CCMA 5M
preguntas.pregunta: How long does the Medicare administrative contractor usually take to decide a first-level appeal?
opciones: About 60 days after it receives the appeal, and the result reaches the patient
About 14 days after it receives the appeal, and the result reaches the patient
About 180 days after it receives the appeal, the same time the patient had to file
There is no set time, since the contractor decides appeals in the order received
preguntas.explicacion: The Medicare administrative contractor generally decides within 60 days of receiving the appeal; a favorable decision turns up on the next summary notice, an unfavorable one arrives as a redetermination notice. At level 2 the qualified independent contractor also has 60 days. The 180 days is the patient's filing window, not the contractor's deadline.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Involve appropriate third parties
preguntas.subtema: Third parties in termination · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.c · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: The patient about to be dismissed belongs to a managed care plan the practice contracts with. What step comes before the letter goes out?
opciones: Asking the insurer whether its contract restricts how and when the practice may end care
Asking the insurer to move her to another clinician in the network before she is told
Asking the insurer to extend her benefits thirty days so that care is not interrupted
No step at all, since a contract with a plan has no bearing on ending a clinical relationship
preguntas.explicacion: Where the patient belongs to a managed care organization the clinician participates in, the insurer should be contacted first to find out what restrictions it places on termination. Contracts with third-party payers often limit referrals to clinicians outside that network, and some insurers require thirty days' notice to the insurer as well as to the patient. Government payers are stricter.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A category offers no unspecified code at all. What may stand in for one?
opciones: The other specified code, which then covers both uses
The code for the symptom that brought her to the office
The three-character category, used as though it were a code
The default code printed beside the main term in the index
preguntas.explicacion: Codes titled unspecified are for a record too thin to support a more specific code, while an other or an other specified title takes the detail the classification has no code of its own for. Where a category carries no unspecified code, the other specified code may stand for both. A three-character category is only a code where nothing is subdivided under it.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.530(b), Standard: Training; StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", To Whom Does HIPAA Apply and Training Employees
preguntas.subtema: Workforce training · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33
preguntas.pregunta: Whom must a covered entity train on its privacy policies and procedures?
opciones: All workforce members, as suited to their functions, including new hires
Only clinical staff who document care in the medical record
Only the privacy official and the contact person for complaints
Only paid employees; volunteers and students fall outside the training rule
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.530(b) has every member of the workforce trained on the policies and procedures for privacy, to the degree their own functions make necessary and appropriate: everyone by the compliance date, each new member within a reasonable time of joining, and anyone whose work is touched by a material change in the policies, with the training documented. Clinical guidance applies the rule to interns, volunteers and administrative, food service, clerical and janitorial staff alike, and recommends refreshing it every year.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse: Prevent, Detect, Report (MLN4649244), Accurate Coding & Billing
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.1.a(3), III.G.2 (2027 III.G.1.a(1), III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46, 6A · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: A practice bills an evaluation service the day after surgery, although the global fee for that surgery already covers it. What is that called?
opciones: Unbundling, billing apart for what one fee already covers
Upcoding, billing a level higher than the record supports
Balance billing, charging above what the plan will allow
A contractual adjustment, taken off the account at posting
preguntas.explicacion: CMS lists billing separately for a service already included in a global fee as unbundling, and gives the visit billed the day after surgery as the example. Upcoding is claiming a higher level of service than was provided or documented. Balance billing and contractual adjustments belong to what the patient owes, not to how the service was coded.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Appeal
preguntas.subtema: Denials and appeals · CMAA 6E · CCMA 5M · CMA III.G.5.b / 2027 III.G.3.b
preguntas.pregunta: A commercial plan denies a claim and the patient disagrees with the decision. What right does she have?
opciones: To appeal and have the decision reviewed, including review by a third party
To appeal only if the plan was bought inside the Health Insurance Marketplace
To appeal only after the provider has resubmitted the claim a second time
To have the service repeated at no cost while the plan reviews the decision
preguntas.explicacion: An appeal is a request that the insurer or the Marketplace review a decision denying a benefit or a payment. When a plan refuses to pay a claim or ends coverage, the patient has the right to appeal and to have the decision reviewed by a third party. The right is not limited to Marketplace plans, does not wait on a resubmission, and does not entitle anyone to free repeat care.

preguntas.subtema: Transmission security · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Records are about to be sent to a specialist across an open network. Which technical standard governs that leg of the journey?
opciones: Transmission security, with integrity controls and encryption as its specifications
Integrity, with a mechanism that shows stored information has not been altered
Access control, with unique identifiers and an automatic close of idle sessions
Audit controls, the mechanisms that capture and review activity in the system
preguntas.explicacion: Transmission security is the standard for information traveling over an electronic communications network. Its two addressable specifications are integrity controls, so that what was sent cannot be modified undetected, and encryption where the practice judges it appropriate. The integrity standard next to it looks at information at rest.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Uses and Disclosures for Treatment, Payment, and Health Care Operations
preguntas.subtema: Permitted uses · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA II.E.2.a(5) · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A primary care office faxes a chart to the specialist it is sending the patient to. What permits that disclosure?
opciones: It is a treatment disclosure, and treatment activities need no authorization from the patient
It is a health care operations disclosure, allowed once both offices sign a shared privacy notice
It is a public interest disclosure, allowed because referrals serve the coordination of care
It is an incidental disclosure, allowed because the fax is a by-product of scheduling the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Treatment is defined as providing, coordinating or managing health care, as consultation between providers, and as the referral of a patient from one provider to another. A covered entity may disclose PHI for the treatment activities of any provider, and the example given is a primary care provider sending a record to the specialist who needs it. No authorization is required.

preguntas.subtema: Discharge summary contents · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3.a · RMA II.B.4.a · CMAA 5H · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A patient checking out after an inpatient stay asks what her discharge summary has to cover. Which three things does the medical record condition name?
opciones: The outcome of the stay, the disposition of the case, and the arrangements for follow-up
The outcome of the stay, the final diagnosis, and the itemised charges for the admission
The admitting diagnosis, the disposition of the case, and the medicines given on the ward
The outcome of the stay, the consultants seen, and the deadline for completing the record
preguntas.explicacion: Among the items every record must document is a discharge summary carrying the outcome of the hospitalization, the disposition of the case and the provisions for follow-up care. The admitting diagnosis, the results of consultative evaluations and the final diagnosis completed within thirty days of discharge are separate items on the same list.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Effective Team Event Tools
preguntas.subtema: Teamwork · CCMA 6L k202 · CMAA 2F k21 · CMA F.4.c / 2027 F.2.c · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Halfway through the morning the team stops to re-establish awareness and check the plan still fits. Which team event is that?
opciones: A huddle, an ad hoc meeting to keep care on track
A brief, held before the start to share the plan
A debrief, held afterward to review performance
A call-out, used to broadcast critical information
preguntas.explicacion: A huddle is the ad hoc meeting held to keep care moving toward the goal, to affirm or re-establish awareness of the situation, to reinforce the plan or to judge whether it needs adjusting. A brief comes before the start, to share the plan and assign roles; a debrief comes after, to trade lessons learned.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Benefits of This Model
preguntas.subtema: No-shows and access · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.b · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: What does the improvement guide say happens to missed appointments once a practice can see patients on the day they call?
opciones: They are likely to fall, so clinical time is used better and less staff time goes on them
They are likely to rise, since a patient who called that morning has less time to plan
They stay where they are, since missed visits follow the reminder system, not the wait
They fall for urgent visits only, since routine ones are still booked several weeks ahead
preguntas.explicacion: Among the benefits listed are savings in cost and in efficiency: with long waits gone, no-shows are expected to fall, clinical time gets used better, and less staff time disappears into managing missed appointments and the backlog. The model also handles routine and urgent requests the same way, so nothing sits waiting for weeks.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Hospice Care: Hospice Levels of Care (Continuous Home Care)
preguntas.subtema: Hospice levels of care · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: Which hospice level of care is used during a brief crisis so that the patient can stay at home?
opciones: Continuous home care, which takes 8 hours of skilled care a day, half by a nurse
General inpatient care, used when symptoms cannot be managed in the patient's home
Routine home care, the level given wherever the patient happens to live
Respite care, allowed for no more than five days in a row each occurrence
preguntas.explicacion: Continuous home care is more intense than routine home care and is given during brief periods of crisis, to manage acute symptoms and hold the patient in the home setting. It calls for direct skilled care 8 hours a day, at least half of it delivered by the nurse; intractable pain managed with intravenous medicine is the example given. A nursing home cannot furnish this level.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Special Enrollment Period; and Glossary: Open Enrollment Period
preguntas.subtema: Coverage enrollment · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A caller wants to buy a Marketplace plan in March, outside the yearly enrollment window. When can she enroll?
opciones: When a qualifying life event, such as marriage or a birth, opens a special period
When she agrees to a higher premium for the months already gone by this year
When her employer confirms in writing that it offers her no coverage at all
When the yearly window reopens on November 1 and closes on December 15
preguntas.explicacion: Open enrollment for the Marketplace runs from November 1 to January 15. Outside it, a person may still sign up if a qualifying life event applies, such as getting married, having a baby, moving, or losing other coverage, and the special period usually allows 60 days before or after the event. Back premiums buy nothing, lack of a job offer is not by itself an event, and the December 15 date is not when the yearly window closes.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.520(c)(2), Specific requirements for certain covered health care providers; 164.520(c)(1)(v)(B)
preguntas.subtema: Notice of privacy practices · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33
preguntas.pregunta: A new patient arrives at a clinic that treats patients directly. When must the clinic hand over its notice of privacy practices?
opciones: No later than the first service delivery, with a good-faith effort to obtain acknowledgment
Within 60 days of the first visit, by mail to the patient's home address
Only when the patient asks for it, since posting the notice in the office is sufficient by itself
At the first visit, and the patient must sign it before any care may be provided
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.520(c)(2) has a covered provider that treats patients directly hand over the notice no later than the day of the first service delivery, electronic service included, or as soon as practicable after an emergency; it must then try in good faith to get the patient's written acknowledgment that the notice arrived, and where that fails, document the attempt and the reason; and it must keep the notice available on site and posted prominently. The acknowledgment is sought, never made a condition of care. Sixty days is the window a health plan without a website has to distribute a materially revised notice.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: Risk Analysis and Management
preguntas.subtema: Risk analysis · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which step does the Security Rule expect a practice to take BEFORE deciding which security measures are reasonable for it?
opciones: An accurate and thorough assessment of the risks and vulnerabilities to its ePHI
An encryption project covering every workstation, laptop and portable drive it owns
A signed acknowledgment from each patient that electronic records carry some risk
A written designation of the practice as a hybrid entity with health care components
preguntas.explicacion: The administrative safeguards begin with the security management process, and its first requirement is a risk analysis: assessing, accurately and thoroughly, what could threaten the confidentiality, the integrity and the availability of the ePHI the entity holds, and how exposed it is. Everything else is built on that analysis, because the measures a practice adopts have to be the ones that bring the risks it found down to a reasonable and appropriate level.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.6 Anatomical Terminology, Directional Terms
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k13 · CMA I.C.6.e (2027 I.C.6.d) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k11 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: An intravenous line is documented as sitting proximal to the wrist. Where on the arm is it?
opciones: Nearer the trunk than the wrist, up toward the elbow
Farther from the trunk than the wrist, out toward the fingers
On the palm side of the wrist rather than the back of it
On the thumb side of the wrist rather than the other side
preguntas.explicacion: Proximal describes a position in a limb nearer to the point of attachment or to the trunk, and distal one farther from it: the upper arm is proximal to the forearm, and the part of the leg below the knee is distal to the thigh. Front and back are anterior and posterior, and the two side terms are medial and lateral.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A nosebleed is charted as rhinorrhagia and a runny nose as rhinorrhea. Which contrast between the two endings is correct?
opciones: -rrhage is bleeding, while -rrhea is a flow or discharge
-rrhage is a suture, while -rrhea is a surgical binding
-rrhage is a bursting, while -rrhea is a narrowing or block
-rrhage is a swelling, while -rrhea is a falling or dropping
