preguntas.explicacion: Both endings start the same way and are easy to swap. The pair -rrhage and -rrhagic means bleeding, while -rrhea means a flow or discharge of any kind. A third one, -rrhaphy, is a suture. Narrowing is steno-, and drooping is -ptosis, as in the eyelid that will not stay open.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Team Performance Observation Tool
preguntas.subtema: Escalation · CCMA 6K k210 · CMAA 2B k25
preguntas.pregunta: Which pair of tools is listed for advocating patient safety with assertive statements?
opciones: The Two-Challenge Rule and CUS
The brief and the debrief session
The call-out and the check-back
STEP and the I'M SAFE checklist
preguntas.explicacion: The observation tool lists advocating effectively for patient safety through the assertive statement, the Two-Challenge Rule or CUS, and resolving conflict through the Two-Challenge Rule or DESC. Both the rule and CUS are two-way interactions: how a challenge is received matters as much as how it is raised.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Clean Claims Ratio
preguntas.subtema: Revenue cycle indicators · CMAA 6 k81 · CCMA 5 k181
preguntas.pregunta: A practice reports that 88% of its claims pass all edits without manual work. How does that compare with the benchmark?
opciones: It is below the benchmark of 95% or more, so the causes of the edits need review
It is above the benchmark of 80%, so the current billing workflow needs no change
It matches the benchmark for days in accounts receivable, which is 30 days or less
It matches the benchmark for denial rate, which normally runs between 5% and 10%
preguntas.explicacion: The clean claim rate is the share of claims needing no edits before submission, and the benchmark cited is 95% or higher; lower figures should trigger a look at why claims are being denied or rejected. The 30-day figure is the target for days in receivables outstanding, and the 5% to 10% range describes typical denial rates, so neither describes a percentage of clean claims.

preguntas.subtema: Record service staffing · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.a · CMAA 7A k90 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: Charts routinely take two days to reach the clinicians who ask for them. Which requirement of the medical record condition of participation is at stake?
opciones: Employing enough personnel to complete, file and retrieve records promptly
Keeping every record in its original or legally reproduced form for five years
Using an author identification system that protects the security of the entries
Releasing information from a record only to individuals authorized to have it
preguntas.explicacion: The condition opens on organization and staffing: the medical record service has to be sized to the scope and the complexity of the work, and the hospital has to employ enough personnel for records to be completed, filed and retrieved promptly. The other three duties in the same section deal with form, authorship and confidentiality, not with staffing.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Definition of PHI and HIPAA and Communication With Patients; StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", Questions to Consider
preguntas.subtema: Oral disclosures · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35
preguntas.pregunta: Two phlebotomists discuss a named patient's HIV result in a crowded elevator. Under HIPAA this conversation is which of these?
opciones: A violation: oral disclosure of identifiable health information is PHI
Permitted, since both are workforce members of the same covered entity
Permitted, since spoken information is not covered, only written or electronic
A violation only if a patient's relative happens to be in the elevator
preguntas.explicacion: PHI covers written, paper, spoken and electronic information, and the elevator conversation about an identifiable patient is the very example used to illustrate an oral violation; discussions of patient information do not belong in public places, hallways, cafeterias or shared phone lines. Being workforce members does not help, because the disclosure reaches people not involved in the patient's care and exceeds the minimum necessary. State law may add stricter rules for HIV results, and the violation does not depend on who happens to overhear.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Pre-existing condition
preguntas.subtema: Affordable Care Act protections · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what the Affordable Care Act did about pre-existing conditions.
opciones: Insurers may not refuse to cover the condition or charge the patient more for it
Insurers may cover the condition after a waiting period set by each state law
Insurers may charge more for the condition only inside the Marketplace plans
Insurers must cover the condition when the patient buys a supplemental policy
preguntas.explicacion: A pre-existing condition is a health problem, such as asthma, diabetes or cancer, that the person had before the new coverage started. Under the health care law, insurance companies can neither refuse to cover treatment for it nor charge extra because of it. There is no waiting period left to serve, the protection is not limited to Marketplace plans, and it does not depend on buying anything additional.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Drug plan coverage rules: Quantity limits
preguntas.subtema: Medication authorization · CMA III.G.5.a(2) (2027 III.G.5.a(2)) · CMAA 4G k67 · CCMA 5H k183 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: A drug plan pays for only thirty tablets a month and the prescriber wants a larger dose. What is that rule, and what is the way round it?
opciones: A quantity limit, and the prescriber may ask the plan for an exception on medical grounds
Step therapy, and the patient must first try the cheaper drug that sits on the plan's list
Prior authorization, and the plan has to approve the drug before it will be covered at all
A transition fill, and the plan covers one thirty-day supply while the matter is settled
preguntas.explicacion: Plans may cap how much of a drug they cover over a period, for safety and for cost, and the example given is thirty tablets a month. The patient or the prescriber may contact the plan for an exception where the prescriber believes the limit is not medically appropriate for her condition, for instance because she needs a higher dose.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fighting Identity Theft with the Red Flags Rule
preguntas.subtema: Who must comply · CCMA 5F · CMA III.H.2.b · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 4C k63 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which practice makes a medical office a creditor for purposes of the Red Flags Rule?
opciones: Regularly reporting delinquent patient balances to a credit reporting company
Regularly deferring payment for services or billing patients afterwards
Regularly accepting payment cards at the front desk for the balance due
Regularly submitting claims to a health plan on the patient's behalf
preguntas.explicacion: The test has two steps, and only the second one decides. Billing patients afterwards answers the first step yes, but the guidance answers the professional who bills at the end of the month plainly: deferring payment on its own is not enough. The second step asks whether the office regularly uses consumer reports in a credit transaction, gives information to credit reporting companies, or advances funds to be repaid; reporting delinquent balances is that second kind, so it is what makes the office a creditor. Taking payment cards does not make anyone a creditor either, and billing a health plan is not credit extended to the patient.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), Table 1
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMAA 5 k77 · CCMA 5 k186 · CMA III.G.3.c
preguntas.pregunta: When must a provider give a Medicare fee-for-service patient an Advance Beneficiary Notice of Non-coverage?
opciones: When a payment denial is expected and the financial liability would pass to the patient
When a payment denial is expected and the service is one Medicare never covers at all
When the patient asks for a written estimate of the charges before a scheduled service
When the patient is enrolled in a Medicare Advantage plan with a network restriction
preguntas.explicacion: The ABN, form CMS-R-131, goes out from fee-for-service providers and suppliers when they expect Medicare to refuse payment and want liability shifted to the patient, typically because what is proposed is custodial care or is neither reasonable nor necessary. For services Medicare never covers no notice is required, though a voluntary one may be given as a courtesy. It is not used for Part C or Part D care.

preguntas.subtema: Visitor control · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A drug representative signs in at the desk and is escorted to the back office. Which physical safeguard specification covers that arrangement?
opciones: Access control and validation, which ties entry to a person's role and covers visitors
Workstation security, which restricts the machines that reach records to their users
Facility security plan, which protects the building and its equipment from intrusion
Contingency operations, which open the facility so lost information can be restored
preguntas.explicacion: Facility access controls carry a specification for procedures that control and validate a person's entry by role or function, and visitor control is named inside it, together with controlling who may reach software programs in order to test or revise them.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule, Documentation and Record Retention
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics · CMAA 3B k39 storage and retention · CCMA 7E k219
preguntas.pregunta: How long must a covered entity keep its privacy policies, its privacy notices and the record of how complaints were resolved?
opciones: Six years from creation or from the last date the document was in effect, whichever is later
Two years from creation or from the last date the document was in effect, whichever is later
Ten years from creation or from the last date the document was in effect, whichever is later
Six years from creation, with no account taken of when the document stopped being in effect
preguntas.explicacion: The documentation clock runs six years, counted from the later of the date a document was created or the last date it was in effect, and it covers privacy policies and procedures, the privacy practices notices, the disposition of complaints, and the other actions and designations the rule requires to be documented. Two years is the CLIA floor for laboratory records, which is a separate obligation.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Introduction to the Endocrine System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(9) (2027 I.C.6.f(9)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: What distinguishes an endocrine gland from an exocrine gland?
opciones: An endocrine gland has no duct and releases hormones into the blood
An endocrine gland has a duct and releases hormones into the blood
An endocrine gland has no duct and releases enzymes onto a surface
An endocrine gland has a duct and releases enzymes onto a surface
preguntas.explicacion: Exocrine glands have ducts that carry their product to a surface, which is how sweat, sebaceous and mammary glands and the digestive enzyme glands work. Endocrine glands are ductless: their hormones go straight into the blood and travel everywhere, but they act only on the cells that carry a receptor for them.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: Required and Addressable Specifications
preguntas.subtema: Required vs addressable · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice concludes that one addressable specification does not suit an office of its size. What must it do?
opciones: Adopt an alternative that meets the purpose of the standard, and document why it did so
Skip it, since addressable means the specification is offered to entities as an option
Adopt it anyway, since addressable and required specifications carry identical obligations
Ask OCR for a written waiver before the standard containing it can be treated as met
preguntas.explicacion: Every standard has to be met, but the specifications inside them come labeled required or addressable. Addressable is not optional: the entity decides whether the specification counts as reasonable and appropriate in its case, and where it does, the entity adopts it. Where it does not, the entity may put in place some other measure that serves the same purpose the standard serves, and it must document why the original did not fit.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Error Prevention and Root Cause Analysis", Function
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.B Quality Improvement, corrective action · CMAA 3E k44 incident reporting
preguntas.pregunta: Leadership reviews the corrective action plan written after a root cause analysis. Which four things does the plan have to state?
opciones: The practical risk-reduction steps, who carries them out, the timeline, and how success gets measured
The staff member at fault, the discipline applied, the retraining date, and the supervisor signing off
The specimens affected, the cost of repeat testing, the payer notified, and the refund that was issued
The analytes involved, the testing event, the score obtained, and the remedial training that followed
preguntas.explicacion: The plan is what turns the analysis into a change. It has to name concrete risk-reduction steps, identify who will implement them, set a timeline, and define how effectiveness will be measured. Plans without measurable outcomes are the classic checkbox failure; naming a culprit is exactly what the analysis is designed to avoid.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, FAQ 570: E-mail with patients
preguntas.subtema: Alternative means · CCMA 6 k204 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.3.g · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 3.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient tells the office that unencrypted e-mail is unacceptable to her. What should the office do?
opciones: Offer another channel, such as a more secure electronic method, mail or telephone
Explain that e-mail is the only channel the Privacy Rule permits for results
Continue using e-mail but omit her name from the subject line of each message
Close her portal account, since electronic access would raise the same problem
preguntas.explicacion: An individual may ask a covered provider to communicate through some other means, or at some other location, where the request is reasonable. The example given is accommodating a request for appointment reminders by e-mail instead of on a postcard. The principle runs the other way too: where unencrypted e-mail will not do for a patient asking for confidential communications, other means should be offered, more secure electronic methods, mail, or the telephone.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Clinical Significance: Clergy and Other Religious Figures
preguntas.subtema: Clergy and the patient list · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k213 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital chaplain asks for the names of admitted patients of his denomination. What does the privacy rule allow?
opciones: Telling him, provided the patient was informed and did not object
Telling him, since clergy are workforce members of the hospital
Refusing, unless each patient signed a written authorization first
Refusing, because religious affiliation is never disclosed at all
preguntas.explicacion: Clergy and religious figures may be told which patients belong to their denomination, on the condition that the patient was informed first and raised no objection. That is why these preferences, along with who may visit and who should be notified, are asked at admission and put in writing. Disclosure can still happen in an emergency or when an incapacitated patient could not consent, if it is consistent with that person's best interest and the reasoning is documented.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Asthma" (NBK430901)
preguntas.subtema: Health center governance · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: How does the federal Health Center Program require a health center to be led in part by the people it serves?
opciones: A majority of the governing board's members must be patients of the health center
A majority of the clinical staff must live inside the area the health center serves
A majority of the board must be licensed providers who practice at the health center
A majority of the patients must have incomes under the federal poverty guidelines
preguntas.explicacion: A health center is based in its community and led partly by its own patients. Program rules say it must have a governing board where most members are patients, must focus on the needs of the people and the areas it serves, must build systems of care centered on the patient, and must see everybody, including anyone who cannot pay. About 90% of its patients have incomes under 200% of the poverty level.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: Two conditions are linked by the word with in the Alphabetic Index, and the note never says one caused the other. How are they coded?
opciones: As related, since the classification presumes a causal link between the two
As unrelated, unless the provider has explicitly documented a link between them
As related only where the two conditions sit inside the same chapter of the book
As related, but with the order of the two codes on the claim reversed for it
preguntas.explicacion: The words with and in are read as associated with or due to wherever they turn up in a code title, in the Index or in an instructional note, and a causal relationship between the conditions they link is presumed by the classification. They are coded as related even where nothing in the record says so, unless the record states they are unrelated or a guideline demands the link be explicit.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Lymphatic System: Components of the Lymphatic System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027 I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Where does lymph come from, and what happens if it is not returned to the blood?
opciones: From interstitial fluid; without return there is edema and a falling blood volume
From arterial blood; without return there is edema and a rising blood volume
From the bone marrow; without return there is anemia and a falling blood volume
From the digestive tract; without return there is edema and a rising blood volume
preguntas.explicacion: Lymph is close in composition to blood plasma and comes from the fluid that leaves the capillaries into the tissues. Once that interstitial fluid enters a lymph capillary it is called lymph, and returning it to the blood is what keeps edema away and holds blood volume and pressure where they belong.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Unique User Identification and Electronic Health Records
preguntas.subtema: HITECH · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7A k214 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k38
preguntas.pregunta: What did the HITECH Act add for covered entities that use electronic health records?
opciones: An audit trail accounting for disclosures, tracking who accesses records and when
A requirement to keep paper copies of every electronic record for 6 years
An exemption from breach notification for encrypted records affecting under 500 patients
A rule allowing shared passwords within a department to speed access
preguntas.explicacion: HITECH pushed providers toward taking up electronic records and using them meaningfully, and it tightened HIPAA along the way. A covered entity running an EHR has to produce an audit trail accounting for disclosures; the system logs who signed on and off, at what time, and what data was viewed or downloaded. Patients may ask for electronic copies of what the record holds, and one who pays out of pocket in full may ask that the information stay away from the health plan. Unique user names and passwords nobody shares are what make that tracking work; a shared password destroys it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Workplace Violence", Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: De-escalation · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k26 · NCMA EKB 22
preguntas.pregunta: How early in a visit can de-escalation be used?
opciones: As early as triage, before any confrontation has started
Once the patient has raised his voice at a staff member
Once the aggression management team has been called in
Only after chemical and physical restraint were refused
preguntas.explicacion: Triage is named as the point where de-escalation can already begin. Managing the workplace turns on prevention and on de-escalation, keeping fight or flight in reserve, with physical restraint used to back up chemical restraint only as a last resort. Waiting for shouting, or for a team to arrive, throws away the early chances to defuse tension.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), Your Responsibilities
preguntas.subtema: Insurance verification · CMAA 5B k66, 4 k58 · CCMA 5E k182
preguntas.pregunta: At check-in, why does the office ask a Medicare patient about other insurance at every visit?
opciones: To identify any payer primary to Medicare before the services are provided
To confirm that the patient has kept paying the Part B monthly premium
To decide whether the visit needs an advance written notice of non-coverage
To record which provider referred the patient for the appointment that day
preguntas.explicacion: Providers are told to build accurate secondary payer data by asking the patient, or the person representing her, at every visit and before services are given, whether she has other coverage that could pay ahead of Medicare, and to check eligibility as well; the point is to head off incorrect billing and overpayments. Premium payment, advance notices of non-coverage and referral sources are separate matters handled elsewhere.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Urinary System: Components of the Urinary System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(7) (2027 I.C.6.f(7)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Name the four components of the urinary system in the order urine travels through them.
opciones: Kidneys, ureters, urinary bladder, urethra
Kidneys, urethra, urinary bladder, ureters
Ureters, kidneys, urethra, urinary bladder
Urinary bladder, kidneys, ureters, urethra
preguntas.explicacion: The kidneys form the urine. The ureters carry it away from them down to the bladder, which holds it only temporarily, and the urethra carries it from the bladder to the outside. Reversing ureter and urethra is the classic slip, and the two words differ by very little in writing.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Administrative Simplification: Transactions Overview
preguntas.subtema: Insurance eligibility verification · CMAA 4 k58 · CCMA 5E · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: Which electronic transaction does an office use to ask a health plan whether a patient's coverage is active?
opciones: The eligibility transaction, one of the standard transactions adopted under HIPAA
The claim status transaction, one of the standard transactions adopted under HIPAA
The remittance advice transaction, which reports the plan's payment decisions
The enrollment transaction, which adds or removes members from a health plan
preguntas.explicacion: Eligibility is one of the standard transactions HIPAA adopted, sitting alongside claim status; coordination of benefits; enrollment and disenrollment; claims and encounter information; referrals and authorizations; and payment with remittance advice. Claim status asks what became of a claim already sent, remittance advice explains how a claim was paid, and enrollment moves members into a plan or out of it.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: HITECH Act
preguntas.subtema: HITECH and business associates · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3B k34 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: What did the HITECH Act change about the position of business associates?
opciones: It made them directly liable, civilly and criminally, for Security Rule violations
It removed the need for a covered entity to sign an agreement with them at all
It made covered entities solely responsible for the acts of a business associate
It limited their obligations to the Privacy Rule and left the Security Rule aside
preguntas.explicacion: HITECH section 13401 extends the Security Rule to business associates: its administrative safeguards, its physical ones and its technical ones, plus its policy, procedure and documentation requirements, now bind them the way they bind covered entities, and violations make them liable both civilly and criminally. Before that the rule touched them only at one remove, through the agreements covered entities had to sign.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse: Prevent, Detect, Report (MLN4649244), Anti-Kickback Statute
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: What do the safe harbor regulations do under the Anti-Kickback Statute?
opciones: They describe payment practices not treated as offenses
They set the fine that applies to each kind of kickback
They list the referrals a physician may never make at all
They exempt an arrangement from the self-referral law too
preguntas.explicacion: Safe harbor regulations set out payment and business practices that would otherwise raise a kickback question but are not treated as offenses when they meet the requirements written into the regulation. Meeting a safe harbor does not release anyone from the other laws that govern the same arrangement, the self-referral law included.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k12 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient says a relative had a heart attack. Which term will appear in the record?
opciones: Myocardial infarction, abbreviated MI
Congestive heart failure, abbreviated CHF
Coronary artery disease, abbreviated CAD
Atrial fibrillation, abbreviated AFIB
preguntas.explicacion: What people call a heart attack is charted as a myocardial infarction, written MI or AMI. The distractors are neighbors on the same problem list but different things: CHF is a heart that cannot pump enough blood, CAD is disease of the coronary arteries, and AFIB is a rhythm disturbance.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 5: Use the Teach-Back Method
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4I evaluate understanding · CMA F.3.a · 2027 F.1.h · CMAA 2G
preguntas.pregunta: Why are "Do you understand?" and "Does that make sense?" not teach-back questions?
opciones: They can be answered yes, and patients say yes whether they understood or not
They can be answered yes, which the toolkit reserves for the end of the visit
They use medical language that most patients will not recognize at all
They ask about the explanation instead of asking about the patient's plan
preguntas.explicacion: Teach-back asks the patient to put in her own words whatever she needs to know or to do. A question that can be closed with a yes gets a yes, understood or not, so those two phrasings prove nothing. The questions are also framed as a check on the explainer, not on the patient, so nobody feels shamed.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, General Compliance Program Guidance (2023), Element 5: Enforcing Standards
preguntas.subtema: Auditing and compliance · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: Two employees at very different levels of the practice commit the same offense. What does the OIG guidance expect?
opciones: The same consequences for both, applied consistently
A lighter consequence for the more senior of the two
A consequence only for the one who supervises the other
Retraining for both, since discipline is not a tool here
preguntas.explicacion: OIG holds that all levels of employees should face the same consequences for similar offenses, and that the commitment reaches contractors and medical staff as well. Officers, managers and supervisors are accountable both for their own failures and for those of the people they supervise. Consequences may be remedial, punitive or both.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Issues of Concern: Inadvertent Disclosure
preguntas.subtema: The chart that travels · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k213 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is wheeled to radiology with the chart on the trolley. What must the transporter be told?
opciones: Not to leave the chart where others could read it
To hand the chart to the first available radiology clerk
To keep the chart closed unless the patient asks to see it
To leave the chart at the desk until the images are done
preguntas.explicacion: Accidental disclosure counts as disclosure. A chart left unattended in a lobby or a procedure suite is the classic example, and when the chart travels with the patient the person pushing the trolley has to know not to leave it anywhere it can be read, on purpose or by accident, by people not involved in that patient's care. Deliberate and accidental disclosure of health information are treated the same way.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, HHS Agencies & Offices: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services
preguntas.subtema: Regulators the office answers to · CMAA 3A · NCMA 4.13
preguntas.pregunta: Which federal agency oversees Medicare, the federal share of Medicaid and the children's program, and the insurance marketplace?
opciones: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, along with quality assurance work
HRSA, the health resources agency, with the health centers it funds
The Office of Inspector General, along with the integrity of those programs
AHRQ, the healthcare research agency, with the evidence it produces
preguntas.explicacion: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services bring together oversight of Medicare, of the federal share of Medicaid, of the State Children's Health Insurance Program and of the Health Insurance Marketplace, along with the related quality assurance work. It sits inside the health and human services department and administers Medicaid in partnership with state governments.

preguntas.fuente: USPS, Compare Mail Services: First-Class Mail
preguntas.subtema: First-Class limits · CCMA 5O · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7G k96 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A large envelope of forms weighing 11 ounces is going out. May it travel as First-Class Mail?
opciones: Yes, large envelopes go up to 13 ounces under that class of mail
No, First-Class stops at 3.5 ounces for envelopes of every shape
No, a piece above 8 ounces moves to a parcel service priced by weight
Yes, but only once a delivery confirmation service has been added
preguntas.explicacion: First-Class Mail is written for flat, bendable pieces, and the ceiling depends on the shape: 3.5 ounces for a letter-sized envelope and 13 ounces for a large one. The 11-ounce envelope sits inside the large-envelope limit, so nothing needs to change.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms: Screening and Diagnostic Test
preguntas.subtema: Insurance coverage · CMA III.G.3 (2027 III.G.3) · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with no symptoms has a test to pick up a disease early. Which term describes it?
opciones: A screening, a preventive service done without symptoms
A diagnostic test, run to find what the problem is
A habilitation service, to keep her daily functioning
An emergency service, to check a serious condition
preguntas.explicacion: A screening is preventive care: a test or exam that looks for something in a patient who has no symptoms, no signs and no history of the condition. A diagnostic test is the opposite errand, carried out to work out what an existing health problem is, as an X-ray does when a bone may be broken.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Referral
preguntas.subtema: Authorizations and referrals · CCMA 5P k183 · CMA II.F.4.a / 2027 II.F.2.a · RMA II.A.4 · CMAA 4G k67 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: In many HMO plans, what must a patient obtain before seeing a specialist if they want the plan to pay?
opciones: A referral, which is a written order from their primary care doctor
A preauthorization, the plan's finding that the visit is necessary
A written order from the specialist, sent back to the primary care doctor
A claim, filed by the primary care doctor before the specialist visit
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov defines a referral as an order, in writing, from the primary care doctor so that the patient can see a specialist or receive certain services. In many HMOs that order is required before getting care from anyone other than the primary care doctor, and without it the plan may refuse to pay. The order runs from the primary care doctor to the specialist, not the other way. A preauthorization is the plan's own decision that a service is medically necessary, a different entry, and a claim is the request for payment that comes after the care, not before it.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A medication list marks one drug BID and another QID. Which pair of schedules is that?
opciones: Twice a day and four times a day
Twice a day and three times a day
Three times a day and four times a day
Twice a day and once a day at night
preguntas.explicacion: The dosing abbreviations differ by one letter and mean quite different schedules: BID is twice a day, TID is three times a day and QID is four times a day. PRN is the odd one out, because it is not a schedule at all: it means the dose is given as needed. Reading that first letter carefully is the whole trick.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: implied contract; and Wex: contract
preguntas.subtema: Contracts in practice · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.d(1) · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.9 · CMAA 3A k31
preguntas.pregunta: A new patient accepts a service at the office without signing any financial agreement. What kind of contract is that?
opciones: An implied-in-fact contract, inferred from what both parties did
An express contract, since the service was requested out loud
An implied-in-law contract, since no benefit was actually given
No contract at all, since payment terms were never agreed in advance
preguntas.explicacion: An express contract is communicated in speech or writing. An implied-in-fact one is formed when the promises are inferred from the parties' intentional conduct and one side knows, or has reason to know, the other will read that conduct as agreement: accepting a merchant's services means paying their reasonable value. An implied-in-law contract is a remedy against unjust enrichment, not a real agreement.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Formative Feedback
preguntas.subtema: Coaching and feedback · CCMA 6L k203 · CMAA 2F k21 · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which description matches formative feedback given to a team member?
opciones: Timely and specific, aimed at behaviors and improvement
General and delayed, aimed at the person's own attributes
Private and formal, aimed at the annual evaluation cycle
Immediate and public, aimed at the team's overall workload
preguntas.explicacion: The point of formative feedback is a team that performs better. It should be appreciative, timely after the behavior, respectful by focusing on behaviors rather than personal attributes, specific to a task, directed toward improvement, considerate of the person's feelings, and tied to the effect on the patient.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Telehealth Systems, Function
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth modalities · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.2.a · CMAA 4B k54 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A dermatologist reviews a photograph of a rash uploaded overnight and answers the next morning. Which kind of telehealth is that?
opciones: Asynchronous telemedicine, the store and forward method of sharing information
Synchronous, because a clinician and a patient are both involved in the exchange
Remote patient monitoring, because a device captured the image that was reviewed
A facilitated virtual visit, because staff at a clinic gathered the data beforehand
preguntas.explicacion: Store and forward, the asynchronous route, packages history, images and diagnostic data and ships them off for a specialist to read and advise on afterwards. Teledermatology fits exactly: a photograph of a skin lesion goes up and is read the next day. The same bucket holds e-consultations, secure messaging through the portal and off-site reading of radiology studies.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Specific Techniques
preguntas.subtema: Therapeutic techniques · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2A k15
preguntas.pregunta: Before asking about alcohol use, the assistant explains why the question is on the form. Which technique is that?
opciones: Providing rationale
Exploring feeling tones
Social pleasantries
Summarizing the answers
preguntas.explicacion: Providing rationale means saying up front why the information or the treatment recommendation is needed. Exploring feeling tones is identifying the patient's emotional state and reflecting it back; social pleasantries at the start of an interview help put her at ease; summarizing puts what she said back to her in the provider's own words.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Workplace Violence", Pearls and Other Issues: Organizational
preguntas.subtema: Difficult situations · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k16
preguntas.pregunta: What has been found about zero-tolerance policies for workplace violence?
opciones: Overall incidence does not drop, although physical violence does
Overall incidence drops, although verbal abuse stays where it was
They cancel any obligation to treat the person in the emergency department
They only work where a buddy system has been set up alongside
preguntas.explicacion: Zero tolerance and the buddy system are named as the most basic organizational policies. Zero tolerance is meant to fight the idea that violence is a normal hazard of the job; adopting it has not brought overall incidence down significantly, although physical violence does fall. Enforcement can also collide with the legal duty to provide care.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse (MLN4649244), Mandatory Exclusions
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A
preguntas.pregunta: Which conviction brings a mandatory exclusion from federal health programs?
opciones: A conviction for patient abuse or neglect, excluded for at least 5 years
A conviction for patient abuse or neglect, excluded for at least 1 year
A misdemeanor conviction for health care fraud outside Medicare programs
A default on a health education loan taken out during the training years
preguntas.explicacion: Mandatory exclusion follows a conviction for Medicare or Medicaid fraud and related offenses, for patient abuse or neglect, for felony health care fraud or for felony theft or other financial misconduct, and for felony drug offenses; five years is the minimum period, and aggravating factors can stretch it. Misdemeanor health care fraud outside those programs, and loan defaults, sit on the permissive list, where the length varies.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information
preguntas.subtema: Notice in emergencies · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives unconscious and is treated as an emergency. What happens with the notice of privacy practices?
opciones: It is furnished as soon as reasonably practicable afterwards, and no acknowledgment is needed
It is skipped altogether, because emergency treatment is outside the reach of the Privacy Rule
It is mailed within sixty days, the period a health plan has after a material revision
It is read aloud to the accompanying relative, who signs the acknowledgment on the patient's behalf
preguntas.explicacion: In an emergency treatment situation the notice comes as soon after the emergency ends as is reasonably practicable. The rule also lifts the duty to make a good faith effort at a written acknowledgment in that situation. Sixty days is the deadline for a health plan to send a revised notice after a material change.

preguntas.subtema: Employee record retention · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA II.B.5.c · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: How long must an employer preserve the medical record of an employee covered by the OSHA access standard?
opciones: For the duration of employment plus thirty years
For thirty years counted from the date of hire
For the duration of employment plus five years
For six years after the employee leaves the job
preguntas.explicacion: Unless a specific standard says otherwise, an employee's medical record is preserved for the whole time she is employed and for thirty years after that. Exposure records get thirty years of their own. The standard also carves out exceptions: health insurance claims kept apart from the medical program, minor first aid records, and the records of anyone employed less than a year where they are handed over on termination.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms: Durable Medical Equipment
preguntas.subtema: Insurance coverage · CMA III.G.3 (2027 III.G.3) · CMAA 5 k68, 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A provider orders oxygen equipment for a patient to use at home every day. Which benefit category does that fall into?
opciones: Durable medical equipment, ordered for extended use
Orthotics and prosthetics, ordered after an injury
Home health care, given at home under doctor's orders
Habilitation services, to keep skills for daily living
preguntas.explicacion: Durable medical equipment is equipment and supplies a provider orders for everyday or extended use, and oxygen equipment, wheelchairs and crutches are the examples given. Braces and artificial limbs fall under orthotics and prosthetics. Home health care is the services and supplies delivered in the home, not the equipment itself.

preguntas.subtema: Operative report · CCMA 5 k174 · CMA III.H.3.a · RMA II.B.4.a · CMAA 7A · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which document does the surgical services condition require the surgeon to sign, written or dictated right after the operation?
opciones: The operative report, with the techniques, the findings and any tissue removed
The discharge summary with the outcome and the provisions for follow-up care
The history and physical examination updated for any change in condition
The consultation report from the anesthesia service covering the procedure
preguntas.explicacion: The surgical services condition calls for an operative report setting out the techniques used, what was found, and any tissue taken out or altered; it is written or dictated straight after the operation and carries the surgeon's signature. The discharge summary, which records the outcome of the stay, the disposition of the case and the plans for follow-up, sits under the medical record condition and runs on the discharge timetable instead.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth workflow · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA k2 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which office processes does HHS say a move to telehealth will change?
opciones: Check-in, triage, consent, scheduling, billing, documentation and appointment structure
Only the billing process, since everything else in the visit stays exactly as it was
Only the clinical examination, since the administrative side of the visit is unaffected
Only the consent process, since the rest of the workflow is set by the software vendor
preguntas.explicacion: Moving care to telehealth forces changes on the in-person workflow. The processes named as affected are check-in, triage, consent, scheduling, billing, documentation and the structure of the appointment. How much has to change turns on the vendor, on the size and setting of the practice, on the patient population and on the services offered, and the electronic health record should merge easily into the new workflow.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Amendment
preguntas.subtema: Amendment denial · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.5
preguntas.pregunta: The provider reviews the amendment request and concludes the entry is accurate. What is the patient entitled to?
opciones: A written denial and the chance to submit a statement of disagreement for the record
A second review by a licensed professional who took no part in the original decision
Automatic deletion of the disputed entry, since the record must reflect what she reports
A refund of any copying fee she paid, since the amendment request was not granted
preguntas.explicacion: When a covered entity denies an amendment request it must give the individual a written denial and let her submit a statement of disagreement to be included in the record. The rule sets out the process for requesting and answering these requests. The independent second review by a licensed professional belongs to the access right, not to amendment.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Individual Notice
preguntas.subtema: Substitute breach notice · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA II.B.3.g · CMAA 3E k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: The practice has out-of-date addresses for 14 of the patients affected by a breach. What substitute notice is required?
opciones: A notice on its home page for at least 90 days, or in major print or broadcast media
A notice on its home page for at least 30 days, with no toll-free number needed
A single telephone call to each of the 14, which is the alternative for small numbers
A notice to prominent media outlets, the step reserved for a breach of any size
preguntas.explicacion: Where contact information is insufficient or out of date for 10 or more individuals, substitute notice means posting on the home page of the web site for at least 90 days or placing the notice in major print or broadcast media where those people probably live, and including a toll-free number that stays active at least 90 days. For fewer than 10, another written form, a telephone call or another means will do.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, National Provider Identifier Standard (NPI)
preguntas.subtema: Third-party billing requirements · CMAA 6C k87, 6 k85 · CCMA 5L k185 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: Who has to use the National Provider Identifier in the transactions adopted under HIPAA?
opciones: Covered providers, health plans and clearinghouses, in place of older identifiers
Covered providers alone, since plans and clearinghouses keep their own numbers
Providers who bill Medicare, since commercial payers assign their own numbers
Providers and patients, since the identifier appears on the insurance card
preguntas.explicacion: Covered health care providers, and every health plan and clearinghouse, have to use the identifier in the HIPAA-adopted transactions, administrative and financial alike, where it takes the place of legacy provider identifiers. A covered provider must also share the number with other providers, with plans, with clearinghouses and with any entity needing it for billing, so its use goes well beyond Medicare claims.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, "Talking With Your Older Patients", Confusion and cognitive problems
preguntas.subtema: Cognitive impairment · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.1.c(6) / 2027 F.1.d(6)
preguntas.pregunta: A confused older patient keeps apologizing for wrong answers. What should the staff member do?
opciones: Make clear this is a search for information, not a test
Correct each wrong answer so the record stays accurate
Move the remaining questions to the family in the hallway
Stop the interview and chart the history as unreliable
preguntas.explicacion: Reassure the patient and support her, acknowledging the responses that are correct or understood, and say plainly that the conversation is not a test but a search for information that will help her. A staff member can telephone afterward about the instructions. Real changes in cognition get screening and diagnostic testing.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow, Preparing for telehealth visits
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth scheduling policy · CMAA 4B k49 k54 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice writing its telehealth policy has already settled how it will judge which visits suit video. Which two scheduling questions are still on the guidance's list?
opciones: Which days video appointments are offered, and whether patients book online or by calling in
Which days video appointments are offered, and which clinician covers each of those days
Whether patients book online or by calling in, and what fee applies to a video appointment
Which days video appointments are offered, and how long each video slot should be booked for
preguntas.explicacion: The scheduling questions put to a practice before it starts are these: when telehealth appointments will be offered, whether on set days of the week or daily; whether patients will schedule online or by telephoning the office; how the practice will decide that a telehealth appointment is appropriate; and how and when appointment reminders will go out.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, General Compliance Program Guidance (2023), Element 6: Risk Assessment, Auditing, and Monitoring
preguntas.subtema: Auditing and compliance · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: How often does the OIG guidance say a compliance risk assessment should be carried out?
opciones: At least once a year, and more often where resources allow
At least once every two years, in step with the audit plan
Only when a report arrives through the disclosure program
Only when the government opens a review of that entity
preguntas.explicacion: OIG asks for periodic compliance risk assessments, at least annually, as part of the sixth element. An entity that wants to assess more often has to put the time and resources behind each round. The compliance committee runs the assessment and works with the compliance officer to turn the priorities into the audit and monitoring plan.

preguntas.subtema: Advance directives and incapacity · CCMA 5D · CMA I.A.5 · RMA I.C.1.f · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: An adult arrives for admission too unwell to take in the written information about advance directives. What does the regulation allow the facility to do?
opciones: Give the information to her family or surrogate, and follow it up with her later
Give the information to her family or surrogate, and treat the duty as discharged
Record that she was incapacitated, which excuses the facility from the duty
Delay the admission until a surrogate can be reached to receive the information
preguntas.explicacion: Where an adult is incapacitated at admission or at the start of care and cannot receive the information or say whether she has an advance directive, the provider may pass it to her family or surrogate the way it issues other policy material. The obligation to the individual survives: follow-up procedures must deliver it to her directly once she is able.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Communication Styles
preguntas.subtema: Communication styles · CCMA 6K k203 · CMAA 2A k13 · CMA F.1.e / 2027 F.1.f
preguntas.pregunta: What marks aggressive communication as opposed to assertive communication?
opciones: It leans on “you” messages and can feel like an attack on the receiver
It leans on “I” messages that name facts and the sender's own feelings
It places the rights of the receiver ahead of the sender's own rights
It repeats the same message until the receiver returns some feedback
preguntas.explicacion: Assertive communication puts the facts and what the sender feels without any disrespect toward the receiver, and it is built on phrases such as “I feel” or “Help me understand.” Aggressive communication uses “you” messages, so the receiver feels attacked instead of hearing the issue. Yielding to others is passive, and repetition is not one of the three styles.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Introduction to the Americans with Disabilities Act (who is protected)
preguntas.subtema: ADAAA compliance · CMAA 3A (ADAAA)
preguntas.pregunta: Who counts as a person with a disability under the ADA?
opciones: Someone impaired, with a record of impairment, or regarded as impaired
Someone impaired who has applied for and been approved for ADA coverage
Someone impaired whose condition is expected to last for the rest of life
Someone impaired who is receiving disability benefit payments
preguntas.explicacion: Three groups are protected: someone with an impairment, physical or mental, that substantially limits one or more of the major life activities; someone with a record or history of such an impairment, cancer in remission for instance; and someone others perceive as having one, such as a person with burn scars. It is a civil rights law, not a benefit program, so nobody applies for coverage.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Yearly "Wellness" visits, Who's eligible and How often
preguntas.subtema: Scheduling considerations · CMAA 4A k52 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient whose Part B enrollment started four months ago asks to book her first yearly Wellness visit. What does the office tell her?
opciones: It cannot take place within 12 months of her Part B enrollment
It can be booked now, since the 12 months run from her birthday
She has to have a Welcome to Medicare visit first to qualify for it
It cannot be booked until she has been enrolled for a full 24 months
preguntas.explicacion: The first yearly Wellness visit cannot fall within 12 months of the start of Part B, nor within 12 months of a Welcome to Medicare preventive visit. Having had that welcome visit is not a condition of qualifying, though: a patient who never had one is still entitled to the Wellness visit once the 12 months have run. After that it is covered once every 12 months.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Uses and Disclosures for Treatment, Payment, and Health Care Operations
preguntas.subtema: Payment activities · CCMA 5 k181 · CMA III.G.3 · RMA II.A.1 · CMAA 6 k89 · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which office task falls within the payment activities a covered entity may carry out without authorization?
opciones: Determining a patient's eligibility for coverage under her plan
Training a new medical assistant on how the practice rooms patients
Evaluating whether a clinician should keep hospital privileges
Preparing a de-identified data set for a population health project
preguntas.explicacion: Payment covers what providers do in order to be paid and what plans do to collect premiums and deliver benefits. The examples offered include working out eligibility or coverage and adjudicating claims, reviewing services for medical necessity and for justification of charges, and a limited set of disclosures made to consumer reporting agencies. Training, credentialing and de-identification are health care operations instead.

preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, leukemia and lymphoma
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k5 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks how leukemia and lymphoma differ. Which answer is accurate?
opciones: Leukemia starts in blood-forming tissue, lymphoma in immune system cells
Leukemia starts in immune system cells, lymphoma in blood-forming tissue
Leukemia starts in the lymph nodes, lymphoma in the marrow of the bones
Leukemia starts in bone or soft tissue, lymphoma in the lining of organs
preguntas.explicacion: Leukemia begins in the tissue that forms blood, the bone marrow above all, and abnormal blood cells are then produced in large numbers and pour into the bloodstream. Lymphoma begins in cells of the immune system and falls into two families: Hodgkin lymphoma, marked by the Reed-Sternberg cell, and the non-Hodgkin lymphomas, a large and varied group.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, National Correct Coding Initiative
preguntas.subtema: Bundling and unbundling · CMAA 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · CMA III.G.1.a(3)
preguntas.pregunta: What does the National Correct Coding Initiative use its procedure-to-procedure edits for?
opciones: To stop payment for pairs of procedures that should not be reported together
To stop payment for services that exceed the units likely for one patient in a day
To set the payment amount for each procedure reported on a professional claim
To assign the diagnosis code that supports the procedure billed on the claim
preguntas.explicacion: The correct coding initiative runs two kinds of edits: procedure-to-procedure edits, which address pairs of codes that should not be billed together, and medically unlikely edits, which cap the units of service a provider would report for one patient on one day. Payment amounts come from the fee schedule, and diagnosis codes are selected from the documentation, not assigned by edits.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, Office for Human Research Protections, The Belmont Report (April 18, 1979), Part C.1
preguntas.subtema: Ethical principles · CCMA 7C · CMA E.7 / 2027 E.6 · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: The Belmont Report breaks the consent process into which three elements?
opciones: Information, comprehension and voluntariness
Disclosure, documentation and attestation
Capacity, competence and authorization
Risks, benefits and alternative treatments
preguntas.explicacion: Belmont analyzes consent under three heads: information, comprehension, voluntariness. Information covers the procedure, its purpose, the risks and expected benefits, the alternatives where therapy is involved, and the chance to ask questions and to withdraw. Comprehension depends on how and when the information is delivered. Voluntariness means conditions free of coercion and of undue influence.

preguntas.fuente: ISMP, List of Error-Prone Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations (2024), Drug Name Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k10 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k8 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: An order is written as MS 4 mg. What is the danger, and what is the correct practice?
opciones: It can mean morphine or magnesium sulfate, so the drug name is spelled out
It can mean morphine or a multiple sclerosis code, so the dose is spelled out
It can mean milligrams or micrograms, so the unit is spelled out in full
It can mean a syrup or a solution, so the dosage form is spelled out in full
preguntas.explicacion: MS and MSO4 stand for morphine sulfate and MgSO4 for magnesium sulfate, and the three are swapped for each other in handwriting. Two very different drugs behind one set of letters is why all of them are banned, and the practice is to write the complete drug name every time.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, SOAP Notes, Assessment
preguntas.subtema: SOAP assessment · CCMA 5 k174 · CMA III.H.3.a · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA k4 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which content belongs in the assessment section of a SOAP note?
opciones: The synthesis of the findings into a diagnosis, with the differential and its reasoning
The chief concern in the patient's own words, followed by the history of present illness
The vital signs and laboratory results gathered during the encounter that day
The tests still needed and the treatment steps planned for each identified problem
preguntas.explicacion: The assessment brings subjective and objective findings together to reach a diagnosis, weighing the problems, their possible interactions and any change in status, and listing problems in order of importance. The differential runs from most to least likely with the reasoning stated, and should include unlikely conditions that could cause harm if missed. Testing and treatment steps belong to the plan.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, General Compliance Program Guidance (2023), Element 7: Reporting to the Government
preguntas.subtema: Auditing and compliance · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: After a reasonable inquiry, a compliance officer has reason to believe credible evidence of a violation exists. How soon should the government hear of it?
opciones: Promptly, and no later than sixty days after that determination
Promptly, and no later than thirty days after that determination
Once the internal investigation has closed, whenever that falls
Only where the program lost money because of the conduct
preguntas.explicacion: Where the conduct may break a criminal, a civil or an administrative law, the entity notifies the authority that fits, promptly and within sixty days of determining that credible evidence exists. Some conduct is grave enough to be reported before or alongside the internal investigation. A violation can be material even where the program lost nothing.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Qualifying life event (QLE)
preguntas.subtema: Coverage enrollment · CMAA 5 k73, 5B k66 · CCMA 5E k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is a qualifying life event for a Special Enrollment Period?
opciones: Turning 26 and losing the coverage held through a parent's plan
Turning 26 and choosing a plan with a lower monthly premium
Changing doctors within the network the current plan contracts with
Reaching the out-of-pocket limit of the plan before the year ends
preguntas.explicacion: Qualifying life events fall into four groups: losing coverage, changes in the household, changes in residence, and other events such as income changes or leaving incarceration. Turning 26 and dropping off a parent's plan is listed as a loss of coverage. Wanting a cheaper premium, switching doctors inside the network, or hitting the out-of-pocket limit are not events that open enrollment outside the yearly window.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Yearly "Wellness" visits, Description
preguntas.subtema: Scheduling considerations · CMAA 4A k52 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient calls to book her yearly Wellness visit and also wants her painful knee looked at. What should the office do?
opciones: Book a separate appointment for the knee so the visit stays on prevention
Add the knee to the Wellness visit, which covers a routine physical exam
Send her to a Welcome to Medicare visit, where new problems are handled
Put the knee on the Health Risk Assessment so it is covered that day
preguntas.explicacion: The yearly Wellness visit is a conversation about a personalised prevention plan, and it is expressly not a routine physical examination. A patient with a specific health worry is told to book a separate appointment for it so that the Wellness visit stays on prevention. The Health Risk Assessment is the questionnaire that feeds the prevention plan, not a way of adding complaints.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Minimum Necessary Requirement: Reasonable Reliance
preguntas.subtema: Reasonable reliance · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A public official states that what he is requesting is the minimum necessary for a purpose the rule permits. May the practice rely on that?
opciones: Yes, where the reliance is reasonable in the circumstances of the request
Yes, and the practice is then barred from making its own determination
No, the practice must always decide for itself what the minimum necessary is
No, unless the official supplies a court order covering the same records
preguntas.explicacion: In certain circumstances the rule lets a covered entity rely on the judgment of the requester about how much information is needed, provided the reliance is reasonable. That is permitted for a public official or agency stating the request is the minimum necessary for a permitted purpose, for a workforce member or business associate professional saying the same, and for a researcher with board documentation. Reliance is never obligatory.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), Issuing a Notice as a Courtesy
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMA III.G.3.c (2027 III.G.3.c) · CMAA 5 k77 · CCMA 5 k186
preguntas.pregunta: A practice wants to warn a patient in writing about an item Medicare never covers at all. What is true of that notice?
opciones: It is voluntary, and she need not tick an option or sign it
It is required, and she has to tick an option and sign it
It is required, or the practice cannot bill her for the item
It is voluntary, and signing it moves the liability to her
preguntas.explicacion: No advance notice is needed before an item or service that Medicare never covers or that is not a Medicare benefit at all. A practice may still hand one over as a courtesy to warn the patient what she will owe; issuing it voluntarily changes nothing about liability, and she is not asked to select an option box or to sign and date it.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Remittance Processing
preguntas.subtema: Charge reconciliation · CMA III.G.7.c (2027 III.G.6.b) · CMAA 6B · CCMA 5K k187
preguntas.pregunta: At posting, a biller takes off a balance that the contract with the payer does not oblige the practice to give up. What is that?
opciones: A non-contractual write-off, which good process should shrink
A contractual adjustment, agreed with the payer in advance
An underpayment, where the payer paid below the schedule
A patient collection, the share the member has to pay
preguntas.explicacion: Once the remittance arrives, payments are posted and the amounts given up are recorded. The revenue cycle literature asks practices to define which write-offs are contractual and which are not, because keeping the two apart is what resolves denials and keeps the non-contractual ones down. The contractual sort is the discount the contract itself sets.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, Patient Identity and Patient Record Matching
preguntas.subtema: Avoiding duplicate records · CMAA 4D k57 · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.2.a · RMA II.B.4.a · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A scheduler asks how the system works out that two records belong to the same person. Which fields does ONC name as the minimum?
opciones: Several demographic fields at once: name, date of birth, telephone number and address
The medical record number by itself, since it is unique inside the system that issued it
The insurance member number and group number carried on the card the patient presents
Name and date of birth only, the two identifiers used to confirm a patient before care
preguntas.explicacion: Patient matching is what identifies a patient's data and links it together, both inside a health system and between systems, so that a full view of the record comes into being. The minimum way it is done is by tying several demographic fields together: name, birth date, telephone number and address. ONC calls it critical to interoperability and to the national health IT infrastructure.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, Office for Human Research Protections, The Belmont Report (April 18, 1979), Part B
preguntas.subtema: Ethical principles · CCMA 7C · CMA E.7 / 2027 E.6 · RMA I.C.4.a · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: Which three principles does the Belmont Report set out?
opciones: Respect for persons, beneficence and justice
Autonomy, confidentiality and truthfulness
Beneficence, nonmaleficence and fidelity
Respect for persons, privacy and fairness
preguntas.explicacion: The Belmont Report, published in 1979 by the national commission the National Research Act created, names three basic principles for research with human subjects: beneficence, justice, and respect for persons. Respect for persons carries two duties, honoring autonomy and protecting those whose autonomy is diminished. Not harming lives inside beneficence there, as the rule to do no harm.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases, chapter 5: Stock Rotation and Removal
preguntas.subtema: Stock rotation · CCMA 5T · RMA II.B.5.a · CMAA 7E k99 · NCMA 4.13
preguntas.pregunta: How should stock be arranged inside a storage unit, and what happens to what has expired?
opciones: The earliest expiration dates go in front, and expired stock is pulled out at once
The newest deliveries go in front, and expired stock is pulled at the next count
The most used items go in front, and expired stock is kept until it is replaced
The earliest expiration dates go behind, and expired stock is marked for return
preguntas.explicacion: Stock is rotated so that whatever expires first is what the hand reaches first, with later dates behind it. Anything already expired is taken out immediately rather than at the next count, because leaving it there is how an invalid dose gets given by mistake.

preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, scope of practice · CPT D1 1D scope of practice · CCMA 7A k214 · RMA I.C.6 scope of practice · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k48
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks the phlebotomist whether her potassium result means she has kidney disease. What is the appropriate response?
opciones: Say that the ordering provider interprets results, and route the question to that provider
Read the reference interval aloud and show her where her own value falls against it
Tell her the value is normal for her age, since age-based intervals are on the report
Refuse to discuss the report at all, because privacy rules bar giving results to patients
preguntas.explicacion: CLIA puts interpretation on the far side of the bench: reference intervals go to whoever was authorized to order the test and to whoever is responsible for using the results, and the results themselves are released only to those people. Refusing outright is wrong for another reason, since a patient may request access to her own completed report.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.3 Adapting Your Communication
preguntas.subtema: Pediatric communication · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(7)(b) / 2027 F.1.d(7)(a) · RMA I.D.1.a · CMAA 2D k17
preguntas.pregunta: A four-year-old is frightened before a procedure. Which approach is recommended?
opciones: Speak calmly and demonstrate the steps on a doll
Explain the anatomy behind each step in order
Promise the child that it will not hurt at all
Offer the choice of skipping the step for today
preguntas.explicacion: With children, speak calmly and gently, and demonstrating what will be done on a doll or stuffed animal helps; play and drawing build trust. Anatomy sits above a preschooler's developmental level, promising no pain is false reassurance, and the choices offered have to stay inside real limits.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medigap basics
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: When may a patient buy any Medigap policy she likes without being refused because of her health?
opciones: In the six months that begin the first month she has Part B and is sixty-five
In the six months that begin the first month she has Part A and is sixty-five
In the Medicare Open Enrollment Period, which comes round once every year
In the eight months that follow the day she or her spouse stops working
preguntas.explicacion: The Medigap Open Enrollment Period runs for six months from the first month in which the person has Part B and is sixty-five or older. During it she may enroll in any Medigap policy and the company cannot refuse her over pre-existing health problems. It happens once and does not come round every year the way the Medicare Open Enrollment Period does.

preguntas.fuente: plainlanguage.gov, Federal plain language guidelines
preguntas.subtema: Testing for understanding · CCMA 6 k206 · CMA II.F.2 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7G k95 · NCMA 3.2
preguntas.pregunta: The office has drafted a letter about a change in visiting hours in language it believes is clear. Which step does the federal plain language guidance add?
opciones: Testing the wording with the audience to see that it is really understood
Having a second staff member read it aloud and correct the punctuation
Sending it to the agency that enforces the writing law for its approval
Rewriting it at the reading level printed on the practice's own website
preguntas.explicacion: The guidance runs in stages: understand the principles, write for understanding, design for understanding, and then test for understanding. Clear writing is judged by whether the specific audience actually makes sense of it, which is the requirement the 2010 statute put on content written for the public.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.4 Handoff Reports
preguntas.subtema: Transitions of care · CCMA 4H k167 · CMAA 2F
preguntas.pregunta: What did The Joint Commission warn about handoffs in 2017?
opciones: Poor handoff communication had led to real harm to patients
Bedside reports had lowered satisfaction where they were tried
A handoff had to be in writing before it counted as complete
Handoff tools other than the preferred one were unacceptable
preguntas.explicacion: A sentinel event alert was issued in 2017 about inadequate handoff communication that had led to harm such as wrong-site surgeries, treatment delays, falls and medication errors. The evidence points the other way on bedside reports: they raise patient safety and both patient and staff satisfaction.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Who is Covered by the Privacy Rule
preguntas.subtema: HIPAA scope · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3B k33 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A solo practitioner bills every claim on paper and never sends a standard electronic transaction. Is that office a HIPAA covered entity?
opciones: No, because a provider is covered only once it sends health information in a standard transaction
Yes, because sending patients e-mail is by itself an electronic transmission of their health data
Yes, because every provider of medical services is a covered entity regardless of how claims go out
No, because only hospitals and health plans are ever treated as covered entities under the rules
preguntas.explicacion: Three kinds of organization are covered: health plans, clearinghouses, and any provider, of any size, that transmits health information electronically in a transaction for which HHS adopted a standard, such as a claim or an eligibility inquiry. Using electronic technology like e-mail does not by itself make a provider covered; the transmission has to be a standard transaction.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Inpatient rehabilitation care: Description and Who's eligible
preguntas.subtema: Transition to inpatient rehabilitation · CCMA 4H · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: What must a provider certify before Part A covers care in an inpatient rehabilitation facility?
opciones: That the condition needs intensive rehabilitation, medical supervision and coordinated care
That the patient has had a qualifying inpatient hospital stay of at least three days
That the patient is homebound and needs part-time or intermittent skilled services
That the patient accepts comfort care in place of treatment meant to cure the illness
preguntas.explicacion: Inpatient rehabilitation helps a person recovering from serious surgery, illness or injury who needs intensive therapy, supervision by a physician, and care coordinated across several providers. The health care provider has to certify that medical condition. The three-day stay belongs to skilled nursing coverage, homebound status to home health, and accepting comfort care to the hospice election.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 160.103, Business associate
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, confidentiality · CCMA 7E k220 · CMAA 3B k33 · CMA II.E.1.a confidentiality
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic sends its specimens to an outside reference laboratory and hires an outside company to file its claims. What does HIPAA require of the clinic here?
opciones: A business associate agreement with the billing company, but not with the reference laboratory
A business associate agreement with each of them before either one handles patient information
A signed patient authorization for every specimen and every claim that leaves the clinic's building
A notice of privacy practices mailed to each patient every time a specimen is referred out
preguntas.explicacion: A business associate is someone outside the workforce who handles identifiable health information while carrying out a function for the covered entity, and claims processing and billing are the named examples, so that contract is required. The laboratory is another matter: a health care provider is left out of the definition where the disclosure concerns treating the patient, and referred specimens are exactly that.

preguntas.subtema: Coding and indexing · CCMA 5 k172 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.d · CMAA 7 k91 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: A quality study needs every record of a given procedure from last year. Which requirement makes that search possible?
opciones: A coding and indexing system that retrieves records by diagnosis and procedure
A confidentiality procedure that limits who may receive information from a record
An author identification system that shows who wrote each entry in the record
A retention rule that keeps every record available for at least five full years
preguntas.explicacion: Keeping the records is not enough: the hospital also needs a coding and indexing system for them, and that system has to allow timely retrieval by diagnosis and by procedure, precisely so that studies evaluating medical care can be supported. Retention keeps the records; indexing is what finds them.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.512(f)(1) and (f)(2), Disclosures for law enforcement purposes
preguntas.subtema: Law enforcement disclosures · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k37
preguntas.pregunta: A police officer asks the laboratory for a patient's blood type and home address to locate a suspect. Which statement reflects HIPAA?
opciones: Name, address and ABO blood type may be given; analyses of body fluids may not
No information may be disclosed without a court order, not even the name
The full record may be disclosed, since law enforcement requests override the Privacy Rule
Only the results of body fluid analyses may be disclosed, not the address
