preguntas.explicacion: When the purpose is to identify or locate a fugitive, a suspect, a material witness or someone missing, 164.512(f)(2) lets a covered entity release only a fixed list: name and address, date and place of birth, Social Security number, ABO blood type and Rh factor, type of injury, date and time of treatment or death, and distinguishing physical characteristics. DNA, dental records and the typing, sampling or analysis of body fluid or tissue are expressly left out. Other law-enforcement disclosures need a court order, a warrant, a subpoena or a qualifying administrative request.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), File Proper & Timely Claims
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMA III.G.3.a (2027 III.G.3.a) · CMAA 6 k87 · CCMA 5B
preguntas.pregunta: Medicare and a state Medicaid agency both claim the same recovered payment. Whose right comes first?
opciones: Medicare's, whose right to recover takes priority over that of any other party
Medicaid's, since it is the payer of last resort in every recovery situation
Medicaid's, since state law settles the order in which recoveries are applied
Neither one's; the two divide the recovery in proportion to what each paid out
preguntas.explicacion: Incorrect payments may be recovered by Medicare straight from a primary payer, from another entity or from a third payer, and its right of recovery outranks anyone else's, Medicaid included. The secondary payer provisions live in federal law, which takes priority over state law and over whatever a private insurance contract says.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, A Roadmap for New Physicians: Fraud & Abuse Laws
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · CMA III.G.2
preguntas.pregunta: Why is the Physician Self-Referral Law described as a strict liability statute?
opciones: Proof of intent to violate it is not required for a violation to exist
Proof of a financial relationship is not required for it to be violated
Penalties are limited to repaying the amount the program overpaid
It applies only when the physician owns the entity outright, not in part
preguntas.explicacion: Stark bars a physician from sending Medicare-payable designated health services to any entity in which he, or an immediate family member, holds a financial relationship, save where an exception applies, and it bars the entity from billing for those referrals. Being strict liability, it needs no proof of intent. The trigger is exactly that financial relationship, by ownership or by compensation, and the penalties go past repayment.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, PSNet Patient Safety Primer: Reporting Patient Safety Events
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 6 k211 · CMA I.B.11.c · 2027 I.B.10.c · CMAA 3 k44 · NCMA 4.10 · CPT 1N k39
preguntas.pregunta: Who normally files the report after a patient falls in the clinic hallway?
opciones: The frontline staff member who was involved in or saw the event
The risk manager, once the chart has been reviewed for the week
The provider who signs the chart at the end of that patient's visit
The office manager, who collects the accounts of everyone involved
preguntas.explicacion: Event reporting is voluntary and depends on the people who were there: the first report usually comes from a frontline staff member who was involved in the event itself, or in what led up to it, rather than from management or the patient safety staff. Falls and medication errors are among the events reported most often through these systems.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), File Proper & Timely Claims
preguntas.subtema: Third-party billing · CMA III.G.3.b(4) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6 k87 · CCMA 5 k185
preguntas.pregunta: How long does a primary payer have to reimburse Medicare once Medicare learns that it should have paid?
opciones: Sixty days from the day that information reaches Medicare, or interest may run
Thirty days from the day that information reaches Medicare, or interest may run
A hundred and twenty days from the date of service, or interest may run on it
Sixty days from the date of service, after which the debt can no longer be pursued
preguntas.explicacion: A primary payer, or any entity that a non-Medicare primary payer has paid, gets sixty days to reimburse Medicare, counted from the day Medicare receives the information that a primary payer made the payment or could have made it. Miss that window and interest can follow, and legal action may follow too, in which recovery reaches twice the amount paid.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Conflict Management", Issues of Concern: Systems-Level and Organizational Factors
preguntas.subtema: Teamwork · CCMA 6L k202 · CMAA 2F k21 · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: What does psychological safety mean in a clinical team?
opciones: The shared belief that speaking up will not bring reprisal
The shared picture of the plan that every member carries
The habit of watching the stress levels of other members
The readiness to take over work when a colleague falls behind
preguntas.explicacion: Psychological safety is the belief, shared across the team, that a member can speak up and face no reprisal for it, and teams that have it report conflict earlier and turn it into learning rather than blame. The other three options describe a shared mental model, cross-monitoring and backup behavior, which are separate teamwork concepts.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: tort
preguntas.subtema: Torts · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3A k31
preguntas.pregunta: Into which three general categories do torts fall?
opciones: Intentional torts, negligent torts and strict liability torts
Intentional torts, criminal torts and administrative torts
Negligent torts, contractual torts and statutory torts
Negligent torts, punitive torts and constitutional torts
preguntas.explicacion: A tort is an act or omission that injures another and amounts to a civil wrong the courts attach liability to. Intentional torts are wrongs the defendant knew or should have known would follow from what they did; negligent torts happen when the conduct was unreasonably unsafe; strict liability torts do not turn on how careful the defendant was, only on whether the harm occurred.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Restriction Request; 45 CFR 164.522(a)(1)(ii) and (vi)
preguntas.subtema: Restriction requests · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks the practice never to discuss her visits with the sister who drives her to them, though the sister waits in the room. What is the practice's position?
opciones: It need not agree to the restriction, but once it agrees it is bound by what it accepted
It must agree to any restriction a patient requests about treatment, payment or operations
It must agree, because a restriction is binding wherever the patient pays the visit in full
It may not agree, because restrictions would conflict with the notice of privacy practices
preguntas.explicacion: Individuals have the right to ask a covered entity to restrict uses and disclosures made for treatment, for payment or for health care operations, and disclosures to people involved in their care or made to notify family, which is what the sister is. As a rule the entity is under no obligation to agree, and once it agrees it must keep to what it accepted, except where it has to treat her in a medical emergency. The regulation writes in a single restriction that cannot be refused, and it does not fit here: a disclosure to a health plan, for payment or for health care operations and not otherwise required by law, about an item or service the patient herself has paid for in full.

preguntas.subtema: Security training · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which measures belong to the security awareness and training standard that a practice must run for its whole workforce?
opciones: Periodic reminders, guarding against malicious software, watching log-ins, passwords
Periodic reminders, a written test each year, a signed policy, a security officer
Guarding against malicious software, encryption of every message, locked cabinets
Watching log-ins, a sanction policy, a risk analysis, and a business associate list
preguntas.explicacion: Training covers the entire workforce, management included, and hangs four addressable specifications off it: security reminders; procedures that guard against malicious software and that detect and report it; monitoring of log-in attempts with any discrepancies reported; and procedures for creating passwords, changing them and keeping them safe.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: Technical Safeguards
preguntas.subtema: Access control · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Staff at the front desk share one login for the practice management system. Which technical safeguard does that defeat?
opciones: Access control, which is meant to let only authorized persons reach the ePHI
Transmission security, which guards ePHI while it moves across an electronic network
Facility access control, which limits who can physically enter the computer room
Device and media controls, which govern hardware coming into and out of the office
preguntas.explicacion: Access control is the technical standard requiring policies and procedures for the electronic systems holding ePHI so that only authorized persons can reach it. A shared login also undermines audit controls, the mechanisms that capture and review what is done inside those systems, because the record no longer shows who did what. Transmission security and the physical standards address different points entirely.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Elder Abuse", Introduction; and Epidemiology
preguntas.subtema: Signs of abuse · CCMA 7F k222 · CMA E.6.c / 2027 E.5.b · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k43
preguntas.pregunta: Which are the recognized categories of elder abuse?
opciones: Physical, emotional, sexual and financial abuse, and neglect
Physical, emotional and sexual abuse, plus abandonment and fraud
Physical and sexual abuse, plus self-neglect and guardianship error
Physical, emotional and financial abuse, plus restraint and seclusion
preguntas.explicacion: Elder abuse means harm, or risk of harm, to an older adult through an act, an omission or negligence by somebody in a position of presumed trust, and it falls into five categories: physical, emotional or psychological, sexual and financial abuse, plus neglect. Victims often suffer several at once, and the commonest are financial exploitation, psychological abuse and neglect.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Conflict Management", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Conflict management · CCMA 6J k209 · CMAA 2B k26 · CMA F.1.f / 2027 F.1.f
preguntas.pregunta: In the Thomas-Kilmann framework, which style is high in both assertiveness and cooperativeness?
opciones: Collaborating, working out an integrative solution
Compromising, trading concessions for a middle ground
Accommodating, yielding in order to save the relationship
Competing, pursuing one's position at the other's expense
preguntas.explicacion: The framework arranges five styles along assertiveness, meaning concern for your own goals, and cooperativeness, concern for the other party's. Collaborating is high on both: the parties surface the underlying interests and build a solution that meets everyone's substantive needs. It is also the most effortful style.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication
preguntas.subtema: Intake accommodations · CCMA 4 k157 · CMA II.F.1.c(2) / 2027 II.F.1.d(3) · RMA I.D.1.c · CMAA 5 k65 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who is blind asks for the intake forms in a format she can use. What does the ADA require?
opciones: Auxiliary aids such as a qualified reader, large print, Braille or an electronic file
That the patient bring a family member who can read the paperwork aloud to her
That staff complete the forms from memory and have a witness sign them instead
That the visit be rescheduled until the office can order printed materials for her
preguntas.explicacion: Where they are needed for effective communication with someone whose disability affects vision, hearing or speech, auxiliary aids and services have to be provided by the covered entity, so that the communication works as well for her as it does for anybody else. For a person who is blind, has low vision or is deaf-blind, the aids named include a qualified reader, large print, Braille, an electronic file for a screen-reading program, and audio recordings.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Acute Ischemic Stroke", Introduction and Epidemiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(3) (2027 I.C.6.g(3)) · RMA I.A.2.a · CMAA 1 k10 · NCMA 1.10
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has the sudden onset of weakness on one side and slurred speech. Which condition does that pattern suggest?
opciones: Acute ischemic stroke, a sudden focal neurological deficit
Acute otitis media, a sudden focal neurological deficit
A transient rise in blood pressure with no neurological deficit
A migraine headache, which produces no focal neurological deficit
preguntas.explicacion: An ischemic stroke means focal neurological deficits appearing suddenly in the territory of one vessel, whether in the brain, the retina or the spinal cord. It is the commonest kind by far, about 87 percent of all strokes, and speed matters: the whole system of care exists to recognize it fast enough to restore blood flow.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms, entry Referral
preguntas.subtema: Referrals · CMAA 4G k67 · CCMA 5P k183 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: What is a referral in an insurance sense?
opciones: A written order from the primary care provider to see a specialist or get services
A written order from the specialist accepting the patient sent by another office
A plan decision that a specific service is medically necessary before it is given
A list of the specialists inside the plan's network sorted by their location
preguntas.explicacion: A referral is the written order the primary care provider gives so the patient can see a specialist or receive certain services, and in many health maintenance organizations the plan may refuse to pay without it. The plan's own finding that a service is medically necessary is preauthorization, and a sorted list of contracted specialists is a network directory.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(c)(1)(ii) and (c)(2)(i), Exposure Control Plan
preguntas.subtema: Exposure Control Plan contents · CPT D1 1H k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k109 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: Which element must a written Exposure Control Plan contain?
opciones: The exposure determination listing job classifications and tasks with occupational exposure
The sharps injury log, with the brand of each device and the department where it happened
The medical record of each exposed employee, including hepatitis B vaccination dates
The safety data sheet for every disinfectant used to decontaminate work surfaces
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (c)(1)(ii) names three required elements: the exposure determination of (c)(2), the schedule and method for implementing paragraphs (d) through (h), and the procedure for evaluating the circumstances of exposure incidents. The exposure determination lists job classifications where all or some employees are exposed and the tasks involved. The sharps injury log and the employee medical record are kept under paragraph (h) as separate records, and safety data sheets belong to the Hazard Communication standard at 29 CFR 1910.1200.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, Sections 2, 4, 6 and 8; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.151(c)
preguntas.subtema: Using the SDS in an emergency · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist splashes a disinfectant concentrate into her eye. Which section of the product's Safety Data Sheet gives the first-aid measures?
opciones: Section 4, First-Aid Measures, by route of exposure
Section 2, Hazard Identification and signal word
Section 8, Exposure Controls and Personal Protection
Section 6, Accidental Release and cleanup measures
preguntas.explicacion: Section 4 sets out the immediate care an untrained bystander can give, sorted by how the chemical got in: breathed in, onto the skin or into the eye, or swallowed, together with the main symptoms and any warning that a doctor is needed at once. Section 2 classifies the hazard and carries the signal word and pictograms; Section 8 lists exposure limits, engineering controls and the equipment to put on before handling; Section 6 covers containing and cleaning up a spill. For the eye itself the practical first step is the eyewash: 29 CFR 1910.151(c) demands equipment able to drench or flush the eyes and the body quickly, inside the work area, wherever workers may meet injurious corrosive materials.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), Other Prohibitions
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMAA 5 k77 · CCMA 5 k186 · CMA III.G.3.c
preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives in acute distress and staff want him to sign an advance written notice of non-coverage before treatment. What is wrong with that?
opciones: The notice may not be used to compel a patient in an emergency or under duress
The notice may not be used before treatment, only after the service is delivered
The notice may not be signed by the patient, only by a legal representative
The notice may not be used unless the coverage denial has already been received
preguntas.explicacion: Among the prohibitions, the notice may not be used to compel or force a patient under great duress or in a medical emergency; nor to shift liability for a service denied by a medically unlikely edit; nor to charge for part of a bundled payment. It is by definition given in advance, and the patient or a representative signs it, so those are not the flaws in this scene.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Issues of Concern: Audits and Risk Assessment; Risk Analysis
preguntas.subtema: Risk analysis is repeated · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k34
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic finished its security risk analysis two years ago and has bought new equipment since. What does the guidance say?
opciones: Repeat it regularly, and whenever practice or technology changes
Repeat it only after a breach has actually been discovered
Repeat it every six years, when the documentation is renewed
Treat the first one as final once the flaws found were fixed
preguntas.explicacion: The security requirements put their weight on risk analysis, and it is not a one-off exercise: the system in place is audited for flaws and gaps that threaten the confidentiality, the integrity or the security of health information; whatever turns up goes through the risk management process and gets corrected; and the analysis is run again at intervals, because technology keeps arriving and clinical practice keeps shifting. The six-year figure is how long the required documentation is kept.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, types of consent · CPT D2 2F k43 · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA II.E.3.a informed consent · RMA I.C.1.a consents · NCMA 4.7 · CMAA 3D k40
preguntas.pregunta: A thorough consent discussion is expected to cover all the relevant risks. Which set does it take in?
opciones: The general risks, those particular to this procedure, the risks of no treatment, and the alternatives
The general risks, those particular to this procedure, the cost to the patient, and the recovery time
The risks particular to this procedure only, since the general ones are printed on the facility's form
The risks particular to this procedure and those of the alternatives, with no treatment left out of it
preguntas.explicacion: Consent is not informed if the risk talk is narrow. It is expected to run across four fronts: what any intervention of this kind can bring, what this one in particular can bring, what follows if nothing is done at all, and what the reasonable alternatives carry with them. Declining care is itself an option that has to be weighed, so dropping it shortens the list. The forms promise nothing either: many say outright that the method proposed is not guaranteed to settle the problem. Cost and recovery time belong to the conversation about the visit, not to the risks this discussion has to cover.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, SOAP Notes, Subjective
preguntas.subtema: History of present illness · CCMA 3 k190 · CMA I.A.4 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA k4 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: In the OLDCARTS mnemonic for the history of present illness, which element does the patient rate on a scale of one to ten?
opciones: Severity
Onset
Duration
Radiation
preguntas.explicacion: The history of present illness opens with a single line giving how old the patient is, the sex and why they came, and is then laid out with OLDCARTS: onset, location, duration, character, alleviating and aggravating factors, radiation, temporal factors and severity. Severity is the element carrying a scale, one being the least and ten the worst. Radiation asks whether the symptom travels or stays put.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fighting Identity Theft with the Red Flags Rule: Identify Relevant Red Flags
preguntas.subtema: Identifying information red flags · CCMA 5F k190 · CMA III.H.2.b · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 5A k66 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A registration form arrives with required boxes empty, and the applicant ignores the notices saying it is incomplete. Which category of red flag covers that?
opciones: Personal identifying information
Suspicious documents presented
Account activity out of pattern
Notice from a law enforcement body
preguntas.explicacion: Under personal identifying information the guidance lists a person who leaves required information off an application and does not answer notices that it is incomplete, alongside addresses that conflict with the credit report, a number listed on the death file, and a person who cannot answer a challenge question.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.512(a) and (b)(1)(i)-(ii), Uses and disclosures required by law and for public health activities
preguntas.subtema: Public health disclosures · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7F k222 · CMA II.E.6 · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k37
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory reports a child's positive lead level to the state health department as state law requires. Under HIPAA this disclosure is which of these?
opciones: Permitted without authorization, as required by law and for public health
Permitted only with the parent's signed authorization
A breach that must be reported to the individual within 60 calendar days of discovery
Permitted only if the child is treated as an emancipated minor
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.512 lists uses and disclosures that need neither authorization nor an opportunity to object: those required by law, and those to a public health authority authorized to collect information to prevent or control disease, injury or disability, including disease reporting and surveillance; reports of child abuse or neglect to an authorized authority are in the same paragraph. Such a disclosure is not a breach. The parent's status as personal representative matters for access requests, not for a report the law compels.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms: Balance Billing
preguntas.subtema: Financial calculations · CMA III.G.8 (2027 III.G.6.b) · CMAA 4 k61, 6C k87 · CCMA 5L k185 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: An out-of-network provider charges $200 and the plan's allowed amount is $110. Beyond her cost sharing, what may he bill the patient?
opciones: Ninety dollars, the gap between what he charged and what the plan allows
A hundred and ten dollars, since the plan pays that sum straight to him
Twenty-two dollars, being twenty percent of the amount the plan allowed
Two hundred dollars, the whole charge, since no contract binds him to the plan
preguntas.explicacion: Balance billing is when a provider bills the patient for the balance the plan does not cover, meaning the difference between the amount actually billed and the allowed amount. The uniform glossary uses these figures as its example. It happens most often with out-of-network providers; a network provider may not balance bill for covered services.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Workplace Violence", Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: De-escalation · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k26 · CMA F.1.f / 2027 F.1.f
preguntas.pregunta: An agitated patient is taken to a safe assessment room. What has been reported about those rooms?
opciones: Most patients settle down there within about twenty minutes
Most patients there need physical restraint within the hour
They cut down verbal abuse but not physical aggression
They only help once an aggression team is already present
preguntas.explicacion: Safe assessment rooms improve the management of acutely agitated patients, and most of those patients calm down inside about twenty minutes. Taking a patient to an available room early is listed as an opportunity to defuse tension that should be seized. Restraint is a last resort, not the expected outcome of the room.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Workplace Violence", Introduction; and Epidemiology
preguntas.subtema: Difficult situations · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k16
preguntas.pregunta: Which form of workplace violence is reported most often in health care?
opciones: Verbal abuse, more common than physical assault
Physical abuse, reported by nearly all the staff
Sexual harassment, the most reported form overall
Property damage, which precedes the other forms
preguntas.explicacion: Violence is split by the nature of the aggression into physical, verbal and psychological forms, the psychological ones taking in bullying, intimidation and sexual harassment. Inside the professional environment, verbal abuse is the commonest form of all. Close to twenty percent of health care workers have met physical abuse.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fighting Identity Theft with the Red Flags Rule: Prevent And Mitigate Identity Theft
preguntas.subtema: Responding to a red flag · CCMA 5F k190 · CMA III.H.2.b · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 5A k66 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A red flag turns up on a patient account and the office has to respond. Which response does the Red Flags guidance offer as an example?
opciones: Reopening the account under a new number, or holding off on collection for now
Reopening the account under a new number, or closing the record to the patient
Referring the account to a debt collector so the balance is chased independently
Freezing the patient's chart until a police report about the account is filed
preguntas.explicacion: The examples of an appropriate response run from watching the account for evidence of theft, changing the passwords or codes that reach it and reopening it with a new number, to declining to pursue collection or to sell the account to a collector, and, in some circumstances, deciding that no response is called for. A recent breach argues for a stronger response.

preguntas.subtema: Retention exceptions · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA II.B.5.c · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which record is exempt from the long retention period of the OSHA access standard?
opciones: A one-time treatment of a minor cut, if it is kept apart from the medical program
A record of exposure monitoring, once the substance is no longer used in the office
A record belonging to an employee who has left, once the final pay has been issued
A safety data sheet, once the product it describes has been taken off the shelves
preguntas.explicacion: The employee medical record is preserved for the length of employment plus thirty years, with narrow exceptions: health insurance claim files kept separately, first aid records of one-time treatment of minor injuries made on site by a non-physician and kept separately, and the records of employees who worked under a year if handed to them on leaving.

preguntas.subtema: Workstation use · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A policy states which programs may be run at the front desk computer, how they are to be used and how the desk is laid out. Which standard is that?
opciones: Workstation use, which sets the functions, the manner of use and the surroundings
Workstation security, the physical guard that limits a machine to authorized users
Access control, the technical limit on who may open which record in the system
Facility access controls, which limit physical entry to where the systems are kept
preguntas.explicacion: Two standards sit side by side. Workstation use calls for policies covering which functions are proper, the manner of carrying them out, and what the physical surroundings of a workstation, or of a class of workstations, should look like. Workstation security is the narrower one: the physical measures that keep an unauthorized person away from the machine.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Skeletal System: Divisions of the Skeleton; and SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology: Appendicular Skeleton
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(2) (2027 I.C.6.f(2)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: How many bones are in the axial skeleton and how many in the appendicular skeleton?
opciones: 80 axial and 126 appendicular
126 axial and 80 appendicular
106 axial and 100 appendicular
60 axial and 146 appendicular
preguntas.explicacion: The skeleton splits in two. The axial part, with 80 bones, is the skull, hyoid, vertebral column and thoracic cage. The appendicular part, with 126, is the limbs plus the pectoral and pelvic girdles that anchor them. The two together give the adult total of 206.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, FAQ 580: Medical record retention
preguntas.subtema: Safeguards through disposal · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: A practice is shredding charts that state law no longer requires it to keep. Does the Privacy Rule have anything to say about that moment?
opciones: Yes, its safeguards run for as long as the information is held, disposal included
No, its safeguards end on the day the state retention period runs out for a chart
Yes, but only if the practice is destroying more than 500 records at one time
No, because destroying a record is a health care operation and needs no safeguard
preguntas.explicacion: HIPAA fixes no retention period for the clinical record itself; State law does. What the Privacy Rule demands is safeguards, administrative and technical and physical, for however long the covered entity holds the information, and it counts disposal as part of that stretch.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Respiratory System: Conducting Passages
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(5) (2027 I.C.6.f(5)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which structures make up the upper respiratory tract and which the lower?
opciones: Nose, pharynx and larynx above; trachea, bronchial tree and lungs below
Nose, pharynx and trachea above; larynx, bronchial tree and lungs below
Nose and pharynx above; larynx, trachea, bronchial tree and lungs below
Nose, larynx and trachea above; pharynx, bronchial tree and lungs below
preguntas.explicacion: The conducting passages split into an upper tract of nose, pharynx and larynx and a lower tract of trachea, bronchial tree and lungs. All of them communicate with the outside air and carry a mucous membrane lining, with hairs in some regions to filter the air and cilia in others to move mucus along.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Clinical Significance: Patient Rights under HIPAA
preguntas.subtema: Asking for a correction · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reads her record and says one entry is wrong. What right does she have?
opciones: To ask for a correction, which the provider may accept or deny
To have the entry deleted within thirty days of the request
To have the entry rewritten by the clinician who made it
To bill the provider for the time spent finding the mistake
preguntas.explicacion: Among the rights the privacy rule gives are the right to a notice of privacy practices, to ask that disclosures be restricted, to say how information should be handled and communicated, to inspect and review one's own information and request a change to anything that looks wrong, to obtain a copy, to receive an accounting of disclosures, and to complain to the Office for Civil Rights. The request for a change is a request: the provider may accept or deny it, and a documented diagnosis a patient dislikes is not erased for that reason.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0, Tool: Two-Challenge Rule
preguntas.subtema: Escalation · CCMA 6K k210 · CMAA 2B k25
preguntas.pregunta: A safety concern has been taken up the chain of command. What does the rule still require?
opciones: Telling the whole team that further input has been sought
Repeating the same concern a third time to the same person
Letting the colleague who was challenged answer it first
Holding any further action until the supervisor arrives
preguntas.explicacion: Turning to the supervisor is meant to overcome the natural tendency to assume the team leader must know what they are doing even when the plan departs from guidelines. When the rule is invoked and the concern moves up, it is essential to let the whole medical team know that additional input has been sought.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Billing: CMS-1500 & 837P (MLN006976), Coding & Billing Dates of Service
preguntas.subtema: Claim submission · CMA III.G.3.b(1) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6C k87, 6 k85 · CCMA 5L k185
preguntas.pregunta: A service begins one evening and ends the following morning. What does the billing rule say?
opciones: Bill it once it is complete, using the start day or the next one
Bill it twice, once on each of the two calendar dates it spans
Bill it on the day it started, before the service has finished
Bill it on the day the note about it is signed by the provider
preguntas.explicacion: For a service spanning two calendar dates, either the day it started or the day it concluded may be reported unless the instructions say otherwise, and the claim waits until the service is complete. Splitting it into two claims would report work that was done once as though it had been done twice.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), File Proper & Timely Claims
preguntas.subtema: Insurance fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 5 k180
preguntas.pregunta: What can follow from repeatedly giving Medicare inaccurate information about a patient's other health coverage?
opciones: A fine, where the inaccurate information is given knowingly, willfully and repeatedly
A fine, wherever the inaccurate information leads Medicare to pay as the primary payer
Exclusion from the program, where the inaccurate information is given more than once
Recovery of the payment alone, since the responsibility rests with the primary payer
preguntas.explicacion: Federal law lets Medicare take back what it paid wrongly as the primary payer, and the provider has to give it up. On top of that, a provider who gives inaccurate information about a patient's other health insurance coverage knowingly, willfully and repeatedly can be fined. Recovery may also be pursued directly from a primary payer, from another entity or from a third payer.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, HETS EDI: How to Enroll
preguntas.subtema: Insurance eligibility verification · CMAA 4 k58 · CCMA 5E · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: An office gets no answer back when it checks Medicare eligibility electronically. Which detail must be on file for the HETS system?
opciones: A HETS enrollment for the provider's National Provider Identifier
A HETS enrollment for the patient's own Medicare Beneficiary Identifier
A signed release of information from the patient for every eligibility check
A paper claim already on file with the Medicare Administrative Contractor
preguntas.explicacion: Providers, suppliers, vendors and clearinghouses enroll in the electronic data interchange for the eligibility system, and every National Provider Identifier submitted for an eligibility check needs an enrollment on file. The enrollment also asks for the Provider Transaction Access Number and for the vendor or clearinghouse relationship. Patients are not enrolled, no release is required for the check, and no prior claim is needed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hypothyroidism", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(9) (2027 I.C.6.g(9)) · RMA I.A.2.a · CMAA 1 k10 · NCMA 1.10
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports cold intolerance, dry skin, constipation, fatigue and weight gain. Which laboratory pattern would confirm the suspected diagnosis?
opciones: A high TSH with a low free T4
A low TSH with a high free T4
A high TSH with a high free T4
A low TSH with a low free T4
preguntas.explicacion: Those complaints point to hypothyroidism, and the serum TSH is the first test. In primary hypothyroidism the gland cannot keep up, so free T4 falls and the pituitary pushes TSH up. When TSH is raised but free T4 is still normal, the picture is subclinical. Symptoms are mild and nonspecific often enough that the labs, not the story, settle it.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Findings and Denial Volume
preguntas.subtema: Revenue cycle phases · CMAA 6 k81, 6E · CCMA 5M k181
preguntas.pregunta: Why is a claim denial expensive beyond the unpaid service itself?
opciones: Staff time to rework and appeal it adds administrative cost and delays the cash
The payer charges the practice a fee for each claim it has to deny in a year
The patient's coinsurance must be refunded whenever a claim ends up denied
The practice must return the contractual adjustment already posted to the account
preguntas.explicacion: Revenue cycle management done well is described as cutting denials, shortening the gap between submission and payment, and bringing down what it costs administratively to bill and to process denials, which is where the extra cost of a denial sits. Payers do not bill practices for denying claims, the patient's share is not refunded automatically, and a contractual adjustment is a write-off recorded at posting.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, FAQ: What is a patient portal?
preguntas.subtema: Portal self-scheduling · CCMA 5U k172 · CMA III.H.1 (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.B.2.a · CMAA 4E k56 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which task can some patient portals let a patient perform, beyond viewing information?
opciones: Scheduling a non-urgent appointment and requesting a prescription refill
Correcting a diagnosis in the chart directly, without asking the practice
Opening the records of a family member who uses the same practice
Canceling a claim the practice has already submitted to the health plan
preguntas.explicacion: Some portals do more than display: they let the patient send a secure message to the doctor, ask for a prescription refill, book appointments that are not urgent, look up benefits and coverage, change contact details, pay a bill, download forms and fill them in, and read educational material. ONC presents the portal as a way of saving time and keeping care going between visits.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, General Compliance Program Guidance (2023), Element 2: Compliance Leadership and Oversight
preguntas.subtema: Auditing and compliance · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: Where does the OIG guidance say the compliance officer should sit in an entity's reporting structure?
opciones: Reporting to the chief executive with independent access to the board, or to the board
Reporting to the billing manager, who sees every claim before it leaves the office
Reporting to the entity's outside counsel, who then directs any investigation there is
Reporting to the human resources director, who imposes the consequences on staff
preguntas.explicacion: Compliance leadership and oversight is the second element, and every entity should designate a compliance officer carrying the authority, the stature, the access and the resources the role needs. That officer should report either to the board itself or to the chief executive, in the latter case with access to the board that is direct and independent, and should stand as an equal among the other senior leaders.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Faxes
preguntas.subtema: Fax safeguards · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k38
preguntas.pregunta: Which safeguard applies when faxing protected health information?
opciones: Keep the fax machine in a secure area and use a cover page saying what to do if misdirected
Place the fax machine at the reception desk so that staff can retrieve incoming pages quickly
Send faxes overnight so that they arrive before the office opens and are not seen
Confirm receipt by mailing a paper duplicate of every fax to the recipient on the same day
preguntas.explicacion: The machine lives somewhere secure, out of reach of the public, of patients and of most staff. The first page is a disclaimer telling whoever receives it what to do if the fax landed on the wrong number. Faxes go out during working hours except in an emergency, so that someone picks them up instead of leaving them in the tray, and the sender then contacts the other party to confirm the pages were collected. A machine at reception and overnight transmissions both leave PHI sitting in the open, and mailing a duplicate adds a second disclosure rather than a confirmation.

preguntas.fuente: NHA Candidate Handbook (2026), Reinstatement
preguntas.subtema: Professional development · CCMA 7C · RMA I.C.4.e · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: A certification expired eight months ago. What does getting it back require?
opciones: Fifteen continuing education credits, plus recertification and reinstatement fees
Ten continuing education credits, plus the recertification fee for that cycle
Re-registering, retaking the examination and paying the full examination price
Twenty continuing education credits, plus a written appeal to the certifying body
preguntas.explicacion: Reinstatement is allowed within one year of the expiration date, and it takes evidence of fifteen continuing education credits — twenty hours for pharmacy technicians — together with the recertification fees and the reinstatement fees. Once more than a year has passed, reinstatement is off the table and the person must re-register, sit the exam again and pay full price.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Formative Feedback
preguntas.subtema: Coaching and feedback · CCMA 6L k203 · CMAA 2F k21 · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas.pregunta: A team member is given feedback after missing a step. Which feature does formative feedback require?
opciones: It stays on the behavior instead of the person's attributes
It is saved for the annual review so that it carries weight
It lists everything that went wrong over the whole shift
It comes from the team leader only and never from a peer
preguntas.explicacion: Formative feedback is shared to improve performance and should be appreciative, timely, respectful, specific, aimed at improvement, considerate and focused on the patient. Respectful is defined as keeping to behaviors rather than personal attributes, and timely means soon after the behavior, which rules out saving it for a yearly review.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, Patient Identity and Patient Record Matching
preguntas.subtema: Duplicate records · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.2.a · RMA II.B.4.a · CMAA 4D k57 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Two records appear to belong to the same woman, one under her maiden name. Which process is meant to resolve that?
opciones: Patient matching, which links a person's data by comparing several demographic fields
Accounting of disclosures, which lists everyone the practice has sent her records to
An amendment request, which lets the patient ask that an incorrect entry be corrected
De-identification, which strips the identifiers so the two files can be compared safely
preguntas.explicacion: ONC defines patient matching as the work of identifying a single patient's data and linking it, inside a health system and across several. The minimum method is to link a handful of demographic fields, and the ones named are name, birth date, telephone number and address. ONC treats it as a cornerstone of interoperability and of the country's health IT infrastructure.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP); and CMS, Medicaid.gov: CHIP
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.c / 2027 III.G.4
preguntas.pregunta: A family earns too much for Medicaid but cannot afford private insurance for their children. Which program is meant for them?
opciones: CHIP, which covers children in that income range and is run by each state
COBRA, which continues children's coverage in that income range for a time
Medigap, which supplements children's coverage while the parents apply
Medicare Part C, which enrolls children whose parents lack job-based coverage
preguntas.explicacion: The Children's Health Insurance Program covers children in families that earn too much for Medicaid yet too little to buy private coverage; the states run it under federal requirements and share the funding with the federal government, and in some states it reaches pregnant women too. Applications are taken at any point in the year. COBRA continues employer coverage, Medigap supplements Original Medicare, and Medicare Advantage is Medicare coverage.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, What Part B covers: Insulin benefit
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74, 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient uses an insulin pump covered under the Part B equipment benefit. What is the most she pays for a month's supply of that insulin?
opciones: Thirty-five dollars, and the yearly Part B deductible is not applied to it
Thirty-five dollars, but only once she has met the yearly Part B deductible
Twenty percent of the approved amount, as for other equipment and supplies
One hundred and five dollars, the ceiling set for one month's covered supply
preguntas.explicacion: Where insulin is covered through the Part B durable medical equipment benefit for a pump, or through a Medicare Advantage Plan, the cost of a month's supply cannot exceed thirty-five dollars and the Part B deductible does not apply. A three-month supply is capped at thirty-five dollars for each month, so generally no more than a hundred and five dollars in all.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Claim Denial Rate
preguntas.subtema: Precertification · CMA III.G.5.a(1) (2027 III.G.5.a(1)) · CMAA 4G · CCMA 5H k183 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: The surgeon changed the procedure on the day of surgery and the authorization still names the old one. What is the warning about fixing that afterwards?
opciones: Some payers will change an authorization only up to fourteen days after the service
Some payers will change an authorization only up to sixty days after the service
No payer will change an authorization once the service has already been provided
Every payer has to reopen the authorization when the record justifies the change
preguntas.explicacion: Where the procedure billed is not the procedure authorized, the advice is to put the information right before the claim goes out, or to justify the discrepancy with solid reasons. A changed code on a service that needed authorization has to be dealt with at once: some payers will not touch an authorization more than fourteen days past the date of service, and after that the denial is likely to be permanent.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, What Part B covers
preguntas.subtema: Insurance types · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what Part B is for in the broadest terms. Which two categories of service does it cover?
opciones: Medically necessary services and preventive services
Medically necessary services and long-term custodial care
Preventive services and inpatient hospital admissions
Preventive services and skilled nursing facility stays
preguntas.explicacion: Part B covers two kinds of thing. Medically necessary services or supplies are those meeting accepted standards of medical practice for diagnosing or treating the patient's condition. Preventive services are the care meant to head off illness or catch it early, when treatment is likeliest to work, and most of them cost the patient nothing when the provider accepts assignment. Inpatient hospital and skilled nursing stays belong to Part A.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 6A, 5 k68 · CCMA 5I k184 · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives for same-day surgery and the surgeon calls it off that morning because of a contraindication. Which diagnosis is listed first?
opciones: The condition the surgery was meant to treat, which is the reason for the encounter
The contraindication that stopped the surgery, which is what the visit finally found
The postoperative diagnosis the surgeon expected, as the more definitive of the two
A code for the surgery that was called off, with the condition added as secondary
preguntas.explicacion: In the outpatient setting the first-listed diagnosis is the reason for the encounter, and for same-day surgery that is the condition the surgery was scheduled to treat. The guideline keeps it first even when the surgery is not carried out because of a contraindication. The postoperative diagnosis rule belongs to surgeries that actually take place.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Closed-Loop Communication
preguntas.subtema: Structured communication · CCMA 6F k198 · CMAA 2E k23 · CMA F.4.c / 2027 F.2.c
preguntas.pregunta: A provider asks the assistant to send a pamphlet and book a follow-up; the assistant restates the task and the provider confirms. Which strategy is that?
opciones: A check-back, which closes the loop on the message
A call-out, which informs the whole team at once
A teach-back, which confirms a patient understood
A handoff, which transfers responsibility for care
preguntas.explicacion: A check-back is the closed-loop strategy for making sure what the sender conveyed is what the receiver understood: the receiver repeats it and the sender confirms. A call-out broadcasts to everyone at once, a teach-back checks a patient or family member, and a handoff moves responsibility between caregivers.

preguntas.fuente: NHA Candidate Handbook (2026), Recertification; and Reinstatement
preguntas.subtema: Professional development · CCMA 7C · RMA I.C.4.e · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: A professional submits the continuing education documents three weeks after the expiration date. What is the position?
opciones: Still inside the one-month grace period the certifying body allows
Outside the deadline, so reinstatement fees are now due as well
Outside the deadline, so the credential is nullified permanently
Still valid, because documents are accepted for a year afterwards
preguntas.explicacion: Documentation of the ten credits and the fees can be submitted annually or all at once before the certification expires, and a one-month grace period is allowed. Failing to meet the requirement before the expiration date nullifies the credential, but reinstatement stays open for a year, with fifteen credits plus recertification and reinstatement fees.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.524(c)(3)(ii), Time and manner of access
preguntas.subtema: Sending records to a third party · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.2.a(5) · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks that a copy of her records be sent directly to another physician. What does HIPAA require of that request?
opciones: That it be written, signed, and clearly name the recipient and where to send it
That the receiving physician sign a business associate agreement before records are sent
That the patient collect the records in person and deliver them herself
That the request be approved by the privacy official within 15 days
preguntas.explicacion: Under 164.524(c)(3)(ii), where the individual directs that the copy go to somebody else, the entity must send it to that person; the individual has to put the request in writing and sign it, naming who is to receive it and saying where the copy should be sent. The 30-day clock runs as it does for any access request. A business associate agreement covers entities working on the covered entity's behalf, not a physician the patient has chosen to receive her own records.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule, Individual Notice
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics · CPT D1 1C k13 · CCMA 7F reportable incidents · CMAA 3E k44 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A laptop holding unencrypted patient results is stolen from a laboratory courier's car. How soon must the affected individuals be notified?
opciones: With no unreasonable delay, and at the latest 60 days after the breach is discovered
With no unreasonable delay, and at the latest 30 days after the breach is discovered
With no unreasonable delay, and at the latest 90 days after the breach is discovered
Within 60 days after the close of the calendar year in which the breach came to light
preguntas.explicacion: Individual notice goes out without unreasonable delay and never later than 60 days after discovery, in writing by first-class mail or by email if the person agreed to that. It must describe the breach, the types of information involved, what people should do to protect themselves, and what the entity is doing about it. The year-end deadline applies to reporting small breaches to the Secretary.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 3, III Glossary
preguntas.subtema: Bias and stereotypes · CCMA 6B k193 · CMAA 2C k17 · RMA I.D.2.b
preguntas.pregunta: Which term names the belief that one's own culture is better than another's?
opciones: Ethnocentrism, rating one's own culture above others
Stereotyping, assigning group traits to an individual
Prejudice, a preconceived and unfavorable judgment
Discrimination, unfair treatment that denies rights
preguntas.explicacion: Ethnocentrism is holding one's own culture, race, ethnicity or country to be preferable to another's. Stereotyping assumes a person carries the attributes and values of a group because they belong to it, prejudice is prejudging, and discrimination is the unfair treatment that denies people rights and opportunities.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.524(c)(2) and (c)(4), Provision of access; Fees
preguntas.subtema: Fees for copies · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: What may a covered entity charge a patient for a copy of her records under HIPAA?
opciones: A reasonable cost-based fee covering labor, supplies, postage and any agreed summary
A flat retrieval fee set by the facility plus a per-page charge at any rate
No fee at all, in any format, since access is a federal right
A fee equal to the cost of the original test, since the results are being duplicated
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.524(c)(4) allows only a reasonable, cost-based fee limited to the labor of copying, the supplies for paper or portable electronic media, postage when the individual asks for mailing, and the preparation of a summary or explanation the individual agreed to in advance. The copy must be provided in the form and format requested if readily producible, including electronic form for electronically held records. Retrieval charges and the cost of the underlying test are not on the list.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Drug plan rules
preguntas.subtema: Medication authorization · CMAA 4G k67 · CCMA 5H k183 · CMA III.G.5.a(2) · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: A drug plan will pay for the medication only after the patient has tried a cheaper one first. What is this rule called?
opciones: Step therapy, a form of prior authorization used by drug plans
Quantity limits, the cap a drug plan sets on the amount it covers
Tiering, the way a drug plan sorts covered drugs by cost sharing
Medication therapy management, the plan's review for complex needs
preguntas.explicacion: Step therapy is described as a type of prior authorization: the patient first tries a less expensive drug on the plan's list that works for most people with the condition, and only then moves up a step. Quantity limits cap how much the plan covers over a period, tiers set different cost sharing by drug group, and medication therapy management is a service for patients with complex needs.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: Technical Safeguards
preguntas.subtema: Audit controls · CCMA 5 k189 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A supervisor wants to find out who opened a particular chart last Tuesday. Which technical safeguard makes that possible?
opciones: Audit controls, the mechanisms that record and examine system activity
Authentication, the procedure that verifies who is seeking the access
Integrity controls, the measures confirming ePHI was not altered
Transmission security, the measures guarding data crossing a network
preguntas.explicacion: Audit controls are mechanisms, in hardware, in software or in procedure, that capture and review what happens inside information systems holding or using ePHI. Authentication is the separate standard for confirming that whoever seeks access is who they claim to be; integrity controls establish that no ePHI was altered or destroyed improperly; transmission security guards data on the move across a network.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Introduction to the Digestive System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(6) (2027 I.C.6.f(6)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which organs form the digestive tract itself, and which are the major accessory organs?
opciones: Mouth to large intestine form the tract; liver, pancreas, gallbladder and salivary glands assist
Mouth to large intestine form the tract; kidneys, spleen, thymus and appendix assist
Liver, gallbladder and pancreas form the tract; mouth, stomach and intestines assist
Stomach and intestines alone form the tract; mouth, pharynx and esophagus assist
preguntas.explicacion: The digestive tract, or alimentary canal, is one continuous tube from mouth to anus: after the mouth come the pharynx and the esophagus, then the stomach, then the small intestine and the large one. The salivary glands and the liver, the gallbladder and the pancreas are the major accessory organs; they pour fluids into that tube without being part of it.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Fee for service; and StatPearls, "Reimbursement Models and Accountable Care", Summary
preguntas.subtema: Payment models · CMAA 6 k82 · CCMA 1 k6 · CMA III.G.4 (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Under fee-for-service payment, how is a provider paid?
opciones: A separate payment is earned for each service performed, such as a test or a visit
A single payment covers the whole episode, regardless of the tests or visits it needs
A fixed amount per enrolled patient per month covers all the services they use
A payment is earned only when the quality measures for the year are met in full
preguntas.explicacion: Fee for service pays doctors and other providers for each service delivered, office visits and tests among them, so the payment follows the volume of work. A fixed amount per patient per month is capitation, which pushes cost control onto the provider, and paying against quality measures is the pay-for-performance idea behind value-based programs. A single bundled amount per episode is a prospective payment, not fee for service.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Administrative Simplification: Transactions Overview
preguntas.subtema: Authorizations · CMAA 4G k67, 6C k87 · CCMA 5H k183 · RMA II.A.4 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which HIPAA standard transaction covers the request a provider sends a plan for a referral or an authorization?
opciones: The referrals and authorizations transaction adopted by HHS under the law
The claims and encounter information transaction adopted by HHS under the law
The premium payment transaction, used between the employer and the plan
The coordination of benefits transaction, used between two health plans
preguntas.explicacion: Referrals and authorizations is one of the electronic transactions HHS adopted under HIPAA, and covered entities that conduct it electronically must use the adopted standard. Claims and encounter information carries the bill for services already given, premium payment moves money for coverage between the employer and the plan, and coordination of benefits exchanges the data payers need to decide who pays first.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Part B (Medical Insurance) costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74, 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient asks what she will owe for the covered blood work her physician ordered at the office.
opciones: Nothing, because covered clinical laboratory services carry no charge under Part B
Twenty percent of the approved amount, as with most other services under Part B
The yearly deductible first, and twenty percent of the approved amount after that
Five percent of the approved amount, the share that inpatient respite care carries
preguntas.explicacion: The Part B cost table puts covered clinical laboratory services at nothing for the patient, alongside covered home health care services. The twenty percent coinsurance applies to most other Part B services and items once the yearly deductible is met, and durable medical equipment such as a wheelchair or walker carries that same twenty percent.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Abandonment, Nursing, Allied Health, and Interprofessional Team Interventions
preguntas.subtema: Notice period · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.b · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who keeps missing visits is being dismissed, and the nearest other clinician is sixty miles away. How does that affect the notice?
opciones: It can stretch the usual thirty days, since ninety may be needed where care is far away
It shortens the usual thirty days, since distance is not something the guidance weighs
It leaves the period alone, because the patient's insurer is the one that sets it
It removes the notice, because the practice cannot name a replacement within reach
preguntas.explicacion: Thirty days between the notice and the end of care is often treated as reasonable, but the time that counts as reasonable can be longer where replacement care is hard to reach, and up to ninety days may be needed when no other clinician is within reasonable driving distance. Rural patients are the example given. State rules on the number of days come first.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Home health services: Provider requirements
preguntas.subtema: Referral coordination · CCMA 4E · CMA II.F.4.a / 2027 II.F.2.a · CMAA 2H k30
preguntas.pregunta: A provider hands a patient a list of home health agencies serving her area. What else must the provider disclose?
opciones: Whether any agency on the list is one the provider's organization has an interest in
Whether the agency has been accredited by an organization holding deemed status
Whether the patient has any days left in the current skilled nursing benefit period
Whether the agency employs a hospice medical director for the plan of care
preguntas.explicacion: When the provider decides a patient needs home health, the patient receives a list of agencies serving her area, and the provider must say whether the organization holds a financial interest in any agency on it. After the referral the agency schedules a visit to discuss needs, then talks with the provider about the care plan and keeps that provider updated on progress.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting started with telehealth, Types of telehealth
preguntas.subtema: Store and forward · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A scheduler is asked which everyday exchanges count as store-and-forward telehealth. Which set is listed under that heading?
opciones: Messages carrying follow-up instructions, images forwarded for review, results and vitals
Messages carrying follow-up instructions, live video visits, and triage by telephone
Images sent for review, results and vitals, and a live call with an interpreter on the line
Messages with appointment reminders, a live video visit, and a wearable reporting continuously
preguntas.explicacion: Store and forward, the asynchronous kind, covers what providers, patients and caregivers send one another at different moments rather than at the same time. The examples listed are images forwarded for review, laboratory results and vital statistics, and messaging that carries follow-up instructions or confirmations.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 7: Improve your telephone system
preguntas.subtema: Telephone etiquette · CCMA 6C k196 · CMAA 2A k27 · NCMA F.23
preguntas.pregunta: A practice is recording the message that plays once the office has closed. What has to be in it?
opciones: To call 911 in an emergency, and the covering clinician's number
The hours the office closes for lunch on each day of the week
The address of the nearest emergency department and its entrance
A request to use secure email rather than wait for a call back
preguntas.explicacion: An after-hours message, or a service covering the phones, has to tell callers to dial 911 in an emergency and give a number for the clinician on call, said twice and slowly so it can be written down. A separate message covers the hours the office is closed for lunch.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Health Maintenance Organization (HMO)
preguntas.subtema: Commercial plan types · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.e (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient enrolled in an HMO asks whether her plan will pay for a specialist in another state who does not belong to the plan. What is the correct answer?
opciones: It generally pays nothing for that visit, because the care is outside the network
It pays a smaller share of that visit, because the specialist is outside the network
It pays the visit in full once her primary care doctor signs a written referral
It pays the visit in full once she has met the yearly deductible of her plan
preguntas.explicacion: An HMO usually restricts coverage to physicians employed by the plan or under contract with it, and it will not pay for care outside that group except in an emergency. Paying a reduced share for outside providers is what a PPO does. A referral changes which specialist she may see inside the network, and the deductible changes how much she owes, not whether an outside provider is covered at all.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Minimum Necessary Requirement, How the Rule Works
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, confidentiality · CPT D1 1C k13 · CCMA 7E k220 · RMA I.C.5 comply with HIPAA · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: In which of these situations does the minimum necessary standard NOT apply?
opciones: A physician requests the chart from another provider so she can treat the patient
A laboratory sends a monthly utilization summary to the practice that ordered tests
A supervisor pulls a record to check that the collection procedure was followed
A billing clerk asks the laboratory for the diagnosis codes attached to a claim
preguntas.explicacion: Minimum necessary is the default, and the exceptions make a short list: disclosures to, or requests by, a provider for treatment; disclosures to the person the information is about; uses made under that person's own authorization; disclosures to HHS for enforcement; and uses that the law requires, or that the rest of HIPAA's administrative simplification rules require. Everything else, internal quality work and billing included, is held to the minimum.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Timeliness
preguntas.subtema: Access extension · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: The records the patient asked for are archived offsite and cannot be pulled in time. What may the office do?
opciones: Take one extension of up to 30 more days, telling her in writing why and when she will get them
Take as many extensions as the retrieval needs, so long as each one is documented internally
Take one extension of up to 60 more days, the period the rule gives for amendment requests
Deny the request outright, since information that is not readily accessible falls outside access
preguntas.explicacion: Where the entity cannot make the 30 days, OCR's own example is this very situation: information archived offsite and not readily reachable. One extension is possible, of 30 further days at most, and inside the original 30 the individual has to be told in writing why it is late and on what date access will come. Only one extension per request is allowed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Tort in Healthcare", Issues of Concern; StatPearls, "Medical Malpractice", Referrals
preguntas.subtema: Respondeat superior · CPT D1 1D · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7A k221 · CMA II.E.4.c · RMA I.C.1.c · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k31
preguntas.pregunta: Under which doctrine is a supervising physician or employer held liable for the acts of an employee working within the scope of employment?
opciones: Respondeat superior, a form of vicarious liability
Strict liability, applied to inherently dangerous activities
Proportional liability, apportioned by degree of fault
Sovereign immunity, which limits awards against governments
preguntas.explicacion: Vicarious liability makes an employer answer for torts its employees commit inside the scope of their work, on the reasoning that the employer is better placed to absorb the loss. That is why a suit against a midlevel provider practicing under a physician's license is aimed at the supervising physician, and respondeat superior is the doctrine that puts it there. Proportional liability instead trims an award by the claimant's own share of fault, strict liability covers dangerous activities and defective drugs or devices, and sovereign immunity caps what can be recovered from governmental bodies.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(f), Standard: Deceased individuals; 164.502(g)(4)
preguntas.subtema: PHI of deceased individuals · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k219 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.4 · CMAA 3B k39
preguntas.pregunta: How long after a patient's death does HIPAA continue to protect their health information?
opciones: For 50 years after death
For 6 years after death
For 30 years after death
Indefinitely, with no time limit
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.502(f) requires a covered entity to comply with the Privacy Rule for the PHI of a deceased individual for 50 years following the death; the 2013 Omnibus Rule changed the protection from indefinite to this fixed period. During that time an executor, administrator or other person with authority over the estate is treated as the personal representative. Six years is the retention period for HIPAA documentation, and employment plus 30 years is the OSHA rule for employee medical records.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow, Conducting telehealth visits
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth intake · CCMA 5R k190 · CMA III.H.2.a · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 5 k80 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A video visit has just been confirmed and the intake step begins. Which information does the workflow guidance have a staff member review and collect there?
opciones: Identity, symptoms, medical history and, where it fits, the patient's vital signs
Identity, symptoms, medical history and the reading of the consent to the visit
Insurance, symptoms, medical history and the patient's preferred pharmacy details
Identity, symptoms, the reason for the visit and the feedback on the last session
preguntas.explicacion: The visit opens with confirmation, which pins down who the patient is and why she has come. Intake follows, and there a staff member goes over and gathers what is needed: verification of identity, the symptoms, the medical history and, where it fits, the vital signs. Consent and the online forms sit among the steps taken before the appointment; evaluation comes after it.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Quality Measures: What are Quality Measures?
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k159 clinical quality measures · CMAA 3 compliance
preguntas.pregunta: What do clinical quality measures measure?
opciones: Processes of care, outcomes, what patients perceive, and the structure of the organization
Health care processes and outcomes only, since perceptions cannot be quantified
Provider productivity and the revenue each visit generates for the practice
Patient satisfaction scores only, gathered after each completed encounter
preguntas.explicacion: Quality measures are tools for quantifying processes, outcomes, what patients perceive, and the structure or systems of an organization, all of it tied to the ability to deliver high-quality care. The goals behind them are care that is safe, effective, timely, efficient, equitable and centered on the patient.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(c)(1)(v) and (c)(1)(vi), Exposure Control Plan
preguntas.subtema: Employee input on safer devices · CPT D1 k12 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k109 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital is selecting a new safety needle. Whose input does the Exposure Control Plan have to document?
opciones: Non-managerial employees who give direct patient care and could be injured by contaminated sharps
The evaluating healthcare professional who provides the written opinions after exposure incidents
The laboratory director or whichever responsible person is named on the biohazard warning signs
The Assistant Secretary and the Director, who may examine and copy the plan on request
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (c)(1)(v), added after the Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act, tells the employer to ask the workers who give direct patient care and are not managers, the ones exposed to sharps injuries, what they think when engineering and work practice controls are identified, evaluated and chosen, and to leave that consultation documented in the plan. The evaluating professional writes opinions under (f)(5); the responsible person appears on the (g)(1)(ii) signs for HIV and HBV laboratories; and the Assistant Secretary and the Director get access under (c)(1)(vi), which is not a say in choosing a device.

preguntas.subtema: Maintenance records · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.5.b · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: After a break-in the practice replaces the back door and its lock. Which addressable specification asks for that work to be documented?
opciones: Maintenance records, for repairs and changes to the parts of the building tied to security
Facility security plan, for keeping the premises and the equipment safe from tampering
Contingency operations, for reaching the building when information has to be restored
Access control and validation, for checking entry by role and for controlling visitors
preguntas.explicacion: Facility access controls carry four addressable specifications. Three of them plan access; the fourth, maintenance records, is about paperwork: policies to document repairs and modifications to physical components related to security, such as hardware, walls, doors and locks.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule, De-Identified Health Information
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, confidentiality · CMAA 3C k36 · CCMA 7E k220
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory wants to publish counts of abnormal results for a quality project. What does the Privacy Rule say about de-identified health information?
opciones: There are no restrictions on its use or disclosure once it is genuinely de-identified
It may be used inside the organization but never released outside it in any form
It still requires a signed authorization from each patient whose result is counted
It may be released only under a business associate agreement with the recipient
preguntas.explicacion: Information that neither identifies a person nor gives a reasonable basis for identifying one falls outside the Privacy Rule's restrictions altogether. Two routes reach that point: a qualified statistician makes a formal determination, or the specified identifiers of the individual, of relatives, household members and employers are removed, provided the entity has no actual knowledge that what remains could still identify anyone.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266)
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMA III.G.3.c (2027 III.G.3.c) · CMAA 5 k77 · CCMA 5 k186
preguntas.pregunta: The patient cannot come in, so the advance written notice is read to her over the telephone. What has to follow?
opciones: A written copy at once, with the contact documented while the signed copy is awaited
No more than that, provided the office documents the telephone call in her record
A witness signature on her behalf, after which the original is filed as issued
A postponement of the service until she can attend and sign the notice in person
preguntas.explicacion: Where the notice cannot be issued in person it may go by telephone, e-mail, mail or fax under HIPAA policy, and the patient should not dispute the contact. A telephone contact has to be followed immediately by a hand-delivered, mailed, e-mailed or faxed notice; the contact is documented and the unsigned copy kept on file while the signed one is awaited.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Hospice care: Who's eligible and Provider requirements
preguntas.subtema: Hospice eligibility · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: Who must certify that a patient is terminally ill before the Medicare hospice benefit can begin?
opciones: The hospice doctor together with the patient's regular doctor, if there is one
The hospice medical director alone, after a face-to-face meeting with the family
