Any two physicians enrolled in Medicare who have examined the patient that month
The attending clinician alone, since that clinician is the one who knows her best
preguntas.explicacion: To elect the benefit the patient needs Part A and must meet three conditions: the hospice doctor and the regular doctor, if the patient has one, certify a terminal illness with a life expectancy of 6 months or less; the patient accepts comfort care instead of care aimed at a cure; and the patient signs a statement choosing hospice. Only those doctors may certify.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Tort in Healthcare", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Assault vs battery · CPT D1 1D · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7A k221 · CMA II.E.4.a · RMA I.C.1.c · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k31
preguntas.pregunta: A patient raises a fist at the front-desk staff but does not strike. In tort terms this may be which of the following?
opciones: Assault: an intentional act creating apprehension of imminent harmful contact
Battery: harmful or offensive contact that actually occurs
Negligence: an unintentional failure to act as a reasonable person would
Strict liability: harm during a known dangerous activity, regardless of fault
preguntas.explicacion: An assault is complete without any touching: it is an intentional act that makes another person reasonably expect harmful or offensive contact is about to happen. A fist raised at the front desk is the illustration used, and if the blow lands, battery is added to the assault. Reasonableness matters, since someone standing several meters away would not yet create that expectation. Negligence, by contrast, is unintentional, and strict liability attaches to inherently dangerous activities and to defective products without regard to fault.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, General Compliance Program Guidance (2023), Element 3: Training and Education
preguntas.subtema: Auditing and compliance · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: Under the OIG's seven elements, who has to receive compliance training and how often?
opciones: Officers, board members, contractors, employees and medical staff, at least yearly
Only the employees who handle claims and coding, at least once every three years
Only the compliance committee and the compliance officer, twice in each year
Everyone in the entity, but only after an audit or an investigation has found a fault
preguntas.explicacion: Training and education is the third element. Officers, board members, contractors, employees and medical staff should all be trained at least once a year on the entity's compliance program and on its compliance risks, with the applicable fraud and abuse laws reviewed in that training. The compliance officer draws up an annual plan taking in whatever the audits and investigations turned up.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Documentation for billing · CMAA 6A, 5 k69 · CCMA 5I k184 · CMA III.G.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: At an office visit the provider writes that a condition is probable, with testing still pending. How is it coded?
opciones: Code the signs and symptoms, since uncertain diagnoses are not coded in the office
Code the probable condition, since the provider named it in the encounter note
Code the probable condition and add the symptoms as additional diagnoses after it
Hold the claim until the testing confirms or rules out the suspected condition
preguntas.explicacion: For outpatient services and office visits, wording such as suspected, probable, questionable, rule out or working diagnosis is not coded at all. The encounter gets coded to the highest degree of certainty on hand: the symptoms, the signs, the abnormal test results or whatever else brought the patient in. That differs from the inpatient rules, which is why the guidelines flag it, and nothing requires holding the claim.

preguntas.fuente: HRSA, Health Center Program Compliance Manual, Chapter 9: Sliding Fee Discount Program
preguntas.subtema: Financial considerations · CMA III.G.6.e (exam from July 2027) · CMAA 6 k83 · CCMA 5E k178
preguntas.pregunta: On what may a health center base a patient's place on the sliding fee discount schedule?
opciones: Her income and the size of her family, and no other factor
Her income and the insurance she holds, and no other factor
Her income and the balance she still owes to the center
Her income and the kind of service she has come in for
preguntas.explicacion: The board-approved policy has to assess every patient for the discount on income and family size alone, with the definitions of both written down. Between the poverty line and twice that line the discounts step down through at least three pay classes, and above twice the line no discount is given. No patient may be turned away for inability to pay.

preguntas.subtema: PSDA · CCMA 7D k217, k219 · CMA E.8.d / 2027 E.7.c · NCMA 4.2 · CMAA 3D k32
preguntas.pregunta: What must the provider record about an adult patient's advance directive?
opciones: Whether or not one exists, in a prominent part of the current record
Whether or not one exists, in the billing file kept with the claim
The full text of the directive, scanned into the record within 90 days
The name of the agent, sent to the state survey and certification agency
preguntas.explicacion: The rule is that the provider documents, in a prominent part of the patient's current medical record, whether an advance directive has been executed by that individual. The state survey and certification agency is where complaints about these requirements are filed, not where agents are registered, and the 90-day clock belongs to updating information after a change in state law.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Academy for Integrating Behavioral Health and Primary Care: What is Integrated Behavioral Health?
preguntas.subtema: Collaborative care · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: Integrated behavioral health care is also known by which other name?
opciones: Collaborative care, or behavioral health in primary care
Accountable care, or the shared savings arrangement of Medicare
Managed care, or the point-of-service arrangement
Custodial care, or long-term services and support
preguntas.explicacion: Integrated behavioral health care brings into one setting the treatment of medical conditions and of the behavioral health factors bearing on health. Other names for it are integrated care, behavioral health integration, collaborative care, and behavioral health in primary care. Behavioral health itself covers conditions of mental health and of substance use, the stressors and crises of life, physical symptoms brought on by stress, and health behaviors.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Pocket Guide, Call-Out
preguntas.subtema: Structured communication · CCMA 6F k198 · CMA F.4.c / 2027 F.2.c · CMAA 2E k23
preguntas.pregunta: What is a call-out meant to accomplish during a critical situation?
opciones: Inform every team member at once and name who acts
Confirm the receiver understood by repeating it back
Confirm the patient can restate the instructions given
Transfer responsibility and accountability to a team
preguntas.explicacion: A call-out communicates important or critical information: it reaches all team members at the same moment, helps them anticipate the next steps, and directs responsibility by name to the person who will carry the task out. Repeating back is the check-back, and moving responsibility is the handoff.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Attempt conflict management techniques before termination
preguntas.subtema: Documenting a conflict · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.b · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: After a heated exchange at the front desk, the clinician apologises for the way the conversation went. What does the guidance say about the record?
opciones: The conflict goes briefly into the clinical notes, and the apology goes in with it
The conflict goes into an incident report kept apart from the clinical notes
Neither goes in, since an apology in the chart can be read as admitting an error
The conflict goes in only once the practice decides to end the relationship
preguntas.explicacion: An apology offered sincerely for perceived rudeness can take the heat out of a disagreement that has escalated, and it is confined to the way the clinician conducted the exchange so that nobody can read it as an admission of a medical error. Record-keeping that is accurate and complete means the conflict goes briefly into the clinical notes, apology and all, leaving a written account that refreshes the clinician's memory before the next encounter.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fighting Identity Theft with the Red Flags Rule: Identify Relevant Red Flags
preguntas.subtema: Suspicious documents · CCMA 5F k190 · CMA III.H.2.b · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 5A k66 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: The photograph on the card a new patient hands over does not look like the person standing at the desk. Which category of red flag is that?
opciones: A suspicious document presented
Suspicious activity on the account
A notice arriving from elsewhere
An alert from a credit agency
preguntas.explicacion: Suspicious documents form one of the listed categories: a bearer who does not match the photograph or the description of physical appearance, details on the card that clash with what the person is saying, or an application that looks altered, forged, or reassembled after being torn up. Account activity and third-party notices are separate categories.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · CMA III.G.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: A code in a category that has an applicable seventh character is reported with only six characters. What is wrong?
opciones: The code is invalid, since a code missing its applicable seventh character cannot be used
The code is valid, since the seventh character is added only when the payer asks for it
The code is valid, but the payer will pay it at a lower level of specificity than usual
The code is invalid, since every diagnosis code has to reach seven characters to be used
preguntas.explicacion: A code that has an applicable seventh character is considered invalid without it, and the character must always sit in the seventh position of the data field. Where the code is shorter than six characters, the placeholder X fills the empty positions so the seventh character lands in place. Codes of three to six characters are perfectly valid when their category calls for no seventh character.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Issues of Concern: Electronic Health Records
preguntas.subtema: Paying out of pocket · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35
preguntas.pregunta: A patient pays the full price of a test himself and asks that it not be reported to his health plan. What must the provider do?
opciones: Honor the request, since the care was paid out of pocket in full
Bill the plan anyway, because contracts require every claim
Honor it only if the privacy officer approves the exception
Ask the plan for permission before withholding the claim
preguntas.explicacion: Among the additions that came with the health information technology legislation, covered entities must acknowledge and fulfill a request that information not be shared with a health insurance plan when the individual has paid for that care out of pocket and in full. The same legislation requires an audit trail accounting for disclosures where electronic records are used, and gives patients an electronic copy of what those records hold.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Closed Loop Communication Training in Medical Simulation", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Structured communication · CCMA 6F k198 · CMA F.4.c / 2027 F.2.c · CMAA 2E k23
preguntas.pregunta: Closed-loop communication is a three-step process. What happens in the third step?
opciones: The sender verifies the message was received correctly
The receiver passes the message to a second team member
The sender documents the exchange in the patient record
The receiver performs the task and reports back later on
preguntas.explicacion: First the transmitter sends the message to the intended receiver, using their name where possible. Second the receiver acknowledges receiving it out loud, asking for clarification if needed. Third the original transmitter verifies that it was received and interpreted correctly, which is what closes the loop.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Deductible
preguntas.subtema: Insurance terminology · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.6.e · RMA II.A.1 · CMAA 5C · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's plan has a $2,000 deductible. What does that number mean for the patient?
opciones: The patient pays the first $2,000 of covered services before the plan starts to pay anything
The plan pays the first $2,000 of covered services and the patient pays the coinsurance on the rest
The patient's monthly premium for the coverage is $2,000, whether or not any services are used
The most the patient will pay in the plan year for covered services, after which the plan pays 100%
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov defines the deductible as what the patient pays for covered care before the plan begins paying, and uses this very figure as its example: with a $2,000 deductible, the first $2,000 of covered services comes out of the patient's pocket, not the plan's. Once it is met, the patient usually still owes a copayment or coinsurance. The monthly payment owed whether or not care is used is the premium, and the yearly ceiling after which the plan pays 100% is the out-of-pocket maximum: two other glossary entries, two different numbers.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Eligibility, Medically Needy
preguntas.subtema: Financial eligibility · CMA III.G.4.c (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 6 k83 · CCMA 5E k178 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's income is above her state's Medicaid limit, but her medical bills are enormous. Which route may her state offer her?
opciones: A medically needy program, where the expenses she incurs spend her income down
A premium tax credit, which lowers what she pays for a plan on the Marketplace
A sliding fee discount, which lowers what a health center charges her directly
The Medicare Savings Programs, which pay premiums and cost sharing for her
preguntas.explicacion: States may set up a medically needy program for people whose health needs are significant but whose income sits above the other eligibility groups. Such a person becomes eligible by spending down: she incurs expenses for medical and remedial care she has no insurance for, and once those exceed the gap between her income and the state's standard, Medicaid picks up what is above it.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Drug plan rules, Prior authorization
preguntas.subtema: Medication authorization · CMAA 4G k67 · CCMA 5H k183 · CMA III.G.5.a(2) · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: A drug plan denies a medicine because it requires prior authorization. What does the prescriber need to send for an exception?
opciones: A supporting statement explaining why the drug is medically necessary for this patient
A supporting statement listing the other drugs the patient took over the past year
A copy of the plan's drug list with the requested medication marked on the page
A new prescription written for a drug from the lowest cost-sharing tier instead
preguntas.explicacion: An exception is the plan's decision to cover a drug that is off its list or to waive a coverage rule. The patient or the prescriber must request it, and the prescriber has to supply a statement supporting the request: that the drug is medically necessary for this patient despite the rule, that another drug would harm the patient, or that another drug would be less effective. Sending a copy of the list or simply switching drugs is not an exception request.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), Prohibitions
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMAA 5 k77 · CCMA 5 k186 · CMA III.G.3.c
preguntas.pregunta: Which practice is forbidden when an advance written notice of non-coverage goes out?
opciones: Giving one to every patient as routine, apart from a few defined exceptions
Giving one before a service that exceeds a frequency limit set by a coverage policy
Giving one before an item that is experimental, investigational or research only
Giving one covering an extended course of treatment listed with its duration
preguntas.explicacion: Handing the notice out routinely is prohibited; the exceptions are items and services that are experimental, services carrying frequency limits set by statute, by regulation or by a national or local coverage determination, equipment refused for a missing supplier number or an unsolicited telephone contact, and services always denied as not medically necessary. One notice may cover an extended course of care if it lists the items and the duration.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", AR more than 90 days
preguntas.subtema: Accounts receivable · CMAA 6B, 6 k86 · CCMA 5K k187
preguntas.pregunta: A manager reviews the practice's aging receivables. Which figure is the benchmark for claims left unpaid more than 90 days?
opciones: Less than 15% of the accounts receivable should sit beyond 90 days
Less than 50% of the accounts receivable should sit beyond 90 days
Less than 15% of the claims should be denied on their first submission
Less than 5% of the coding workload should wait in a queue at any time
preguntas.explicacion: The benchmark cited is that under 15% of claims should be more than 90 days old in accounts receivable, with submission errors, slow appeals and delayed payer processing behind the older balances. Denials typically run between 5% and 10%, and the target of less than 5% waiting in a queue belongs to coding productivity, so those figures answer different questions.

preguntas.fuente: AAMA, Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Standards for CMAs (AAMA), Procedures for Adjudicating Alleged Violations
preguntas.subtema: Unethical conduct · CCMA 7C · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: What is the certificant entitled to when a disciplinary complaint is opened?
opciones: Written notice of the basis, a chance to submit evidence, and an appeal
Written notice of the basis and a hearing before a panel of three peers
Written notice of the basis and the identity of the person who complained
Written notice of the basis, after which the sanction takes effect at once
preguntas.explicacion: The procedure gives the certificant or applicant written notice of the basis for discipline or for denial of eligibility, a chance to submit written evidence about the alleged violations, a decision taken by the certification director, and the chance to appeal that decision to a panel of appeals the certifying board has established. Cooperating with the investigation is itself required.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Medicare and Medicaid Accreditation and Deemed Status: Definitions
preguntas.subtema: Compliance with regulators · CMAA 3A k42
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital administrator asks why the facility seeks accreditation. What is accurate?
opciones: It is voluntary, but required for a facility that wants to take part in Medicare
It is mandatory for every facility, whether or not it bills a federal program
It replaces the state license the facility needs in order to operate at all
It is granted by the state health department after an annual fire inspection
preguntas.explicacion: Accreditation is the evaluation and recognition of providers such as hospitals and clinics, confirming that they meet standards of care. It is voluntary, and yet it is required of any facility wanting to take part in the Medicare and Medicaid programs. The process measures the policies, the procedures and the clinical practices of a provider against the guidelines the agency has set.

preguntas.subtema: Documentation updates · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: A practice rewrites its password policy after moving to a hosted record system. What else does the documentation standard ask of it?
opciones: Reviewing the documentation periodically and updating it as operations change
Keeping the version it replaced for ten years counted from the day of the change
Obtaining a written acknowledgment from each patient that the policy has changed
Filing an amended notice of privacy practices with the Secretary within 60 days
preguntas.explicacion: Security Rule documentation carries three required specifications: hold it for six years from when it was created or from the day it was last in effect, whichever is later; make it available to whoever has to carry the procedures out; and review it and bring it up to date whenever the environment or the operation changes. A newly hosted system is exactly such a change.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(j)(1) and (j)(2), Disclosures by whistleblowers and workforce member crime victims
preguntas.subtema: Whistleblower disclosures · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7F k214 · CMA II.E.6 · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3E k37
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist reports to the state health oversight agency that her employer is reusing single-use devices, and her report includes patient information. How does HIPAA treat this?
opciones: It is protected when made in good faith to a health oversight agency about unlawful conduct
It is a breach of unsecured PHI that the employer must report to HHS within 60 days of discovery
It is permitted only if the patients signed authorizations first
It is permitted only if made to the news media, which is exempt from the Privacy Rule
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.502(j)(1) shields whistleblowers: the rule is not broken when a workforce member or a business associate, believing in good faith that the entity has acted unlawfully, breached professional standards or put patients, workers or the public in danger, passes PHI to a health oversight agency, to a public health authority, to an accrediting organization, or to an attorney consulted about it. The same section covers a workforce member who is the victim of a crime and reports limited information about the perpetrator. The media are not on the list of protected recipients.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Days in Accounts Receivable
preguntas.subtema: Accounts receivable · CMAA 6B, 6 k86 · CCMA 5K k187
preguntas.pregunta: Days in accounts receivable have climbed while patient volume stayed flat. What does that suggest?
opciones: Gaps in the billing process, such as submission errors or delayed appeals
A drop in the practice's charges, since fewer services were billed this month
A rise in the contractual adjustments the payers granted the practice
An improvement, since a higher figure means more claims are being filed
preguntas.explicacion: Days in accounts receivable usually hold steady or fall when patient volumes are consistent, so a rise with no matching rise in volume points to gaps in the revenue cycle. The causes named are errors in claim submission, appeals on denials that run late, secondary insurance, and workers' compensation settlements that drag. A higher number means money waits longer, which is the opposite of an improvement.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Distal (Medical Encyclopedia 002346)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k13 · CMA I.C.6.e (2027 I.C.6.d) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k11 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A chart reads: the lesion is distal to the elbow. Where on the arm should you look?
opciones: Farther from the trunk than the elbow, toward the hand
Nearer to the trunk than the elbow, toward the shoulder
On the back of the arm at the level of the elbow itself
Deeper than the elbow joint, under the muscles of the arm
preguntas.explicacion: Distal describes a position in a limb farther from the point of attachment or from the trunk, and proximal is its opposite. The hand is distal to the forearm; the upper arm is proximal to the forearm. A lesion distal to the elbow therefore sits somewhere between the elbow and the fingers.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Electronic Billing & EDI Transactions
preguntas.subtema: Claim submission · CMA III.G.3.b(1) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6C k87, 6 k85 · CCMA 5L k185
preguntas.pregunta: A biller asks what electronic data interchange means when Medicare uses the term about claims.
opciones: The automated transfer of data in a set format and content between provider and Medicare
The conversion of a paper claim into an image that is stored inside the record
The movement of funds from the payer into the provider's own bank account
The list of code sets that were adopted for use in the standard transactions
preguntas.explicacion: Electronic data interchange means data moving automatically in a set format, under set rules about content, either between Medicare and a provider or between Medicare and some other health plan; that transfer may pass through a clearinghouse or a billing service. It makes processing transactions faster and cheaper for both sides.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth documentation · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 5E · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: What must the record show after a visit conducted by video, according to the telehealth workflow?
opciones: That the encounter was a telehealth visit, with the matching billing code or modifier
That the patient waived her right to an in-person appointment for the same complaint
That the video was retained by the platform for the period the practice specifies
That the clinician held a license in every State where the practice has patients
preguntas.explicacion: Documentation appears among the steps of the visit itself: the encounter is written up as a telehealth visit, and when the claim goes in it carries either a billing code specific to telehealth or a modifier on the ordinary code. Evaluation comes next, collecting the patient's experience and her suggestions for making future visits better.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Making Health Care Safer II (2013), capítulo «The Joint Commission's "Do Not Use" List: Brief Review» (NBK133373)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k10 · CMAA 1 k8 · RMA I.B.3.a
preguntas.pregunta: Within which accreditation program was the Do Not Use list created?
opciones: The National Patient Safety Goals
The Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments
The Bloodborne Pathogens standard
The Medication Guide program
preguntas.explicacion: The list of banned abbreviations was announced as one of the National Patient Safety Goals, and accredited hospitals had to drop the nine listed notations by April 2004. Its aim is that staff communicate with one another effectively, and that is why enforcement travels through accreditation.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Introduction and Beneficence (conflicts with respect for patient autonomy)
preguntas.subtema: Autonomy · CPT D1 1D k26 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7C · CMA II.E.7 · RMA I.C.4.a · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: A competent adult refuses a blood draw and the phlebotomist does not proceed. Which ethical principle is being honored?
opciones: Autonomy, respecting the patient's right to decide about their own care
Beneficence, doing what is in the patient's medical best interest
Justice, spreading a limited supply fairly among the patients
Nonmaleficence, avoiding actions known to expose the patient to harm
preguntas.explicacion: Patient rights rest on a small set of ethical principles: valuing the patient's dignity, acting with goodwill to preserve life and autonomy, avoiding known harm, and distributing resources fairly. Respect for autonomy is the principle at work when a patient with capacity decides against advice; the clinician should still explain the reasons for the recommendation at the level a reasonable person would need, and document capacity, but the decision belongs to the patient. Beneficence is the principle that most often conflicts with it.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Point of Service (POS) Plans
preguntas.subtema: Commercial plan types and referrals · CMAA 4G k67, 4 k61 · CCMA 5H k183 · RMA II.A.4 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: A new patient's card says POS. Before booking him with a cardiologist, what does the office need?
opciones: A referral from his primary care doctor, which this type of plan requires
A written waiver of liability, which this type of plan requires up front
A signed assignment of benefits form, which this type of plan renews each year
A copy of the drug list, since this type of plan ties tiers to specialists
preguntas.explicacion: Point of service plans charge the patient less inside the network and, like an HMO, require the primary care doctor to refer the patient before a specialist visit. A waiver of liability is the Medicare advance notice used when denial is expected, not a scheduling step. Assignment of benefits is an intake form that lets the plan pay the office directly, and the drug list sorts covered medicines into tiers.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A term in the Alphabetic Index sits inside parentheses. What does the coder take from that?
opciones: It is a nonessential modifier and may be present or absent without changing the code
It is a manifestation code and is always to be sequenced after the etiology code
It is a synonym or alternative wording offered to explain the title of the code
It is an incomplete term needing one of the modifiers that follow it to be assignable
preguntas.explicacion: Words set inside parentheses are supplementary: they may appear in a statement of the disease or not appear at all, and either way the code assigned is the same. Those are the nonessential modifiers. Brackets do two other jobs: in the Tabular List they carry synonyms and explanatory phrases, and in the Index they mark manifestation codes. A colon follows an incomplete term.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Protected Health Information
preguntas.subtema: What counts as PHI · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3B k35 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these, held by a medical office, is protected health information under HIPAA?
opciones: A patient's e-mail address stored with the record of a visit the office billed last month
The personnel file the office keeps on a receptionist in its role as her employer
A student immunization list held by a school district under the education records law
A journal article on hypertension saved in the practice's shared clinical reference folder
preguntas.explicacion: PHI means health information that identifies an individual and that a covered entity holds or transmits, in any medium; demographic data counts when it travels alongside information about care or payment. Among the common identifiers the rule names name, address, birth date and Social Security number. Two things are carved out expressly: employment records the covered entity keeps in its role as employer, and education records covered by FERPA.

preguntas.fuente: NAIC, Coordination of Benefits Model Regulation (Model 120), Order of Benefit Determination Rules
preguntas.subtema: Insurance rules · CMAA 5B k75 · CCMA 5E k182
preguntas.pregunta: The divorced parents of a patient both carry coverage, and a court decree puts the father in charge of the child's health care costs. Which plan is primary?
opciones: The father's plan, once that plan has actual knowledge of the decree
The father's plan, from the date the child was first enrolled in it
The mother's plan, because the birthday rule governs divorced parents
The mother's plan, because she is the parent the child resides with
preguntas.explicacion: Where the parents of a child are divorced or separated and a court decree names one of them as responsible for health care expenses or for coverage, that parent's plan is primary, and the rule bites for plan years beginning after the plan has notice of the decree. A decree naming both parents, or granting joint custody without saying who is responsible, throws the question back to the birthday rule.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Making Health Care Safer II (2013), capítulo «The Joint Commission's "Do Not Use" List: Brief Review» (NBK133373)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k10 · CMAA 1 k7
preguntas.pregunta: Of the medication errors traced to abbreviations in a national reporting program, which single abbreviation accounted for the largest share?
opciones: QD, for once daily, at about 43 percent of the errors
MSO4, for morphine sulfate, at about 43 percent of the errors
cc, for milliliter, at about 43 percent of the errors
HS, for at bedtime, at about 43 percent of the errors
preguntas.explicacion: Of roughly 30,000 abbreviation-related errors reported over three years, QD came first at about 43 percent of the roughly 18,000 that carried enough detail to be classified, followed by U for units and cc for milliliters at roughly 13 percent each, then MS or MSO4 near 10 percent and HS around 3 percent. Most of them, about 81 percent, happened while the order was being written.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Issues of Concern; and 42 CFR 482.13
preguntas.subtema: Patient rights · CCMA k215 · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32
preguntas.pregunta: What weight does a bill of rights published by a health care organization carry?
opciones: It is not enforceable on its own, unlike a right written into regulation
It is enforceable once the organization publishes it and posts it publicly
It is enforceable in the states that have adopted it into their own statutes
It replaces the federal patient rights whenever the organization is accredited
preguntas.explicacion: Various American health care organizations wrote their own bills of rights starting in the 1970s, and those documents are not enforceable in themselves. What makes a right enforceable is a body with the authority to enforce it doing so: the rights a hospital must honor come from regulation, such as the federal conditions on notice, decision-making, privacy and grievances.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Billing: CMS-1500 & 837P (MLN006976), ASETT
preguntas.subtema: Claim submission · CMA III.G.3.b(1) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6C k87, 6 k85 · CCMA 5L k185
preguntas.pregunta: A practice wants to know whether its electronic claims meet the HIPAA standards before it sends any. What does CMS offer?
opciones: A testing tool that checks the transaction against the standards
A look-up service run by the correct coding edit contractor
A license for the implementation guide of the claim format
A monthly report drawn from the eligibility system it uses
preguntas.explicacion: The enforcement and testing tool weighs a transaction against the rules of compliance, of syntax and of business, across the adopted formats, the diagnosis and procedure codes and the unique identifiers, and the same tool takes complaints about a payer that will not accept a standard. The coding edit program, by contrast, offers no look-up or clean claims service.

preguntas.subtema: Notification recipients · CCMA 5 k179 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 7 k90 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Who is a hospital expected to reach with the electronic notifications it sends when a patient arrives at or leaves its emergency department?
opciones: The primary care practitioner the patient has, or the practice he names
Every provider who has treated the patient during the previous twelve months
The patient's health plan, which coordinates the rest of the care from there
The state health department, which forwards the message to the care team
preguntas.explicacion: Notifications go out when the patient registers in the emergency department, when he is admitted, and when he is discharged or transferred, and the hospital has to make a reasonable effort to send them to the applicable post-acute care providers and to the primary care practitioner or practice the patient is established with, or whichever clinician he names as primarily responsible.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, When can I sign up for Medicare?; and CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Secondary Payer (MLN006903), Table 1
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74, 5B k75 · CCMA 5E k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient of sixty-six works for a company with twelve employees and asks whether she really needs Part B. What does Medicare tell her?
opciones: Her job-based plan may not pay unless she holds Part A and Part B
Her job-based plan pays first, so she may put Part B off for now
Her job-based plan pays second, so Part B is not needed for now
Her job-based plan ends the moment she signs up for Part A alone
preguntas.explicacion: Where the employer has fewer than twenty employees, Medicare pays first and the group plan pays second, and Medicare warns that the job-based coverage may not pay for services unless the patient holds both Part A and Part B. The rule that lets someone put off Part B without penalty is the one for larger employers, where the group plan pays first.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Coordination of Benefits & Recovery Overview
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMA III.G.3.a (2027 III.G.3.a) · CMAA 6 k87 · CCMA 5 k185
preguntas.pregunta: Medicare paid a claim as the primary payer and it later turns out an employer group plan should have. Which entity pursues the money?
opciones: The Commercial Repayment Center, which seeks it from the employer and the group plan
The Benefits Coordination & Recovery Center, which seeks it from the patient herself
The Medicare Administrative Contractor, which seeks it from the billing provider
The Commercial Repayment Center, which seeks it from the patient's own attorney
preguntas.explicacion: When new information shows Medicare made a primary payment by mistake, recovery follows. Where a group health plan turns out to be the one that should have paid first, the Commercial Repayment Center goes after the employer and the plan. Payments made in error on workers' compensation, no-fault and liability claims go to the Benefits Coordination & Recovery Center, where it is the beneficiary who has to repay Medicare.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Your Rights Under HIPAA, Who Must Follow These Laws
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, confidentiality · CPT D1 1C k13 · CCMA 7A k214 · RMA I.C.5 comply with HIPAA · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these organizations has to follow the HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules as a covered entity?
opciones: A clinic that bills insurers electronically for the laboratory tests it collects
A life insurer that keeps the results of the physicals it required of applicants
An employer that stores the pre-employment drug screens run on its new drivers
A school district that keeps immunization records on file for every student
preguntas.explicacion: Covered entities are health care clearinghouses, health plans, and health care providers who transmit health information electronically in connection with a standard transaction such as a claim. Employers, life insurers, carriers of workers compensation, most schools and most law enforcement agencies all hold health information about people, and none of them is covered by these two rules.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Elder Abuse", Introduction; and Treatment/Management
preguntas.subtema: Signs of abuse · CCMA 7F k222 · CMA E.6.c / 2027 E.5.b · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k43
preguntas.pregunta: An older patient arrives underweight and unwashed, with medications that were never refilled. Which category fits, and what follows?
opciones: Neglect, and the case is reported even though it is only suspected
Neglect, and the case is reported once the findings are confirmed
Financial abuse, and the case is referred to the hospital's legal team
Psychological abuse, and the case is handled by the social work team
preguntas.explicacion: Neglect is the caregiver's failure to meet obligations to the older adult: withholding food, water, clothing, medication refills or assistive devices. It shows up as being underweight or dehydrated, poor hygiene, dirty clothing and overgrown nails. Reporting is done even when the abuse is only suspected and not proven, so that Adult Protective Services can investigate.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Credentialing", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Credentialing · RMA I.C.2.a · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k48
preguntas.pregunta: Which professionals have to go through credentialing at a health care institution?
opciones: Licensed independent practitioners who may provide care without supervision
Every employee of the institution who has any contact with patients at all
Only physicians and surgeons who intend to admit patients to the hospital
Only staff whose salary is billed to Medicare, Medicaid or a private insurer
preguntas.explicacion: Credentialing is required of any licensed, independent professional whom law and a licensing body permit to provide services without supervision, within the scope of that license. Holding a license does not mean a person may do any service they like. It used to be a hospital process; today ambulatory centers, long-term care institutions and urgent care clinics do it too.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 3, III Glossary; and 3.6 Culturally Sensitive Care
preguntas.subtema: Culturally responsive care · CCMA 6A k193 · CMA F.2.a / 2027 F.1.d(8) · RMA I.D.1.d · CMAA 2C k17
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's cultural practice does not interfere with the treatment plan. What is the approach?
opciones: Accommodate it, since the plan is not adversely affected
Set it aside until a provider signs off on it in the chart
Document it as a partial refusal of the plan of care
Ask the patient to choose between the practice and care
preguntas.explicacion: Cultural negotiation is a reciprocal, collaborative search for a mutually acceptable way to handle competing interests between the care given, the care prescribed and the patient's cultural needs. When the cultural need does not significantly or adversely affect the treatment plan, it can be accommodated.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, FAQ 580: Medical record retention
preguntas.subtema: Record retention · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks how long the practice must keep her chart under HIPAA. What is the accurate answer?
opciones: HIPAA sets no retention period for medical records; State law generally governs that
HIPAA sets six years, the same period it applies to its own policies and notices
HIPAA sets seven years from the date of the last service the patient received
HIPAA sets five years, the period Medicare applies to hospital medical records
preguntas.explicacion: OCR answers the question head on: the Privacy Rule lays down no retention period for medical records, and how long they are kept is generally a matter of State law. What the rule does demand is that safeguards of the administrative, technical and physical kinds protect the privacy of the records for as long as the entity holds them, disposal included. Six, seven and five years come from other rules.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Workplace Violence", Pearls and Other Issues: Environment
preguntas.subtema: Difficult situations · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k16
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic adds better lighting, transparent doors, cameras and weapons screening. Which type of violence do those measures reduce?
opciones: Type I, the violence that comes with criminal intent
Type II, the violence from patients and their visitors
Type III, the violence between colleagues and staff
Type IV, the violence tied to a personal relationship
preguntas.explicacion: Environmental measures work by deterrence, and they cut type I incidents and the number of weapons brought in. The pitfall is spelled out: they do not reduce type II violence, which is impulsive and contextual rather than planned, and neither visibility nor physical barriers stop verbal abuse. Types III and IV are not what the doors and cameras address.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Incidental Uses and Disclosures: General Provision
preguntas.subtema: Telephone messages · CCMA 6 k204 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.3.a · CMAA 7F k94 · NCMA 3.2
preguntas.pregunta: Staff leave a message on a patient's home answering machine about a lab result. What governs how much may be said?
opciones: The minimum necessary standard and the reasonable safeguards the rule requires
The accounting of disclosures, which must list the message before it is left
The patient's written authorization, needed before any message may be left
The rule on marketing communications, which limits unsolicited contacts
preguntas.explicacion: Messages left where somebody else may overhear them are the classic incidental disclosure: permitted as a by-product of a use the rule allows, so long as reasonable safeguards and the minimum necessary policies have been applied by the entity to the underlying disclosure. An incidental disclosure that follows from failing to apply either one is not permitted.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266), Issuing a Notice When Multiple Entities Provide Care
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMA III.G.3.c (2027 III.G.3.c) · CMAA 5 k77 · CCMA 5 k186
preguntas.pregunta: A physician orders a laboratory test that an independent laboratory performs and bills. Who has to issue the advance written notice?
opciones: Any notifier taking part may issue it, and the one that bills answers for it
Both of them have to issue one, and each keeps its own signed copy on file
Only the physician who ordered the test may issue it to that patient
Only the laboratory that runs the test may issue it to that patient
preguntas.explicacion: Where several entities take part in the care, separate notices are not required. Any notifier involved may issue one, and more than one notifier may be entered in the header of the form so long as the patient can tell whom to ask about the bill. Responsibility for issuing it rests with the notifier that bills the service.

preguntas.fuente: EEOC, Overview: About the EEOC
preguntas.subtema: Employment law compliance · CMAA 3A (federal employment law)
preguntas.pregunta: Which employers are covered by the laws the EEOC enforces?
opciones: Most with at least 15 employees, or 20 in age discrimination cases
Most with at least 25 employees, or 15 in age discrimination cases
All employers, regardless of how many people they have on payroll
Only those holding a federal contract or receiving federal funding
preguntas.explicacion: The commission enforces the federal laws making it illegal to discriminate against an applicant or an employee on grounds of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age of 40 or over, genetic information or disability. Employers are mostly covered from 15 employees upward, and the threshold rises to 20 for age discrimination. Most unions and employment agencies are covered too.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", Children
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, types of consent · CPT D2 2G · CCMA 7B k216 minors · CMA II.E.3.c exceptions · CMAA 3D k40 consent
preguntas.pregunta: A 15-year-old arrives alone for a blood draw her physician ordered. Who normally agrees to the procedure on her behalf?
opciones: A parent or legal guardian, in a process properly called informed permission
The patient herself, since a minor who understands a procedure may agree to it
The ordering physician, who decides for any patient younger than eighteen years
A parent or guardian, unless the phlebotomist judges the patient mature enough
preguntas.explicacion: Children under 18 generally cannot give informed consent; a parent or legal guardian permits the intervention, and that process carries the name informed permission. The exception is the legally emancipated minor, for example one who is married, serving in the military, financially independent, or a mother. Which minors qualify is a matter of state law, not of a bedside judgment about maturity.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Workplace Violence", Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: De-escalation · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k26 · NCMA EKB 22 · CMA F.1.f / 2027 F.1.f
preguntas.pregunta: Where do prevention and de-escalation sit in managing a patient who may turn violent?
opciones: First, with restraints held back as a last resort
Last, once a security team has already come in
First, but only after a supervisor authorizes it
Last, and only after chemical restraint is given
preguntas.explicacion: Management centers on prevention and de-escalation, with the fight-or-flight reaction as the last resort. Triage is early enough for de-escalation to begin, staff should be trained in it, and physical restraints used alongside chemical ones are likewise a last resort rather than a first move.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse (MLN4649244), Permissive Exclusions; and OIG, Exclusions Program
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: A provider's license was revoked over her professional competence. What kind of exclusion may follow?
opciones: A permissive one, which OIG may impose and whose length varies
A mandatory one, which runs for a minimum of five years
A mandatory one, which lasts as long as the license is gone
None at all, since no criminal conviction has been entered
preguntas.explicacion: Losing a health care license for reasons of professional competence, performance or financial integrity is one of the grounds on which OIG may exclude, and permissive exclusions vary in length. The mandatory exclusions, with their floor of five years, follow convictions such as program fraud or patient abuse.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266)
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMAA 5 k77, 6 k85 · CCMA 5 k186 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: An office is clearing out old files. How long must a signed advance written notice of non-coverage be kept?
opciones: 5 years from the date the care was delivered, where no state rule demands longer
3 years from the date the care was delivered, where no state rule demands longer
5 years from the date the claim for that care was finally paid or denied
Until the claim is paid, after which the signed copy may be discarded safely
preguntas.explicacion: Notices are held for 5 years from the date care was delivered where no state-law requirement says otherwise, and every record is held, including those where the patient turned care down, refused an option or would not sign. The clock starts on the date of service, not on payment of the claim, and the record is not thrown out once the claim closes.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms, entry Out-of-pocket Limit
preguntas.subtema: Insurance terminology · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient lists what she has paid this year and asks what counts toward her out-of-pocket limit. Which one does?
opciones: The coinsurance the patient paid for covered care given inside the network
The monthly premiums the patient paid to keep the coverage in force this year
The balance billed by a provider who charged above the plan's allowed amount
The cost of a service the plan lists among the benefits it does not cover
preguntas.explicacion: The out-of-pocket limit totals the patient's own share of covered services: what she paid as deductible, as copayments and as coinsurance on care inside the network. Once it is reached the plan usually pays the whole allowed amount for the rest of the year. Three things stay outside that tally by definition: premiums, amounts balance billed above the allowed amount, and care the plan does not cover at all.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · CMA III.G.1.b
preguntas.pregunta: What is the role of the placeholder character X in ICD-10-CM?
opciones: It fills an empty position so the code keeps room for future expansion or a later character
It marks a code the coder could not verify against the medical record documentation
It replaces a character the provider left out of the documentation for the encounter
It flags a code as unspecified when the record gives no further detail about the case
preguntas.explicacion: The X is a placeholder, sitting at certain codes so that future expansion is possible, notably in the categories for poisoning, adverse effect and underdosing, and it also fills empty positions so an applicable seventh character lands in the seventh place. Where a placeholder exists it has to be used or the code is not valid. It says nothing about missing documentation or about unspecified conditions.

preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.F Laboratory Regulations · CPT D1 1C k13 · CCMA 7E k220 release of information · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's husband telephones the laboratory for her results, saying he will pass them along to her. What does CLIA require?
opciones: Release results only to authorized persons and to those responsible for using them
Release results to any adult of the household once his identity has been confirmed
Release results to him if the patient named him in the notice of privacy practices
Release results to him, because a spouse counts as the patient's personal representative
preguntas.explicacion: Test results go only to authorized persons, that is, to whoever state law lets order a test or take its results, plus whoever is responsible for using them and the laboratory that requested the test. The one widening is the patient's own access: on request, a laboratory may hand the completed reports it can authenticate as hers to the patient herself, or to her personal representative.

preguntas.fuente: Child Welfare Information Gateway, Mandatory Reporting of Child Abuse and Neglect (May 2023), Professionals Required To Report; and Child Welfare Information Gateway, Mandatory Reporting of Child Abuse and Neglect - State Statutes
preguntas.subtema: Mandatory reporting · CCMA 7F k222 · CMA E.6.c / 2027 E.5.b · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k43
preguntas.pregunta: Are health care workers mandatory reporters of suspected child maltreatment?
opciones: Yes, in every state except the four that instead require everyone to report
Yes, but only in the states that also require training for those reporters
No, unless the child is a patient of that clinician's own practice already
No, the duty falls on the head of the facility, who files on their behalf
preguntas.explicacion: Physicians, nurses and other health care workers are named as mandated reporters in 46 states plus the District of Columbia and several territories. The four missing ones, Wyoming, North Carolina, New Jersey and Indiana, do not list professions at all, because they require every person to report. Training requirements exist in some states and change nothing about who must report.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse (MLN4649244), Open Payments Program
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which program makes drug and device manufacturers report publicly what they pay physicians and teaching hospitals?
opciones: Open Payments, whose data goes up by the end of June each year
The exclusion list, which OIG refreshes at the start of a month
The compliance guidance, which the industry follows voluntarily
The designated health services code list, kept for the Stark law
preguntas.explicacion: The Open Payments program requires manufacturers of drugs, devices and biologics to report nearly every payment or transfer of value made to physicians, to certain practitioners who are not physicians and to teaching hospitals, together with ownership interests, and CMS posts the data by 30 June each year. Covered recipients are encouraged, not required, to review their entries.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Implementation of This Model
preguntas.subtema: Appointment lengths · CMAA 4A k51 k52 · CCMA 5B k173 · CMA III.H.1.a-b · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice simplifying its appointment book asks how many different appointment lengths it should keep. What does the improvement guide suggest?
opciones: Two, short and long, with a long appointment worth roughly two short ones
Three, short, standard and long, one for each of the three appointment types
One, since the guide asks that every appointment be made exactly the same length
Four, one for each appointment type plus a longer slot reserved for new patients
preguntas.explicacion: The advice is to cut the number of appointment types down to three — personal, team and unestablished — so as to minimize complexity, and to make them all roughly the same length. Length itself is then reduced to two options, short and long, where a long appointment is about the equivalent of two short ones.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: An entry in the alphabetic index ends with a dash. What is the coder being told?
opciones: More characters are needed, and only the tabular list has them
The entry is a manifestation code that has to be sequenced second
The code is invalid and another main term has to be looked up
The entry carries an excludes note over in the tabular list
preguntas.explicacion: The index does not always give the full code. A dash at the end of an index entry says that more characters are required, and laterality or an applicable seventh character can only be picked up in the tabular list. Even where no dash appears, the tabular list still has to be checked to see whether a seventh character is required.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 160.103, definition of health care clearinghouse
preguntas.subtema: Clearinghouse · CMAA 6C k89 · CCMA 5L k185
preguntas.pregunta: A practice manager says the office sends its claims through a clearinghouse. What does a health care clearinghouse do?
opciones: It converts health information between standard and nonstandard formats for others
It reviews the medical necessity of claims and decides whether the payer pays them
It holds the payer's funds until the electronic funds transfer reaches the provider
It assigns the diagnosis and procedure codes for practices that have no coder
preguntas.explicacion: In the HIPAA definition, a health care clearinghouse, billing service or similar entity either turns health information received in a nonstandard format into a standard transaction, or takes a standard transaction and renders it in the nonstandard form the receiver needs. That makes it a covered entity. Deciding medical necessity is the payer's adjudication, banks move the funds, and coding stays with the provider.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Uses and Disclosures for Treatment, Payment, and Health Care Operations
preguntas.subtema: Consent versus authorization · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.3 · RMA I.C.1.a · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: A practice asks new patients to sign a consent for use of their information in treatment, payment and operations. What is the status of that form?
opciones: Voluntary, and it does not substitute for an authorization where one is required
Mandatory, since the rule requires written consent before any treatment begins
Mandatory, and it doubles as the acknowledgment of the notice of privacy practices
Voluntary, but once signed it permits every disclosure the practice may wish to make
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity may choose to obtain consent for treatment, for payment and for health care operations, but nothing obliges it to, and one that does has complete discretion over how the process runs. A consent document is not valid permission where the rule demands an authorization instead, nor where the rule attaches other conditions to the use or disclosure.

preguntas.subtema: Record completion · CCMA 5 k174 · CMA III.H.3.a · RMA II.B.4.a · CMAA 7A · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Within what period after discharge must the hospital medical record be completed with a final diagnosis?
opciones: Thirty days following discharge
Twenty-four hours following discharge
Ninety days following discharge
Five years following discharge
preguntas.explicacion: The content standard closes with the final diagnosis and completion of the medical record within 30 days following discharge. The 24 hour figure belongs to the history and physical, which must be in the record within a day of admission and before anesthesia; five years is the minimum retention period for the record once it is complete.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Ethical Duties Relevant to Termination of the Therapeutic Relationship
preguntas.subtema: Mediation before dismissal · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.b · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: Attempts to repair the relationship with a patient who keeps missing appointments have come to nothing. Which step does the guidance place before termination?
opciones: Formal mediation by an ombudsperson, a professional mediator or a hospital ethics committee
Formal review by the state medical board, which rules on whether a dismissal is justified
A written warning setting out how many further missed visits will end the relationship
Notice to the insurer, which decides whether the patient may be dropped from the panel
preguntas.explicacion: Conflict resolution is expected to start by exploring the reasons underneath the disagreement and setting reasonable, clear expectations for the relationship going forward. Where those efforts fail, the step to consider is formal mediation by an ombudsperson, a professional mediator or a hospital ethics committee. Only where the conflict proves intractable does the standard notification procedure begin.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: The Intervention
preguntas.subtema: Open access scheduling · CMAA 4A k51 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A caller with a routine problem is told the next opening is six weeks away, and the practice is considering open access. What does that model do?
opciones: It offers every caller a slot on the day of the call, almost always with her own physician
It sorts callers by how urgent the problem sounds and books routine ones into a later week
It reserves about half of each day for the follow-up visits clinicians asked for in advance
It lets plan members go straight to a specialist, since the gatekeeper has been removed
preguntas.explicacion: Open access, also called advanced access or same-day scheduling, gives patients a slot the day they call, usually with their own clinician. Roughly half the day is left open; the rest holds clinically necessary follow-ups and the patients who preferred another day, normally no more than a quarter. The same words also name the removal of HMO gatekeepers, which is a different idea.

preguntas.fuente: Child Welfare Information Gateway, Mandatory Reporting of Child Abuse and Neglect (May 2023), Institutional Responsibility To Report
preguntas.subtema: Mandatory reporting · CCMA 7F k222 · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k43
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital policy says staff must tell the department head, who then calls child protective services. Does that policy discharge the staff member's duty?
opciones: In many states no: internal policy does not relieve the reporter
Yes, once the notification to the department head is documented
Yes, because institutional reporting replaces individual reporting
Yes, in the nine states where the institution's head files the report
preguntas.explicacion: States handle institutional reporting differently: in some the staff member notifies the head of the institution, in some the head then files, and in others the person reports to the child protection authority first and tells the institution afterwards. What 17 states and two other jurisdictions make explicit is that whatever the organization's policy says, the mandatory reporter is not relieved of the duty.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Error Reduction and Prevention", Function: Analyzing Root Causes and Sentinel Events
preguntas.subtema: Incident reporting · CCMA 7F · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3E k44
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is a sentinel event?
opciones: A surgical instrument left inside the patient and found afterwards
A near miss intercepted by the pharmacist before the dose was given
A latent equipment fault found during preventive maintenance rounds
An adverse drug reaction that the patient's chart already warned about
preguntas.explicacion: A sentinel event is an occurrence, unexpected, that involves death or serious injury of body or mind, or the risk of one. The published list runs to an object left inside a patient once the operation is over, procedures on the wrong patient or the wrong site, abduction, a child discharged to the wrong family, and a hemolytic transfusion reaction. Each triggers an immediate investigation.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, "Talking With Your Older Patients", Compensating for visual deficits
preguntas.subtema: Vision impairment · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(2) / 2027 F.1.d(3) · RMA I.D.1.a · CMAA 2D k17
preguntas.pregunta: An office is reprinting its handouts for a geriatric clinic. What is the minimum type size recommended for older patients?
opciones: 14-point type, in a typeface that is easy to read
10-point type, in a typeface that is easy to read
12-point type, in a typeface that is easy to read
18-point type, in a typeface that is easy to read
preguntas.explicacion: Printed handouts and questionnaires for older patients should use at least 14-point type in an easy-to-read typeface, with enough space between items to answer. Where low vision makes reading hard, offer something else: instructions in audio, diagrams enlarged, or pillboxes with raised markings.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 2.1
preguntas.subtema: Downtime drills · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Staff have never worked a shift on paper. Which training practice does the contingency guidance recommend to fix that?
opciones: Unannounced downtime drills held at least once a year for the whole staff
A yearly written test on the downtime policy graded by the security official
A refresher whenever the record system is upgraded by its own developer
A briefing given to every new hire during the first week of employment
preguntas.explicacion: At any moment an organization is likely to have staff who have never worked in a paper-based environment. The guidance answers that with training requirements, paper-based ordering and charting practice, and downtime drills held without warning at least once a year, so people meet the situation before it is real.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 3, Guidelines for Using a Medical Interpreter
preguntas.subtema: Interpreters · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17
preguntas.pregunta: Why is an interpreter matched to the patient's gender sought where that is possible?
opciones: To spare embarrassment when the matter discussed is sensitive
Because certification requires it whenever an exam is intimate
Because it is the only way to keep the exchange confidential
So the interpreter may answer for the patient where needed
preguntas.explicacion: Where it can be arranged, the guidance asks for a medical interpreter matched to the patient's gender, to head off embarrassment when a sensitive matter is being discussed. It is a preference, not a certification requirement, and an interpreter never answers on the patient's behalf.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", Other Issues: Violations of HIPAA; StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Civil and Criminal Violations
preguntas.subtema: Penalty tiers · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k34
preguntas.pregunta: Among the HIPAA civil penalty tiers, which category carries the highest penalty per violation?
opciones: Willful neglect that is not corrected
Willful neglect corrected within the period
Reasonable cause, not willful neglect
A violation the person did not know about
preguntas.explicacion: The four civil tiers climb with culpability: not knowing of the violation, reasonable cause short of willful neglect, willful neglect put right inside the required period, and willful neglect left uncorrected, which tops the scale at $50,000 per violation. Criminal liability is a separate ladder, starting with knowingly obtaining or disclosing identifiable information, rising when it is done under false pretenses, and rising again when it is done for commercial advantage, for personal gain, or to do malicious harm. The civil side is enforced by the Office for Civil Rights.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Common Barriers to Communication
preguntas.subtema: Barriers to communication · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.3.b / 2027 F.1.i
preguntas.pregunta: A patient holds beliefs about her plan of care that the assistant does not share. How should the information be given?
opciones: In a nonjudgmental way, even though the beliefs are not the same
By agreeing with the belief so that she stays in the conversation
After moving her to a quieter area where the beliefs can be argued
Through a family member who already shares the same viewpoint
preguntas.explicacion: Differences in perception and viewpoint are a listed barrier: patients who feel their beliefs are not valued tend to disengage from the conversation and from the plan of care, so information is given without judgment even when the views differ. Agreeing is named as a pitfall, and routing the message through a relative is what the interpreter guidance warns against.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, When can I sign up for Medicare?
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who kept working past sixty-five retires in March. How long does she then have to sign up for Part B?
opciones: Eight months from the day she or her spouse stops working, COBRA notwithstanding
Eight months from the day the job-based coverage itself ends, COBRA included
Seven months around her sixty-fifth birthday, a period that has already passed
Sixty-three days, the gap allowed before a drug coverage penalty begins to run
preguntas.explicacion: The eight-month Special Enrollment Period for Part B starts when the person or the spouse stops working, even if COBRA or some other non-Medicare coverage is taken up in the meantime. Someone who loses job-based coverage before that date has eight months from then. Missing the period means a wait, a gap and a monthly penalty for as long as Part B is held.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Managed Care, Summary
preguntas.subtema: Managed care · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.e (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: Which three plan designs are usually grouped together as managed care?
opciones: Health maintenance, preferred provider and point of service plans
Health maintenance, preferred provider and prescription drug plans
Health savings, flexible spending and high deductible health plans
Hospital insurance, medical insurance and supplemental policies
preguntas.explicacion: Managed care plans contract with providers and facilities to care for members at reduced cost, and the three types described are the health maintenance organization, the preferred provider organization and the point of service plan, which lets the patient choose between the two approaches at each visit. Savings and spending accounts are ways to pay costs, not plan designs, and hospital plus medical insurance describes the two parts of Original Medicare.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Cost sharing
preguntas.subtema: Cost sharing · CMA III.G.6.e (2027 III.G.6.d) · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: How does cost sharing in Medicaid and CHIP differ from cost sharing in a commercial plan?
opciones: In those programs the premium counts as cost sharing too
In those programs the deductible is never counted into it
In those programs only the copayment is counted into it
In those programs the balance billed amount is counted in
preguntas.explicacion: Cost sharing is the member's own share of the cost of covered services, and it generally covers deductibles, coinsurance and copayments while leaving out premiums, balance-billed amounts and non-covered care. In Medicaid and CHIP the federal glossary counts premiums within cost sharing as well, which is the exception worth remembering.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Administrative Simplification: Transactions
preguntas.subtema: Claim submission · CMA III.G.3.b(1) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6C k87 · CCMA 5L k185
preguntas.pregunta: An employer and a health plan exchange the payment of the plan premium electronically. Is that one of the transactions HIPAA standardized?
opciones: Yes, premium payment is on the list of adopted transactions
No, only claims and remittances are on that adopted list
No, only exchanges between a plan and a provider are on it
Yes, but only where a clearinghouse handles it for the two
preguntas.explicacion: The adopted transactions run wider than the claim. On the list sit payment and remittance advice; the status of a claim; eligibility; how benefits are coordinated; claims and encounter data; enrollment and disenrolment; referrals and authorizations; and the payment of the premium. Several of them, that last one included, never involve a provider at all.

preguntas.subtema: Consent in the record · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.a · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which item does the medical record condition of participation expect to find in the chart before a procedure the medical staff has designated?
opciones: An informed consent form, properly executed, for that procedure or treatment
A copy of the notice of privacy practices signed by the patient at check-in
An advance beneficiary notice explaining what the health plan may not pay for
A statement from the patient describing why the procedure is being requested
preguntas.explicacion: The record must document, as appropriate, informed consent forms properly executed for whichever procedures and treatments the medical staff, or Federal or State law, has specified as needing written consent. The same list runs to consultative evaluations, complications and infections acquired in hospital, every practitioner order and the nursing notes, records of treatment and of medication, reports from radiology and from the laboratory, and the vital signs.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare Summary Notice (MSN)
preguntas.subtema: Explanation of benefits · CMAA 5 k78 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.3.b(2) · RMA II.A.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient calls upset about the explanation of benefits she received, saying she cannot pay that bill today. What should she be told?
opciones: It explains how the claim was handled and what she may owe; it is not the bill itself
It is the bill from her health plan, and payment goes to the plan rather than the office
It is the plan's request for more information before it decides whether to pay
It is the written order her primary care doctor sent so the plan would pay
preguntas.explicacion: The notice a patient gets after adjudication reports the services billed, what the plan paid, and the most the patient may owe the provider. In Original Medicare the equivalent document is the Medicare Summary Notice, which states plainly that it is not a bill. A request for more information and a referral from the primary care doctor are entirely different documents.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0, Tool: Two-Challenge Rule
preguntas.subtema: Escalation · CCMA 6K k210 · CMAA 2B k25
preguntas.pregunta: Where did the Two-Challenge Rule come from?
opciones: Human factors work on keeping airline captains from disaster
Military radio traffic, where every message is confirmed back
Crew resource management courses written for operating rooms
An alert on handoff communication issued to hospitals in 2017
preguntas.explicacion: Human factors experts built the rule so that airline captains could head off disaster when decision makers who were otherwise excellent had a momentary lapse of judgment, and it was carried into clinical work. Closed-loop communication is the one that comes from military radio transmissions, and the 2017 alert concerned inadequate handoffs.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: What should I know before my telehealth visit?
preguntas.subtema: What to ask before booking · CMAA 4E k59 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient about to book her first video visit says she has no health insurance and is worried about the bill. What does the patient guidance tell her to do?
opciones: Ask beforehand what the visit will cost, since her provider may know of local resources
Book the visit anyway, since a visit taken by video is free of charge to the patient
Ask her plan for a preauthorization, which will fix in advance what she is going to owe
Wait for an in-person appointment instead, since a price is quoted only for those visits
preguntas.explicacion: Before a telehealth visit the patient is told to know the costs and to ask what the visit will come to. If she cannot afford it or has no health insurance, her provider may have local resources. The same list asks her to say if she needs help such as a screen reader or closed captioning, to check the details in the reminder she is sent, to find a quiet spot with good internet, and to test her device beforehand.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, Exclusions Program
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: A nurse practitioner on the exclusion list writes an order that the practice then acts on. What does exclusion mean for payment?
opciones: No federal program pays for anything she furnishes, orders or prescribes
No federal program pays her directly, though her employer may still bill for it
No federal program pays her until the exclusion period ends and lapses by itself
No federal program pays for what she furnishes, but her written orders are payable
