preguntas.explicacion: An excluded person can be paid nothing by federal health care programs for any item or service she furnishes, orders or prescribes, and that bites on every program whose health benefits the United States funds, directly or indirectly, with the Federal Employees Health Benefits Plan as the one carve-out. The order itself is caught, not only the hands-on service.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Personal Representatives: General Provisions
preguntas.subtema: Personal representatives · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.3.c · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A man holds a limited health care power of attorney covering only his mother's life support decisions. What may he access?
opciones: Only the protected health information relevant to the decision his authority actually covers
The complete designated record set, because any power of attorney makes him her representative
No information, since a power of attorney is not a document the Privacy Rule recognizes
Only the billing records, because clinical information stays with the patient in every case
preguntas.explicacion: A personal representative must generally be treated as the individual, but the scope of that authority comes from the underlying law. Where it is broad, as with a parent of a minor or the guardian of an incompetent adult, the representative is treated as the individual for all purposes; where it is limited to particular decisions, the representative is treated as the individual only for information relevant to that representation.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.404(c), Content of notification
preguntas.subtema: Breach notice content · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3E k33
preguntas.pregunta: Which element must a breach notification letter to an individual include?
opciones: Steps the individual can take to protect against potential harm
The name of the workforce member who caused the breach
A copy of the covered entity's complete privacy policies and procedures
The civil penalty amount the covered entity expects to pay to HHS
preguntas.explicacion: In plain language, and as far as it can, the letter describes what happened, with the date of the breach and the date it was discovered; which types of unsecured PHI were involved, such as a name, a Social Security number, a date of birth or a diagnosis; what individuals should do to protect themselves; what the entity is doing to investigate, to limit the harm and to stop it happening again; and how to make contact, by toll-free number, e-mail, website or postal address. Naming the employee, attaching the policies and estimating penalties are no part of the required content.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Issues of Concern: Specific Techniques
preguntas.subtema: Therapeutic techniques · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2E k21 · CMA F.2 / 2027 F.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: A patient says she is scared her results will be bad. The assistant answers, "You are scared about the results." Which technique is that?
opciones: Reflecting, repeating back what the patient said
Summarizing, restating the visit in the staff member's words
Clarifying, guiding the patient to give more detail
Providing rationale, explaining why the test was ordered
preguntas.explicacion: Reflecting repeats back what the patient said, at times word for word, to show that they are being listened to. Summarizing gathers several points in the interviewer's own words and often closes an interview; clarifying is a guiding statement that draws out more; providing rationale explains why the information is needed.

preguntas.subtema: Security official · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA I.C.5 · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which Security Rule standard does a practice meet by naming one person to develop and run its security policies?
opciones: Assigned security responsibility, which asks for an identified security official
Security management process, which is met by writing out the policies themselves
Workforce security, which settles which staff members may reach the information
Evaluation, which reviews whether the safeguards still fit how the practice works
preguntas.explicacion: Assigned security responsibility is a standard in its own right: name the security official who will develop the policies the subpart requires and put them into effect. It is the security counterpart of the privacy official the Privacy Rule asks for, and one person may hold both roles.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: De-Identified Health Information
preguntas.subtema: De-identification · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3B k35 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A quality committee wants a data file with no restrictions on its later use. Which step achieves that under the Privacy Rule?
opciones: Stripping the listed identifiers of the patient, relatives, employers and household members
Removing only the names and leaving birth dates, addresses and account numbers in place
Replacing each patient name with the medical record number used inside the practice
Having the privacy official sign a statement that the file is for internal use only
preguntas.explicacion: De-identified information carries no restrictions on use or disclosure, and two routes lead to it. One is a qualified statistician making a formal determination; the other is stripping out the identifiers specified for the individual herself and for her relatives, household members and employers, which counts only where the entity has no actual knowledge that what remains could still identify somebody. Medical record numbers, account numbers and full-face photographs are on the safe harbor list.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(b)(1) and (b)(2), Standard: Minimum necessary
preguntas.subtema: Minimum necessary exceptions · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: To which disclosure does the HIPAA minimum necessary standard NOT apply?
opciones: A disclosure to a health care provider for treatment
A disclosure to a health plan for payment
A disclosure to a business associate for operations
A disclosure to a researcher under a privacy board waiver
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity using, disclosing or requesting PHI must make reasonable efforts to keep it to the minimum necessary for the purpose. Section 164.502(b)(2) sets out where that does not apply: a provider disclosing for treatment or asking for what treatment needs; uses and disclosures to the individual; anything done under an authorization; disclosures to the Secretary for compliance; and uses required by law or by the rule itself. Payment, operations and research disclosures all stay under the minimum necessary limit.

preguntas.subtema: Business associate agreements · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33
preguntas.pregunta: An outside company will digitize the clinic's paper charts. What does HIPAA require before it receives the PHI?
opciones: Satisfactory assurances in a written business associate contract that it will safeguard the PHI
A signed authorization from every patient whose chart will be digitized by the company
Only the notice of privacy practices, since scanning counts as a health care operation
A certificate of accreditation for the company from a CMS-approved organization, renewed yearly
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.502(e) lets a covered entity disclose PHI to a business associate, and let it create, receive, maintain or transmit PHI on its behalf, if it first secures satisfactory assurances that the associate will safeguard the information, documented in a written contract or arrangement meeting 164.504(e); the associate may then use the PHI only as its contract or the law permits, and must secure the same assurances from any subcontractor. Patient authorizations are not needed for this kind of operational service, and accreditation is a CLIA concept.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Hospice care: Coverage details and Who's eligible
preguntas.subtema: Coordinating with the patient's provider · CCMA 4E · CMA II.F.4.a / 2027 II.F.2.a · CMAA 2H k30
preguntas.pregunta: Once hospice starts, may a patient keep seeing the doctor who has treated her for years?
opciones: Yes, if she named that doctor or nurse practitioner as the attending professional
Yes, but only for health problems that are unrelated to the terminal illness
No, because every clinician involved must be employed by the hospice agency itself
No, unless the hospice medical director signs a new election statement first
preguntas.explicacion: All care for the terminal illness has to be given or arranged by the hospice the patient chose, and care from a hospice the team did not set up is not covered. One opening remains: the patient may keep her own doctor or nurse practitioner if she named that person the attending professional who helps supervise hospice care. The election statement records that choice.

preguntas.subtema: Amendment of the record · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.5
preguntas.pregunta: A patient says her chart lists an allergy she does not have and asks the office to fix it. How long does the practice have to act?
opciones: Sixty days, with one thirty day extension if the patient is told the reason in writing
Thirty days, the same period the rule gives for responding to a request for access
Ten working days, after which the entry must be deleted from the electronic record
Six years, the period the rule sets for keeping its privacy policies and procedures
preguntas.explicacion: The amendment right lets an individual ask a covered entity to correct PHI in the designated record set that is inaccurate or incomplete. The regulation gives 60 days to act on the request, with a single 30 day extension. If the amendment is accepted, the entity must make reasonable efforts to pass it on to those the individual names and to those it knows may rely on the old information to her detriment.

preguntas.fuente: TRICARE, About TRICARE; and VA, CHAMPVA benefits; and DOL, Office of Workers' Compensation Programs
preguntas.subtema: Insurance types · CMA III.G.4.d (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which agency manages TRICARE?
opciones: The Defense Health Agency, under the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Health Affairs
The Department of Veterans Affairs, through the Veterans Health Administration
The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, through its own regional offices
The Office of Workers' Compensation Programs, through the Department of Labor
preguntas.explicacion: TRICARE is the health care program serving members of the uniformed services, retirees and their families, wherever in the world they are, and it is run by the Defense Health Agency, which answers to the Defense Department's Assistant Secretary for Health Affairs. Veterans' benefits and CHAMPVA belong to the Department of Veterans Affairs, and the federal injury compensation programs to the Labor Department.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Authorization
preguntas.subtema: Authorization to release · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A life insurance company asks the office for a patient's records to decide on a policy. What does the office need?
opciones: The patient's written authorization, since this purpose is outside treatment, payment or operations
No document at all, since disclosures to insurers count as payment activities of a plan
A note in the accounting of disclosures, which by itself makes the release permissible
The good faith acknowledgment the patient signed for the notice of privacy practices
preguntas.explicacion: Written authorization is required for any use or disclosure that falls outside treatment, outside payment and outside health care operations, and that is not otherwise permitted or required. The examples OCR gives are a disclosure to a life insurer weighing coverage, a pre- employment physical result going to an employer, and information going to a drug company for its own marketing. The payment definition reaches the patient's health plan, not a life insurer.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet MLN006397 Federally Qualified Health Center: Certification
preguntas.subtema: FQHC certification · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: Under the Public Health Service Act's section 330, which requirement must a center meet to be certified as an FQHC?
opciones: Offer a sliding fee scale to people with incomes below 200% of the poverty guidelines
Keep no more than 25 inpatient beds, counting swing beds, the way a rural hospital does
Sit more than a 35-mile drive on primary roads away from any other hospital or clinic
Report an annual average acute inpatient length of stay of 96 hours or less each year
preguntas.explicacion: Certification asks for comprehensive services with ongoing quality assurance, compliance with health and safety rules, and no approval as a rural health clinic. Section 330 adds three conditions: serving a designated underserved area or population, a sliding fee scale below 200% of the poverty guidelines, and a board most of whose members get care there. Bed and mileage limits belong to critical access hospitals.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicare Coverage Determination Process
preguntas.subtema: Medical necessity · CMA III.G.1.d (2027 III.G.1.d) · CMAA 5 k69 · CCMA 5J k180
preguntas.pregunta: CMS receives a complete request for a national coverage determination that needs no outside technology assessment and no advisory committee review. How long may the decision take?
opciones: No more than six months after the completed request is received
No more than nine months after the completed request is received
No more than sixty days after the completed request is received
No more than one year after the completed request is received
preguntas.explicacion: Coverage of an item or service is limited to what is reasonable and necessary, and national determinations are reached through an evidence-based process with fixed deadlines. A request that needs no external assessment and no advisory committee is decided within six months of the completed request; one that needs either of them, within nine.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Outpatient hospital services: Description
preguntas.subtema: Outpatient hospital services · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas.pregunta: Which service is paid as a hospital outpatient service rather than as inpatient hospital care?
opciones: Observation services, which may include a night in the hospital, and same-day surgery
A stay that begins with a doctor's written order for admission and lasts at least one night
A semi-private room, meals and general nursing supplied after a formal admission
Care in a long-term care hospital for a patient with several serious conditions
preguntas.explicacion: Part B covers a great many services of diagnosis and treatment given to a patient as a hospital outpatient. The list takes in observation or emergency services that can involve a night in the building, laboratory and radiology tests the hospital bills, partial hospitalization for mental health, and supplies such as splints and casts. Admission with an order is what makes a stay inpatient.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Parts of Medicare
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.b / 2027 III.G.4 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: Which services does Medicare Part A help cover?
opciones: Inpatient hospital stays, skilled nursing facility care, hospice and home health
Inpatient hospital stays, doctors' services in the office and durable equipment
Outpatient care, preventive screenings and yearly wellness visits with a doctor
Prescription drugs bought at the pharmacy and many recommended vaccines
preguntas.explicacion: Part A is the hospital insurance half of Original Medicare: inpatient hospital care, care in a skilled nursing facility, hospice, and some home health care. Doctors' services, outpatient care, durable medical equipment and preventive services sit under Part B, and drugs bought at the pharmacy come through Part D, either as a standalone plan or built into a Medicare Advantage plan.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Mandatory & Optional Medicaid Benefits
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.c (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A family moving out of state asks whether their new state's Medicaid has to cover the child's dental care. What is the accurate answer?
opciones: Dental care is optional, so a state adds it only through the state plan process
Dental care is mandatory, in the same way family planning services are mandatory
Dental care is mandatory, in the same way nurse midwife services are mandatory
Dental care is mandatory, as federally qualified health center services are
preguntas.explicacion: The federal list separates the benefits every state has to provide from those a state may add through the state plan process. Family planning, nurse midwife services and federally qualified health center services are mandatory; dental services, clinic services, physical therapy, private duty nursing and other licensed practitioner services are optional.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information: Providing the Notice
preguntas.subtema: Availability of the notice · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Besides handing the notice of privacy practices to new patients, where must a treatment provider keep it available?
opciones: Posted at the facility, with copies to take away, and on a website describing its services
Posted at the facility, with copies to take away, and filed with the state licensing board
Posted in the staff area, with copies to take away, and sent to each health plan it bills
Posted at the facility, with copies on request, and read aloud before the first appointment
preguntas.explicacion: The latest version, the one reflecting any change in privacy policies, has to be available at the office for people to ask for and take with them, and posted where it can be seen clearly. Any website the entity keeps that describes its customer services or benefits must carry the notice prominently, and anyone who asks for a copy gets one.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.3 Strategies for Communicating with Patients with Impaired Hearing and Vision
preguntas.subtema: Vision impairment · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(2) / 2027 F.1.d(3) · CMAA 2D k17
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant walks into the room of a patient with very low vision. What comes first?
opciones: Identifying themselves as they enter the patient's space
Handing over the large-print copy of the instructions
Turning the overhead lighting off to cut down the glare
Taking the patient by the arm to guide them to the chair
preguntas.explicacion: For impaired vision the opening step is to identify yourself on entering the patient's space. After that, check that glasses are present, clean and current, provide enough room lighting while minimizing glare, and supply material in large print or read the pertinent parts aloud.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Function
preguntas.subtema: Therapeutic communication · CCMA 6C k199 · CMAA 2A k13 · CMA F.2 / 2027 F.1.d
preguntas.pregunta: What is the goal of therapeutic communication as it is generally defined?
opciones: Helping the patient get past some form of emotional or mental distress
Gathering the history in the shortest time the appointment allows
Making sure the record holds everything the provider will need later
Keeping the rest of the team informed of changes in the patient
preguntas.explicacion: The definition in general use describes an exchange between patient and provider using verbal and nonverbal methods, whose ultimate goal is to help the patient overcome emotional or psychological distress. Speed, documentation and reports to other team members are real duties, but they are not what this term names.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Workplace Violence", Pathophysiology: Incognizance
preguntas.subtema: Difficult situations · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k16
preguntas.pregunta: What does incognizance mean as a reason for not reporting workplace violence?
opciones: Not knowing what actually counts as workplace violence
Treating the abuse as an ordinary part of that kind of job
Fearing that a report will draw the abuser's attention back
Finding the reporting process too slow for a busy shift
preguntas.explicacion: Roughly seven in ten staff have never reported the violence they suffered, and two themes explain it. Trivialization is treating abuse as part of the job. Incognizance is not understanding what actually counts as workplace violence, including the mistaken belief that with no physical injury nothing happened. Fear of retaliation and a cumbersome process are separate obstacles.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms: Coinsurance and Out-of-network Coinsurance
preguntas.subtema: Financial calculations · CMA III.G.8, III.G.6.e (2027 III.G.6.b, III.G.6.d) · CMAA 5C k76, 4 k61 · CCMA 5K k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A plan allows $150 for a visit, the patient has met her deductible, and her out-of-network coinsurance is 40%. What is her coinsurance for that visit?
opciones: Sixty dollars, which is forty percent of the amount the plan allows
Thirty dollars, which is twenty percent of the amount the plan allows
Ninety dollars, which is the share the plan itself pays on that visit
A hundred and fifty dollars, since out-of-network care sits outside the plan
preguntas.explicacion: Coinsurance is the patient's share of a covered service, worked out as a percentage of the allowed amount and paid on top of any deductible owed. Out-of-network coinsurance is the share owed to providers who have no contract with the plan, and it usually costs more than the in-network share, with forty percent against twenty percent given as the illustration.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: Cataract surgery was done on the right eye last month and the left eye is treated today, with the right one now resolved. Which code fits today's visit?
opciones: The unilateral code for the eye that still has the condition
The bilateral code, since both eyes had the condition this year
The unspecified side code, because only one side is treated now
Two codes, one for each of the eyes that have been treated so far
preguntas.explicacion: The bilateral code is assigned while the condition exists on both sides, including at the encounter that treats the first side. At the second encounter, once treatment has resolved the condition on the side already done, the appropriate unilateral code is used for the side that still has it. If the first treatment did not resolve it, the bilateral code still fits.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse: Prevent, Detect, Report (MLN4649244), Physician Self-Referral Law
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: A group bills for a designated health service, unaware that the referral behind it broke the self-referral law. What is the position?
opciones: Filing the claim is prohibited anyway, since intent is not needed
Filing the claim is allowed, because the group did not know of it
Filing is allowed if the referral is put right after the payment
Filing is prohibited only where the referral was made on purpose
preguntas.explicacion: The self-referral law stops the entity from billing at all for a designated health service that came from an improper referral, and it does so whether or not the entity knew of the problem or meant to claim for it. If Medicare pays such a claim the entity holds an overpayment, which has to be reported and returned within 60 days of being identified.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology
preguntas.subtema: Access barriers · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient books her first video visit and says she has no internet at home. Which option does HHS suggest the office raise with her?
opciones: A public library, which usually offers high-speed internet and often a private room
A relative's telephone, which she can borrow for the length of the appointment
The clinic waiting room, where she can join the call on the practice's own tablet
A paper questionnaire she can post back instead of attending the appointment
preguntas.explicacion: Having no internet service with the bandwidth for video is named as one of the biggest barriers keeping patients away from telehealth. The suggestions offered are that the patient might be eligible for federal help under the Lifeline program, that plenty of fast food restaurants throw free Wi-Fi as far as the parking lot, and that most public libraries provide high-speed internet and often a private room.

preguntas.fuente: TRICARE, About TRICARE; and HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Grandfathered health plan
preguntas.subtema: Insurance types · CMA III.G.4.d (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182
preguntas.pregunta: How do most TRICARE health plans stand against the Affordable Care Act's coverage requirement?
opciones: They satisfy the law's standard for minimum essential coverage
They are exempt from that law, being run by the Department of Defense
They meet the requirement for active-duty members but not for families
They count as grandfathered plans, so the requirement never reaches them
preguntas.explicacion: Minimum essential coverage is the standard the Affordable Care Act sets, and most of the program's health plans meet it. What TRICARE gives its beneficiaries is comprehensive: dental plans, prescriptions, special programs and health plans. A grandfathered plan is a different thing altogether, an individual or job-based plan that already existed when the law was signed and has not changed much since.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth check-in · CCMA 5R · CMA III.H.2.a · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 5A · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A video visit is about to begin. Which step belongs to the start of the encounter?
opciones: Confirming who the patient is and why she has come to the visit
Submitting the claim with the telehealth modifier already attached
Collecting the patient's feedback on how the technology performed
Sending the appointment reminder with the link to the platform
preguntas.explicacion: The workflow lists the steps in order. Ahead of the visit come the reminder, guidance on using the technology, the online paperwork, a walk-through of the equipment, troubleshooting information, consent and a request that the patient find somewhere quiet and private. The visit itself opens with confirmation, establishing who the patient is and what has brought her, and intake follows. Billing and evaluation come afterwards.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases, chapter 5: Scheduling and Receiving Deliveries
preguntas.subtema: Receiving deliveries · CCMA 5T · RMA II.B.5.a · CMAA 7D k99 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: What does the storage and handling guidance say about when a delivery of temperature-sensitive stock may be scheduled?
opciones: Only on days and at hours when staff will be there, and it is never left unattended
On any weekday, provided the carrier leaves the container in a shaded doorway
Only on the first working day of the week, so the count matches the month's order
On any day, provided the container is opened within four hours of its arrival
preguntas.explicacion: Delivery dates and times are chosen so that somebody is there to receive them, and the container is never left standing alone. The coordinator or the alternate is told the moment it arrives, and the contents are unpacked and put into the storage unit straight away rather than left in the shipping box.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms: Minimum Value Standard
preguntas.subtema: Insurance types · CMA III.G.4.a (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: An employee is told her job-based plan meets the minimum value standard. What does that mean about the plan?
opciones: It pays at least sixty percent of the total allowed costs of benefits
It pays at least eighty percent of the total allowed costs of benefits
It covers at least sixty percent of the essential health benefits
It caps her own share of the allowed costs at sixty percent a year
preguntas.explicacion: The minimum value standard measures the percentage of permitted costs a plan covers. An employer plan that pays for at least sixty percent of the total allowed costs of benefits offers minimum value, and the employee offered it may then not qualify for premium tax credits or cost-sharing reductions on the Marketplace.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Reimbursement Models and Accountable Care", Capitated payment
preguntas.subtema: Payment models · CMAA 6 k82 · CCMA 1 k6
preguntas.pregunta: What is capitation?
opciones: A fixed amount paid per patient regardless of the services they receive
A fixed amount paid per service regardless of how many patients receive it
A share of the savings paid when a group beats its spending benchmark
A penalty applied to payment when readmissions exceed the expected rate
preguntas.explicacion: Capitation pays clinicians a set amount for each patient whatever services that patient uses, which encourages cost control and preventive care but raises concerns about patient selection and about care being withheld. Paying for each service delivered is fee for service, shared savings belong to accountable care arrangements, and readmission penalties come from a separate hospital program.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Evacuation Plans and Procedures eTool, Emergency Action Plan: Minimum Requirements [29 CFR 1910.38(b)]
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.B.8.a · 2027 I.B.7.a · CMAA 3 k45 · RMA II.7.c · NCMA 2A.9 EKB 8
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic with 8 employees asks whether its emergency action plan has to be in writing. What is the answer?
opciones: No: with 10 or fewer employees the plan may be communicated orally
No: any employer may keep the plan oral if the staff are trained yearly
Yes: the plan is written whenever the workplace has any employees at all
Yes: only a plan of 25 or fewer employees may be communicated orally
preguntas.explicacion: The plan is normally written down and held at the workplace where employees can consult it; the exception is an employer of 10 employees or fewer, who may pass it on by word of mouth. That is the only exception in the rule; the six minimum elements still have to be covered, and everyone still has to know how to respond.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Long-term care: Description and Facility
preguntas.subtema: Non-clinical community resources · CCMA 4D k164 · CMAA 2H k30
preguntas.pregunta: A family asks what non-medical long-term supports exist in the community. Which list fits?
opciones: Adult day health care, transportation, and meals delivered to the home
Skilled nursing visits, physical therapy, and durable medical equipment
Partial hospitalization, psychiatric evaluation, and medication management
Laboratory work, radiology billed by the hospital, and same-day surgery
preguntas.explicacion: Long-term care, which also goes by custodial care or by long-term services and support, is mostly help with the basic personal tasks of daily life. The examples given are personal care assistance with dressing, bathing and using the bathroom, meals delivered to the home, adult day health care and transportation. It can be arranged in the community, at home, in a nursing home or in assisted living.

preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, prognosis
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k5 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what the doctor meant by prognosis. Which answer is accurate?
opciones: The likely course of the disease and the chance of recovery or recurrence
The name given to the disease after the exam and the tests are reviewed
The extent of the disease within the body at the moment it is discovered
The cause or origin of the disease that brought the patient to the visit
preguntas.explicacion: A prognosis is what the disease is expected to do: how it will probably run, and what chance there is of recovery or of a return. The distractors are the terms that sit next to it: diagnosis is identifying the disease from its signs and symptoms, staging measures how far it has spread, and etiology is its cause or origin.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Marketing
preguntas.subtema: Marketing and PHI · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A vendor offers to pay the practice for its patient list so it can promote a product. What does the Privacy Rule require?
opciones: An authorization from each patient, and it must reveal the payment involved
A business associate agreement, after which no authorization is needed
A notice in the accounting of disclosures listing the names that were sold
Removal of the diagnoses from the list, after which it may be sold freely
preguntas.explicacion: Marketing means any communication that talks up a product or a service so as to encourage buying or using it, and it also reaches an arrangement where a covered entity discloses PHI for payment, direct or indirect, so that another entity can push its own products. Authorization is required, save for face-to-face marketing between the entity and the individual and for promotional gifts of nominal value; where a third party is paying, the authorization has to say so.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 7: Improve Telephone Access
preguntas.subtema: Telephone etiquette · CCMA 6C k196 · CMAA 2A k27 · NCMA F.23
preguntas.pregunta: A practice is rebuilding the automated menu callers hear. How many options should that menu offer at most?
opciones: No more than five
No more than three
No more than eight
No more than twelve
preguntas.explicacion: A patient-friendly automated system keeps the menu to five choices at most, offers the languages patients commonly speak, and always leaves a way to reach a person, because some callers are intimidated by machines. A confusing system or a long wait makes some patients simply hang up.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Billing: CMS-1500 & 837P (MLN006976), Procedure Coding; and CMS, ICD-10 Codes
preguntas.subtema: Procedural coding · CMA III.G.1.c (2027 III.G.1.c) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which code set reports the procedures on an inpatient hospital claim to Medicare Part A?
opciones: The procedure coding system of ICD-10, which CMS keeps
ICD-10-CM, which reports the reason for the admission
HCPCS Level II, which names supplies and equipment
HCPCS Level I, which names professional services
preguntas.explicacion: Procedures on inpatient facility claims under Part A are reported with the ICD-10 procedure coding system, which CMS maintains and updates each October. The clinical modification of ICD-10 is for diagnoses, and the two levels of HCPCS carry professional services and the products and supplies billed outside them.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Health Care Payment and Remittance Advice (835/ERA)
preguntas.subtema: Remittance advice · CMA III.G.3.b(3) (exam through June 2027) · CMAA 5 k79 · CCMA 5 k181
preguntas.pregunta: A small practice cannot read the electronic remittance file its Medicare contractor sends. What does Medicare offer it?
opciones: Free software from the contractor that displays and prints the remittance advice
A paid subscription through a clearinghouse that translates the remittance file
A paper remittance mailed alongside each electronic one the contractor sends out
A page on the contractor's website where each remittance can be viewed for 30 days
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare gives providers free software for reading the electronic remittance and printing something equivalent to the paper version; institutional and professional providers get their own version from their contractors. It lets the remittance be viewed and printed whenever it is wanted, instead of requesting the paper one and waiting for the mail, and the version for professional providers also exports reports to a spreadsheet.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10 Codes
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · CMA III.G.1.b · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: When do new ICD-10 codes take effect each year?
opciones: October 1, for encounters and discharges from that date onward
January 1, for encounters and discharges from that date onward
July 1, halfway through the federal fiscal year for that update
The date each Medicare contractor loads the files into its system
preguntas.explicacion: Updated diagnosis and procedure codes take effect on October 1: CMS announces the new ICD-10-PCS codes and the CDC the new ICD-10-CM codes, and they apply to discharges and patient encounters from that date. January 1 is the start of the calendar year used for other purposes, and contractors load the files to meet the national date rather than setting their own.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0, Tool: Two-Challenge Rule
preguntas.subtema: Escalation · CCMA 6K k210 · CMAA 2B k25 · CMA F.1.f / 2027 F.1.f
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant raises a safety concern and it is brushed aside. What does the Two-Challenge Rule require?
opciones: Voicing the concern assertively at least two times
Filing an incident report before speaking up again
Waiting for the next huddle to bring the matter up
Accepting the decision of the team leader as final
preguntas.explicacion: Where a first assertive statement goes ignored, it falls to the challenger to restate the concern assertively so that it has certainly been heard, at least twice. The person being challenged has to acknowledge hearing and understanding it, and rephrasing the anticipated danger is the next move.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, "Talking With Your Older Patients", Obtaining a thorough history
preguntas.subtema: Questioning techniques · CCMA 6C k200 · CMAA 2A k15
preguntas.pregunta: Why is a patient asked more than once whether there is something else to raise?
opciones: The main concern often is not the first one mentioned
It gives the patient a yes-or-no question to rest on
It signals that the physical examination is about to start
It takes the place of the summary that closes the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Patients rarely lead with their main complaint, especially when the topic is sensitive, so a prompting question repeated once or twice gets every concern on the table early. If there are too many for one visit, the plan for which wait is made with the patient. A transition statement is what signals the exam.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3636, Hazard Communication Standard: Labels and Pictograms, Signal Words and Hazard Statements
preguntas.subtema: Signal words · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: A chemical carries two hazards: one warrants the signal word Danger and the other Warning. What appears on the label?
opciones: Only Danger, since one signal word appears and it is the more severe
Both words, each next to its own hazard statement
Only the word Warning, since the less severe word applies to the mixture as a whole
Neither; when hazards conflict the label shows pictograms only
preguntas.explicacion: There are only two signal words. Within a hazard class, Danger marks the more severe hazards and Warning the less severe ones, and a label carries a single signal word no matter how many hazards the chemical has; when one hazard calls for Danger and another for Warning, only Danger appears. The hazard statements, by contrast, are all included, and may be combined to improve readability. Pictograms never replace the signal word; they are a separate required element.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Disclosure Accounting
preguntas.subtema: Accounting of disclosures · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks for an accounting of disclosures. What period does it cover, and what is left out of it?
opciones: The six years before the request, leaving out treatment, payment and operations disclosures
The six years before the request, including every release the practice made in that time
The two years before the request, leaving out each release made to a business associate
The whole life of the record, leaving out only disclosures the patient authorized in writing
preguntas.explicacion: The accounting reaches back six years at most from the date of the request. Whole categories never appear on it: disclosures made for treatment, for payment or for health care operations; those to the individual or her personal representative; those for notification, disaster relief or facility directories; those made under an authorization; those of a limited data set; those for national security; those to correctional institutions; and those incidental to a permitted use.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Section 6.P The Axioms of Service Recovery
preguntas.subtema: Service recovery · CCMA 6J k207 · CMAA 2B k16
preguntas.pregunta: Among the five basic customer expectations, which one is called the most important?
opciones: Reliability, which signals competence and builds trust
Responsiveness, that things happen in a timely fashion
Assurance, that a problem will be put right quickly
Tangibles, the visible signs that a place is in control
preguntas.explicacion: Five categories of expectation account for most of the difference between high and low satisfaction: reliability, assurance, tangibles, empathy and responsiveness. Reliability is named the most important of the five because it signals organizational competence and builds confidence in the office and the clinician.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: One code classifies a diagnosis together with the complication it produced. What is such a code, and when is a second one added?
opciones: A combination code; a second is added when it lacks the specificity required
A manifestation code; a second is added because it may never be listed first
A default code; a second is added when the record gives no further detail
A placeholder code; a second is added to fill the seventh character position
preguntas.explicacion: A combination code is one code classifying two diagnoses together, or a diagnosis together with a manifestation associated with it, or a diagnosis together with an associated complication. Only the combination code is assigned where it fully identifies the conditions or where the Index directs it, and an additional code goes on as a secondary one only when the combination lacks the necessary specificity.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, "Talking With Your Older Patients", Families and caregivers as part of the health care team
preguntas.subtema: Difficult situations · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k16 · CMA F.1.c(7)(a) / 2027 F.1.d(7)(b)
preguntas.pregunta: An adult son wants to decide about his mother's treatment. No health care agent has been named. Who decides?
opciones: The patient, who stays responsible for her own choices
The son, as the closest relative present at the visit
The provider, until the paperwork naming an agent is signed
Whichever family member brought her to the appointment
preguntas.explicacion: Families, adult children in particular, may want to step in for a parent with cognitive impairment. A relative named as health care agent or proxy has legal authority to decide in some circumstances; without it, the choices remain the patient's own to make, and staff are told to set clear boundaries with the family.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Workplace Violence", Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: De-escalation · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k26 · CMA F.1.f / 2027 F.1.f
preguntas.pregunta: A first attempt to calm an angry relative has not worked. What does the guidance call for next?
opciones: Listening, acknowledging and guiding again, as often as it takes
Chemical restraint, with physical restraint added as an adjunct
Falling back on the fight-or-flight reaction the moment triggers
Calling the aggression management team before any second try
preguntas.explicacion: Staff are told to listen to the person, acknowledge what worries her and steer her respectfully toward a goal, and to run through that as many times as the result requires. Restraint is a last resort and so is the fight-or-flight reaction; aggression management teams are used if needed, not before the conversation has been tried.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Rights & protections under the health care law; and Glossary: Grandfathered health plan
preguntas.subtema: Insurance types · CMA III.G.4.a (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's individual policy is a grandfathered one. What follows from that under the health care law?
opciones: Some of the law's rights and protections may not reach her plan
All of the law's rights and protections reach her plan the same
Her plan has to be replaced by one bought on the Marketplace
Her plan has to add the ten categories of essential benefits
preguntas.explicacion: A grandfathered plan is an individual policy bought on or before 23 March 2010, and the rights and protections the law lays out may not apply to it. Nothing in the law forces the member off that policy or forces the policy to take on the benefit package that plans sold afterwards have to carry.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Balance billing; and Glossary: Allowed amount
preguntas.subtema: Third-party billing · CMAA 4 k61, 6C k87 · CCMA 5L k185 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A provider charges $100 for a service and the plan's allowed amount is $70. Billing the patient the remaining $30 is called what?
opciones: Balance billing, which a preferred provider may not do for covered services
Balance billing, which any provider may do once the deductible has been met
Coinsurance, which the patient owes as a percentage of the allowed amount
A contractual adjustment, which the provider records as revenue not collected
preguntas.explicacion: Billing the patient the gap between the charge and the allowed amount is balance billing, and the glossary uses this exact arithmetic as its example. A provider inside the network has agreed to the allowed amount and may not bill the difference for covered services, so it happens mostly out of network. Coinsurance is the patient's percentage share of the allowed amount, and the write-off of that gap by a contracted provider is the contractual adjustment.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Genetic Information; and EEOC, Genetic Information Discrimination
preguntas.subtema: Sharing information · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA E.2.a(4) · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: What do the two titles of the Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act cover?
opciones: Title I covers health coverage; Title II covers employment decisions
Title I covers employment; Title II covers research participation
Title I covers health coverage; Title II covers genetic laboratories
Title I covers hiring; Title II covers promotion, pay and training
preguntas.explicacion: The 2008 law splits in two. Title I bars health coverage from discriminating on the basis of genetic information, and the rules for it are written by the Treasury and by the Departments of Labor and of Health and Human Services. Title II bars it in employment, with enforcement by the commission on equal employment opportunity; it took effect on November 21, 2009.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, General Compliance Program Guidance (2023), Element 4: Effective Lines of Communication
preguntas.subtema: Auditing and compliance · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which written policies does the OIG guidance say should reach every employee so that concerns are actually reported?
opciones: Confidentiality and non-retaliation policies, given out to all employees
The code of conduct and the privacy notice, given out to all employees
The schedule of consequences and incentives, given out to all employees
The risk assessment findings and audit plan, given out to all employees
preguntas.explicacion: The fourth element is about keeping the lines to the compliance officer open. Policies on confidentiality and on non-retaliation should be written and put into every employee's hands, so that people feel able to raise questions and report possible fraud. The guidance adds that whistleblowers ought to be protected from retaliation, a principle the False Claims Act already carries.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Common Barriers to Communication
preguntas.subtema: Barriers to communication · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.3.b / 2027 F.1.i
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant with five tasks pending walks into a room still thinking about the next one. Which strategy answers that barrier?
opciones: Pause, take a breath and focus on the patient in front of you
Close the door and turn the volume of the television down
Set the lighting to the level that the patient says he prefers
Give the ordered pain relief before starting any teaching
preguntas.explicacion: Lack of attention is its own barrier: it is easy to focus on the tasks instead of the person, so the guidance is to stop at the door, breathe and give the patient your full attention. The other three answers are real strategies for other barriers on the same list, namely noise, light and physiological barriers such as pain.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: The note does not say which side was affected, and the coder reaches for an unspecified code. When is that the right choice?
opciones: When the record does not hold enough detail to assign a more specific code
When the record holds detail for which no specific code has been created
When the provider cannot be reached to be queried before the claim goes out
When the payer's own policy accepts unspecified codes on outpatient claims
preguntas.explicacion: A code titled unspecified is the one to use when the record does not hold enough information to assign something more specific. Codes titled other, or other specified, do a different job: they come in when the record does give detail but no specific code exists for it. Where a category carries no unspecified code, the other specified code may serve for both.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.6 Anatomical Terminology, Directional Terms
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k13 · CMA I.C.6.e (2027 I.C.6.d) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k11 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A note states that the skin is superficial to the bones and the brain is deep to the skull. What do those two terms measure?
opciones: How close a structure lies to the surface of the body
How far a structure lies from the midline of the body
How far a structure lies from the point of attachment
How high a structure lies compared with the head end
preguntas.explicacion: Superficial and deep form a pair about depth alone: superficial is closer to the body surface, deep is farther from it. Distance from the midline is medial and lateral, distance from the trunk within a limb is proximal and distal, and height relative to the head is superior and inferior.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, National Correct Coding Initiative, Replacement Files
preguntas.subtema: Coding applications · CMA III.G.1 (2027 III.G.1) · CMAA 6A · CCMA 5I k184
preguntas.pregunta: How often are the procedure to procedure and medically unlikely edit files updated?
opciones: Quarterly, with a replacement file in between when one is needed
Yearly, on the first of October alongside the diagnosis codes
Yearly, on the first of January alongside the procedure codes
Monthly, on the same schedule as the list of excluded parties
preguntas.explicacion: The edit files are updated four times a year, and CMS issues a replacement file when a change cannot wait for the next quarter. The policy manual behind the edits is revised once a year. Diagnosis codes take effect each October and the exclusion list is checked monthly, which is where the other dates come from.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, HETS EDI: How to Enroll
preguntas.subtema: Eligibility verification · CMA III.G.3.a (2027 III.G.3.a) · CMAA 4 k58 · CCMA 5E · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A group practice bills Medicare electronically under its group number but registered for eligibility checks under an individual number. What is wrong with that?
opciones: The eligibility enrollment has to carry the same number used to bill claims
The eligibility enrollment has to carry the individual number of each provider
The eligibility enrollment has to carry a separate number issued by a contractor
The eligibility enrollment has to carry the number of the vendor that transmits it
preguntas.explicacion: The enrollment asks for the individual or group National Provider Identifier, whichever one is used to bill Medicare claims electronically. A practice that registered for electronic claims under its group number must use that same group number when it registers to check eligibility. The vendor or clearinghouse supplies its own unique identifier separately, and more than one of those can be linked to a single enrollment.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, Information Blocking
preguntas.subtema: Cures Act · CCMA 5 k179 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA I.C.1.c · CMAA 7 k90 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which law turned the sharing of electronic health information into the default expectation, and where do its exceptions live?
opciones: The 21st Century Cures Act of 2016, with the exceptions set out in 45 CFR Part 171
The HITECH Act of 2009, with the exceptions set out in 45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C
The Medicare Access and CHIP Reauthorization Act of 2015, with exceptions in 42 CFR Part 424
The Plain Writing Act of 2010, with the exceptions set out in 45 CFR Part 160
preguntas.explicacion: The 2016 Cures Act turned the sharing of electronic health information into the default expectation and gave the Secretary authority to name activities that are reasonable and necessary and therefore do not amount to information blocking. Those exceptions live in 45 CFR Part 171 and are voluntary: fitting one buys an actor certainty, while missing one does not automatically mean blocking occurred, since every case is judged on its own facts.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Workplace Violence", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Difficult situations · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k16
preguntas.pregunta: Violence by a patient or a visitor directed at staff falls into which type?
opciones: Type II, from a patient, a former patient or a visitor of theirs
Type I, criminal intent with no legitimate relationship
Type III, by colleagues and other members of the staff
Type IV, by someone with a personal tie to an employee
preguntas.explicacion: Workplace violence is classified by intent and by the relationship to the organization. Type I comes from outside, usually with criminal intent; Type II from a patient, a former patient or one of their visitors; Type III from colleagues and staff; and Type IV from someone with a personal relationship to an employee.

preguntas_es.fuente: StatPearls, "Pharmacy Communication Strategies", Other Issues: Health Literacy
preguntas_es.subtema: Health literacy · CCMA 4F k160 · CMAA 2D k17
preguntas_es.pregunta: ¿Qué señales hacen pensar que un paciente puede tener baja alfabetización en salud?
opciones: Citas perdidas, pocas preguntas, no sigue lo indicado
Muchas preguntas, notas detalladas, llega temprano
Una lista larga de medicamentos y varios referidos a especialistas
Un idioma preferido distinto del inglés en el formulario
preguntas_es.explicacion: Entre las señales están las citas perdidas una y otra vez, la medicación que no se toma como se recetó, la dificultad para nombrar los medicamentos o recordar para qué es cada uno y en qué dosis, las pocas preguntas y las pruebas o los referidos a los que no se les da seguimiento. Como la baja alfabetización en salud (health literacy) no se nota por el aspecto de una persona, la atención se da como si todos tuvieran una alfabetización limitada.

preguntas_es.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medicaid: Summary
preguntas_es.subtema: Government insurance plans · CCMA 5 k181 · CMAA 6 k74 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas_es.pregunta: Una paciente que se muda a otro estado pregunta si su Medicaid funcionará igual allí. ¿Cómo se fijan las reglas?
opciones: El gobierno federal fija pautas generales y cada estado escribe sus propias reglas
El gobierno federal escribe un único conjunto de reglas que rige en todos y cada uno de los estados
Cada estado escribe sus reglas sin ninguna pauta federal de ningún tipo por encima
El mercado de seguros de cada estado escribe las reglas de sus propios planes estatales
preguntas_es.explicacion: Medicaid, un seguro de salud del gobierno, ayuda a muchísimas personas de bajos ingresos a pagar sus cuentas médicas. Las pautas generales del programa vienen del gobierno federal, pero las reglas son de cada estado, y un estado puede pedirle a la persona que pague parte del costo de algunos servicios. La elegibilidad puede depender de la edad, el embarazo, la ceguera, la discapacidad, los ingresos y recursos, y la situación migratoria.

preguntas_es.fuente: StatPearls, Telehealth Systems, Issues of Concern
preguntas_es.subtema: Telehealth coverage · CMAA 4C k58 · CCMA 5 k181 · CMA III.G.3 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA 3.7
preguntas_es.pregunta: Una paciente con seguro comercial pregunta si su plan pagará una visita por video en las mismas condiciones que una visita al consultorio. ¿Qué lo decide?
opciones: Las leyes estatales de paridad, que varían y fijan cobertura y pago
La ley federal, que obliga a todo plan a pagarlas con la misma tarifa
Las reglas de Medicare, que los seguros privados están obligados a seguir
Que viva en una zona rural, algo que la cobertura todavía exige
preguntas_es.explicacion: Las leyes de paridad para los seguros privados se fijan estado por estado y son distintas, así que tanto si una visita de telesalud (telehealth) se cubre como cuánto se paga por ella dependen de dónde se emitió el plan. Las políticas de Medicaid también varían por estado. El requisito de ubicación rural era de las viejas reglas de sitio de origen de Medicare, que se dispensaron.

preguntas_es.fuente: CMS, HETS EDI - How to Enroll, Enrollment Information for Providers
preguntas_es.subtema: Eligibility without HETS · CMAA 4C k58 · CCMA 5 k181 · CMA III.G.3 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA 3.7
preguntas_es.pregunta: Una consulta pequeña le factura en papel a Medicare Original y por eso pierde su acceso a HETS. ¿Cómo puede seguir verificando la elegibilidad de Medicare de un paciente?
opciones: Registrándose en el portal seguro de Internet de su contratista de Medicare
Llamando al plan Medicare Advantage del beneficiario para que le den una respuesta
Pasando la consulta por cualquier cámara de compensación ya inscrita en HETS
Pidiéndole a la paciente que imprima su elegibilidad desde su propia cuenta en línea
preguntas_es.explicacion: Un profesional que se salta los pasos de inscripción, o que no manda por vía electrónica las reclamaciones de Medicare Original (Original Medicare), pierde el acceso a HETS. La vía que queda abierta es registrarse en el portal seguro de Internet de un contratista administrativo de Medicare y consultar ahí la elegibilidad. Una cámara de compensación no puede ocupar el lugar del profesional: la inscripción es un acto del propio profesional.

preguntas_es.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, 3rd ed.: Health Literacy Universal Precautions
preguntas_es.subtema: CCMA 4 k160 education methods · CMAA 2D · CMA F.3.a · 2027 F.1.h
preguntas_es.pregunta: ¿Qué significa aplicar en una práctica las precauciones universales de alfabetización en salud?
opciones: Organizar la información y los servicios para que todos los puedan entender y usar
Organizar la información para que sólo reciban ayuda los pacientes con baja alfabetización
Organizar la información a nivel universitario y simplificarla si el paciente lo pide
Organizar los servicios para que el material escrito sustituya del todo la explicación oral
preguntas_es.explicacion: Aquí, las precauciones universales (universal precautions) de alfabetización en salud (health literacy) son la misma postura que se usa con las infecciones: suponer la necesidad y aplicarla a todos. La información y los servicios de salud se organizan para que cualquiera los pueda entender y usar, la comunicación se simplifica y la comprensión se confirma con cada paciente, el sistema se hace más fácil de recorrer y se apoya el autocuidado.

preguntas_es.fuente: AAMA, Code of Ethics
preguntas_es.subtema: Codes of ethics · CCMA 7C · CMA E.7 / 2027 E.6 · RMA I.C.4.a · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas_es.pregunta: ¿Qué principio aparece en el Código de Ética de la AAMA?
opciones: Respetar la información confidencial salvo que la ley exija divulgarla
Denunciar a cualquier compañero que se aparte del protocolo escrito del consultorio
Negarse a ayudar en un procedimiento con el que el asistente no esté de acuerdo
Remitir toda solicitud de expedientes directamente al abogado del consultorio
preguntas_es.explicacion: El código de ética (code of ethics) enumera cinco principios que los miembros se comprometen a buscar: prestar servicio con pleno respeto a la dignidad humana; respetar la información confidencial obtenida en el empleo salvo que la ley autorice divulgarla o un deber responsable lo exija; defender el honor de la profesión y sus altos principios y aceptar sus disciplinas; mejorar continuamente los conocimientos y las habilidades; y participar en actividades de salud comunitaria.

preguntas_es.fuente: HealthIT.gov, FAQ: What is a patient portal?
preguntas_es.subtema: Portal self-service · CMAA 4E k56 · CCMA 5U k172 · CMA III.H.3.a (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.B.6.c · NCMA 3.3
preguntas_es.pregunta: Una paciente acaba de mudarse y quiere que la consulta tenga su dirección nueva sin tener que llamar. ¿Qué funciones del portal enumera la ONC?
opciones: Actualizar sus propios datos de contacto, y descargar y llenar formularios
Actualizar sus propios datos de contacto, y corregir un error de su diagnóstico
Descargar y llenar formularios, y leer las notas de evolución del propio clínico
Cambiar la imagen de su tarjeta del seguro, y firmar el aviso de prácticas de privacidad
preguntas_es.explicacion: Un portal del paciente (patient portal) abre a toda hora el acceso a las alergias, los medicamentos, las vacunas, las visitas recientes, los resúmenes de alta y los resultados. Algunos van más allá y dejan que la paciente le mande un mensaje seguro al clínico, pida un resurtido, reserve una cita no urgente, consulte beneficios y cobertura, pague, corrija sus datos de contacto, descargue formularios y los llene, y lea material educativo.

preguntas_es.fuente: AHRQ, PSNet Patient Safety Primer: Reporting Patient Safety Events
preguntas_es.subtema: CCMA 6 k211 · CMA I.B.11.c · 2027 I.B.10.c · CMAA 3 k44 · NCMA 4.10
preguntas_es.pregunta: ¿Qué característica necesita un sistema de notificación de eventos que sea eficaz?
opciones: Una manera fija de revisar los informes y convertirlos en planes de acción
Una regla que nombre a quien informa en el resumen que se manda a todo el personal
Un límite que deje presentar el informe de un suceso solo a los profesionales con licencia
Una fecha límite anual para la que se presenten todos los informes del año
preguntas_es.explicacion: Cuatro atributos hacen que el sistema funcione: un ambiente que apoye la notificación y cuide la privacidad de quien informa, informes que lleguen de un abanico amplio de personal, resúmenes compartidos sin demora, y una manera estructurada de revisar los informes y construir planes de acción. La notificación suele ser confidencial, con protección legal salvo cuando hay conducta indebida.

preguntas_es.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0, Tool: Two-Challenge Rule
preguntas_es.subtema: Escalation · CCMA 6K k210 · CMAA 2B k25 · RMA I.D.2.a
preguntas_es.pregunta: Un compañero cuestiona una decisión que usted tomó y señala un riesgo para el paciente. ¿Cuál es su responsabilidad?
opciones: Reconocer la preocupación en vez de ignorar a la persona
Explicar el razonamiento una vez y seguir con lo previsto
Mandarlo con el supervisor antes de darle una respuesta
Anotar el desafío en el expediente médico del paciente
preguntas_es.explicacion: Recibir un desafío trae su propio deber: reconocer la preocupación en lugar de ignorar a quien la plantea. Cualquiera del equipo debería tener el poder de detener el proceso cuando percibe una falla esencial de seguridad, lo que para todo hasta que el asunto se resuelve. Ese intercambio marca el tono de los que vienen después.

preguntas_es.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medigap basics
preguntas_es.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1
preguntas_es.pregunta: Dos aseguradoras venden el Plan G de Medigap. ¿En qué se diferencian las dos pólizas?
opciones: En el precio, porque las pólizas con la misma letra dan los mismos beneficios básicos
En los beneficios, porque cada compañía diseña la cobertura que dará su propia póliza
En el período de espera, porque cada compañía fija cuánto esperan las afecciones previas
En la red, porque cada compañía contrata hospitales para sus pólizas con letra
preguntas_es.explicacion: Las pólizas Medigap están estandarizadas: dos pólizas con la misma letra dan los mismos beneficios básicos dondequiera que viva el comprador y quienquiera que las venda, así que entre dos pólizas del Plan G la diferencia es el precio. En la mayoría de los estados se venden diez tipos, con las letras de la A a la D, la F, la G y de la K a la N; Massachusetts, Minnesota y Wisconsin estandarizan sus pólizas de otra manera.

preguntas_es.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet MLN006400 Information for Critical Access Hospitals: regulatory requirements
preguntas_es.subtema: Critical access hospital services · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1
preguntas_es.pregunta: Además de su límite de camas, ¿qué requisito de funcionamiento debe cumplir un hospital de acceso crítico?
opciones: Servicios de emergencia a toda hora, los siete días, con personal presente o de guardia
Un quirófano con personal a toda hora para que ningún paciente tenga que esperar sala
Un programa intensivo de rehabilitación supervisado a diario por un médico para cada paciente
Una junta directiva cuya mayoría está formada por pacientes atendidos en el hospital
preguntas_es.explicacion: Entre los requisitos básicos, el hospital debe dar servicios de emergencia las 24 horas del día, los siete días de la semana, con personal presente o de guardia dentro de tiempos de respuesta fijados. También informa una estadía promedio de internación aguda de 96 horas o menos al año, sin contar los días de cama de transición ni de unidades separadas. La junta con mayoría de pacientes es del programa de centros de salud.

preguntas_es.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse: Prevent, Detect, Report (MLN4649244), Physician Self-Referral Law
preguntas_es.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas_es.pregunta: Según la ley de autorreferido del médico, ¿qué cuenta como relación financiera con una entidad?
opciones: Propiedad o inversión en la entidad, o un acuerdo de compensación
Sólo una participación de propiedad, sea directa o sea indirecta
Sólo un acuerdo de compensación, y únicamente cuando es directo
Cualquier referido que se le mande a una entidad del mismo grupo médico
preguntas_es.explicacion: La ley alcanza al médico que refiere servicios de salud designados a una entidad en la que él, o alguien de su familia directa, tiene una relación financiera. Esa relación puede ser una participación de propiedad o de inversión en la entidad, o bien un acuerdo de compensación con ella, y cualquiera de las dos puede ser directa o indirecta.

preguntas_es.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Error Reduction and Prevention", Function: Active and Latent Errors
preguntas_es.subtema: Incident reporting · CCMA 7F · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3E k44
preguntas_es.pregunta: ¿Qué diferencia hay entre un error activo y un error latente?
opciones: El activo es el acto que daña; el latente es el fallo que espera su momento
El activo se detecta a tiempo; el latente le llega al paciente más tarde
El activo se notifica en el acto; el latente se encuentra en una auditoría
El activo involucra un equipo; el latente, una decisión del personal
preguntas_es.explicacion: Un error activo (active error) es un hecho concreto que daña al paciente y en el que participa el profesional que da la atención: operar el ojo equivocado, por ejemplo. Un error latente (latent error) es un fallo metido en el proceso —equipo defectuoso, un mal diseño del sistema, una estructura organizativa débil— que puede pasar inadvertido mucho tiempo. Un ventilador mecánico que falla es un error latente; no revisarlo antes de usarlo es uno activo.

preguntas_es.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas_es.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.b) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas_es.pregunta: Un panel de lípidos informa HDL y LDL. ¿Qué afirmación corresponde a esas dos abreviaturas?
opciones: HDL es lipoproteína de alta densidad, el colesterol bueno; LDL es el malo
HDL es lipoproteína de densidad pesada, el colesterol malo; LDL es el bueno
HDL es lípido alto de la dieta, el colesterol bueno; LDL es el lípido bajo de la dieta
HDL es lipasa de densidad hepática, la enzima buena; LDL es la de origen hepático
preguntas_es.explicacion: HDL es high density lipoprotein, la lipoproteína de alta densidad, descrita como el colesterol bueno, y LDL es low density lipoprotein, la de baja densidad, el malo. Las dos son tipos de colesterol que viajan en la sangre y las dos salen en el mismo panel, así que confundirlas le invierte al paciente el sentido de todo el resultado.

preguntas_es.fuente: CMS, Administrative Simplification: Health Care Payment and Remittance Advice and EFT
preguntas_es.subtema: Remittance advice · CMA III.G.3.b(3) (exam through June 2027) · CMAA 5 k79 · CCMA 5 k181
preguntas_es.pregunta: ¿Por qué la transferencia de fondos de un plan de salud y su aviso de remesa llevan el mismo segmento de rastreo?
opciones: Para emparejar el pago con la remesa que lo explica, lo que se llama reasociación
Para que el banco confirme el número de ruta antes de liberar los fondos
Para que el plan pruebe que entregó la remesa antes de hacer el pago
Para que el profesional registre el pago antes de que llegue el aviso de remesa
preguntas_es.explicacion: A los planes de salud se les exige poner el segmento de rastreo del 835 en el registro adicional de la entrada de crédito o depósito corporativo que lleva el dinero. Ese segmento tiene que coincidir con el del aviso de remesa (remittance advice) que describe el pago, para que los fondos y su explicación se puedan juntar: el paso que se conoce como reasociación.

preguntas_es.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Part A (Hospital Insurance) costs
preguntas_es.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas_es.pregunta: ¿Para qué se usan los sesenta días de reserva vitalicios de la Parte A de Medicare?
opciones: Para los días noventa y uno a ciento cincuenta de una hospitalización, a $868 al día
Para los días sesenta y uno a noventa de una hospitalización, que cuestan $434 al día
Para los días veintiuno a cien de una estancia de enfermería especializada, a $217 al día
Para los primeros sesenta días de cada período de beneficio, que no tienen ningún cargo
preguntas_es.explicacion: Los días de reserva vitalicios (lifetime reserve days) son los sesenta días extra de internación que llevan al paciente del día noventa y uno al día ciento cincuenta, a $868 al día en 2026, y una vez usados se pierden. Los días sesenta y uno a noventa cuestan $434, y la tarifa de enfermería especializada de $217 es de otro beneficio distinto.

preguntas_es.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 2 Communication, 2.2 Common Barriers to Communication
preguntas_es.subtema: Barriers to communication · CCMA 6D k195 · CMAA 2D k17 · CMA F.3.b / 2027 F.1.i
preguntas_es.pregunta: A un paciente le acaban de dar un sedante y un opioide para el dolor. ¿Qué significa eso para los formularios que todavía esperan su firma?
opciones: No puede firmarlos después de que le dieron esos medicamentos
Puede firmarlos siempre que un familiar sea testigo de la firma
Puede firmarlos una vez que le repita a usted las instrucciones
Puede firmarlos porque el alivio del dolor se dio antes de enseñar
preguntas_es.explicacion: El dolor es una barrera fisiológica, así que el alivio debe venir antes de la enseñanza. El mismo párrafo añade el límite que toma a muchos por sorpresa: los sedantes y algunos analgésicos afectan la capacidad de recibir y percibir un mensaje, lo que significa que el paciente no debe firmar documentos de atención médica una vez que se los han dado. Un testigo o una repetición no lo arreglan.

preguntas_es.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology
preguntas_es.subtema: Setup walk-through · CMAA 4H k62 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas_es.pregunta: Al guiar a una paciente nueva por la preparación, ¿qué dos puntos quiere la guía que se cubran para que pueda volver a encontrar la cita?
opciones: Cómo le llegará la invitación y cómo se ve, y cómo crear un acceso directo a la aplicación
Cómo le llegará la invitación y cómo se ve, y cómo restablecer la contraseña de su cuenta
Cómo crear un acceso directo a la aplicación, y cómo grabar la visita para sus propias notas
Cómo restablecer la contraseña de su cuenta, y cómo llamar a la mesa de ayuda del proveedor
preguntas_es.explicacion: El recorrido de preparación cubre instalar el programa que haga falta, actualizar el navegador y desbloquear los complementos, abrir la plataforma, comprobar que la cámara y el audio funcionan, y qué funciones va a necesitar de verdad para no abrumarse. También cubre cómo volver a encontrar la aplicación o crear un acceso directo, y cómo se compartirá la invitación a la cita y cómo se verá.

preguntas_es.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare Summary Notice (MSN)
preguntas_es.subtema: Explanation of benefits · CMAA 5 k78 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.2
preguntas_es.pregunta: ¿Cada cuánto recibe un Resumen de Medicare un paciente con Medicare Original?
opciones: Al menos dos veces al año, y sólo por los períodos en que se facturaron servicios
Al menos una vez al mes, se haya facturado o no algún servicio en el período
Después de cada reclamación, porque cada reclamación procesada genera un aviso en papel
Una vez al año, junto con el aviso de los nuevos montos del deducible
preguntas_es.explicacion: En Medicare Original (Original Medicare), el Resumen de Medicare (Medicare Summary Notice) llega por correo al menos dos veces al año, es decir, cada 6 meses, y sólo si la persona recibió servicios o suministros en ese período. Quien elige los avisos electrónicos recibe un enlace por correo electrónico cada mes en que hay una reclamación procesada, que es la única situación parecida a un aviso por reclamación. Las cifras anuales de costos se publican aparte.
